body.translated_text: Compiled by the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Avalokitasiṃha</s>
<s>Dharmasamuccaya</s> (Compendium of Dharma)
First <s>udāna</s> (inspired utterance)

children.translated_text: (The chapters of the <s>jitadharmakāya</s> section are: impermanence,

children.text: apramādaḥ kāmatṛṣṇe strī ca madyena te daśa // ) //
children.translated_text: non-negligence, sensual craving, women, and intoxication — these are the ten.)

body.translated_text: (1) Chapter on Victory
Auspicious invocation
// Oṃ, homage to the <s>Buddha</s> //

children.translated_text: He who, having abandoned all outflows, possessing stainless glory,
lifts up the world submerged in the mire of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) through the quality of impartial compassion — homage to that supreme one of the three realms. // Dhs_1.1 //

body.translated_text: The author's pledge

children.translated_text: From the vast ocean of the <s>Saddharma Smṛtyupasthāna Sūtra</s>,
I shall extract verses devoted to being the eye of the world. // Dhs_1.2 //

body.translated_text: The six abodes of liberation

children.translated_text: Non-negligence, faith, the exertion of vigor, steadfastness,
the practice of knowledge, and attachment to the good — these are the six abodes of liberation. // Dhs_1.3 //

body.translated_text: The nine causes for attaining peace

children.translated_text: Generosity, morality, self-control, patience, loving-kindness toward beings, non-violence,
compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity — these are the causes for attaining peace. // Dhs_1.4 //

body.translated_text: The chief causes of hell

children.translated_text: Fickleness, association with evil, cruelty, false speech,
wrong views, and negligence — these are the chief causes of hell. // Dhs_1.5 //

body.translated_text: Six causes of birth among <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts)

children.text: mātsaryamīrṣyā kaṭuvākyatā hi pramādasevā viratiḥ śubhācca /
children.translated_text: Miserliness, envy, harsh speech, indulgence in negligence, abstaining from virtue,

children.text: tattveṣvabhidroharataṃ manaśca preteṣu panthāna ihodbhavanti // Dhs_1.6 //
children.translated_text: and a mind delighting in hostility toward truths — these paths of birth among <s>pretas</s> arise here. // Dhs_1.6 //

body.translated_text: Means of birth in the animal realm

children.text: ajñānasevā jaḍa (tā) ca buddheḥ saddharmanāśaḥ priyamaithunatvam /
children.translated_text: Indulgence in ignorance, dullness of intellect, the destruction of the true Dharma, fondness for sexual intercourse,

children.text: āhāraśaktiḥ prabalā ca nidrā tiryaggatau ca pravadanti hetum // Dhs_1.7 //
children.translated_text: powerful appetite for food, and excessive sleep — these are declared the causes of birth in the animal realm. // Dhs_1.7 //

body.translated_text: The fruit of <s>karma</s>

children.translated_text: Having performed great threefold unwholesome action of body, speech, and mind,
the succession of consequences is seen through <s>karma</s>. // Dhs_1.8 //
For the foolish too, that succession continues ever upward.

children.text: śubhañca trividhaṃ kṛtvā sādhavo yānti nirvṛtim // Dhs_1.9 //
children.translated_text: But having performed threefold wholesome action, the virtuous go to bliss. // Dhs_1.9 //

children.text: tasmāt karmaphalaṃ matvā pramādasya ca varjanam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, having understood the fruit of <s>karma</s> and the avoidance of negligence,
one acts for one's welfare through wisdom — this is the unsurpassed happiness. // Dhs_1.10 //
For one who always gives and is moral, who has compassion for all beings,
all accomplishments succeed equally — therefore one should be devoted to morality. // Dhs_1.11 //

body.translated_text: Whose endeavors succeed?

children.translated_text: For one endowed with <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), a being who has abandoned anxious expectations,
who is devoted to benefiting others — success of endeavors is firmly established. // Dhs_1.12 //
For one who is content and vigilant, who seeks the welfare of all beings,
who is free from desire and hatred — success of endeavors is firmly established. // Dhs_1.13 //
For one who has abandoned the distinction of friend and foe, whose mind is equanimous,
who has transcended the paths of lower rebirths — success of endeavors is firmly established. // Dhs_1.14 //

children.text: evaṃ ca tasya dhīrasya dharmadānaratasya ca /
children.translated_text: Thus for that steadfast one who delights in the gift of Dharma,
who is free from miserliness and envy — success of endeavors is firmly established. // Dhs_1.15 //
For one who abides in restraint, who is peaceful, who delights in honoring the teacher,
who knows the proper procedure for what should and should not be done — success of endeavors is firmly established. // Dhs_1.16 //
For one who is guileless, extremely skillful, who always speaks pleasant words,
who is capable of meditation and study — success of endeavors is firmly established. // Dhs_1.17 //
For one who knows the proper procedure of place and time, who discerns the achievable from the unachievable,
who knows the proper means within one's power — success of endeavors is firmly established. // Dhs_1.18 //

body.translated_text: Exposition of the true nature of dharmas through the means of conquering anger and the like

children.text: akrodhena hataḥ krodhaḥ kṣamayā krūratā jitā /
children.translated_text: Anger is destroyed by non-anger; cruelty is conquered by patience;

children.text: dharmeṇa nirjito 'dharmaḥ prabhayā vijitaṃ tamaḥ // Dhs_1.19 //
children.translated_text: non-dharma is vanquished by Dharma; darkness is conquered by radiance. // Dhs_1.19 //

body.translated_text: Praise of truth and the like

children.translated_text: False speech is destroyed by truth; slander by concentration;

children.text: pārūṣyaṃ mārdava jitaṃ abaddhaṃ bandhanā jitam // Dhs_1.20 //
children.translated_text: harshness is conquered by gentleness; incoherent talk is conquered by coherence. // Dhs_1.20 //

children.text: prāṇātipāto maitryā ca steyaṃ dānaiḥ sadā jitam /
children.translated_text: Taking life is conquered by <s>maitrī</s>; theft is always conquered by generosity;
unwise mental engagement is always conquered by wise engagement. // Dhs_1.21 //

children.text: avidyā vidyayā jitā divasena tathā kṣapā /
children.translated_text: Ignorance is conquered by knowledge, just as night by day;

children.text: śuklapakṣeṇa ca kṛṣṇapakṣo (hi) sarvaśo jitaḥ // Dhs_1.22 //
children.translated_text: the dark fortnight is conquered in every way by the bright fortnight. // Dhs_1.22 //
Unvanquished in wrong desires, through the wisdom of investigating reality,

children.text: āryāṣṭāṅgena mārgeṇa yonijena sadā jitaḥ // Dhs_1.23 //
children.translated_text: one is always conquered by the noble eightfold path through wise engagement. // Dhs_1.23 //
By the four confidences, miserliness is indeed conquered;

children.text: vismṛtiśca hatā smṛtyā kṣaṇenātmānameva ca // Dhs_1.24 //
children.translated_text: forgetfulness is destroyed by mindfulness, and the self by the moment. // Dhs_1.24 //
Those devoted to dwelling in the forest conquer people subject to passion;
mountains are conquered by <s>Meru</s>; garlands of trees by a great tree. // Dhs_1.25 //
All water-born fords are conquered by the ocean;
all planets and stars are conquered by the splendor of the sun. // Dhs_1.26 //
The permanent is conquered by the impermanent; poverty by the wealth of generosity;

children.text: śāṭhyaṃ na mārdava jitaṃ satyenānṛtiko hataḥ // Dhs_1.27 //
children.translated_text: fraud is conquered by gentleness; the liar is destroyed by truth. // Dhs_1.27 //
The unreal is vanquished by the real; trees and vegetation by fire;
thirst is conquered by water; hunger by food likewise. // Dhs_1.28 //

body.translated_text: Praise of vigor

children.text: siṃhena vijitāḥ sarve mṛgāḥ sattvādhikāśca ye /
children.translated_text: By the lion are conquered all beasts and those of greater strength;

children.text: santāpena mahecchā ca jitā nityaṃ prakīrtyate // Dhs_1.29 //
children.translated_text: through austerity, great desire is declared always conquered. // Dhs_1.29 //
Compassion is always praised; lack of compassion is never praised;

children.text: vīryeṇa nirjitaṃ sarva kausīdyaṃ mohavardhanam // Dhs_1.30 //
children.translated_text: by vigor is conquered all laziness, which increases delusion. // Dhs_1.30 //
Praise of the person who sees reality: By those ever-subdued persons endowed with superior knowledge, who see reality,
are conquered those of cruel deeds, those given to false speech. // Dhs_1.31 //
By the <s>Buddha</s> are all conquered — the heretics and crooked speakers;
<s>asuras</s> are conquered by the <s>devas</s> — this is established through the Dharma. // Dhs_1.32 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the first chapter on Victory //
(2) Chapter on Dharma Teaching
What should a teacher be like?

children.text: yo hi deśayate dharma kṣemaṃ nirvāṇagāminam /
children.translated_text: One who teaches the Dharma that is secure and leads to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>,
that one, the cutter of all bonds, becomes the teacher of beings. // Dhs_2.1 //

children.text: chittvā mohamayaṃ pāśaṃ yo hi deśayate śivam /
children.translated_text: One who, having cut the noose of delusion, teaches what is auspicious,
is called the guide to the right path, the averter from the wrong path. // Dhs_2.2 //

children.text: dharmasya pravaratvam yena dharmeṇa manujāstaranti bhavasāgaram /
children.translated_text: The excellence of the Dharma: The Dharma by which humans cross the ocean of existence,

children.text: saddharmaprabaraḥ prokto na dharmo laukiko hi saḥ // Dhs_2.3 //
children.translated_text: is declared the supreme true Dharma — it is not a worldly dharma. // Dhs_2.3 //
The being who possesses these four fields —

children.text: tasyedaṃ saphalaṃ janma kathitaṃ mārgadeśakaiḥ // Dhs_2.4 //
children.translated_text: his birth is said to be fruitful, as declared by those who show the path. // Dhs_2.4 //
Having obtained complete faculties and having attained the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: yo na dharmarato martyaḥ sa paścādanutapyate // Dhs_2.5 //
children.translated_text: the mortal who does not delight in the Dharma repents afterward. // Dhs_2.5 //
Union with <s>Yama</s>: For those whose minds are always attached, who always seek pleasures,
who are addicted to sons and wives — the Ender approaches those beings. // Dhs_2.6 //
Mastering the mind: The mind confused by various faults, by those defects of intention,

children.text: cittaṃ nayatyupāyena cittabaddhā hi dehinaḥ // Dhs_2.7 //
children.translated_text: is led by skillful means — for beings are bound by the mind. // Dhs_2.7 //
Of the extremely fierce and difficult to tame, especially for one who desires attainment,

children.text: na cittasya vaśaṃ gacchet śatrubhūtaṃ hi tannṛṇām // Dhs_2.8 //
children.translated_text: one should not come under the power of the mind — for it is the enemy of people. // Dhs_2.8 //
Through learning, through proper instruction, through repeated cultivation,

children.text: dharmeṇa śāmyate cittaṃ jālineva yathā hayaḥ // Dhs_2.9 //
children.translated_text: the mind is pacified by the Dharma, just as a horse by the bridle. // Dhs_2.9 //

children.text: saddharmaśravaṇaphalam saddharmaśravaṇaṃ kṛtvā pāpād viramate pumān /
children.translated_text: The fruit of hearing the true Dharma: Having heard the true Dharma, a person desists from evil;
one always attains the practice leading to welfare. // Dhs_2.10 //
Having heard the true Dharma, the mind attains delight;

children.text: kuśalaṃ cāsya sumahat sandhāne sampratīkṣate // Dhs_2.11 //
children.translated_text: great merit awaits one in the future. // Dhs_2.11 //

children.text: śrutvā bhavati dharmātmā śrutvā pāpaṃ na kurvate /
children.translated_text: Having heard, one becomes righteous; having heard, one does not commit evil;
having heard, knowing the fruit of <s>karma</s>, one attains <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_2.12 //

children.text: śrutvā vedayate dharma śrutvā buddhaḥ prasīdati /
children.translated_text: Having heard, one understands the Dharma; having heard, one delights in the <s>Buddha</s>;

children.text: śrutvā dharmaṃ vimokṣāya yatate paṇḍito naraḥ // Dhs_2.13 //
children.translated_text: having heard, the wise person strives for liberation from the Dharma. // Dhs_2.13 //
Having heard, a person becomes a knower of the true characteristics of the Dharma;

children.text: tasmācchrutvā prayatnena buddhiḥ kāryā prayatnataḥ // Dhs_2.14 //
children.translated_text: therefore, having heard, one should diligently apply wisdom with effort. // Dhs_2.14 //
Having heard the discourse taught by the <s>Sugata</s> that turns one away from <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: prahāya tṛṣṇāṃ vividhāṃ prayāti padamavyayam // Dhs_2.15 //
children.translated_text: abandoning manifold craving, one goes to the imperishable state. // Dhs_2.15 //
Having heard the fourfold dependability of dharmas, the imperishable arising and cessation,

children.text: śrutvā tāṃ jñāyate sarvā pumān śraddhāvibhāvitaḥ // Dhs_2.16 //
children.translated_text: a person established in faith knows all of it. // Dhs_2.16 //
These two characteristics of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases), and <s>dhātus</s> (elements) —

children.text: śrutvā tajjñāyate sarva tasmāt dharmaparo bhavet // Dhs_2.17 //
children.translated_text: having heard, one knows all that; therefore one should be devoted to the Dharma. // Dhs_2.17 //
The three powerful faults that are the bonds of all <s>saṃsāra</s> —
they are completely destroyed through hearing the true Dharma. // Dhs_2.18 //
The complete characteristic of origination and also of cessation without remainder —
the learned one understands that; therefore learning is supreme. // Dhs_2.19 //
For a being who has reached the time of death, who is afflicted by painful feelings,

children.text: na vyathā śrutamālambya svalpāpi hṛdi jāyate // Dhs_2.20 //
children.translated_text: not even the slightest distress arises in the heart, relying on what has been heard. // Dhs_2.20 //
Those trees of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) that have been burned on all sides by right knowledge —
their re-growth is never again found. // Dhs_2.21 //
Learning refined by non-negligence gives rise to all happiness;

children.text: śreyasaśva śrutaṃ mūlaṃ tasmācchrutaparo bhavet // Dhs_2.22 //
children.translated_text: learning is the root of welfare — therefore one should be devoted to learning. // Dhs_2.22 //
Having heard the true Dharma and having attended upon the wise elders,
the learned person goes to the unsurpassed state, free from old age and death. // Dhs_2.23 //

children.text: dharmeṇa vartate śrutvā duḥkhānmucyeta vai yathā /
children.translated_text: Having heard, one acts by the Dharma so that one may be freed from suffering;

children.text: śrutvā bhavati maitryātmā tasmācchreyaḥ paraṃ śrutam // Dhs_2.24 //
children.translated_text: having heard, one becomes one whose nature is loving-kindness — therefore learning is the highest good. // Dhs_2.24 //
Through hearing, wisdom of body, speech, and mind arises for beings;
therefore, one who desires right understanding should listen with respect. // Dhs_2.25 //
Having heard and having resorted to cultivation, with firm vigor and exertion,

children.text: taranti puruṣāstūrṇa tribhava vipulaṃ mahat // Dhs_2.26 //
children.translated_text: people quickly cross the vast, great triple existence. // Dhs_2.26 //
The person who has heard becomes wealthy in all respects through all;
one endowed with the wealth of unlearned matters, the wise call a pauper. // Dhs_2.27 //

body.translated_text: The fruit of the destruction of the true Dharma

children.translated_text: For one whose wealth of true Dharma is lost, who is abandoned by the teacher,

children.text: viphalaṃ jīvitaṃ ceṣṭaṃ pāpairupahatasya ca // Dhs_2.28 //
children.translated_text: life and effort are fruitless — for one who is stricken by evil. // Dhs_2.28 //

body.translated_text: The capacity of negligence and the like to produce undesirable fruits

children.translated_text: For the negligent one, the lazy one, one with evil friends —

children.text: jīvitaṃ niṣphalaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ bījamuptaṃ yathosare // Dhs_2.29 //
children.translated_text: life is seen as fruitless, like a seed sown on barren ground. // Dhs_2.29 //

body.translated_text: The authority of the scriptures

children.translated_text: The discerning say that the meaning freed from hearing and seeing is the true meaning;
a meaning freed only from the eyes is not called the true meaning. // Dhs_2.30 //

children.text: dharmasevanāgrahaḥ yo hi dharma parityajya adharmamanutiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: The imperative of practicing the Dharma: One who, having abandoned the Dharma, follows <s>adharma</s>,
that person abandons medicine and indulges in disease. // Dhs_2.31 //
By practicing and practicing, the Dharma manifests in many ways for people,
just as a garden flourishes through the assembly of rains. // Dhs_2.32 //
Here at the <s>vajrāsana</s> (diamond seat) is the ground; it does not exist otherwise in <s>saṃsāra</s>;
the arising of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) and the supreme attainment of <s>bodhi</s>. // Dhs_2.33 //
One who practices the Dharma, whose self is peaceful, who rises early, who is composed —

children.text: avaśyaṃ śubhabhāgīsyāt sa pramādena vañcitaḥ // Dhs_2.34 //
children.translated_text: will certainly be a partaker of the good, though deceived by negligence. // Dhs_2.34 //
The imperative of cultivating knowledge: Therefore, having understood the qualities of knowledge, the wise person should cultivate knowledge;

children.text: nahyajñānena saṃyuktaṃ pumān kaścit pratibhavet // Dhs_2.35 //
children.translated_text: for no person endowed with ignorance can attain distinction. // Dhs_2.35 //

children.text: dharmānusāriṇī śraddhā dharmānusāriṇī śraddhā yathā yāti sukhāvahā /
children.translated_text: Faith that follows the Dharma: Faith that follows the Dharma, as it proceeds, brings happiness.
She (the Dharma-teaching) rescues from the worst lower realms and is a great strength in calamities. // Dhs_2.36 //
Like a lamp in darkness, like medicine for the sick,

children.text: arthānāṃ netra bhūtā sā daridrāṇāṃ mahadbalam // Dhs_2.37 //
children.translated_text: she is a guide for the goals and a great strength for the destitute. // Dhs_2.37 //
For those being swept away by existence and the rest, she precedes and brings happiness;
for those intoxicated and maddened by heedlessness, she is the destroyer of heedlessness. // Dhs_2.38 //

children.text: śāntapadaprāpteḥ phalam sa hi yattatpadaṃ śāntaṃ nirvāṇamunibhirvṛtam /
children.translated_text: The fruit of attaining the peaceful state: For that state which is peaceful, <s>nirvāṇa</s>, resorted to by sages,
she leads one to that tirelessly, preceded by right knowledge. // Dhs_2.39 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the second chapter, on Dharma-teaching. //
(3) Chapter on Loathing the Body
Examination of the body's true nature

children.translated_text: Even with honors, nourishment, flesh, and beds and seats and the like,

children.text: na svīkartumayaṃ kāyaḥ kadācit kenacit kṛtaḥ // Dhs_3.1 //
children.translated_text: this body cannot be made one's own — it was never made by anyone. // Dhs_3.1 //

body.translated_text: The body's enmity

children.translated_text: Of the ungrateful, the incompetent, the one who always strikes at vulnerable points —

children.text: kaḥ kāyasya riporartha pāpaṃ kuryād vicakṣaṇaḥ // Dhs_3.2 //
children.translated_text: what wise person would do evil for the sake of the body, which is an enemy? // Dhs_3.2 //
A vessel of disease and many misfortunes,
a mass of impure limbs — this is what is called the body. // Dhs_3.3 //

body.translated_text: Death is unknowable and life is momentary

children.translated_text: Death, which is imminent, is unknowable by those who reflect on truth;

children.text: jīvitaṃ ca kṣaṇādūrdhvaṃ na gacchati nirūpyate // Dhs_3.4 //
children.translated_text: and life does not extend beyond a single moment, when examined. // Dhs_3.4 //

body.translated_text: The body is to be abandoned

children.translated_text: This body, constructed by lifespan, karma, and purpose, is to be abandoned;

children.text: api viddhastathā śete kāṣṭhaloṣṭhasamo bhuvi // Dhs_3.5 //
children.translated_text: even when pierced, it lies upon the ground like wood or a clod of earth. // Dhs_3.5 //

children.text: kṣaṇe kṣaṇe 'pi kāyo 'yaṃ jīryate na nivartate /
children.translated_text: This body decays moment by moment and does not reverse;
yet the young are deluded by the intoxication of youth (with bewildered minds). // Dhs_3.6 //
Intoxicated by the pride of wealth and grain, they do harm to themselves;

children.text: tannāśamupayātyevaṃ sa ca pāpena dahayate // Dhs_3.7 //
children.translated_text: that [wealth] proceeds to destruction, and he is burned by his sin. // Dhs_3.7 //

body.translated_text: Censure of the unrighteous

children.text: na manuṣyā manuṣyāste yebhyo dharmo na rocate /
children.translated_text: Those are not human beings for whom the Dharma is not pleasing;

children.text: na mārge ca sthitāstattve nirvāṇapuragāmike // Dhs_3.8 //
children.translated_text: they do not stand on the path to truth, which leads to the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_3.8 //

body.translated_text: The human birth as a means to cross the ocean of existence

children.text: kathaṃ prāpya hi mānuṣyaṃ śreyasāmālayaṃ mahat /
children.translated_text: How, having obtained this human birth, a great abode of blessings,
do they not board the raft of knowledge and cross over from the ocean of existence? // Dhs_3.9 //

body.translated_text: The momentariness of life

children.translated_text: Resembling lightning and a firebrand, like a city of <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians),

children.text: sadā tad yāti rabhasaṃ jīvitaṃ sarvadehinām // Dhs_3.10 //
children.translated_text: the life of all embodied beings always passes swiftly. // Dhs_3.10 //

children.text: śarīre na madaṃ kuryāt kṣaṇike bhaṅgure sadā /
children.translated_text: One should not take pride in the body, which is always momentary and perishable,
transient, fickle, without essence, and fearful of old age and death. // Dhs_3.11 //
Unperceived by the meditator, this is a great abode of sorrows,
and the body is to be understood as a field of the auspicious and the inauspicious. // Dhs_3.12 //

body.translated_text: The secret of a fruitful life

children.translated_text: He whose body is adorned with knowledge, moral conduct, compassion, and generosity —

children.text: tasya sattvaikasārasya śarīraṃ saphalaṃ matam // Dhs_3.13 //
children.translated_text: the body of that being, whose sole essence is beings' [welfare], is considered fruitful. // Dhs_3.13 //

body.translated_text: Liberation through knowledge of the elements

children.translated_text: This entire body, freed from the destroyer of the elements,

children.text: śarīradhātu vicayāt sākṣād bhavati netarāt // Dhs_3.14 //
children.translated_text: comes about through the analysis of the bodily elements — directly, not otherwise. // Dhs_3.14 //
He who, having released the bodily element, is attached to other elements —
he is liberated only through suffering, from the instruction on the nature of elements. // Dhs_3.15 //
The gold element does not serve for the cessation of suffering
as one who knows the truth of the bodily elements is liberated from suffering. // Dhs_3.16 //
From suffering arises suffering; by that, the sufferer is not protected;
the skilled one is afflicted by all fears of kings, thieves, and the like. // Dhs_3.17 //
Therefore one should always avoid from afar that which is purposeless;

children.text: varjanāt sukhito duṣṭasaṅgrahād duḥkhitaḥ pumān // Dhs_3.18 //
children.translated_text: by avoidance a person is happy; by harboring the wicked, he is miserable. // Dhs_3.18 //
He who knows the truth of the bodily elements, who knows the true nature of the characteristics of the elements,
devoted to meditation and study, burns down the mountains of defilements. // Dhs_3.19 //
Therefore the wise one examines the elements born of the body;

children.text: teṣāṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ jñātvā mokṣo bhavati dehinām // Dhs_3.20 //
children.translated_text: having known their own-characteristics, liberation comes about for embodied beings. // Dhs_3.20 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the third chapter, on Loathing the Body. //
(4) Chapter on Passing Away (<s>Parivarta</s>)
For whom does time revolve?

children.translated_text: For one who is not free from desire for sense pleasures, who is parched by craving,
whose senses and mind are restless — time revolves for him. // Dhs_4.1 //
For the embodied being who meditates on impermanence yet is attached to happiness,
who is intoxicated by the sight of women — time revolves for him. // Dhs_4.2 //
For one who is subject to birth and death, deluded by craving,

children.text: bālasya tu janasyāsya kālo 'yaṃ parivartate // Dhs_4.3 //
children.translated_text: for this foolish person — time revolves for him. // Dhs_4.3 //
For one bound by the conduct of the destinies, subject to agitation,
confused by the poison of heedlessness — time revolves for him. // Dhs_4.4 //
For one attached to excitement and the rest, delighting in bodily beauty,
whose mind is not sated by gains — time revolves for him. // Dhs_4.5 //
For one bound by the five bonds, deluded by the six,
confused about the nature of the three worlds — time revolves for him. // Dhs_4.6 //
For one unaware of downfalls, afflicted by discursive thought,
for the person whose mind is attached — time revolves for him. // Dhs_4.7 //
For one whose mind is attached to pleasures that are delightful at the time
but result in transformation — time revolves for him. // Dhs_4.8 //
For one unaware of former sufferings, delighting in divine pleasures,
unaware of separation — time revolves for him. // Dhs_4.9 //
For one bound by the net of karma, who acts only in mind,
who has fallen from the true path — time revolves for him. // Dhs_4.10 //
For one unaware of the faults of existence, whose mind is deluded by craving,
who is sunk in the darkness of delusion — time revolves for him. // Dhs_4.11 //
For the embodied being bound by the sole snare of desire, without a companion,
confused by the host of goddesses — time revolves for him. // Dhs_4.12 //
For one drawn away from the faculties, wandered from the true path,
who relishes the three realms of existence — time revolves for him. // Dhs_4.13 //
For one who knows not restraint from non-restraint, who is full of ill-will,
who has lost the path of the perfectly awakened — time revolves for him. // Dhs_4.14 //
For one ignorant of the beneficial and harmful, dull regarding what should and should not be done,
resembling a child at play — time revolves for him. // Dhs_4.15 //
On the heights of rivers and waterfalls, in forests and groves,
for one intent on playing about — time revolves for him. // Dhs_4.16 //
On the ridges of celestial palaces and mountains, in forests of Dharma-mines,
for one who delights in sensual enjoyments — time revolves for him. // Dhs_4.17 //
For the embodied being unattached to the ripening of karma and Dharma,
attached solely to food — time revolves for him. // Dhs_4.18 //

body.translated_text: Ignorance of the body even while dwelling in it

children.translated_text: By karma, lifespan is exhausted; this three-realm [existence] is always [so];

children.text: bhramanti cakravannityaṃ na ca vindanti bāliśāḥ // Dhs_4.19 //
children.translated_text: they revolve constantly like a wheel, yet fools do not perceive it. // Dhs_4.19 //

body.translated_text: Ignorance of the world's faults

children.translated_text: This world rises and falls in downfalls,

children.text: na ca doṣāvadheyatvaṃ prakurvanti vimohitāḥ // Dhs_4.20 //
children.translated_text: yet the deluded do not attend to its faults. // Dhs_4.20 //

body.translated_text: The wise one's abandonment of desires is the cause of happiness

children.translated_text: This indeed is the supreme happiness — the abandonment of desires,
for the wise one free from anxiety, whose sorrow has departed, who is ardent. // Dhs_4.21 //

body.translated_text: The fruit of the sages' attainment of the final state

children.translated_text: Auspicious, secure, and supreme in its beginning, middle, and end —
having attained that, the wearied sages wander free from fever. // Dhs_4.22 //

body.translated_text: Desires are causes of suffering

children.text: satkāmajaṃ bhavet saukhyaṃ vinipātagataṃ tu tat /
children.translated_text: Whatever happiness is born of sensual desire, that leads to downfall;

children.text: na hi kāmaviśeṣaṃ ca kiñcid duḥkhavipākajam // Dhs_4.23 //
children.translated_text: for there is nothing superior about desires — [their fruit] is the ripening of suffering. // Dhs_4.23 //

children.text: tasmāt kāmeṣu matimān na lubhyet kathañcana /
children.translated_text: Therefore the wise one should never covet desires;

children.text: te hi saṃsāraduḥkhānāṃ hetubhūtāḥ sudāruṇāḥ // Dhs_4.24 //
children.translated_text: for they are the terribly harsh causes of the sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s>. // Dhs_4.24 //
In forests, groves, and mountains, in lotus pools and woodlands,

children.text: vibhrāntāstṛṣṇayā bālāḥ patanti saha daivataiḥ // Dhs_4.25 //
children.translated_text: fools, led astray by craving, fall down together with the deities. // Dhs_4.25 //

body.translated_text: Instruction to those unattached to meritorious action

children.translated_text: On mountains of gold and on peaks of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl),

children.text: kṣīyate hi śubhaṃ karma yatasva saha daivataiḥ // Dhs_4.26 //
children.translated_text: indeed, meritorious karma is exhausted — strive, together with the deities! // Dhs_4.26 //
Among delightful wishing-trees and by waterfalls of rivers,

children.text: caratastaiḥ śubhaṃ kṣīṇaṃ yatasva saha daivataiḥ // Dhs_4.27 //
children.translated_text: for those wandering with them, merit is exhausted — strive, together with the deities! // Dhs_4.27 //
In delightful regions of the earth and in forests of jewel-mines,

children.text: na śubhaṃ te sadā cīrṇa yatasva saha daivataiḥ // Dhs_4.28 //
children.translated_text: the merit you have always practiced is not [permanent] — strive, together with the deities! // Dhs_4.28 //
With the fivefold vigor that gladdens the mind,

children.text: hatasya gatakālasya yatasva saha daivataiḥ // Dhs_4.29 //
children.translated_text: for one who is spent and whose time has passed — strive, together with the deities! // Dhs_4.29 //

body.translated_text: The gods' ignorance of what is beneficial

children.translated_text: By those whose minds are always attached to desires, intent on sense objects,

children.text: na jñāyate hitaṃ devairyadamantrāhitaṃ bhavet // Dhs_4.30 //
children.translated_text: the gods do not discern what is beneficial — what is not beneficial is not without consequence. // Dhs_4.30 //

body.translated_text: Censure of the gods

children.translated_text: This merit is nearly exhausted; falling [from heaven] is at hand;
the gods who have enjoyed the fruits of good karma must go elsewhere. // Dhs_4.31 //

children.text: ye nityaṃ śubhasaṃsaktāḥ kurvanti vā śubhaṃ sadā /
children.translated_text: Those who are always attached to the meritorious and who always perform good deeds —

children.text: teṣāṃ visadṛśo heturmūrkhāṇāṃ hi vivartate // Dhs_4.32 //
children.translated_text: for them, the cause becomes dissimilar; for fools, it revolves [into misfortune]. // Dhs_4.32 //

body.translated_text: Who awaits death?

children.text: bhuktvā mṛtyuṃ pratīkṣante te janāḥ kāmamohitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed, those people deluded by desire await death —
ignorant of meritorious conduct, forever without a [spiritual] refuge. // Dhs_4.33 //

children.text: bhuktvā mṛtyuṃ pratīkṣante te janāḥ kāmamohitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed, those people deluded by desire await death —

children.text: ye na karmavipākasya jñānaṃ roṣavadhe ratāḥ // Dhs_4.34 //
children.translated_text: those who delight in the destruction of anger but have no knowledge of the ripening of karma. // Dhs_4.34 //

children.text: bhuktvā mṛtyuṃ pratīkṣante te janāḥ kāmamohitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed, those people deluded by desire await death —
they cannot teach the equal, surrounded by the fire of craving. // Dhs_4.35 //

children.text: bhuktvā mṛtyuṃ pratīkṣante te janāḥ kāmamohitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed, those people deluded by desire await death —

children.text: viprayogakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ ye na paśyanti dāruṇam // Dhs_4.36 //
children.translated_text: those who do not see the terrible suffering caused by separation. // Dhs_4.36 //

children.text: bhuktvā mṛtyuṃ pratīkṣante te janāḥ kāmamohitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed, those people deluded by desire await death —
with hearts attached to women, they do not perceive rebirth. // Dhs_4.37 //

children.text: bhuktvā mṛtyuṃ pratīkṣante te janāḥ kāmamohitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed, those people deluded by desire await death —
they are never alarmed by misfortune, disease, or grief. // Dhs_4.38 //

children.text: bhuktvā mṛtyuṃ pratīkṣante te janāḥ kāmamohitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed, those people deluded by desire await death —
those who form great association with evil companions. // Dhs_4.39 //

children.text: bhuktvā mṛtyuṃ pratīkṣante te janāḥ kāmamohitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed, those people deluded by desire await death —

children.text: bhāvitaṃ cetasā yairna na ca tattvapraveśitā // Dhs_4.40 //
children.translated_text: those by whom the mind has not been cultivated and who have not entered into truth. // Dhs_4.40 //

children.text: bhuktvā mṛtyuṃ pratīkṣante te janāḥ kāmamohitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed, those people deluded by desire await death —
they who in all states are terrified by the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>. // Dhs_4.41 //

children.text: bhuktvā mṛtyuṃ pratīkṣante te janāḥ kāmamohitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed, those people deluded by desire await death —

children.text: kāryākāryeṣu ye nityaṃ na subhāṣitacetasaḥ // Dhs_4.42 //
children.translated_text: those who, regarding what should and should not be done, never have well-directed minds. // Dhs_4.42 //

children.text: bhuktvā mṛtyuṃ pratīkṣante te janāḥ kāmamohitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed, those people deluded by desire await death —

children.text: ye na tattvadhiyo nityaṃ sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ // Dhs_4.43 //
children.translated_text: those who never have minds [directed toward] truth, [yet are] devoted to the welfare of all beings. // Dhs_4.43 //

children.text: bhuktvā mṛtyuṃ pratīkṣante te janāḥ kāmamohitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed, those people deluded by desire await death —

children.text: ye śarīra sukhārthena dharma hiṃsanti mohitāḥ // Dhs_4.44 //
children.translated_text: those who, deluded, harm the Dharma for the sake of bodily pleasure. // Dhs_4.44 //

body.translated_text: The mark of a wise person

children.translated_text: With single-pointed mind, one should always diligently perform meritorious action;

children.text: aśubhaṃ ca sadā varjyametat paṇḍitalakṣaṇam // Dhs_4.45 //
children.translated_text: and the inauspicious should always be avoided — this is the mark of a wise person. // Dhs_4.45 //

body.translated_text: Causes of downfall

children.text: kṣayaṃ yātaṃ ca yat śīlaṃ spṛṣṭvā yaḥ samupāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: One whose moral conduct has declined, who has arrived after touching [sin],
deceived by heedlessness — downfall will surely follow. // Dhs_4.46 //

body.translated_text: It is the subject of desire who changes, not the sense objects

children.translated_text: They have gone, are going, and will go — the lords of the gods, everywhere;
they abide on delightful peaks adorned with various jewels. // Dhs_4.47 //
The delightful peaks of <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, and others garlanded with forests —
The sense objects remain just the same, but people pass away. // Dhs_4.48 //
The charming grounds of forests and groves everywhere,
they remain quite intact, but people pass away. // Dhs_4.49 //
The stalks made of <s>vaidūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), and especially those of gold,
those lotus ponds remain the same, but people pass away. // Dhs_4.50 //
Lakes and delightful rivers, with flocks of birds unceasing —
these too remain quite intact, but people pass away. // Dhs_4.51 //

children.text: vimānāni rathāścaiva harmyāṇi ca tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Aerial palaces, chariots, and mansions likewise —
these remain quite intact, but people pass away. // Dhs_4.52 //
Though the world revolves, deceived by sense objects,

children.text: tathāpi nāmalokasya nodvego hṛdi jāyate // Dhs_4.53 //
children.translated_text: even so, no alarm arises in the hearts of worldly people. // Dhs_4.53 //
Through habitual practice, the mind of one who wanders in <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) has become hardened like a donkey,

children.text: yena manye mahad duḥkhaṃ hṛdaye naiva vartate // Dhs_4.54 //
children.translated_text: whereby, I think, even great suffering does not stir the heart. // Dhs_4.54 //
Just as animals bound in the butcher's pen,

children.text: ekaikaśo vinaśyanti śeṣāṇāṃ nāsti sambhramaḥ // Dhs_4.55 //
children.translated_text: perish one by one, while the rest feel no alarm. // Dhs_4.55 //
This earth remains only for the pleasure of the lustful,
and those foolish <s>devas</s> (gods) fall away and are reborn thus. // Dhs_4.56 //

body.translated_text: The ignorance of death among those turned toward sense objects:

children.translated_text: Beings slain by heedlessness — death, the giver of momentary suffering —
do not recognize death; like cattle, they are free from alarm. // Dhs_4.57 //
They, of long-reaching minds, having come under the power of time,
the fire of remorse will burn them, without remedy. // Dhs_4.58 //
Terrible, without remedy, inevitable for all embodied beings —

children.text: maraṇaṃ kālavaśagaṃ tad viditvāgamaṃ caret // Dhs_4.59 //
children.translated_text: knowing death to be subject to time, one should practice what leads to liberation. // Dhs_4.59 //

body.translated_text: All unions end in separation:

children.translated_text: Meetings with the dear and separations from the dear are always painful;
union ends in separation — this is the eternal <s>dharmatā</s> (natural law). // Dhs_4.60 //

children.text: kṣaṇe lave muhūrte ca divārātrau tathādhvani /
children.translated_text: In each moment, instant, and hour, by day and night, and throughout one's journey,

children.text: maraṇaṃ cintayed dhīrastasya nāsti pratikriyā // Dhs_4.61 //
children.translated_text: the wise one should contemplate death — for against it there is no remedy. // Dhs_4.61 //

body.translated_text: Only those free from defilement attain peace:

children.translated_text: They praise the recollection of death at the fire —
those free from defilement attain the supreme peace that is solely for the good. // Dhs_4.62 //
Recollecting the purpose of death, whose fault is this that is approved?

children.text: nirdoṣaṃ hi manaḥ sarvaṃ śāntaṃ bhavati nityaśaḥ // Dhs_4.63 //
children.translated_text: For indeed a faultless mind is always completely at peace. // Dhs_4.63 //

body.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgatas</s> (Thus-Gone Ones) have declared heedfulness to be supreme:

children.translated_text: "Heedfulness is supreme" — this has been declared by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>;

children.text: yanmṛtyoḥ smaraṇaṃ nityamaśubhānāṃ ca varjanam // Dhs_4.64 //
children.translated_text: namely, the constant recollection of death and the avoidance of unwholesome deeds. // Dhs_4.64 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the fourth chapter, the chapter on transmigration. //
(5) The Chapter on Impermanence.
All happiness ends in destruction:

children.text: kṣayāntaṃ hi sukhaṃ sarva na sukhaṃ vidyate dhruvam /
children.translated_text: Indeed all happiness ends in destruction; no happiness is found to be permanent.

children.text: saṃsṛjenna sukhaṃ tasmāt yadīcchet sukhamātmanaḥ // Dhs_5.1 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should not associate with happiness if one desires happiness for oneself. // Dhs_5.1 //

body.translated_text: Death drags away all:

children.translated_text: Of those going, standing, laughing, and playing alike,
death, irresistible with great force, destroys terribly. // Dhs_5.2 //
There is no place here or hereafter where one can escape it;

children.text: tathāpi nāma saṃmūḍhā janayitvā vaśaṃgataḥ // Dhs_5.3 //
children.translated_text: even so, the deluded, having produced offspring, come under its power. // Dhs_5.3 //

children.text: (na bālaṃ na yuvānaṃ vā) na sthavirameva vā /
children.translated_text: Neither the young nor the old,
neither householder nor renunciant — when does it not drag away? // Dhs_5.4 //

children.text: sukhitaṃ duḥkhitaṃ vāpi guṇavantaṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Whether happy or suffering, whether endowed with virtues,
whether observing vows or not — when does it not drag away? // Dhs_5.5 //
Whether immoral or virtuous, whether a giver or the most excellent,

children.text: rājānaṃ cottamaṃ cāpi yadāsau nāpakarṣati // Dhs_5.6 //
children.translated_text: whether a king or the most eminent — when does it not drag away? // Dhs_5.6 //

children.text: daivaṃ vā nārakaṃ vāpi tiryañca pratajaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Whether divine, hellish, animal, or human,
whether heedful or heedless — when does it not drag away? // Dhs_5.7 //
Whether born in the desire realm, or abiding in the form realm,
or born in the formless realm — when does it not drag away? // Dhs_5.8 //
With the noose of <s>karma</s> (action), the rod of old age, the rod of disease — the great forest;
this death, like one stained with blood, seizes beings and carries them away. // Dhs_5.9 //
When such a fearful and supremely terrible death
is at hand, the gods proceed, deluded by sensual desires. // Dhs_5.10 //

body.translated_text: All happiness ends in falling — one should renounce it:

children.text: yad duḥkhaṃ cyavamānasya devalokāt surasya ca /
children.translated_text: The suffering of a god falling from the heavenly world,
and the suffering that exists in hell, preceded by separation — // Dhs_5.11 //
Just as food mixed with poisonous flies, though beautiful —
so one should relinquish the happiness of the divine state, which ends in falling. // Dhs_5.12 //
For one whose merit is exhausted, who is wretched, abandoned by one's own spouse —

children.text: yad duḥkhaṃ cyavamānasya tasyaupamyaṃ na vidyate // Dhs_5.13 //
children.translated_text: the suffering of one who is falling has no comparison. // Dhs_5.13 //
Like a feeble elephant whose splendor has departed,

children.text: śāmyati devasya yadduḥkhaṃ mahadduḥkhaṃ prajāyate // Dhs_5.14 //
children.translated_text: when a god's glory fades, great suffering arises. // Dhs_5.14 //

body.translated_text: Even a god falls away:

children.translated_text: For one whose craving and sense objects have grown, whose mind is stricken with grief,
whose speech, body, and movements have become feeble — there is fear from the falling of a god. // Dhs_5.15 //

body.translated_text: Suffering is more bitter than sense objects:

children.translated_text: The more one savors pleasures — those supremely deceptive sense desires —

children.text: (tathā) tathā bhavatyeva teṣāṃ duḥkhaṃ mahattaram // Dhs_5.16 //
children.translated_text: the greater becomes the suffering from them. // Dhs_5.16 //
The suffering that arises from the heavenly world for one who strives —

children.text: tasyāntareṇa narakaṃ kalāṃ nārhati ṣoḍaśīm // Dhs_5.17 //
children.translated_text: even hell does not equal a sixteenth part of that. // Dhs_5.17 //
Seeing the heavenly world as ending in falling, and earthly life as ending in death,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā duḥkhaṃ (bhavatyeva śreyase kriyatāṃ manaḥ) // Dhs_5.18 //
children.translated_text: seeing that there is suffering, one should turn the mind to what is beneficial. // Dhs_5.18 //

body.translated_text: Happiness ends in falling:

children.text: patanāntaṃ sadā saukhyaṃ nāsti lokasya nityajāḥ /
children.translated_text: Happiness always ends in falling; nothing in the world is born permanent.

children.text: tad buddhvā kāraṇaṃ sarva śreyase kriyatāṃ manaḥ // Dhs_5.19 //
children.translated_text: Knowing this, the cause of all, one should turn the mind to what is beneficial. // Dhs_5.19 //

body.translated_text: Everything ends in suffering:

children.translated_text: All accumulations end in depletion, all elevations end in falling;

children.text: saṃyogā viprayogāntā maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitam // Dhs_5.20 //
children.translated_text: all unions end in separation, and life ends in death. // Dhs_5.20 //

children.text: jātasya maraṇaṃ nityaṃ na tasyāstīti nityatā /
children.translated_text: Death is certain for one who is born; there is no permanence for that one.

children.text: na bhūtārāvitānena triṣu dhātuṣu dṛśyate // Dhs_5.21 //
children.translated_text: Not under the canopy of living beings in the three realms is this seen. // Dhs_5.21 //
Some perish in the womb, some in the birth-chamber,
some while still crawling, and likewise some who are perishable. // Dhs_5.22 //

body.translated_text: Death is certain:

children.translated_text: The rising and setting of the sun is observed;

children.text: tathā jātasya sarvasya sthitaṃ maraṇamagrataḥ // Dhs_5.23 //
children.translated_text: likewise, death stands before everything that is born. // Dhs_5.23 //

body.translated_text: All happiness ends in destruction:

children.text: kṣayāntaṃ hi sukhaṃ sarva yo na vindati mohadhīḥ /
children.translated_text: Indeed, all happiness ends in destruction — one who, through deluded understanding, does not perceive this,
when death arrives afterward, will be destined for suffering births. // Dhs_5.24 //

children.text: kuśalaṃ kārya(karaṇaṃ kuśalī ca) priyaḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: Performing wholesome deeds, the one who is skillful is always dear;

children.text: sukhaṃ hi dharmācaraṇaṃ kathayanti manīṣiṇaḥ // Dhs_5.25 //
children.translated_text: for the wise declare that the practice of Dharma is happiness. // Dhs_5.25 //
Everything is impermanent and unstable, always bitter in its transformation;
<s>Saṃsāra</s> is declared by the wise to be the cause for investigating the truth. // Dhs_5.26 //
Those gods who are heedless in pleasure — their happiness is impermanent;

children.text: cyavamānasya ca yadduḥkhaṃ devalokāt surasya hi // Dhs_5.27 //
children.translated_text: and the suffering of a god falling from the heavenly world — // Dhs_5.27 //
its comparison does not exist — for that is hell after hell.

children.text: kimete nāvabudhyante patanāntaṃ sadā sukham // Dhs_5.28 //
children.translated_text: Do they not understand that happiness always ends in falling? // Dhs_5.28 //

body.translated_text: Deluded by happiness, they see the world as ageless and deathless;

children.translated_text: the world of falling and rebirth — its count is not known,
and people do not feel alarm, deceived by craving. // Dhs_5.29 //

body.text: abhiyāti sadā janma tvaritaṃ yāti yauvanam /
body.translated_text: Birth always approaches swiftly, youth passes quickly;

children.translated_text: union and separation are seen as inseparable companions;
the deluded do not perceive this, deceived by sense objects. // Dhs_5.30 //

body.translated_text: Gods, powerless under craving, fall away:

children.translated_text: The gods fall away, powerless, deluded by craving —

children.text: sā bhūmistāni padmāni vanāni vividhāni ca // Dhs_5.31 //
children.translated_text: that ground, those lotuses, and the various forests. // Dhs_5.31 //

body.translated_text: All things are charming only at first sight:

children.translated_text: Lovely mountain peaks, jewel-studded and great,
lakes and various rivers adorned with jewel-stones, // Dhs_5.32 //
trees with variegated flowers, standing in various rows,

children.text: harmyāgrāṇi ca ramyāṇi ratnavanti mahānti ca // Dhs_5.33 //
children.translated_text: and lovely mansion-tops, jewel-studded and great, // Dhs_5.33 //
wish-fulfilling trees made of gold, some of spotless <s>vaidūrya</s>,
some of silver, some of refined gold, and mixed with excellent climbing plants, // Dhs_5.34 //
lotus ponds resounding with the songs of bees,

children.text: vibhūṣaṇāni ramyāṇi devārhāṇi ca sarvataḥ // Dhs_5.35 //
children.translated_text: lovely ornaments worthy of the gods everywhere — // Dhs_5.35 //

body.translated_text: Everything is momentary:

children.translated_text: All this remains just the same, but people pass away;
like illusion, bubbles, and foam, like a city of the <s>Gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians). // Dhs_5.36 //

children.text: sukhaṃ sarvasya devasya tṛṣṇayā vañcitasya hi /
children.translated_text: The happiness of every god, deceived by craving —

children.text: sa vināśya janaṃ sarva bhrāmayitvā bhavārṇave // Dhs_5.37 //
children.translated_text: having destroyed that, it carries away all people, whirling them in the ocean of existence. // Dhs_5.37 //

body.translated_text: Craving itself is the root of suffering:

children.translated_text: Craving, resembling the fire of poison, abides here among people;
unsatisfied by enjoyment of desires, yet heated by what arises from pleasure. // Dhs_5.38 //

children.text: kālānalena nirdagdhā kva te devagaṇāḥ gatāḥ /
children.translated_text: Burned by the fire of time, where have those hosts of gods gone?
This craving, spreading throughout the world, has been completely obtained. // Dhs_5.39 //
By which the gods, deluded, have come under the power of time —

children.text: devāsurā narā yakṣā narake yānti jaṅgamāḥ // Dhs_5.40 //
children.translated_text: gods, <s>asuras</s> (demons), humans, <s>yakṣas</s> (spirits), and moving beings go to hell. // Dhs_5.40 //

body.translated_text: This triple world is yoked by the noose of time:

children.translated_text: All go, powerless, to the irresistible noose of time;
this entire triple world is yoked by the noose of time. // Dhs_5.41 //

body.translated_text: Those deluded by craving do not see death:

children.translated_text: Powerless, deluded by the delusion of craving, they do not see

children.text: anena hi yathā devāḥ śataśo 'tha sahastraśaḥ // Dhs_5.42 //
children.translated_text: how by this very thing, gods by the hundreds and thousands // Dhs_5.42 //
have gone, burned by the fire of time, through sense objects arising from wealth.

children.text: parasya dṛśyate maraṇamātmano naiva dṛśyate // Dhs_5.43 //
children.translated_text: The death of another is seen, but one's own death is not seen. // Dhs_5.43 //
Afterward, when calamity strikes, they find suffering for themselves;
the mind, polluted by heedlessness, always delighting in sense objects, // Dhs_5.44 //

children.text: na vindanti dhruvaṃ mṛtyuṃ dehināṃ sahajasthitam /
children.translated_text: does not perceive the certain death, ever-present companion of embodied beings.
For one who hopes for endless happiness and delights in heedlessness, // Dhs_5.45 //
this army of death approaches, overwhelming, resembling poison;

children.text: na mantrauṣadhakarmāṇi na devā nāsurāstathā // Dhs_5.46 //
children.translated_text: neither mantras, nor medicines, nor rituals, neither gods nor <s>asuras</s> — // Dhs_5.46 //

body.translated_text: For one bound by the noose of time, there is no savior:

children.text: kālapāśena baddhasya trātāro na bhavanti te /
children.translated_text: For one bound by the noose of time, there are no saviors;

children.text: rajasā guṇṭhitaṃ vaktraṃ ātmano naiva vindati // Dhs_5.47 //
children.translated_text: one's face covered with dust, one does not even recognize oneself. // Dhs_5.47 //

body.translated_text: The reason craving should be abandoned:

children.translated_text: This death, which is the nature of falling from what has been attained, will come afterward
for one who is always greedy, insatiable with craving. // Dhs_5.48 //
Death approaches suddenly, unseen by those who seek happiness;

children.text: ayaṃ tavāgraho duḥkhaṃ mṛtyunā preṣito mahān // Dhs_5.49 //
children.translated_text: this great attachment of yours is suffering, dispatched by death. // Dhs_5.49 //
Immediately after this, death will be supremely terrible;
from this great mountain adorned with forests and groves, // Dhs_5.50 //

body.translated_text: people bound by sense objects, experiencing the fruits of their own <s>karma</s>,

children.translated_text: sporting and enjoying — yet nowhere is there happiness in craving;

children.text: tarṣyayā tṛṣṇayā mūḍhāḥ patanti vivaśā bhuvi // Dhs_5.51 //
children.translated_text: deluded by thirst and craving, they fall powerless to the earth. // Dhs_5.51 //
Just as fire always follows after smoke,
so falling stands behind one who shows the signs of falling. // Dhs_5.52 //

children.text: jātyā jātyā dhruvaṃ mṛtyuścārogye sati ruk sthitā /
children.translated_text: In every birth, death is certain; even when healthy, disease stands ready;
in prosperity, calamity arrives; in youth, old age is an innate companion;

children.text: sarvaiḥ priyairviyogaśca na saṃyogo dhruvaṃ sthitaḥ // Dhs_5.53 //
children.translated_text: and separation from all that is dear — union is never permanently established. // Dhs_5.53 //

body.translated_text: The greatness of <s>dharmatā</s> (natural law):

children.translated_text: This truth of dharma in the world has been taught by the Perfectly Awakened One:

children.text: ubhayasya kṣayo nāśo janasyo parivartate // Dhs_5.54 //
children.translated_text: The destruction and annihilation of both befall a person in turn. // Dhs_5.54 //

children.text: jātau satyāṃ yathā mṛtyuravaśyaṃ sthita eva hi /
children.translated_text: Just as, when birth exists, death is inevitably established,

children.text: kṣīyate sukṛtaṃ karma āyūṃṣi kṣaṇikāni hi // Dhs_5.55 //
children.translated_text: meritorious <s>karma</s> is exhausted, and lifespans are momentary indeed. // Dhs_5.55 //

body.translated_text: Cultivate restraint and the rest

children.translated_text: Cultivate restraint in the Dharma and Discipline, O best of men!

children.text: abhyeti yauvanaṃ sarvaṃ jīvitaṃ cānugacchati // Dhs_5.56 //
children.translated_text: All youth passes away, and life too follows after it. // Dhs_5.56 //

body.translated_text: The perishable nature of all things

children.text: naśyanti sarvadā sarvā mā pramāde manaḥkṛthā /
children.translated_text: All things perish at all times — do not set your mind on heedlessness!

children.text: na nityaṃ labhyate svargo na nityaṃ kṣaṇasampadā // Dhs_5.57 //
children.translated_text: Heaven is not eternal, nor is the fortune of a favorable moment. // Dhs_5.57 //
As long as the fall has not yet occurred, let one swiftly exert oneself,

children.text: (tasya jāte hi patane tat prayogo vṛthā bhavet) // Dhs_5.58 //
children.translated_text: (For once the fall has taken place, that exertion would be in vain.) // Dhs_5.58 //
This is that forest of trees, adorned with various jewels,
Covered with thickets of creepers, adorned with lotus pools. // Dhs_5.59 //
With palaces of pure gold, studded with gems,
Beautified with various waterfalls and creepers. // Dhs_5.60 //
Witness to the <s>karma</s> of these beings — having split open, rising to the sky,

children.text: kalpāgnivirato meruḥ sarvathā na bhaviṣyati // Dhs_5.61 //
children.translated_text: Even <s>Meru</s>, surviving the fire at the end of the <s>kalpa</s>, will utterly cease to be. // Dhs_5.61 //
How much more so the gods there, who are like foam and bubbles —
They arise and perish, deluded by heedlessness and intoxication. // Dhs_5.62 //
Happiness and suffering are endless, born from the fruits of desire and one's own will;

children.text: devalokād yathā devāḥ patanti narake punaḥ // Dhs_5.63 //
children.translated_text: Just as gods fall from the heavenly realm back into hell. // Dhs_5.63 //

body.translated_text: That suffering is supreme and bitter

children.translated_text: While bodily and mental sufferings exist everywhere,

children.text: na tacchakyaṃ pramatte syāt tadduḥkhaṃ paramaṃ kaṭu // Dhs_5.64 //
children.translated_text: For the heedless, that suffering cannot be borne — it is supreme and bitter. // Dhs_5.64 //
The suffering of separation is recited foremost among the names of suffering;
That indeed, in the divine state, continually proceeds foremost. // Dhs_5.65 //
There will be separation from all that is dear and pleasing;

children.text: na ca devāḥ prapaśyadhvaṃ maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitam // Dhs_5.66 //
children.translated_text: O gods, do not fail to see: life ends in death. // Dhs_5.66 //
When the time of falling from heaven has arrived, with senses and mind bewildered,

children.text: jānīdhvaṃ tatparaṃ duḥkhaṃ yadavaśyaṃ bhaviṣyati // Dhs_5.67 //
children.translated_text: Know that supreme suffering which will inevitably come. // Dhs_5.67 //

body.translated_text: All is momentary

children.translated_text: Like the wheel of untimely death, like a <s>gandharva</s> city (mirage),
All existence in the three realms is like foam and bubbles. // Dhs_5.68 //
One who, deluded in a mass of foam, would make a covering and bed —

children.text: sa mūḍhaḥ saṃskṛte kuryādabhisvādaṃ bhramātmakam // Dhs_5.69 //
children.translated_text: That fool would seek deluded enjoyment in the conditioned, which is illusion by nature. // Dhs_5.69 //

body.translated_text: The greatness of death

children.text: na devā na narā yakṣā nāsurā garuḍāstathā /
children.translated_text: Neither gods, nor humans, nor <s>yakṣas</s>, nor <s>asuras</s>, nor <s>garuḍas</s> —
None can protect at the time of death those tormented by <s>karma</s>. // Dhs_5.70 //
As long as the terrible king of death has not yet arrived,

children.text: tāvattu sukṛtaṃ kārya mā paścāt paritapyatha // Dhs_5.71 //
children.translated_text: So long should meritorious deeds be done — do not later feel remorse! // Dhs_5.71 //
Whatever happiness arises from elemental desires, natural and born of sense objects —

children.text: mṛtyukāle samutpanne tiṣṭhanti na budharṣamā // Dhs_5.72 //
children.translated_text: When the time of death has arisen, even the wise cannot remain. // Dhs_5.72 //

children.text: kiṃ kariṣyanti saukhyāni kiṃ striyaḥ kiñcabāndhavāḥ /
children.translated_text: What will pleasures do? What will women? What will kinsmen?
For one being carried away by death from the heavenly realm on all sides. // Dhs_5.73 //
All those lands are firm, adorned with forests and groves,

children.text: mṛtyurajjvā vibaddhaśca tvantu kālena nīyase // Dhs_5.74 //
children.translated_text: But you, bound by death's rope, are carried away by time. // Dhs_5.74 //
Just as clouds in the sky, stirred by the wind,
Come together and separate — so too are living beings in <s>saṃsāra</s>. // Dhs_5.75 //
Just as flowers are seen by people who come in each season,

children.text: vyatīte tu ṛtau sarve pratiyānti yathāgatāḥ // Dhs_5.76 //
children.translated_text: But when the season has passed, all depart as they came. // Dhs_5.76 //

children.text: yathā kāle samutpanne modante sukṛtaiḥ surāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as when the favorable time has come, the gods rejoice through merit,

children.text: vyatīte tu śubhe kāle pratiyānti yathāgatāḥ // Dhs_5.77 //
children.translated_text: But when the auspicious time has passed, they depart as they came. // Dhs_5.77 //
Just as in each season, leaves arise abundantly on a tree,

children.text: vyatīte tu śubhe kāle śīryate tat samantataḥ // Dhs_5.78 //
children.translated_text: But when the auspicious time has passed, they wither away on all sides. // Dhs_5.78 //
Just as those leaves illustrate — there is no happiness or safety in existence;

children.text: śīryate satataṃ saukhyaṃ nāsaukhyaṃ vidyate dhruvam // Dhs_5.79 //
children.translated_text: Happiness constantly decays, and no unhappiness is found to be permanent. // Dhs_5.79 //
Just as rain in the monsoon season does not return to the sky,

children.text: tathā saukhyamidaṃ sarva gacchati na nivartate // Dhs_5.80 //
children.translated_text: So too all this happiness departs and does not return. // Dhs_5.80 //

children.text: barhiṇāṃ ca yathā nādo vāyunā samudīritaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the cry of peacocks, stirred by the wind,

children.text: śrūyate tatpraṇāśāya tathā saukhyamidaṃ smṛtam // Dhs_5.81 //
children.translated_text: Is heard only to vanish — so is this happiness to be regarded. // Dhs_5.81 //

children.text: yathā hi jvalane kṣiptaṃ dhruvaṃ kālaṃ pradahayate /
children.translated_text: Just as that which is cast into a blaze is surely consumed in time,

children.text: tathā vahanyupamaḥ kālaḥ kāṣṭhavaccaratāṃ smṛtaḥ // Dhs_5.82 //
children.translated_text: So time, resembling fire, is said to consume those who move like firewood. // Dhs_5.82 //
Hundreds and thousands have come and gone,

children.text: saṃvego na bhavatyeṣā tṛṣṇayā mohitāstathā // Dhs_5.83 //
children.translated_text: Yet no spiritual urgency arises in those deluded by craving. // Dhs_5.83 //

children.text: yathā yathā mahāsaukhyaṃ svayaṃ bhogo yathā yathā /
children.translated_text: The greater the happiness, the greater the enjoyment,

children.text: tathā tathā mahad duḥkhaṃ patanāntodbhavaṃ dhruvam // Dhs_5.84 //
children.translated_text: The greater too is the suffering, inevitably arising and ending in a fall. // Dhs_5.84 //

body.translated_text: The chain of suffering beginning with birth

children.text: jātirduḥkhā jarā duḥkhā maraṇaṃ duḥkhameva ca /
children.translated_text: Birth is suffering, old age is suffering, death too is indeed suffering;

children.text: priyaiśca saha viśleṣo duḥkhasyaiṣā paramparā // Dhs_5.85 //
children.translated_text: Separation from the dear — this is the chain of suffering. // Dhs_5.85 //

body.translated_text: One should not fear death

children.text: ekasya patanaṃ dṛṣṭvā kathaṃ nodvijate janaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having seen the fall of one, how does a person not become alarmed?
'This fall will surely befall me too through all my evil deeds.' // Dhs_5.86 //

children.text: yaḥ paśyati bhayaṃ dūrāt pratipattau ca vartate /
children.translated_text: One who sees danger from afar and lives in accordance with practice,
When the time of death arrives, does not tremble, free from anguish. // Dhs_5.87 //
Being torn apart by the lowly, by death, by one's own kinsfolk —

children.text: yadduḥkhaṃ mṛtyusamaye tanna śakyaṃ prabhāṣitum // Dhs_5.88 //
children.translated_text: The suffering at the time of death cannot be expressed. // Dhs_5.88 //

children.text: patanāntaṃ hi maraṇaṃ patamāno yathā giriḥ /
children.translated_text: Death ends in a fall; like a mountain falling,
It is powerful, irresistible, dragging people away,

children.text: saṃśliṣyate mahāvegaḥ samprahārī ca sarvadā // Dhs_5.89 //
children.translated_text: Approaching with great force and always striking. // Dhs_5.89 //

children.text: taṃ jñātvā mā pramādeṣu stubadhvaṃ devasattamāḥ /
children.translated_text: Knowing this, do not be caught in heedlessness, O best of gods!

children.text: saṃśleṣayati viśleṣaṃ yauvane ca sadā jarā // Dhs_5.90 //
children.translated_text: In union there is always separation, and in youth there is always old age. // Dhs_5.90 //

children.text: jīvite ca sadā mṛtyuḥ padametat sadā sthitam /
children.translated_text: In life there is always death — this state is ever established;
By the fire of impermanence, those in its range are inevitably consumed. // Dhs_5.91 //
At the end of the <s>kalpa</s>, what of the gods who are like foam and plantain trees?

children.text: na tadasti bhavet kiñcid yad jñānaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ calam // Dhs_5.92 //
children.translated_text: There is nothing whatsoever that exists as conditioned and permanent and stable. // Dhs_5.92 //

children.text: yannityaṃ (ca) sukhaṃ vā syādetatsthānaṃ na vidyate /
children.translated_text: That which would be permanent or pleasant — no such state is found;
Death should be known as standing near by all living beings. // Dhs_5.93 //
Since no remedy against it is possible by any means,

children.text: rūpaṃ kṣaṇikameteṣāṃ vayo 'pi kṣaṇikaṃ tathā // Dhs_5.94 //
children.translated_text: Their form is momentary, and their lifespan too is equally momentary. // Dhs_5.94 //

children.text: kṣīyate ca tathā saukhyaṃ na ca buddhayantyamedhasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Happiness likewise decays, yet the unintelligent do not understand;
When all their manifold auspicious marks — // Dhs_5.95 //
From birth, by the wheel of time, are destroyed in succession,
Just so, previously destroyed were those of manifold hundredfold marks. // Dhs_5.96 //
Just so, the king of death will carry away this birth of theirs too,
Of those whose minds are heedless, who always dwell in pleasure. // Dhs_5.97 //
This noose of time approaches for destruction, destroyer of happiness,
Causing separation from happiness, health, strength, vitality, and the beloved. // Dhs_5.98 //
That powerful king of death approaches near,
Having drawn near to these manifold heedless ones. // Dhs_5.99 //

body.translated_text: The destruction of happiness is certain

children.translated_text: Life together with happiness he will quickly destroy;
For a long time this has been destroyed — the gods are overcome by heedlessness. // Dhs_5.100 //
Blinded by delusion, awakened only by pleasure, they do not understand;
When they become diminished in radiance, with bewildered senses and minds, // Dhs_5.101 //
They will fall into the world of <s>Yama</s> — then is the fruit of that knowledge.

children.text: jīyate bata kālo 'yaṃ kṣaṇikaṃ ca yathā sukham // Dhs_5.102 //
children.translated_text: Alas, this time is wasted, and happiness is momentary; // Dhs_5.102 //
Yet those with passionate minds, without eyes, do not understand;

children.text: ramyād ramyataraṃ yānti nityaṃ sukhavihāriṇaḥ // Dhs_5.103 //
children.translated_text: From delight to ever greater delight they go, always dwelling in pleasure. // Dhs_5.103 //
As they will depart, the king of death will carry them away;

children.text: jarā jātivipattīnāṃ yo na mūḍho viṣīdati // Dhs_5.104 //
children.translated_text: One who, not deluded, grieves over birth, old age, and calamities — // Dhs_5.104 //
He later, at the time of death, is tormented with a lowly mind.
Having obtained happiness among the gods, regarded as meritorious — // Dhs_5.105 //
The sacrificial offering ends in destruction, life is momentary and unstable;

children.text: yathā hi yad vināśāntaṃ tathaiṣāmapi jīvitam // Dhs_5.106 //
children.translated_text: Just as that which ends in destruction — so too is the life of these beings. // Dhs_5.106 //
In no long time, there is no doubt, this will come to pass.
As long as death has not arrived, as long as the mind is unclouded, // Dhs_5.107 //

body.translated_text: One should cultivate delight in the Dharma with the mind

children.translated_text: So long should the wise one maintain delight in Dharma with strength of mind,
For the destruction of all life and the exhaustion of all happiness. // Dhs_5.108 //

body.translated_text: Separation from the dear is certain

children.translated_text: For separation from all that is dear, death approaches as refuge;
When that great calamity has arrived — death, the supremely terrible. // Dhs_5.109 //

children.text: nānyat trāṇamṛte dharmāt tasmād dharmarato bhavet /
children.translated_text: There is no other protection save the Dharma — therefore one should delight in the Dharma.
Whatever joy arises in a god who has been reborn — // Dhs_5.110 //
It does not equal a sixteenth part of the suffering of falling from heaven.

children.text: mṛtyukāle samutpanne na kaścit kasyacit tathā // Dhs_5.111 //
children.translated_text: When the time of death has arisen, no one is anything to anyone. // Dhs_5.111 //

body.translated_text: The perishable nature of all

children.text: na ca gacchantimapyekaṃ padamekaṃ hi gacchati /
children.translated_text: None accompany even one step, for one goes alone;

children.text: yadā jātaṃ tadāramya naro mṛtyuparāyaṇaḥ // Dhs_5.112 //
children.translated_text: From the moment one is born, a person is headed toward death. // Dhs_5.112 //
Surrounded by manifold delusions, that danger is not perceived;

children.text: yadā te cyavanaṃ prāpte bhavabhogakaraṃ param // Dhs_5.113 //
children.translated_text: When the fall has been reached, causing supreme enjoyment of existence — // Dhs_5.113 //

children.text: tadā vindati mūḍhātmā yad bhayaṃ mṛtyujaṃ mahat /
children.translated_text: Then the deluded soul discovers the great fear born of death.
Bitten by the serpent of sense objects, deluded by the poison of craving, // Dhs_5.114 //

children.text: na vindanti sadā devāścyavanānte mahad bhayam /
children.translated_text: The gods never perceive the great fear at the end of their fall;

children.text: cyavanti ca tathā duḥkhamutpādayanti dehinām // Dhs_5.115 //
children.translated_text: They fall and thus produce suffering for embodied beings. // Dhs_5.115 //
Just as rebirth occurs, so too occurs the fall of the gods;
Tossed about by the wind of <s>karma</s> and tormented through action, // Dhs_5.116 //
Death leads the helpless person, deprived of happiness;

children.text: na mātaro na pitaro na mitrāṇi na bāndhavāḥ // Dhs_5.117 //
children.translated_text: Neither mothers, nor fathers, nor friends, nor kinsmen // Dhs_5.117 //
Go as companions for a person impelled by time.
And this person is without companion, this person is deceived by nature. // Dhs_5.118 //

body.translated_text: The mind itself is the noose-fetter

children.translated_text: It is only by the nooses and bonds of the mind that a person is bound;

children.text: na janaḥ svajanaśceha trātā bhavati kasyacita // Dhs_5.119 //
children.translated_text: Neither a person nor one's own people can be a protector for anyone. // Dhs_5.119 //
Seized as if by the hair by death, one should practice the Dharma.
When the time of death has arisen, even one's own people are as strangers;
That happiness and great fortune of the gods which you behold — // Dhs_5.120 //
The great lord, the king of death, will forcibly carry it away.

children.text: tvaritaṃ yāti janmedaṃ na ca vindati bāliśaḥ // Dhs_5.121 //
children.translated_text: This life swiftly passes, yet the fool does not perceive it; // Dhs_5.121 //
Later, when calamity has arrived, the suffering ones discover it.

children.text: yadi duḥkhādbhayaṃ tvaritaṃ yadi mṛtyubhayaśca yaḥ // Dhs_5.122 //
children.translated_text: If there is swiftly fear from suffering, and if there is fear of death — // Dhs_5.122 //
Let the mind be set on Dharma; thus you shall obtain happiness.
Happiness always ends in destruction, is impermanent, and unstable in every way. // Dhs_5.123 //

body.translated_text: Divinity ends in a fall

children.text: sarvadevakṛtaṃ saukhyaṃ na ca vindanti mohitāḥ /
children.translated_text: All the happiness made by the gods — the deluded do not perceive it;

children.text: abhūtvā ca cyavantyete bhūtvāvaśyaṃ hi cañcalāḥ // Dhs_5.124 //
children.translated_text: Having not-been and having been, they inevitably fall, being unsteady. // Dhs_5.124 //
The gods exist for the sake of falling — this truth of dharma is established.
Those gods who are heedless in sense pleasures, of fickle minds, // Dhs_5.125 //

children.text: na paśyanti surāstīvraṃ vyasanāntaṃ hi jīvitam /
children.translated_text: The gods do not see that life ends sharply in calamity.

children.text: yadaiva jāyate devastadaiva maraṇāya saḥ // Dhs_5.126 //
children.translated_text: The very day a god is born, that very day he is destined for death. // Dhs_5.126 //

body.translated_text: One should set one's mind on what is beneficial.

children.translated_text: Just as night inevitably follows at the day's end,

children.text: divasaṃ jīvitaṃ proktaṃ rātriḥ sthānmaraṇopamā // Dhs_5.127 //
children.translated_text: the day is called life, and night is likened to death. // Dhs_5.127 //

children.text: tasmāt tadubhayaṃ jñātvā śreyase kriyatāṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, knowing both of these, let the mind be set on what is beneficial.
This is the condition of men who are under the sway of passion for women. // Dhs_5.128 //
That which is cherished is forcefully crushed by the army of death.
Having deceived men and women who are deluded by existence and non-existence, // Dhs_5.129 //
at the time of death they depart, experiencing the fruits of their own karma.
Having sported many times in lotus groves, on mountains, // Dhs_5.130 //
by rivers and waterfalls — the beloved ones have gone to the pit.
Death is inevitable and separation is certain, // Dhs_5.131 //
yet men are always subject to the sway of passion.

children.text: sukhitaṃ duḥkhitaṃ vā(pi) jīrṇamanyatra yauvanam // Dhs_5.132 //
children.translated_text: Whether happy or suffering, whether aged or in youth, // Dhs_5.132 //

body.translated_text: the king of death crushes all.

children.translated_text: Whether of low birth or noble birth, the king of death crushes all.

children.text: surūpaṃ vā virūpaṃ vā balavantaṃ tathābalam // Dhs_5.133 //
children.translated_text: Whether beautiful or ugly, whether strong or weak, // Dhs_5.133 //
whether protected or bereft of protector, the king of death crushes all.

children.text: rājānaṃ vā tathā mṛtyuḥ gṛhiṇaṃ vā tathā yatim // Dhs_5.134 //
children.translated_text: Whether a king, likewise death takes the householder or the ascetic. // Dhs_5.134 //
Whether cruel or gentle, the king of death crushes all.

children.text: nirdhanaṃ vā daridraṃ vā saguṇaṃ nirguṇaṃ tathā // Dhs_5.135 //
children.translated_text: Whether poor or destitute, whether virtuous or without virtue, // Dhs_5.135 //
whether woman or man, the king of death crushes all.

children.text: pravāsinaṃ gṛhasthaṃ vā jale vāpi sthalesthitam // Dhs_5.136 //
children.translated_text: Whether a traveler or a householder, whether in water or on land, // Dhs_5.136 //
whether standing on mountain peaks, the king of death crushes all.

children.text: jāgarantaṃ tathā suptaṃ bhuñjānaṃ vā tathā sthitam // Dhs_5.137 //
children.translated_text: Whether awake or asleep, whether eating or standing still, // Dhs_5.137 //
the destroyer of all the world — the king of death crushes all.

children.text: bhūmisthaṃ (vā) vimānasthaṃ videśasthaṃ tathā gṛhe // Dhs_5.138 //
children.translated_text: Whether on the ground or in a celestial palace, whether abroad or at home, // Dhs_5.138 //
this wheel of time is like a saw — the king of death crushes all.

children.text: bhāgyavantaṃ tathā dhanya nistriśaṃ (caiva) dharmikam // Dhs_5.139 //
children.translated_text: Whether fortunate or prosperous, whether unarmored or righteous, // Dhs_5.139 //
whether sick or healthy of body, the king of death crushes all.

children.text: caṇḍaṃ suśīlinaṃ cāpi kadarya dhaninaṃ tathā // Dhs_5.140 //
children.translated_text: Whether fierce or well-mannered, whether miserly or wealthy, // Dhs_5.140 //
whether heedless or heedful, the king of death crushes all.

children.text: nārakeyaṃ tathā pretaṃ tiryañco manujaṃ tathā // Dhs_5.141 //
children.translated_text: Whether a hell-being, a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost), an animal, or a human, // Dhs_5.141 //
with unrelenting force and vigor, the king of death crushes all.

children.text: kāmadhātau ca ye devā rūpadhātau ca ye sthitāḥ // Dhs_5.142 //
children.translated_text: And those gods in the desire realm, and those established in the form realm, // Dhs_5.142 //
all those powerful ones — the king of death crushes all.
And those gods in the formless realms, abiding in attainments,

children.text: tān sarvānapi vai devān mṛtyurājo 'vamardati // Dhs_5.143 //
children.translated_text: all those gods too — the king of death crushes all. // Dhs_5.143 //

body.translated_text: Everything ends in destruction.

children.text: yad jātaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ kiñcid tad vināśāntameva hi /
children.translated_text: Whatever is born, whatever is conditioned — that indeed ends in destruction.

children.text: tannāsti saṃskṛtaṃ kiñcid yasya nāśo ca vidyate /
children.translated_text: There is nothing conditioned whose destruction does not occur.

children.text: mṛtyorbalamidaṃ jñātvā kāmadoṣaṃ ca sarvataḥ // Dhs_5.144 //
children.translated_text: Knowing this power of death and the faults of desire everywhere, // Dhs_5.144 //
and the deception of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) — desist from the ocean of existence!

children.text: tadaitad vyasanaṃ matvā mṛtyorapi calācalam // Dhs_5.145 //
children.translated_text: Knowing this calamity of death, ever-wavering, // Dhs_5.145 //

body.translated_text: let the mind be well-tamed.

children.text: sudāntaṃ kriyatāṃ cittaṃ yenedaṃ bhrāmyate jagat /
children.translated_text: Let the mind be well-tamed, by which this world is whirled about.
From forests, groves, and mountains, and from celestial palaces everywhere, // Dhs_5.146 //
all the gods shall fall, cast down by the fire of time.
Deluded with heedless minds, desirous again of sense-objects, // Dhs_5.147 //
bound by the noose of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), the gods shall go to lower realms.

children.text: rabhasaṃ jīvitaṃ saukhyaṃ prayāti khalu dehinām // Dhs_5.148 //
children.translated_text: The life and happiness of embodied beings passes swiftly indeed, // Dhs_5.148 //

children.text: na ca vindanti vibudhā jātyandhā iva satpatham /
children.translated_text: and the wise do not find the good path, like those born blind.
Like a water-bubble is the life of all embodied beings, // Dhs_5.149 //
fickle as a river-wave, youth passes away.
Impermanent indeed are those <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, grieved by the glances of desire. // Dhs_5.150 //

body.translated_text: The abandonment of passion:

children.translated_text: Helplessly and miserably one is extinguished, like a lamp from exhaustion of oil.
Hurled by the exhaustion of karma, this great and powerful twelve-spoked // Dhs_5.151 //
wheel of dharma brings about a fall, never wavering.
Adorned with various delightful sense-objects and manifold pleasures, // Dhs_5.152 //

body.translated_text: all become the prey of time.

children.translated_text: The <s>Tuṣita</s> gods fall helplessly, having come under the power of time.

children.text: kālasya vaśamāpannā yathā rohanti pādapāḥ // Dhs_5.153 //
children.translated_text: Just as trees grow, having come under the power of time, // Dhs_5.153 //
they again, meeting time, lose their splendor.

children.text: yathā kālaṃ samāpadya bhavanti sukhitāḥ surāḥ // Dhs_5.154 //
children.translated_text: Just as gods become happy upon meeting time, // Dhs_5.154 //

children.text: punastamaiva saṃsṛtya patanti vivaśā hi te /
children.translated_text: they fall again helplessly, reverting to that very same <s>saṃsāra</s>.
Meeting the time of karma, this world revolves. // Dhs_5.155 //

children.text: sukhaṃ vrajati duḥkhaṃ hi kālasya vaśamāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: Happiness turns to suffering, having come under the power of time.

children.text: yadvṛttaṃ prākśubhaṃ karma tacca duṣṭamahodayam // Dhs_5.156 //
children.translated_text: Whatever previous wholesome karma was done, and that which produced great result, // Dhs_5.156 //

children.text: tadidaṃ bhuñjate svargaṃ kṣīyate ca tataḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: they enjoy that heaven, and then it is exhausted again.
Of everything that has a cause and is momentary in particular, // Dhs_5.157 //
