the contemplation of impermanence does not pervade everything.

children.text: ye bhāvāḥ saṃskṛtā nityāḥ sarve te vipralobhinaḥ // Dhs_5.158 //
children.translated_text: Those conditioned things that seem permanent — all those are deceptive. // Dhs_5.158 //
Having deceived people, they pass — this is the established nature of things.

children.text: śīghrasrotā yathā nadyastathā saukhyaṃ śarīriṇām // Dhs_5.159 //
children.translated_text: Like swift-flowing rivers is the happiness of embodied beings. // Dhs_5.159 //

children.text: kṣaṇikaṃ jīvitaṃ sarva na ca vindanti bāliśāḥ /
children.translated_text: All life is momentary, yet the foolish do not perceive it.

children.text: jarā vyādhiśca mṛtyuśca vipattiḥ karmasaṃkṣaye // Dhs_5.160 //
children.translated_text: Old age, disease, and death, and calamity when karma is exhausted — // Dhs_5.160 //
these befall even the gods who seem eternal and roam in pleasures.

children.text: nāyurdhruvaṃ bhavatyeva na saukhyaṃ triṣu dhātuṣu // Dhs_5.161 //
children.translated_text: Life-span is never fixed, nor is happiness in the three realms. // Dhs_5.161 //

children.text: na (ca) vindanti vivaśā devāḥ kāmena mohitāḥ /
children.translated_text: The gods, helpless and deluded by desire, do not perceive this.

children.text: varṣadhārā yathākāśe duḥsthā bhavati sarvataḥ // Dhs_5.162 //
children.translated_text: Just as a stream of rain in the sky is unstable everywhere, // Dhs_5.162 //
so is all this happiness, always like a stream of rain.

children.text: vāyunā pāṃsavo yānti anyonya parighaṭṭitāḥ // Dhs_5.163 //
children.translated_text: Just as dust particles are carried by the wind, striking against one another, // Dhs_5.163 //
so helplessly is the attachment of embodied beings whirled about in space.

children.text: suciramapi saṃramyaṃ nityatā nāsti dehinām // Dhs_5.164 //
children.translated_text: Even after long enjoyment, there is no permanence for embodied beings. // Dhs_5.164 //

children.text: acintyārthe saukhyamidaṃ na ca vindanti bāliśāḥ /
children.translated_text: This happiness is of inconceivable nature, yet the foolish do not perceive it.

children.text: vāteritaṃ tu yat saukhyaṃ vināśāntaṃ bhaviṣyati // Dhs_5.165 //
children.translated_text: That happiness which is stirred by the wind shall end in destruction. // Dhs_5.165 //

body.translated_text: The mixture of suffering in happiness:

children.translated_text: Those who desire, their minds deceived, do not understand destruction.
This happiness is mixed with suffering, as if hidden. // Dhs_5.166 //
Like a pot filled with poison, covered with lotus garlands,

children.text: odanaṃ viṣasammiśraṃ maraṇāntaṃ (hi) tat tathā // Dhs_5.167 //
children.translated_text: like food mixed with poison, ending in death — so is that. // Dhs_5.167 //

children.text: tathā saukhyamidaṃ sarva tasmāt tat parivarjayet /
children.translated_text: So is all this happiness; therefore one should abandon it.

children.text: ādau madhye tathā cānte narakāya bhaviṣyati // Dhs_5.168 //
children.translated_text: In the beginning, middle, and end, it leads to hell. // Dhs_5.168 //

body.translated_text: Arising, abiding, and destruction — all things:

children.translated_text: All that is conditioned is said to end in arising, abiding, and destruction.

children.text: sarva ca saṃskṛtaṃ saukhyaṃ nanu bhaṭṭārameva tat // Dhs_5.169 //
children.translated_text: All conditioned happiness — is it not indeed a mere show? // Dhs_5.169 //
Show and enjoyment are momentary and quickly spent.

children.text: sukhaṃ ca jīvitaṃ sarva tasmāt tat parivarjayet // Dhs_5.170 //
children.translated_text: All happiness and life — therefore one should abandon them. // Dhs_5.170 //

children.text: ādau madhye tathā cānte śreyasyeva manaḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: In the beginning, middle, and end, let the mind always be set on what is beneficial.

children.text: sudāntaḥ śuddhacitasya mṛtyukāle na sīdati // Dhs_5.171 //
children.translated_text: One who is well-tamed and pure of mind does not falter at the time of death. // Dhs_5.171 //

body.translated_text: The inevitability of death:

children.translated_text: Death is inevitable, and separation from the beloved is certain.

children.text: na ca cintayataḥ kāle viṣaye vipralobhinaḥ // Dhs_5.172 //
children.translated_text: And at the time when one does not reflect, sense-objects are deceptive. // Dhs_5.172 //
That unbearable and terrible wheel of old age and death

children.text: pādapān devagān sattvān na ca buddhayantyacakṣuṣaḥ // Dhs_5.173 //
children.translated_text: — trees, gods, and beings — those without eyes do not perceive it. // Dhs_5.173 //

body.translated_text: Of everything born, there is passing away.

children.translated_text: For a god who is passing away, whose faculties and mind are impaired,

children.text: yad duḥkhaṃ sukaraṃ tasya naupamyamiha vidyate // Dhs_5.174 //
children.translated_text: the suffering that is easily done to him has no comparison here. // Dhs_5.174 //
The greater the happiness of one whose mind is afflicted by craving,

children.text: tathā tathā mahad duḥkhaṃ cyavamānasya duḥsaham // Dhs_5.175 //
children.translated_text: the greater the unbearable suffering when passing away. // Dhs_5.175 //

children.text: kṛtvā hi saṃskṛtaṃ karma na jñātvā karmaṇaḥ sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having performed conditioned karma, not knowing the stability of karma,
when the time of death arises, one is burned with remorse. // Dhs_5.176 //

body.translated_text: One's own welfare should be established before death:

children.translated_text: As long as death has not arrived, as long as there is opportunity,
one should establish one's own welfare — this is the path that brings happiness. // Dhs_5.177 //
Passing away in the god-realms, death in the human realms —

children.text: viditvā kaḥ pumān āsthāṃ kuryātsopadrave bhave // Dhs_5.178 //
children.translated_text: knowing this, what person would place confidence in this perilous existence? // Dhs_5.178 //

body.translated_text: Everything is destructible.

children.translated_text: Just as a lamp's destruction is certain from the exhaustion of the oil-wick,
so the fall from the divine abode is certain when karma-activity is exhausted.
Just as the destruction of a wall is inevitable, so the destruction of mind is firmly established. // Dhs_5.179 //
Likewise, from the destruction of karma, happiness inevitably falls.

children.text: kṣīṇapuṇyāḥ nipatyante devāḥ sarve surālayāt // Dhs_5.180 //
children.translated_text: All gods whose merit is exhausted fall from the divine abode. // Dhs_5.180 //
This impermanence causes the downfall of all these beings.

children.text: mṛtyuḥ pivati bhūtāni jarā pivati yauvanam // Dhs_5.181 //
children.translated_text: Death drinks beings, old age drinks youth. // Dhs_5.181 //

children.text: vyādhiḥ pivati cārogyaṃ na ca loko 'vabudhyate /
children.translated_text: Disease drinks health, and the world does not awaken.
Having been born many times and having died many times, // Dhs_5.182 //
one is born, one ages, one passes away and is reborn.

children.text: na kṣaṇo 'sti muhūrto vā parivartastathāpi vā // Dhs_5.183 //
children.translated_text: There is not a moment, not an instant, not even a turn, // Dhs_5.183 //
in which death delays, yet the world does not awaken.
Having been born many times and having died many times, // Dhs_5.184 //
there is no delay of death, yet the world does not awaken.

children.text: anityaṃ jīvitaṃ sarva na vilambi ca yauvanam // Dhs_5.185 //
children.translated_text: All life is impermanent, and youth does not linger. // Dhs_5.185 //
All beings are impermanent, yet the world does not awaken.

children.text: ante krameṇa naśyanti bhāvāḥ kṣaṇavilamvinaḥ // Dhs_5.186 //
children.translated_text: In the end, all things that linger momentarily perish in sequence. // Dhs_5.186 //
Bound by the thread of karma, yet the world does not awaken.
Thousands of koṭis of gods dwelling in forests and groves // Dhs_5.187 //
have been closed off by time, yet the world does not awaken.
Gods who dwell in mud-free realms, heedless with craving for enjoyment, // Dhs_5.188 //

children.text: yāsyanti vilayaṃ sarve na ca loko 'vabudhyate /
children.translated_text: shall all go to dissolution, yet the world does not awaken.
Like foam and bubbles, like dream-objects is happiness. // Dhs_5.189 //

children.text: kṣayaṃ prayāti śīghraṃ ca na ca loko 'vabudhyate /
children.translated_text: It swiftly goes to exhaustion, yet the world does not awaken.

children.text: sarvasya sarvathā sarvo vināśo niyato bhave // Dhs_5.190 //
children.translated_text: Of everything, in every way, destruction in existence is certain for all. // Dhs_5.190 //
Yet disenchantment with <s>saṃsāra</s> does not arise in the fool.

children.text: na sarvaḥ sarvathā sarva sarvopāyaiḥ prayatnaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Not everyone, in every way, by all means and efforts,

children.text: saṃtrātā bhavane prāpte mṛtyukāle sudāruṇe // Dhs_5.191 //
children.translated_text: can be saved when the terrible time of death arrives in existence. // Dhs_5.191 //

body.translated_text: It is called 'death':

children.translated_text: The destroyer of all happiness, the great source of suffering,
the separation of all bonds — it is called 'death.' // Dhs_5.192 //
The bringer of fear to beings, equal to an ocean of sufferings,
the confuser of intellects — it is called 'death.' // Dhs_5.193 //
The cutter of lives, the destroyer of faculties,
untouchable by all beings — it is called 'death.' // Dhs_5.194 //
Unassailable by all beings, unconquerable by all actions,
the destruction of all beings — it is called 'death.' // Dhs_5.195 //
The inevitable end of all realities, the final limit of all embodied ones,
this destruction of the class of beings — it is called 'death.' // Dhs_5.196 //
Of gods, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, <s>uragas</s>, and <s>rākṣasas</s> —
The destroyer of the wheel of time is called death. // Dhs_5.197 //
Unrestrained, destructive, like fire for all beings,
cruel and irreversible — that is called death. // Dhs_5.198 //
The destruction of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases), and also of the formless mind —
the law of time, the great possession — that is called death. // Dhs_5.199 //

children.text: śreyase matiḥ karaṇīyā na tu pramāde
children.translated_text: One should set one's mind toward welfare, not toward heedlessness

children.text: sa eva dhā(ta)ve śīghraṃ vinipātāya dehinām /
children.translated_text: He (death) indeed hastens to cast down beings;

children.text: śreyase kriyatāṃ yatno mā pramādeḥ manaḥ kṛthāḥ // Dhs_5.200 //
children.translated_text: make effort for welfare — do not let the mind dwell in heedlessness. // Dhs_5.200 //

body.translated_text: Life, once gone, does not return

children.text: yathā (hi śīghra) gamanaṃ pakṣiṇāṃ pavanasya vā /
children.translated_text: Just as the swift movement of birds or of the wind,

children.text: tathā śīghrataraṃ yāti jīvitaṃ sarvadehinām // Dhs_5.201 //
children.translated_text: even more swiftly passes the life of all beings. // Dhs_5.201 //
The wind, having gone, returns; birds too return;

children.text: jīvitaṃ yanniruddhaṃ tu tasya nāgamanaṃ punaḥ // Dhs_5.202 //
children.translated_text: but life, once ceased, never comes back again. // Dhs_5.202 //
Quickly <s>karma</s> is exhausted; quickly the Ender approaches;

children.text: avaśyambhāvi viśleṣaṃ na ca vindanti devatāḥ // Dhs_5.203 //
children.translated_text: separation is inevitable — and even the gods cannot prevent it. // Dhs_5.203 //
Without respite, of great velocity, eradicating the four truths,
inevitable and powerful — this death approaches. // Dhs_5.204 //
The gods, having heard, heedless and deceived by pleasure,

children.text: na vindanti mahad duḥkhaṃ yadavaśyaṃ bhaviṣyati // Dhs_5.205 //
children.translated_text: do not perceive the great suffering that will inevitably come. // Dhs_5.205 //
Of all that is conditioned, and especially of time,

children.text: vināśo bhavati (cā)sau dharmateyaṃ bhave bhave // Dhs_5.206 //
children.translated_text: destruction occurs — this is the law in every existence. // Dhs_5.206 //
Old age comes, the destroyer of youth; the Ender, for the destruction of life;
for the destruction of health and power, the rod of disease has arrived;
this triple rod is terrible, the destroyer of gods and <s>asuras</s> alike. // Dhs_5.216 //

children.text: pramādino hi yad devāḥ nūnamete ca cetanāḥ // Dhs_5.208 //
children.translated_text: It approaches, yet the deluded fool does not see the world;
through mutual greed, one's own people are agitated by affection. // Dhs_5.217 //

children.text: sa paṇḍita iti jñeyo viparītastu bāliśaḥ // Dhs_5.209 //
children.translated_text: One who sees future danger with the eye of knowledge —

body.translated_text: he should be known as wise; the opposite is foolish. // Dhs_5.209 //

children.translated_text: The exhaustion of <s>karma</s> destroys happiness

children.text: karmakṣaye tu naśyanti dīpā snehavaśādiva // Dhs_5.210 //
children.translated_text: All with deluded minds, deceived by their own consciousness,
when <s>karma</s> is exhausted, they perish like lamps when oil is spent. // Dhs_5.210 //

children.text: bhuktvā karmakṣayo bhūta vinipāto bhaviṣyati // Dhs_5.211 //
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed this unsurpassed happiness of manifold objects,
when <s>karma</s> is exhausted, a fall will surely follow. // Dhs_5.211 //
From not understanding impermanence, delight in <s>adharma</s>
The life of beings passes like the ripples of water,
yet the foolish do not understand its bubblelike essencelessness. // Dhs_5.212 //

children.text: na tu devāściraṃ tiṣṭhantyanityo bhāvanamiti // Dhs_5.213 //
children.translated_text: How long might a mass of foam endure by any means?

body.translated_text: Yet gods do not endure long — for existence is impermanent. // Dhs_5.213 //

children.translated_text: Through the power of greed, death is disregarded
This entire earth is cultivated by people desiring fruits,

children.text: kṣaṇe kṣaṇe vivardhante lobhāśā mohite jane /
children.translated_text: yet death is not perceived by the unwise who are attached to gain. // Dhs_5.214 //

children.text: na ca vindanti saṃsārāḥ kṣīyamāṇāḥ kṣaṇe kṣaṇe // Dhs_5.215 //
children.translated_text: Moment by moment, greedy hopes increase in deluded people,

body.translated_text: yet they do not perceive <s>saṃsāra</s> diminishing moment by moment. // Dhs_5.215 //

children.translated_text: He summarizes the three rods
This rod of old age approaches, the destroyer of youth for people;
for the destruction of the power of health, this rod of disease has arrived;

children.text: abhyeti na ca mūḍho 'yaṃ lokaṃ paśyati bāliśaḥ /
children.translated_text: this triple rod is terrible, the destroyer of gods and <s>asuras</s>. // Dhs_5.216 //
It approaches, but this deluded fool does not see the world;
through mutual greed, one's own people are agitated by affection. // Dhs_5.217 //
Those bound by delusion do not understand death and separation
People go, clinging to one another, while people are bound by delusion;

body.translated_text: and those who are subject to sons, grandsons, and great-grandsons. // Dhs_5.218 //

children.text: sarve tena bhaviṣyanti tvaṃ tu saṅgena bādhyase /
children.translated_text: The aggregate of <s>karma</s> brings suffering
All will become that — yet you are obstructed by attachment;
the enemy that ends life is fearless and of great power. // Dhs_5.219 //
He is swift, of great velocity — this death approaches;

body.translated_text: the law of the moving and the unmoving should be known, as demonstrated by the aggregates of <s>karma</s>. // Dhs_5.220 //

children.translated_text: The destruction of gods and others occurs

children.text: na śaktāścyavane kṣāntaṃ balaṃ tasya tathāgatam // Dhs_5.221 //
children.translated_text: Divine <s>nāgas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, serpent-demons, and <s>rākṣasas</s> —

body.translated_text: they are not able to endure at the time of falling; his power is thus-gone. // Dhs_5.221 //

children.translated_text: One who sees reality does not attain a bad rebirth

children.text: aliptaḥ pāpakairdharmairna sa gacchati durgatim // Dhs_5.222 //
children.translated_text: The law of the moving and unmoving should be known by the seer of reality through <s>karma</s>;

body.translated_text: unstained by evil dharmas, he does not go to a bad rebirth. // Dhs_5.222 //
Thus ends the fifth chapter on Impermanence.
(6) Chapter on Non-Negligence

children.translated_text: There is no liberation for one who delights in negligence
A being who delights in negligence is not suited for liberation;

body.translated_text: for one deluded by the poison of negligence, <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is indeed far away. // Dhs_6.1 //

children.translated_text: The mind should not be set on negligence

children.text: pramādaparamā devāḥ patanti narake punaḥ // Dhs_6.2 //
children.translated_text: One should not be bound by negligence — negligence is the supreme enemy;
the gods who are devoted to negligence fall again into hell. // Dhs_6.2 //

children.text: na pramāde manaḥ kārya pramādaviṣamuttamam // Dhs_6.3 //
children.translated_text: Having known this own-nature of dharmas — their arising and passing away —
the mind should not be set on negligence — the supreme poison of negligence. // Dhs_6.3 //
The mutual opposition of negligence and non-negligence

children.text: apramattā na bhriyante pramattāstu sadātmṛtāḥ // Dhs_6.4 //
children.translated_text: Non-negligence is the state of the deathless; negligence is the state of death;

children.text: yathā viṣaṃ tathā vahniḥ pramādaḥ prāṇināṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: the non-negligent are not ruined, but the negligent are as if ever dead. // Dhs_6.4 //

children.text: pramādonmāditāḥ satvāḥ duḥkhād duḥkhaṃ prayānti te // Dhs_6.5 //
children.translated_text: Just as poison, just as fire — so is negligence for living beings;
beings maddened by negligence go from suffering to suffering. // Dhs_6.5 //

children.text: prayānti paramāṃ śānti pramādo yatra nāsti hi // Dhs_6.6 //
children.translated_text: The non-negligent, always immortal, endowed with all endeavors,
go to supreme peace, where indeed negligence does not exist. // Dhs_6.6 //

children.text: tasya dharmavimūḍhasya kutaḥ svargo bhaviṣyati? // Dhs_6.7 //
children.translated_text: A being who delights in negligence does not pursue the good;
for one deluded about the Dharma, how will there be heaven? // Dhs_6.7 //

children.text: apramattā na bhriyante pramattāstu sadātmṛtāḥ // Dhs_6.8 //
children.translated_text: One should avoid negligence, since negligence is the supreme poison;

children.text: saubhāgyaṃ prāpya yo martyaḥ pramādeṣu ca vartate /
children.translated_text: the non-negligent are not ruined, but the negligent are as if ever dead. // Dhs_6.8 //

children.text: na paṇḍita itikhyāto viparītastu nānyathā // Dhs_6.9 //
children.translated_text: A mortal who, having obtained good fortune, engages in negligence,

children.text: na pramādasya kālo hi harṣasya na kathañcana /
children.translated_text: is not known as wise — the opposite is the case, not otherwise. // Dhs_6.9 //
There is never a time for negligence or for merriment,

body.translated_text: since the mind generates delusion, and at the time of death one is greatly powerful. // Dhs_6.10 //

children.translated_text: Description of negligence through the metaphor of negligence

children.text: viṣayairmohitā mūḍhā na ca vindantyacakṣuṣaḥ // Dhs_6.11 //
children.translated_text: Merriment is the smoke, negligence is the fire — it burns the gods in many ways;
the deluded, deluded by sense objects, being blind, do not perceive. // Dhs_6.11 //

children.text: yathā hi viṣayairmūḍhā nāvagacchanti yaddviṣaḥ // Dhs_6.12 //
children.translated_text: They see the uninterrupted formations of beings,
yet, deluded by sense objects, the foolish do not understand what enemies are. // Dhs_6.12 //

children.text: sukhaṃ na dṛśyate pūrva pramādomandabuddhibhiḥ // Dhs_6.13 //
children.translated_text: Therefore the wise declare negligence to be like poison;
happiness is not formerly seen through negligence by those of dull intellect. // Dhs_6.13 //

children.text: phale prāpte pramādo 'yaṃ paścāt santapyate vyathā // Dhs_6.14 //
children.translated_text: Those served by negligence go to hell again;

body.translated_text: when the fruit is obtained, this negligence afterwards burns with suffering. // Dhs_6.14 //

children.translated_text: Negligence produces misfortune

children.text: tathā ca kuśalaṃ prāyo yaḥ pramādaṃ na sevate // Dhs_6.15 //
children.translated_text: Negligence is seen by wise people as the cause of all misfortune;

children.text: duḥkhaṃ yasya bhavediṣṭaṃ sa pramādaṃ niṣevatām /
children.translated_text: and so, one who does not indulge in negligence is mostly virtuous. // Dhs_6.15 //

children.text: na pramādaparaḥ kaścit kadācit sukhamāpnuyāt // Dhs_6.16 //
children.translated_text: Let one whose wish is for suffering indulge in negligence;

body.translated_text: no one devoted to negligence ever attains happiness. // Dhs_6.16 //

children.translated_text: Those free from negligence attain the imperishable state
The virtuous, who have abandoned negligence, go to the imperishable state;
no one devoted to negligence would lead beings in hell to suffering. // Dhs_6.17 //

children.text: tiraścāṃ hi surāṇāṃ ca viśeṣo naiva vidyate // Dhs_6.18 //
children.translated_text: If the gods endure this and delight in it, being of dull intellect,

body.translated_text: then there is no distinction between animals and gods. // Dhs_6.18 //

children.translated_text: Through negligence, they fall from the realm of the gods
The gods, who are devoted to negligence, each with diverse <s>karma</s>,

children.text: sannikṛṣṭaṃ sadā duḥkhaṃ patanaṃ vā bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: do not understand that falling from the realm of the gods will come. // Dhs_6.19 //

children.text: devalokottarā devā yathā syāt sukhamātmanaḥ // Dhs_6.20 //
children.translated_text: Suffering is always near; falling will surely come;
even for the gods in the higher realms — as if happiness were for oneself! // Dhs_6.20 //
One who, having reached the realm of the gods, guards against negligence,
at the end of falling, when meritorious <s>karma</s> is exhausted, awakens. // Dhs_6.21 //
Do not become devoted to negligence! Negligence is not proper for the gods;

body.translated_text: struck by the faults of negligence, they fall from the abode of the thirty-three. // Dhs_6.22 //

children.translated_text: A person under the power of negligence goes to destruction

children.text: sa paścād vigate tasmin pratyādeśena rakṣyate // Dhs_6.23 //
children.translated_text: Every person is burned, deluded by negligence;
afterward, when that passes, one is protected by reproach. // Dhs_6.23 //

children.text: vicaranti sadā mūḍhāḥ surāḥ satkṛtamohitāḥ // Dhs_6.24 //
children.translated_text: This ground, born of faults, with negligence as its green grass —
the deluded gods, deceived by honor, always roam about. // Dhs_6.24 //

children.text: na teṣāṃ viśvased vīro yasmāt svapnopamā hi te // Dhs_6.25 //
children.translated_text: Fickle, treacherous, intense — negligences are the causes of desire;

body.translated_text: the hero should not trust in them, since they are like dreams. // Dhs_6.25 //

children.text: na svapno narake hetuḥ kāmāḥ svapnasya hetukāḥ /
children.translated_text: Desire is the cause of hell

children.text: tasmāt kāmamimaṃ muktvā nityaṃ sucaritaṃ caret // Dhs_6.26 //
children.translated_text: Dreams are not the cause of hell; desires are the cause of dreams;

body.translated_text: therefore, having abandoned this desire, one should always practice good conduct. // Dhs_6.26 //

children.translated_text: Through non-negligence, one can attain everything
That station obtained entirely by the gods deluded by desires —

body.translated_text: that station is attained by heroic people devoted to non-negligence. // Dhs_6.27 //

children.translated_text: <s>Saṃsāra</s> is rooted in negligence
<s>Saṃsāra</s>, rooted in negligence, is the abode of the gods likewise;
those intoxicated by the poison of negligence are sunk in the straits of existence. // Dhs_6.28 //

children.text: andhakāreṇa ye mūḍhāsteṣāṃ cakṣurna vidyate // Dhs_6.29 //
children.translated_text: Darkness is rooted in negligence, and ignorance is harmful;

body.translated_text: those deluded by darkness have no eye of wisdom. // Dhs_6.29 //

body.text: tejasā hi tathā mūlairagninā na ca kathyate /
body.translated_text: Negligence is of the nature of delusion
Just as fire is not described by its brilliance or roots,

children.translated_text: so negligence is proclaimed as the chief among delusions. // Dhs_6.30 //

children.text: muhayante yena te bālāḥ prayānti narakaṃ punaḥ // Dhs_6.31 //
children.translated_text: With a mind heated by the fire of negligence, one acts thus;

body.translated_text: by which those fools are deluded and go to hell again. // Dhs_6.31 //

children.translated_text: One maddened by negligence experiences only happiness
The gods, maddened by negligence, threefold, of restless nature,

body.translated_text: forgetting the suffering of separation, they desire happiness in union. // Dhs_6.32 //

children.translated_text: Life ends only in falling

children.text: paścād vahanti virasaṃ patanāntaṃ sukhaṃ calam // Dhs_6.33 //
children.translated_text: When great suffering is at hand, when life ends in falling,
afterward they carry the tasteless, unstable happiness that ends in falling. // Dhs_6.33 //

children.text: jarāntaṃ yauvanaṃ sarva karmāntaḥ sarvadehinām // Dhs_6.34 //
children.translated_text: Union always ends in separation; happiness always ends in falling;

body.translated_text: all youth ends in old age; all of beings ends in <s>karma</s>. // Dhs_6.34 //

children.translated_text: <s>Saṃsāra</s> is connected with the drama of <s>karma</s>

children.text: naṭavannaṭayantyete gatyāṃ gatyāṃ pṛthak pṛthak // Dhs_6.35 //
children.translated_text: All beings are bound by <s>karma</s>, both wholesome and unwholesome;
like actors, they play their parts in each and every destiny. // Dhs_6.35 //

children.text: na tatra viśvaseddhīmānanityā karmaṇāṃ gatiḥ // Dhs_6.36 //
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃsāra</s>, connected with the drama of <s>karma</s>, revolves always;

body.translated_text: the wise should not trust therein — the course of <s>karma</s> is impermanent. // Dhs_6.36 //

children.translated_text: Negligence is the supreme fault

children.text: pramādena tu ye muktā (ste) tīrṇāsti bhavārṇavāt // Dhs_6.37 //
children.translated_text: Like poison, all evils — negligence should be completely avoided;
those who are freed from negligence have crossed the ocean of existence. // Dhs_6.37 //

children.text: na pramādaprapatitaḥ kadāpi sukhavān bhavet // Dhs_6.38 //
children.translated_text: A sinner who has fallen from a precipice sometimes lives;
but one who has fallen through negligence will never be happy. // Dhs_6.38 //

children.text: na rātrau na divā tasya śubhaṃ bhavati karhicit // Dhs_6.39 //
children.translated_text: Negligence is the supreme fault in all <s>karma</s>;

children.text: yat sukhaṃ laukikaṃ kiñcid yacca lokottaraṃ matam /
children.translated_text: for such a one, nothing good arises, neither at night nor by day. // Dhs_6.39 //

children.text: naśyate tat pramādena tasmāt tat parivarjayet // Dhs_6.40 //
children.translated_text: Whatever worldly happiness there is, and whatever is considered supramundane —

body.translated_text: it is destroyed by negligence; therefore one should avoid it. // Dhs_6.40 //

children.translated_text: Non-negligence is the state of the deathless

children.text: apramādena te devāḥ devānāṃ śreṣṭhatāṃ gatāḥ // Dhs_6.41 //
children.translated_text: Non-negligence is the state of the deathless; negligence is the state of death;
through non-negligence, those gods have attained the highest rank among the gods. // Dhs_6.41 //

children.text: tasmād pramādavirataḥ sukhī bhavati sarvadā // Dhs_6.42 //
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃsāra</s> is rooted in negligence; non-negligence is the good destiny;

body.translated_text: therefore one who has abandoned negligence is always happy. // Dhs_6.42 //

children.text: icchate yatsukhaṃ nityaṃ yaśca duḥkhād vibheti (vai) /
children.translated_text: If one fears suffering, one should abandon negligence: One who always desires happiness and who fears suffering —

children.text: sa (hi) pramādād viramet pramādo viṣavannṛṇām // Dhs_6.43 //
children.translated_text: One should desist from heedlessness, for heedlessness is like poison to humans. // Dhs_6.43 //
Struck down by the sleep of heedlessness, deluded by the poison of heedlessness,

children.text: prapātaṃ hi prapadyante janāḥ śukla kṛtātmakāḥ // Dhs_6.44 //
children.translated_text: people of meritorious nature fall into the abyss. // Dhs_6.44 //

body.translated_text: Non-heedlessness is the supreme good

children.text: apramādaḥ paraṃ śreyo na pramādaḥ kathañcanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Non-heedlessness is the supreme good; heedlessness, never;
through non-heedlessness one is happy; through heedlessness, greatly miserable. // Dhs_6.45 //

body.translated_text: Those deluded by heedlessness go to hell

children.text: pramādamūḍhā hi narā bhūyo madyena mohitā /
children.translated_text: Men deluded by heedlessness, further intoxicated by liquor —

children.text: dhik pramādavimūḍhāste caranti narakaṃ punaḥ // Dhs_6.46 //
children.translated_text: shame on those deluded by heedlessness! They go to hell again. // Dhs_6.46 //
Bound by the net of heedlessness, situated in the ocean of sense objects,
the god, bound by the sense objects of craving, plays in manifold ways. // Dhs_6.47 //

children.text: jātamātrasya devasya tat kṣaṇaṃ kṣīyate sukham /
children.translated_text: At the very moment of a god's birth, his happiness begins to diminish;
the helpless ones, their minds enveloped in heedlessness, do not perceive it. // Dhs_6.48 //
One subject to heedlessness and subject to desire remains forever unsatisfied
Those whose minds are bewildered by heedlessness, always intent on sense objects,

children.text: atṛptāḥ kāmabhogeṣu sukhena sukhitā hi ca // Dhs_6.49 //
children.translated_text: unsatisfied in sensual enjoyments, yet happy with happiness — // Dhs_6.49 //
Burned by the fire of desire, deluded by recklessness,

children.text: na vindanti balaṃ sarva vināśāntaṃ hi jīvitam // Dhs_6.50 //
children.translated_text: they do not perceive that all strength, indeed all life, ends in destruction. // Dhs_6.50 //
Hundreds and tens of millions of gods
are burned by the fire of desire, deluded by heedlessness. // Dhs_6.51 //

body.translated_text: Those endowed with heedlessness fall

children.translated_text: Every person, deluded by heedlessness, is carried away;

children.text: sa paścād vyasane prāpte budhyate tasya tatphalam // Dhs_6.52 //
children.translated_text: later, when calamity has arrived, he realizes its fruit. // Dhs_6.52 //
Heedlessness is seen by seers of truth as life-destroying like poison;

children.text: agnivad dahyate nityaṃ śastravacca nikṛntatiḥ // Dhs_6.53 //
children.translated_text: it always burns like fire and cuts like a weapon. // Dhs_6.53 //

children.text: mitravad dṛśyate pūrva paścād bhavati śatruvat /
children.translated_text: At first it appears like a friend, later it becomes like an enemy;
heedlessness proceeds as a fire for all the gods. // Dhs_6.54 //
For gods, <s>asuras</s>, humans, and <s>nāgas</s> especially,

children.text: pramādaḥ kāraṇaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ sarvānnarthān karoti saḥ // Dhs_6.55 //
children.translated_text: heedlessness is seen as the cause — it produces all misfortunes. // Dhs_6.55 //
He who is always struck by heedlessness does not deserve good fortune;
a person bereft of good fortune is dragged into the hells. // Dhs_6.56 //
Various creatures in the animal realm, deceived by heedlessness,

children.text: maithune bhojane caiva yeṣāṃ buddhiḥ sadāratāḥ // Dhs_6.57 //
children.translated_text: are those whose minds are always set on mating and eating. // Dhs_6.57 //
When the meritorious karma of the gods has come to an end,

children.text: bhaviṣyati tadābhūyaḥ kva yāsyanti pramādinaḥ // Dhs_6.58 //
children.translated_text: where will the heedless ones go then? // Dhs_6.58 //
Struck by the winds of karma amid the waters of heedlessness,

children.text: patanti vṛkṣavad devā gatyāṃ gatyāṃ pṛthak pṛthak // Dhs_6.59 //
children.translated_text: the gods fall like trees, each to different destinies. // Dhs_6.59 //

body.translated_text: Even for the gods, grief born of spiritual urgency arises

children.text: śataśo na hutaścaiva divi jātā divaukasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even though born in heaven as celestials, having offered hundreds [of sacrifices],

children.text: na ca saṃvegajanito hṛdi śokaḥ prajāyate // Dhs_6.60 //
children.translated_text: grief born of spiritual urgency (<s>saṃvega</s>) does not arise in their hearts. // Dhs_6.60 //
Having drunk the beverage of heedlessness, polluted through delusion, the celestials

children.text: patanti narakaṃ tīvraṃ vahninā parivāritam // Dhs_6.61 //
children.translated_text: fall into intense hell, surrounded by fire. // Dhs_6.61 //

body.translated_text: The fruitfulness and fruitlessness of the extremely rare human birth

children.text: sulabdhaṃ mānuṣaṃ janma ye labdhvā apramādinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who, having well obtained a human birth, are free from heedlessness
and perform meritorious deeds — they go to the heavenly worlds. // Dhs_6.62 //

children.text: durlabhaṃ mānuṣaṃ karma labdhvāpi ye pramādinaḥ /
children.translated_text: But those who, having obtained the rare human action, are heedless —

children.text: te pramādāt paribhrāntāḥ patanti narake narāḥ // Dhs_6.63 //
children.translated_text: those men, led astray by heedlessness, fall into hell. // Dhs_6.63 //

body.translated_text: At the time of death, the heedless one is scorched

children.translated_text: The being who delights in heedlessness revolves [in <s>saṃsāra</s>] through compassion [for none];
later, at the time of death, he is scorched by his own mind. // Dhs_6.64 //

body.translated_text: The burning nature of heedlessness

children.text: na tathā dahyate vahnirna ca śastraṃ vikṛntati /
children.translated_text: Fire does not burn so, nor does a weapon cut so,
as heedlessness, born of the five senses, burns. // Dhs_6.65 //

children.text: sukharūpaṃ tathā duḥkhaṃ mitrarūpaṃ tathā ripuḥ /
children.translated_text: Suffering in the form of happiness, an enemy in the form of a friend —

children.text: pramādināṃ hi tannityaṃ tasmāttaṃ parivarjayet // Dhs_6.66 //
children.translated_text: this is always so for the heedless; therefore one should avoid it. // Dhs_6.66 //
Passion mixed with heedlessness and craving — each augments the other;

children.text: trayaste ripavaḥ kruṣṭāḥ nāśayanti sukhaṃ nṛṇām // Dhs_6.67 //
children.translated_text: these three, called enemies, destroy the happiness of humans. // Dhs_6.67 //

children.text: ye pramādaratā nityaṃ na ca dharmaratā budhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who always delight in heedlessness and are not wise ones delighting in the Dharma —

children.text: te mṛtyusamaye prāpte yamadūtaiḥ parākṛtāḥ // Dhs_6.68 //
children.translated_text: when the time of death has arrived, they are overpowered by the messengers of <s>Yama</s>. // Dhs_6.68 //

body.translated_text: Blessed are those who regard heedlessness as poison and abandon it

children.text: pramādaṃ viṣavad ye tu parirakṣanti paṇḍitāḥ /
children.translated_text: The wise who guard against heedlessness as if it were poison —

children.text: te mṛtyusamaye prāpte bhavanti sukhabhāginaḥ // Dhs_6.69 //
children.translated_text: when the time of death has arrived, they become partakers of happiness. // Dhs_6.69 //
Heedlessness is the supreme death; non-heedlessness is the supreme happiness;

children.text: tasmāt sukhārthināḥ nityaṃ mā pramāde matiṃ kṛthāḥ // Dhs_6.70 //
children.translated_text: therefore, those who desire happiness should never set their mind on heedlessness. // Dhs_6.70 //

body.translated_text: Confusion about elements and sense bases is an obstacle to welfare

children.translated_text: Confusion about elements and sense bases is an obstacle to welfare;
the abandonment of all actions proceeds from heedlessness. // Dhs_6.71 //
A messenger of the gateway of illusion for one caught in the machinery of faults,
the foremost of delusion, sinful — heedlessness proceeds. // Dhs_6.72 //

body.translated_text: Those who delight in heedlessness go toward the mouth of death

children.translated_text: Those fools who delight in heedlessness stand in the hand of death;

children.text: pramādasevakā ye tu te sarve nidhanaṃgatā // Dhs_6.73 //
children.translated_text: and those who serve heedlessness — they have all gone to destruction. // Dhs_6.73 //

body.translated_text: Even heedless gods become depleted in merit

children.translated_text: Harmed by heedlessness, for the exhaustion of the gods' merit,

children.text: patanti sukhasaṃmūḍhāstrāṇaṃ teṣāṃ tadā kutaḥ // Dhs_6.74 //
children.translated_text: those deluded by happiness fall — where then is protection for them? // Dhs_6.74 //

body.translated_text: Right Dharma-practice is compassion for beings

children.translated_text: The one Dharma that is auspicious, restrained by compassion, is great;

children.text: kṣāntiścāpi sadā yuktā dayā bhūteṣu sarvadā // Dhs_6.75 //
children.translated_text: patience too, always applied, and compassion for beings at all times. // Dhs_6.75 //
These become a strength at the time of death, in the great danger;
therefore, by those free from heedlessness, they should be diligently cultivated. // Dhs_6.76 //

body.translated_text: Peace arises only for the being who knows learning and its methods

children.translated_text: The turning from ignorance is auspicious; the guarding of knowledge is always [so];
for the being who knows learning and its methods, heedlessness is pacified.

children.text: puruṣārtho niyato (hyatra) yat pramādasya varjanam // Dhs_6.77 //
children.translated_text: The highest human goal is this: the avoidance of heedlessness. // Dhs_6.77 //
Only for one who delights in non-heedlessness is the human goal accomplished
Only for one who delights in non-heedlessness is the human goal esteemed by the good;
heedlessness is generally bondage; liberation comes from its non-heedlessness. // Dhs_6.78 //

body.translated_text: From serving heedlessness comes bondage

children.translated_text: This is regarded by the good as the mark of liberation and bondage.

children.text: evaṃ matvā sadā devo yaḥ pramādena rakṣati /
children.translated_text: Having understood thus, the god who always guards through heedlessness —

children.text: sa paścānmṛtyusamaye jñāsyate tasya tatphalam // Dhs_6.79 //
children.translated_text: later, at the time of death, he will know its fruit. // Dhs_6.79 //

body.translated_text: Contentment itself is the means to <s>nirvāṇa</s>

children.text: yathā yathā hi santoṣaḥ sevyate yatibhiḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: To the extent that contentment is cultivated by ascetics always,

children.text: tathā tathā hi nirvāṇamanike tasya vartate // Dhs_6.80 //
children.translated_text: to that very extent does <s>nirvāṇa</s> come near to them. // Dhs_6.80 //
May there be dispassion toward all desires and engagement with <s>nirvāṇa</s>;

children.text: nāsau mārasya viṣayaḥ kadācit sampravartate // Dhs_6.81 //
children.translated_text: such a one never becomes the domain of <s>Māra</s>. // Dhs_6.81 //

body.translated_text: Only through knowledge is suffering abandoned

children.text: narāṇāṃ paśya manaso nityaṃ vyāpārameva ca /
children.translated_text: Behold the constant activity of the minds of human beings,

children.text: udyogaśca sadājñānaṃ sa kathaṃ duḥkhameṣyati // Dhs_6.82 //
children.translated_text: and their constant effort for knowledge — how will he come to suffering? // Dhs_6.82 //

body.translated_text: Who becomes freed from bondage?

children.translated_text: One endowed with awareness of past dangers, wise regarding the present,

children.text: anāgatavidhijño yaḥ sa muktaḥ kleśabandhanāt // Dhs_6.83 //
children.translated_text: who knows the methods for the future — he is freed from the bondage of defilements. // Dhs_6.83 //
Always delighting in non-heedlessness, apprehensive in matters of distrust,
devoted to consciousness, pure — he stands near to <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_6.84 //

body.translated_text: Great happiness is destroyed by heedlessness

children.translated_text: Even gods, having attained great happiness, are destroyed by heedlessness;

children.text: kiṃ punaryena vā mūḍhāḥ pramādavaśasevinaḥ // Dhs_6.85 //
children.translated_text: how much more so the deluded, those who are servants of heedlessness! // Dhs_6.85 //

children.text: mṛtaḥ sa naro bhavati yaḥ pramādavihāravān /
children.translated_text: That person who dwells in heedlessness is as good as dead;

children.text: jīvite ca pramatto 'yaṃ satataṃ jñānadhāraṇe // Dhs_6.86 //
children.translated_text: he is heedless about life and about the constant holding of knowledge. // Dhs_6.86 //

body.translated_text: The difference between heedlessness and non-heedlessness

children.translated_text: This difference between non-heedlessness and heedlessness is declared:

children.text: mṛtyuṃ ca varjayed doṣaṃ pramādaṃ duḥkhamūlakam // Dhs_6.87 //
children.translated_text: one should avoid the fault of death — heedlessness, the root of suffering. // Dhs_6.87 //

children.text: nityaṃ pramuditā devāḥ nityaṃ pramuditā vayam /
children.translated_text: The gods are always joyful; we too are always joyful;

children.text: pakṣiṇāṃ ca surāṇāṃ ca viśeṣo nopalabhyate // Dhs_6.88 //
children.translated_text: no difference is found between the birds and the gods. // Dhs_6.88 //

children.text: na dharmācaraṇaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ mokṣacaryā na yātyasau /
children.translated_text: No practice of the Dharma is seen; the conduct of liberation does not proceed;

children.text: tathaiva yadi devānāṃ te gatāḥ pakṣibhiḥ samā // Dhs_6.89 //
children.translated_text: if the gods are likewise, they have gone the same way as the birds. // Dhs_6.89 //

children.text: ye pramādavinirmuktā ye ca dharmaratāḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: Those who are free from heedlessness and who always delight in the Dharma —

children.text: te devāḥ satpathā loke na pramādavihāriṇaḥ // Dhs_6.90 //
children.translated_text: those gods are on the true path in the world; not so those who dwell in heedlessness. // Dhs_6.90 //
If the gods delight in play and are always given to heedless conduct,

children.text: devānāṃ ca khagānāṃ ca viśeṣo nopalabhyate // Dhs_6.91 //
children.translated_text: then no difference is found between the gods and the birds. // Dhs_6.91 //

body.translated_text: One fallen from the Dharma is not made distinguished by birth

children.translated_text: By the excellence of actions is birth distinguished by dharmas;

children.text: na dharmapatitaḥ kaścid jātyā bhavati śobhanaḥ // Dhs_6.92 //
children.translated_text: no one fallen from the Dharma is made distinguished by birth alone. // Dhs_6.92 //
Those who censure this <s>saṃsāra</s>, whose nature is complete destruction —
those gods are always equal to birds of deluded understanding. // Dhs_6.93 //
Those whose wisdom is established and who are devoted to the domain of the Dharma —

children.text: te devāḥ sammattā loke na pramādavicāriṇaḥ // Dhs_6.94 //
children.translated_text: those are [truly] gods, honored in the world; not those who wander in heedlessness. // Dhs_6.94 //
Those who understand suffering whose origin and cause is birth, as noble —

children.text: te devā na tu ye saktāḥ kāmeṣu hitakāriṣu // Dhs_6.95 //
children.translated_text: those are gods; not those who are attached to desires that [seem] to bring benefit. // Dhs_6.95 //
Being separated repeatedly from servants, one's own people, and kinsmen,

children.text: ye nodvijanti saṃsāre te devāḥ pakṣibhiḥ samāḥ // Dhs_6.96 //
children.translated_text: those who are not alarmed in <s>saṃsāra</s> — those gods are equal to birds. // Dhs_6.96 //

body.translated_text: Heedlessness is worse than drinking liquor

children.translated_text: Heedlessness is seen by seers of truth as worse than drinking liquor;

children.text: jīryate madyapānaṃ hi pramādo naiva jīryate // Dhs_6.97 //
children.translated_text: for the effects of drinking liquor are digested, but heedlessness is never digested. // Dhs_6.97 //

body.translated_text: One intoxicated by heedlessness wanders in the five destinies

children.translated_text: The world, afflicted by heedlessness, wanders in the five destinies;
therefore, one intoxicated by heedlessness is distinguished by all [remedial] means. // Dhs_6.98 //

body.translated_text: Heedlessness is more degraded even than liquor

children.translated_text: Liquor intoxicates embodied beings for one day at most;
heedlessness is not digested even by one wandering for billions of <s>kalpas</s>. // Dhs_6.99 //
Those who are free from heedlessness have gone to the imperishable state;

children.text: ye tu pramādavaśagāste bhavanti khagā narāḥ // Dhs_6.100 //
children.translated_text: but those subject to heedlessness — those people become [like] birds. // Dhs_6.100 //
By a person who desires welfare, heedlessness is indeed to be avoided;

children.text: yasmāt pramādavaśagāḥ kleśā buddhena deśitāḥ // Dhs_6.101 //
children.translated_text: for the defilements subject to heedlessness have been taught by the <s>Buddha</s>. // Dhs_6.101 //

body.translated_text: Even for the gods, heedlessness is to be abandoned

children.translated_text: If even birds, being light-minded, act through heedlessness,

children.text: kasmāddevāḥ pramādaṃ(taṃ) na jahaṃti viśeṣataḥ // Dhs_6.102 //
children.translated_text: why do the gods not especially abandon that heedlessness? // Dhs_6.102 //

children.text: yastu dūrāt pramādena bhayaṃ nāvaiti durmatiḥ /
children.translated_text: But the evil-minded one who does not perceive the danger of heedlessness from afar —

children.text: so 'vaśyaṃ vyasane prāpte paścāttāpena dahyate // Dhs_6.103 //
children.translated_text: he, when calamity has arrived, is surely burned with remorse. // Dhs_6.103 //

children.text: patanaṃ devalokāt te dānai rakṣanti dāruṇam /
children.translated_text: By gifts they protect themselves from the terrible fall from the heavenly realm;

children.text: tad vicintya pramādaste na saṃsevyaḥ kathañcana // Dhs_6.104 //
children.translated_text: having reflected on that, one should never serve heedlessness in any way. // Dhs_6.104 //

children.text: ye pramādaratā nityaṃ na te saukhyasya bhāginaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who always delight in heedlessness are not partakers of happiness;
heedlessness is the root of suffering — the one terribly harsh root. // Dhs_6.105 //
Hundreds of thousands of billions of <s>padma</s>s and <s>arbuda</s>s

children.text: asaṃkhyāni ca devānāṃ pramādena vitanvitāḥ // Dhs_6.106 //
children.translated_text: and innumerable [beings] among the gods are spread out through heedlessness. // Dhs_6.106 //

body.translated_text: Non-heedlessness is the supreme friend; heedlessness is the enemy

children.translated_text: Non-heedlessness is the supreme friend, always beneficial to humans;
but heedlessness is the supreme enemy — one should be devoted to its friend [non-heedlessness]. // Dhs_6.107 //
This destroyer of merit, terribly harsh like poison —

children.text: durgatīnāṃ paraṃ mārgaḥ pramāda iti kathyate // Dhs_6.108 //
children.translated_text: the supreme path to the lower realms is called heedlessness. // Dhs_6.108 //
Those who are heedless through heedlessness and also delighted by sense objects —

children.text: narāste mūḍhamanaso nityaṃ duḥkhasya bhoginaḥ // Dhs_6.109 //
children.translated_text: those people of deluded minds are always experiencers of suffering. // Dhs_6.109 //

body.translated_text: Those void of knowledge, disregarding fear and suffering, become equal to animals

children.text: yeṣāṃ bhayaṃ na duḥkhaṃ (ca) na ca jñānāvalokanam /
children.translated_text: Those for whom there is no fear, no suffering, and no illumination of knowledge —

children.text: paśubhiste samāviṣṭā na purā sukhakāṃkṣiṇaḥ // Dhs_6.110 //
children.translated_text: They are possessed by beasts, not formerly seekers of happiness. // Dhs_6.110 //
The delight in food and sexual intercourse dwells in the hearts of animals;

children.text: sā ratiryadi devānāṃ te gatāḥ paśubhiḥ samāḥ // Dhs_6.111 //
children.translated_text: if that same delight belongs to the gods, then they have become equal to beasts. // Dhs_6.111 //

body.translated_text: Heedlessness is indeed a synonym for death:

children.translated_text: These who sport exceedingly, standing before death's approach —
when the time of death arrives, they will yield a terrible fruit. // Dhs_6.112 //
This should be avoided like poison by all, being utterly unbearable;

children.text: mṛtyoḥ paryāyanāmaiṣa pramādo hṛdi dehinām // Dhs_6.113 //
children.translated_text: this heedlessness in the hearts of embodied beings is a synonym for death. // Dhs_6.113 //
Those first slain by heedlessness, death then crushes afterward;
this is declared to be the one portion of those whose happiness lies in a life of Dharma. // Dhs_6.114 //

body.translated_text: Heedfulness alone is the path to heaven:

children.translated_text: That which is called heedfulness indicates the path to heaven;
both benefit and harm are encountered, and afterward liberation likewise. // Dhs_6.115 //

body.translated_text: Heedfulness is a virtue; heedlessness is a fault:

children.translated_text: Heedfulness and heedlessness are characterized by virtue and fault respectively;

children.text: tatraiva mūḍhamanaso vijānanti ca dehinaḥ // Dhs_6.116 //
children.translated_text: therein deluded-minded embodied beings do understand. // Dhs_6.116 //

children.text: śatruṇā saha rakṣanti jñāne pariharanti ca /
children.translated_text: They guard against enemies yet abandon in knowledge;
the three branches of the poison-tree of heedlessness are established: // Dhs_6.117 //
old age, disease, and death, always standing over it.

children.text: jarādayo na bādhyante puruṣaṃ satkriyānvitam // Dhs_6.118 //
children.translated_text: Old age and the rest do not afflict a person endowed with good deeds. // Dhs_6.118 //

body.translated_text: One who is heedful, always freed from fear, abides in happiness:

children.translated_text: The wise one abides in <s>saṃsāra</s>, always delighting in heedfulness;

children.text: nikṛntanti sadā doṣā na pramādaṃ pariṣvajet // Dhs_6.119 //
children.translated_text: faults always cut away — one should not embrace heedlessness. // Dhs_6.119 //
Always freed from fear, one attains supreme happiness;

children.text: (a) pramādācca yat saukhyaṃ śāśvataṃ sa bhayaṃ hi tat // Dhs_6.120 //
children.translated_text: and the happiness that arises from heedfulness — that is indeed eternal and fearless. // Dhs_6.120 //

children.text: yattu tasmād vinirmuktaṃ tat saukhyaṃ dhruvamacyutam /
children.translated_text: But that happiness which is freed from it is permanent and unfailing;
hundreds of people here have been deluded by heedlessness. // Dhs_6.121 //
Even so, those who have come under its power are established in heedlessness;
for the four perversions stand above heedlessness. // Dhs_6.122 //
Through freedom from heedlessness, even those enemies of the world are destroyed;
for this is of manifold conceptualization and manifold dangers and difficulties. // Dhs_6.123 //
Gods free from heedlessness, being virtuous, enjoy unfailing happiness:

children.text: saṃsāro bhramate duḥkhe tat pramādasya ceṣṭitam /
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃsāra</s> wanders in suffering — that is the doing of heedlessness;
through freedom from heedlessness alone, unfailing happiness is attained. // Dhs_6.124 //
Through heedlessness, all dharmas perish, their remedies destroyed;
and this heedlessness of the gods keeps growing higher and higher. // Dhs_6.125 //
How will gods deluded by heedlessness attain peace?
Having reflected on this with a gentle mind, one should discriminate: // Dhs_6.126 //

children.text: tathā me hita māstheyaṃ yathā yat syāt (sukhāvaham) /
children.translated_text: "May that benefit be mine which would be conducive to happiness;"

children.text: ye devā yacca tatsaukhyaṃ paśyan yadapikiñcana // Dhs_6.127 //
children.translated_text: those gods and that happiness of theirs — seeing it to be nothing at all — // Dhs_6.127 //

body.translated_text: What is conditioned attains only a fixed end:

children.text: tat sarva (hi) dhruvaṃ gatvā saṃskṛtasyaiṣa sambhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: All that has surely gone to a fixed end — such is the nature of what is conditioned;

children.text: avaśyaṃ te vinaśyanti ye bhāvāḥ saṃskṛtāścalāḥ // Dhs_6.128 //
children.translated_text: those states that are conditioned and unstable inevitably perish. // Dhs_6.128 //

body.translated_text: Through heedlessness, even gods become sharers of suffering:

children.translated_text: Gods devoted to heedlessness are always sharers of suffering;
what mind does one who is stricken by heedlessness make toward them? // Dhs_6.129 //
When separation has arisen, one is tormented with suffering;
regarding sense objects accompanied by desire and possessed by craving — // Dhs_6.130 //
by that the gods, subject to the power of heedlessness, are deceived;
this is the root of all misfortunes — the habitual pursuit of heedlessness. // Dhs_6.131 //

body.translated_text: Abandoning heedlessness brings safety:

children.translated_text: The abandoning of it is blessed, bringing great safety in every way;
beings do not obtain happiness and are also beset by sufferings. // Dhs_6.132 //
Wisdom should be practiced just as fish follow water;

children.text: svarge pramādavaśagā strīvidheyāśca te surāḥ // Dhs_6.133 //
children.translated_text: in heaven, subject to heedlessness, those gods are governed by women. // Dhs_6.133 //

body.translated_text: The heedless become sharers of suffering:

children.translated_text: They, burned by the fire of women, are always sharers of suffering;
therefore, gods should diligently avoid women. // Dhs_6.134 //
For one whose mind is fickle with desire, firmness should be increased;
for one deluded about what should and should not be done, and about Dharma and non-Dharma — // Dhs_6.135 //
<s>Nirvāṇa</s> (liberation) is far indeed for a person who is self-destructive;
one who knows the truth of what is to be revered, skilled in the domain of Dharma — // Dhs_6.136 //

body.translated_text: Only the righteous attain happiness:

children.translated_text: One who desires Dharma and desires its fruit obtains such happiness;
those whose sins and stains are washed away, who always follow the Dharma — // Dhs_6.137 //

body.translated_text: Those deluded by heedlessness obtain suffering:

children.translated_text: They are always seen as happy, not those who dwell in heedlessness;
one struck down by heedlessness is first deluded by heedlessness. // Dhs_6.138 //

body.translated_text: Even a god becomes heedless through intoxicants:

children.text: devo vā puruṣaścāpi na sukhasyāntike hi saḥ /
children.translated_text: Whether a god or a man, he is not near happiness;

children.text: mṛtaḥ sa puruṣo nityaṃ yo madyena pramādyati // Dhs_6.139 //
children.translated_text: that person is always as good as dead who becomes heedless through intoxicants. // Dhs_6.139 //
All people who are carried away by the faults of intoxicants end up in hell;
intoxicants are declared to be a fault that destroys all association. // Dhs_6.140 //
Gods who are always deluded by intoxicants go to hell;

children.text: asambhūteṣu rakṣante na sambhūte kathañcanaḥ // Dhs_6.141 //
children.translated_text: they guard against things that have not arisen, but not at all against things that have arisen. // Dhs_6.141 //
Gods, defiled in form by intoxication, deluded by desires —

children.text: kāmena mohitā devā madyenāpi tathaiva ca // Dhs_6.142 //
children.translated_text: gods deluded by desire and likewise by intoxicants. // Dhs_6.142 //

body.translated_text: The heedless one does not see the truth:

children.text: na tattvamatra paśyanti jātyandhā iva satpatham /
children.translated_text: They do not see the truth here, like the congenitally blind the good path;
the mind disturbed by heedlessness does not perceive the truth. // Dhs_6.143 //
Therefore heedlessness, like fire, should be completely avoided;
through heedlessness, the wholesome sources of Dharma perish. // Dhs_6.144 //

body.translated_text: The consumption of the poison of heedlessness leads only to destruction:

children.text: mārga ca viṣasaṃspṛṣṭaṃ sarvathā naiva paśyati /
children.translated_text: One who is touched by the poison of the path does not see at all;
ten dharmas perish for one who consumes the poison of heedlessness. // Dhs_6.145 //
The four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions) also perish for the heedless;
the Buddhas, who have abandoned desires, praise heedfulness. // Dhs_6.146 //

body.translated_text: The heedful become freed from old age:

children.translated_text: They abhor heedlessness — the cage of old age and death;
the heedful are freed from old age; the heedless are experiencers of suffering. // Dhs_6.147 //

body.translated_text: Heedlessness itself is bondage:

children.translated_text: Heedlessness is indeed this bondage, the suffering of those of dull understanding;
through heedfulness, the skillful go to the assembly of the gods. // Dhs_6.148 //

children.text: tasmāt te patitā bhūyo ye pramādānusevinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore those who pursue heedlessness fall again;
a heedless person is never freed from <s>saṃsāra</s> at all. // Dhs_6.149 //
By the noose and snare of heedlessness, embodied beings are bound;

children.text: akārya kāryasadṛśaṃ kārya kurvanti sarvadā // Dhs_6.150 //
children.translated_text: they always do what should not be done as if it were what should be done. // Dhs_6.150 //

body.translated_text: The heedful attain a succession of blessings:

children.translated_text: Through heedfulness, a person sees all things in their true opposite;

children.text: na laukikeṣu kāryeṣu kuto na śraiyaseṣu ca // Dhs_6.151 //
children.translated_text: not in worldly affairs — how much less in matters of spiritual welfare! // Dhs_6.151 //
The wise, who have reached the far shore of understanding, do not praise heedlessness;

children.text: yathā śubhaṃ parikṣīṇaṃ bhaviṣyati divaukasām // Dhs_6.152 //
children.translated_text: when the merit of the heavenly beings will be exhausted — // Dhs_6.152 //

body.translated_text: The fruit of heedlessness leads to loss:

children.text: tadā pramādasya phalaṃ jñāsyanti kaṭukaṃ hi tat /
children.translated_text: then they will know the fruit of heedlessness, for it is bitter;
for those whose minds are attached to desires, who pursue pleasure to the very end — // Dhs_6.153 //
from that happiness there will be a great fall into ruin;
for those whose desires are always directed toward sense objects, whose minds are absorbed in expectation — // Dhs_6.154 //
for those intoxicated by the sight of women, there will be a fall;
those who always pursue desires, devoted to heedlessness and passion — // Dhs_6.155 //
all those women will abandon them at the time of death;

children.text: cyavamānaṃ suraṃ sarve na kaścidanugacchati // Dhs_6.156 //
children.translated_text: no one follows a god who is falling away. // Dhs_6.156 //

body.translated_text: Those who desire liberation abandon misdeeds:

children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> follows from behind everyone who goes;

children.text: yuktaṃ ca (hi) sadā sevyaṃ varjanīyaṃ ca duṣkṛtam // Dhs_6.157 //
children.translated_text: one should always pursue what is proper and avoid misdeeds. // Dhs_6.157 //

children.text: pramādaṃ ca madaṃ jahayāt pramāda (vi)rato bhavet /
children.translated_text: One should abandon heedlessness and intoxication, and become free from heedlessness;

children.text: pramādo bhavamūlo 'yaṃ pramādastu na śāntaye // Dhs_6.158 //
children.translated_text: this heedlessness is the root of existence, and heedlessness does not lead to peace. // Dhs_6.158 //

body.translated_text: Having reflected on heedlessness and heedfulness, the wise one flourishes in happiness:

children.translated_text: This has been declared regarding the characteristics of heedfulness and heedlessness;

children.text: tad vicintya sadā dhīraḥ sukhaṃ sucaritaṃ caret // Dhs_6.159 //
children.translated_text: having always reflected on this, the wise one should pursue good conduct and happiness. // Dhs_6.159 //

body.translated_text: One who practices the Dharma never obtains suffering:

children.translated_text: A person who practices the Dharma never encounters suffering;

children.text: saṃsarantyatha saṃsāre prāṇinaḥ svena karmaṇā // Dhs_6.160 //
children.translated_text: beings wander in <s>saṃsāra</s> by their own <s>karma</s>. // Dhs_6.160 //

body.translated_text: Heedlessness leads to downfall:

children.translated_text: Why is this world here destroyed by heedlessness?

children.text: pramādaḥ śreyasāṃ nāśaḥ pramādo bandhanaṃ param // Dhs_6.161 //
children.translated_text: Heedlessness is the destruction of blessings; heedlessness is the supreme bondage. // Dhs_6.161 //
Heedlessness leads to downfall; heedlessness leads to hell;
heedlessness alone is declared to be the single cause of suffering. // Dhs_6.162 //

body.translated_text: One who delights in heedfulness attains <s>Nirvāṇa</s>:

children.translated_text: Therefore, a person who desires happiness should avoid heedlessness;

children.text: yaiḥ pramādaḥ parityaktaḥ prāptaṃ taiḥ padamacyutam // Dhs_6.163 //
children.translated_text: those who have abandoned heedlessness have attained the unfailing state. // Dhs_6.163 //
One who delights in heedfulness is indeed near <s>Nirvāṇa</s>;
for the state of heedfulness is the state that stands foremost before <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_6.164 //

body.translated_text: The heedless one is always afflicted with suffering:

children.translated_text: Heedlessness is declared to be the cause of downfall;

children.text: pramattaḥ puruṣaḥ sarvaḥ sonmāda iva lakṣyate // Dhs_6.165 //
children.translated_text: every heedless person appears as if mad. // Dhs_6.165 //
One becomes light in this world and ripens in adversities;

children.text: pramattaḥ puruṣaḥ śakto viparīteṣu vartate // Dhs_6.166 //
children.translated_text: a heedless person, though capable, moves in what is contrary. // Dhs_6.166 //

children.text: hetau karmavipāke ca mṛtyūtpattau tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: In causes and in the ripening of <s>karma</s>, and likewise in death and birth —
the sharp fire of heedlessness drags one down to hell;
therefore, for the sake of liberation from hell, one should abandon heedlessness. // Dhs_6.167 //

children.text: ye pramādaṃ vinirjitya nityaṃ jñānaratā narāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who, having conquered heedlessness, always delight in knowledge —

children.text: te kleśabandhanaṃ chitvā padaṃ yātāḥ sukhodayam // Dhs_6.168 //
children.translated_text: they, having cut the bondage of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), have gone to the state from which happiness arises. // Dhs_6.168 //
Bound by the threads of <s>karma</s>, resting on the swing of the mind,

children.text: bhramanti vibhave sattvā mā pramādeṣu rakṣathaḥ // Dhs_6.169 //
children.translated_text: beings wander in fortune — do not indulge in heedlessness! // Dhs_6.169 //

children.text: sukhī bhavati duḥkhī vai duḥkhitaścāpi sukhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The happy one becomes suffering, and the suffering one becomes happy;

children.text: bhartāpi tṛpto bhavati mā pramādeṣu rakṣathaḥ // Dhs_6.170 //
children.translated_text: even a lord becomes satisfied — do not indulge in heedlessness! // Dhs_6.170 //

children.text: mātā pitā vā bhavati bhāryā mātṛtvameva ca /
children.translated_text: One becomes a mother or a father, a wife becomes a mother too;

children.text: parivarto mahāneṣu mā pramādeṣu rakṣathaḥ // Dhs_6.171 //
children.translated_text: there is a great revolution in these — do not indulge in heedlessness! // Dhs_6.171 //
From heedlessness, desire arises; from desire, hatred proceeds;
having entered the path of faults, one runs toward hell. // Dhs_6.172 //

body.translated_text: One who has ascended wisdom, free from heedlessness, attains the auspicious path:

children.translated_text: Ascend the palace of wisdom — the supreme welfare and security;

children.text: eṣa panthāḥ śivaḥ śreṣṭho yaḥ pramādavivarjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: this is the best and most auspicious path, which is free from heedlessness;

children.text: tena mārgeṇa satataṃ nirvāṇaṃ yānti paṇḍitāḥ // Dhs_6.173 //
children.translated_text: by that path, the wise constantly go to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_6.173 //
Opposition to the attainment of the path, that which corrupts the stream of mind —
the cutter of the bridges of Dharma — heedlessness is declared. // Dhs_6.174 //

body.translated_text: Those stricken by heedlessness go to destruction:

children.translated_text: It is seen as the corrupter of mindfulness, the destroyer of conduct for liberation;

children.text: durgatīnāṃ paraṃ netā pramādaḥ sampravartate // Dhs_6.175 //
children.translated_text: heedlessness operates as the supreme guide to the lower realms. // Dhs_6.175 //

children.text: aneka puruṣaḥ kṣipto nātmano vindate hitam /
children.translated_text: Many a person, distracted, does not find what is beneficial for oneself;

children.text: nāvācyaṃ na ca kāryāṇāṃ vindate 'mṛtakopamaḥ // Dhs_6.176 //
children.translated_text: one finds neither what is unspeakable nor the fruit of deeds, being like one who is dead. // Dhs_6.176 //
Those who bear divine forms yet are equal to animals,

children.text: pramādopahatā mūḍhā nṛtyanti ca hasanti ca // Dhs_6.177 //
children.translated_text: Overcome by heedlessness and deluded, they dance and laugh. // Dhs_6.177 //

children.text: utpannāvicyutāḥ mārgāt kṣāntiṃ ye nāśayanti ca /
children.translated_text: Those who have arisen yet deviated from the path and destroy patience,
Who have become an ocean of human existence — they follow after heedlessness. // Dhs_6.178 //
The progenitor of all faults, the bondage of sinful deeds,
The spoiler of all dharmas — the enemy of heedlessness proceeds. // Dhs_6.179 //

body.translated_text: Heedlessness is indeed the enemy of all meritorious actions

children.translated_text: Neither inner actions nor outer ones in any way —
A creature overcome by heedlessness knows them not, having lost its seat. // Dhs_6.180 //
With minds absorbed in play, indulging in dance and music,
Unsatiated by divine sense objects, the abodes of the wise shall perish. // Dhs_6.181 //
In a place of danger, these ones laugh, deluded by heedlessness;

children.text: mārgāmārga na vindanti jātyandhena surāḥ samāḥ // Dhs_6.182 //
children.translated_text: They find neither the path nor the non-path — the gods are equal to the born-blind. // Dhs_6.182 //

body.translated_text: The heedless wander only in the desire realm

children.translated_text: These wander in the desire realm, revolving like a wheel in the five destinies;

children.text: dhyānebhyo yaddhi patanaṃ tat pramādasya ceṣṭitam // Dhs_6.183 //
children.translated_text: The fall from the <s>dhyānas</s> — that is the doing of heedlessness. // Dhs_6.183 //

body.translated_text: The action wrought by heedlessness leads to a fall

children.translated_text: And from the formless realms, having attained the fourth worldly state,

children.text: bhramanti bhramadolāyāṃ tat pramādasya ceṣṭitam // Dhs_6.184 //
children.translated_text: They wander on the swinging cradle of wandering — that is the doing of heedlessness. // Dhs_6.184 //
Bound by the bonds of heedlessness, fettered by the nooses of craving,

children.text: traidhātukamidaṃ kṛtsnaṃ na ca buddhayantya cetasaḥ // Dhs_6.185 //
children.translated_text: This entire triple world — yet they do not understand in their minds. // Dhs_6.185 //
That they proceed to the station of Dharma, shown the way by fear of craving —

children.text: na bhūyaḥ khedamāyāti tat pramādasya ceṣṭitam // Dhs_6.186 //
children.translated_text: They do not again come to sorrow — that is the doing of heedlessness. // Dhs_6.186 //

body.translated_text: Through the power of heedlessness, one obtains only suffering

children.translated_text: That suffering born of separation from the beloved that arises in people's hearts —

children.text: sevanād yat pramādasya kathayanti tathāgatā // Dhs_6.187 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgatas</s> declare it arises from association with heedlessness. // Dhs_6.187 //

children.text: anarthā hi trayo loke yairidaṃ naśyate jagat /
children.translated_text: Indeed there are three calamities in the world by which this world is destroyed:

children.text: vyādhirjarā ca mṛtyuśca pramādālasya sambhavāḥ // Dhs_6.188 //
children.translated_text: Disease, old age, and death — they arise from heedlessness and laziness. // Dhs_6.188 //
Just as herbs, grass, and other things sprout upon the earth,

children.text: tathā pramādināṃ kleṣāḥ pravartante pṛthagvidhāḥ // Dhs_6.189 //
children.translated_text: So too do the various defilements arise in the heedless. // Dhs_6.189 //

body.translated_text: The poisonous sprout of heedlessness

children.text: strīśleṣo madyapānaṃ ca krīḍā ca viṣayaiḥ saha /
children.translated_text: Embracing women, drinking liquor, and sport with sense objects,
Fickleness and laziness — these are the poisonous sprouts of heedlessness. // Dhs_6.190 //

body.translated_text: The characteristics of heedlessness and non-heedlessness

children.translated_text: Heedlessness is supreme suffering, non-heedlessness is supreme happiness;
In brief, the characteristic of non-heedlessness and heedlessness has been stated. // Dhs_6.191 //

body.translated_text: Therefore heedlessness should not be pursued

children.text: tasmāt pramādo na nareṇa sevyaḥ, sa durgatīnāṃ prathamāgrameva /
children.translated_text: Therefore heedlessness should not be pursued by a person — it is the very forefront of lower rebirths;

children.text: vihāya taṃ duḥkhasahastrayoniṃ, prayānti buddhā bhavapāragrayam // Dhs_6.192 //
children.translated_text: Abandoning that womb of a thousandfold suffering, the Buddhas proceed to the far shore of existence. // Dhs_6.192 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the sixth chapter on Non-heedlessness (<s>Apramādavarga</s>). //
(7) Chapter on Revulsion from Sense Desires (<s>Kāmajugupsāvarga</s>)
Sense desires lead to hell

children.text: na kāmeṣu ratiṃ kuryāt kāmāḥ paramavañcakāḥ /
children.translated_text: One should not take delight in sense desires — desires are supremely deceptive;
They are terrible bonds of <s>saṃsāra</s>, all leading to hell. // Dhs_7.1 //
For one who clings to sense desires, suffering is endless;
For one bitten by the serpent of desire, there is no happiness whatsoever. // Dhs_7.2 //

body.translated_text: The conduct of those enslaved by passion and the rest

children.translated_text: Better that one's tongue be cut by oneself

children.text: saṃkṣoditā bhavejjihvā na coktaṃ kāmagaṃva(caḥ) // Dhs_7.3 //
children.translated_text: With a sharp razor's edge, than that speech of desire be uttered. // Dhs_7.3 //
Beings deceived by passion, tormented by hatred,
Having fallen under the power of delusion, speak unsweet words. // Dhs_7.4 //

body.translated_text: One enslaved by passion always experiences the worst suffering

children.translated_text: One who, restrained by slight passion, commits many misdeeds —

children.text: sa rāgavaśago mūḍho duḥkhād duḥkhamavāpnuyāt // Dhs_7.5 //
children.translated_text: That fool, enslaved by passion, would obtain suffering upon suffering. // Dhs_7.5 //

body.translated_text: He describes the ripening of desire

children.text: atṛptirasmāt kāmāste na sukhā nāpi śāśvatāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore those desires bring no satisfaction — they are neither pleasant nor eternal;
In their ripening they are extremely intense — therefore one should avoid them. // Dhs_7.6 //
People overcome by passion dwell in the abodes of hell;

children.text: na rāgavaśagā ye tu na teṣāṃ narakād bhayam // Dhs_7.7 //
children.translated_text: But those who are not enslaved by passion — for them there is no fear of hell. // Dhs_7.7 //

body.translated_text: The poison of desire should be abandoned
Arising from the fierce and the non-fierce, and fierce in their ripening,
Desires are like poison and fire — they should be avoided with effort. // Dhs_7.8 //

children.translated_text: For one who has abandoned desires and always delights in liberation,
Unwholesome dharmas perish, as darkness at sunrise. // Dhs_7.9 //

body.translated_text: The fire of desire causes one to fall into hell

children.translated_text: Having deluded the senses and the knower of sense objects in various ways,
These desires, charming to the foolish mind, cause one to fall into hell. // Dhs_7.10 //

body.translated_text: The greatness of the fire of passion

children.translated_text: For one attached to the five senses with the five sense objects,
Even for a moment the fire of passion is not satisfied by sense objects. // Dhs_7.11 //
From contact the fire is born; from separation it is not born;
From contact too comes separation — the fire of passion consumes people. // Dhs_7.12 //
From afar, ordinary fire does not burn — it has no such range;
Equally terrible from far and near, the fire of passion burns fiercely. // Dhs_7.13 //
Born from the fuel of mental fabrication, with the crooked force of longing,
Nourished by the ghee of craving — this fire of passion too is a burner. // Dhs_7.14 //
Having burned this body, ordinary fire subsides;
But the fire of passion, freed from name and form, never subsides. // Dhs_7.15 //
Fire, the supreme burner, causes alarm in beings;
Yet the fire of passion, though extremely sharp, causes no alarm in people. // Dhs_7.16 //
This fire, arisen from the five senses, surrounded by the five sense objects,
By the force of the wind of craving, the fire of passion burns all creatures. // Dhs_7.17 //
Born from the fire-sticks of discursive thought, nourished by sense objects,

children.text: kāṣṭhavad dahyate tena na ca dṛśyo janasya saḥ // Dhs_7.18 //
children.translated_text: One is burned like firewood by it — yet it is not visible to people. // Dhs_7.18 //

children.text: yathā yathā hi prabalo rāgāgnistapyate mahān /
children.translated_text: The more the great fire of passion blazes forth,

children.text: tathā tathā (ca) rāgāndhaiḥ svasukhaṃ parisevyate // Dhs_7.19 //
children.translated_text: The more those blinded by passion indulge in their own pleasure. // Dhs_7.19 //
Ordinary fire is illuminating, but the fire of passion is veiled in darkness;
Therefore the wise one should avoid the fire of passion like cold. // Dhs_7.20 //

body.translated_text: He describes the ripening of sense objects

children.translated_text: A creature delighting in sense objects can never be happy;

children.text: viṣayāḥ viṣayairdaṣṭāḥ pariṇāme ca dāruṇāḥ // Dhs_7.21 //
children.translated_text: Sense objects are bitten by sense objects and are terrible in their ripening. // Dhs_7.21 //

children.text: nādye nānte na madhye ca nāsmiṃlloke na cāpare /
children.translated_text: Neither at the beginning, nor at the end, nor in the middle, neither in this world nor in the next,

children.text: sukhadā viṣayā kāmaṃ bhavantīha kathañcana // Dhs_7.22 //
children.translated_text: Do sense desires ever bring happiness in any way. // Dhs_7.22 //
For every fool, by the productions of craving and sport,
Is not satisfied by sense objects — as fire is not satisfied by fuel. // Dhs_7.23 //
Unsatisfied by sense objects, all these people are deceived;
Devoted to the practice of death, they are burned by these faults. // Dhs_7.24 //

body.translated_text: He describes the state of those blinded by the delusion of desire

children.translated_text: The pleasure of freely roaming desires — that is indeed the doing of delusion;

children.text: tadeva yadi devānāṃ khagaiḥ syuste samāḥ surāḥ // Dhs_7.25 //
children.translated_text: If that is the case even for gods, those gods are equal to birds. // Dhs_7.25 //
At the end of <s>kalpas</s>, the lord of rivers is burned up;
Yet the eye is not satisfied by forms even in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. // Dhs_7.26 //
There might be a filling of the ocean by submissive waters and the like,

children.text: na tu dṛṣṭiḥ samudrasya rūpārthaistṛptirasti hi // Dhs_7.27 //
children.translated_text: But for the eye of the ocean there is no satisfaction with forms and objects. // Dhs_7.27 //
For one unsatisfied with desires, what happiness can be imagined?
Satisfaction belongs to one who is free from craving, to the embodied being who has gone beyond sorrow. // Dhs_7.28 //

children.text: mādyante bahumohāndhā na ca buddhayanti bāliśāḥ /
children.translated_text: Many who are blinded by great delusion become intoxicated, and the foolish do not understand;
Like sandalwood trees that are momentary in a gentle breeze. // Dhs_7.29 //

body.translated_text: Desires are without substance and deceptive

children.translated_text: Having the nature of deception like a dream, resembling a <s>gandharva</s> city (mirage),
Empty, hollow, and without substance — desires are supremely deceptive. // Dhs_7.30 //
Desires are equal to delusion — what comparison is there to their ripening?
Desires are proclaimed as harmful to the world, like fire. // Dhs_7.31 //
Knowing the danger of desire, those who are deluded by its fruit —
Those who see it are pleased, of an embodied being who has gone beyond longing. // Dhs_7.32 //
Those that are thought of as otherwise, when obtained are again just so;

children.text: sarvataḥ pāpakartāraḥ kāmā loke viṣopamāḥ // Dhs_7.33 //
children.translated_text: In every way evil-doers, desires in the world are like poison. // Dhs_7.33 //
Those gods whose minds are unsatisfied by desires, having fallen,

children.text: patanti narake mūḍhāḥ kāmena parivañcitāḥ // Dhs_7.34 //
children.translated_text: Fall again into hell, deluded, deceived by desire. // Dhs_7.34 //

body.translated_text: He censures women

children.translated_text: Fickle as river waves, like streaks of lightning,
With the force of a fish-whirlpool — women are the abode of poison in the world of desire. // Dhs_7.35 //
When thought upon, they increase; when increased, they are like fire;

children.text: ādau cānte tathā kāmāstasmāt kāmān vivarjayet // Dhs_7.36 //
children.translated_text: At the beginning and at the end too — desires are thus; therefore one should abandon desires. // Dhs_7.36 //

body.translated_text: The fruit of indulging in desire

children.text: yathā yathā hi sevyante vivardhante tathā tathā /
children.translated_text: The more they are indulged, the more they increase;
Desires, released like flames of fire, ripen bitterly. // Dhs_7.37 //

body.translated_text: He states the fruit of abandoning desire

children.text: evaṃ doṣaṃ sadā jñātvā dhīraḥ kāmān vivarjayet /
children.translated_text: Thus knowing the fault always, the wise one should abandon desires;
For one who has turned away from desires, there is ultimate happiness. // Dhs_7.38 //
