body.translated_text: The fire of desire causes even gods to fall

children.translated_text: Innumerable thousands and tens of millions of gods
Fall into the hell of desire's conflagration, terrifying as fire. // Dhs_7.39 //
Just as those who seek happiness avoid fire, poison, and weapons,

children.text: tathā kāmāḥ sadā varjyā hetavo narakasya te // Dhs_7.40 //
children.translated_text: So should desires always be avoided — they are the causes of hell. // Dhs_7.40 //

children.text: na dṛṣṭo na śrutaḥ kaścid yaḥ kāmavaśagaḥ pumān /
children.translated_text: No one has been seen or heard of who, being enslaved by desire,

children.text: na kāmairvipralabdhaḥ syānna ca duḥkhena pīḍitaḥ // Dhs_7.41 //
children.translated_text: Was not deceived by desires nor afflicted by suffering. // Dhs_7.41 //
Therefore, enough, enough with desires! Do not set your mind on them!
In all circumstances, all desires are like fire and poison. // Dhs_7.42 //
Without beginning in <s>saṃsāra</s>, the enemies are born of the mind;

children.text: ahantvāttu bhavet prītirna sā kāmaiḥ kathañcana // Dhs_7.43 //
children.translated_text: Joy would come from the destruction of the ego-sense, never from desires. // Dhs_7.43 //
Full of defilement, with bitter fruit, delight born from suffering is caused by desire;

children.text: yā tu kāmavinirmuktā sā ratiḥ pari(bhāṣitā) // Dhs_7.44 //
children.translated_text: But that delight which is freed from desire — that is called true delight. // Dhs_7.44 //

body.translated_text: The supreme destination of the <s>yogin</s>

children.text: tāṃ samāśritya gacchanti yoginaḥ paramāṃ gatim /
children.translated_text: Relying on that, <s>yogins</s> reach the supreme destination;

children.text: na tu kāmakṛtā prītirnayate padamacyutam // Dhs_7.45 //
children.translated_text: But delight born of desire does not lead to the imperishable state. // Dhs_7.45 //

body.translated_text: He censures desire-born delight

children.translated_text: Sweet at first contact, delightful — but in ripening like blazing fire;
Delight born of the fire of desire leads to hell. // Dhs_7.46 //

children.text: āpātaramyā madhurā madhye ramyā ca sarvadā /
children.translated_text: Sweet at first, delightful, and always pleasant in the middle;

children.text: śāntamante ca vimalaṃ nayate padamacyutam // Dhs_7.47 //
children.translated_text: Peaceful and pure at the end — it leads to the imperishable state. // Dhs_7.47 //
Beautiful at beginning, end, and middle, always lovely like a mother —

children.text: tāṃ vyudasya kathaṃ bālā rakṣante (kāmajāṃ ratim) // Dhs_7.48 //
children.translated_text: Having cast that aside, how do fools cling to desire-born delight? // Dhs_7.48 //

body.translated_text: Desire-born delight constantly burns

children.translated_text: Painful from the middle to the end, always surrounded by faults —

children.text: kathaṃ sā sevyate bālairyā na dṛṣṭā sukhāvahā // Dhs_7.49 //
children.translated_text: How is it indulged by fools, when it has never been seen to bring happiness? // Dhs_7.49 //
Lovely like a garland of poison, producing fire upon contact —

children.text: tathā kāmakṛtā prītiḥ pariṇāme viṣopamā // Dhs_7.50 //
children.translated_text: So too is desire-born delight, like poison in its ripening. // Dhs_7.50 //
Just as fire, when fed with offerings, does not subside from blazing,

children.text: dāhena ca prarohaḥ syāt tadvat kāmakṛtā ratiḥ // Dhs_7.51 //
children.translated_text: But rather grows from burning — so too is desire-born delight. // Dhs_7.51 //

children.text: pataṅgaḥ paśyati hyagni dāhadoṣaṃ na paśyati /
children.translated_text: The moth sees fire but does not see the fault of burning;
So too do those of uncultivated understanding see desire-born delight. // Dhs_7.52 //

children.text: yastu rāgakṛto dāhaḥ pacyate kāmināṃ sadā /
children.translated_text: But that burning caused by passion, which constantly torments the lustful,

children.text: pataṅgasadṛśaṃ dāhaṃ sarvathā nai(va) paśyati // Dhs_7.53 //
children.translated_text: They see not the burning, which is like that of the moth — not at all. // Dhs_7.53 //

body.translated_text: Through heedlessness regarding desire, a fall is certain indeed

children.text: tasmāt kāma(viṣaṃ) tyaktvā nityaṃ jīvatha he surāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, having abandoned the poison of desire, live eternally, O gods! /

children.text: bhavantu mā vṛthā janmapramādena prapātanam // Dhs_7.54 //
children.translated_text: Let there be no downfall through heedlessness in a futile birth! // Dhs_7.54 //
Those whose wholesome karma is exhausted, always deluded by desires,

children.text: taṃ hitvā narakaṃ yānti kāmamohena vañcitāḥ // Dhs_7.55 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned that, they go to hell, deceived by the delusion of desire. // Dhs_7.55 //

body.translated_text: One deluded by desire drinks the blossom of the poison-tree:

children.translated_text: Just as bees drink the blossoms of a poison-tree,

children.text: tathā viṣātmakamidaṃ sukhaṃ bhuṅkte hi mohitaḥ // Dhs_7.56 //
children.translated_text: so the deluded one enjoys this happiness that is poisonous in nature. // Dhs_7.56 //

children.text: jīveyuḥ pāmarāḥ kecit viṣaṃ pītvāpi durbhagāḥ /
children.translated_text: Some wretched fools may live even after drinking poison,

children.text: na kāmaviṣapītasya jīvitaṃ durlabhaṃ bhavet // Dhs_7.57 //
children.translated_text: but for one who has drunk the poison of desire, life becomes unattainable. // Dhs_7.57 //
Just as fire in hell burns the thoughtless one,
so the fire of desire burns the celestial beings here. // Dhs_7.58 //

body.translated_text: The fire of desire is indeed harmful:

children.translated_text: The fire in the form of the noose of scripture burns the <s>pretas</s> exceedingly.
The fire of seeking is harmful to men, burning them. // Dhs_7.59 //
Thus, one should avoid on all sides that which is like fire.
The entire world without remainder is burned — one deluded by desire. // Dhs_7.60 //

body.translated_text: A mind attached to sense-objects causes downfall into calamity:

children.translated_text: The great, fickle mind that always runs toward sense-objects —

children.text: na tyājyaṃ vyasane mūḍha yad paśyasi bhaviṣyati // Dhs_7.61 //
children.translated_text: the fool does not abandon it in calamity: see what will come of it! // Dhs_7.61 //
Guard your mind against desires — it is awakened through calamity.

children.text: vyasanaughe samutpanne tat paścāt paritapyate // Dhs_7.62 //
children.translated_text: When a flood of calamity arises, one is tormented afterward. // Dhs_7.62 //

body.translated_text: Those deluded by desire do not see even great danger:

children.translated_text: Intoxicated in vain by the pride of desire, the gods are weak by nature.

children.text: bhramanti bhramitāḥ kāmairna paśyanti mahad bhayam // Dhs_7.63 //
children.translated_text: Whirled about by desires, they do not see the great danger. // Dhs_7.63 //
Those gods who trust in desires that are harmful —
those fools awaken only later, when the reversal comes. // Dhs_7.64 //

body.translated_text: Desires are supremely deceptive:

children.translated_text: And the gods, their minds deceived, do not see it.

children.text: kṣaṇikā madhurā jātāḥ kāmāḥ paramavañcakāḥ // Dhs_7.65 //
children.translated_text: Momentary and sweet-born, desires are supremely deceptive. // Dhs_7.65 //

body.translated_text: One should not trust desire:

children.translated_text: By hundreds, by thousands, by <s>koṭis</s>, and by <s>padmas</s>,

children.text: labdhā naṣṭā punaḥ kāmā na teṣāṃ viścaset pumān // Dhs_7.66 //
children.translated_text: desires are gained and lost again — a man should not trust them. // Dhs_7.66 //

body.translated_text: One deluded by desire, like a moth, is burned by the fire of hell:

children.translated_text: From sense-objects comes severe bondage — all are causes of hell.
Therefore, having completely abandoned them, let the mind be set on what is beneficial. // Dhs_7.67 //

children.text: rāgeṇa rañjitāḥ pūrvaṃ dveṣeṇa ca tiraskṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: First colored by passion, then scorned by hatred,
and deluded by delusion — those who act unheard and unlearned. // Dhs_7.68 //
The fool is sought by those who desire pleasure; again deluded by desires,

children.text: sa pataṅgasamo mūḍhaḥ dahyate narakāgninā // Dhs_7.69 //
children.translated_text: that confused one, like a moth, is burned by the fire of hell. // Dhs_7.69 //

body.translated_text: Those subject to desire fall even from the celestial world:

children.translated_text: The fall from the celestial world on all sides is inevitable.

children.text: na jñātvā kāmavaśago syādiha kathañcana // Dhs_7.70 //
children.translated_text: Not knowing this, one subject to desire shall in no way escape. // Dhs_7.70 //

children.text: kāmena vañcitāḥ sattvāḥ kāmena ca vimohitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Beings are deceived by desire and deluded by desire.
Dragged by the noose of desire, they always fall into hell. // Dhs_7.71 //

body.translated_text: Having abandoned desire, one should set the mind on one's own welfare:

children.text: tadetad vyasanaṃ sattvāḥ svahite kriyatāṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is that calamity, O beings — let the mind be set on one's own welfare.
Those with a well-tamed mind do not suffer remorse. // Dhs_7.72 //
Those who are bitten by the poison of the mind through the force of desire always —

children.text: te mūḍhā mṛtyuvaśagāḥ kāmānalahatā narāḥ // Dhs_7.73 //
children.translated_text: those fools, subject to death, are men struck by the fire of desire. // Dhs_7.73 //
There is no satisfaction in desires for those who benefit from craving.

children.text: tṛṣṇāpi tṛptijanikā mano naiva hi tṛpyati // Dhs_7.74 //
children.translated_text: Even though craving generates satisfaction, the mind is never truly satisfied. // Dhs_7.74 //

body.translated_text: Through the lamp of knowledge, satisfaction of the senses from objects arises:

children.translated_text: There will never be satisfaction of the senses through sense-objects

children.text: yadi na jñānadīpena kṣapayiṣyanti (te narāḥ) // Dhs_7.75 //
children.translated_text: unless those people extinguish them with the lamp of knowledge. // Dhs_7.75 //

body.translated_text: Destruction through association with women is quite certain:

children.translated_text: Women, when resorted to, are garlands of a hundred thoughts.
They grow like fire fanned by the wind. // Dhs_7.76 //

body.translated_text: Those inflamed by the fire of desire never attain peace:

children.translated_text: Knowing that desire, always swift and violent, is kindled by fire,
the wise one who contemplates the truth of the <s>Buddha</s> abandons desires. // Dhs_7.77 //
Those whose minds are always deluded, always intent on sense-objects —

children.text: ramante vibudhāḥ sarve tat sarvaṃ mohaceṣṭitam // Dhs_7.78 //
children.translated_text: all the gods enjoy — all that is the activity of delusion. // Dhs_7.78 //
When resorted to by the gods, the fire of sense-objects grows.
Bound by this noose, the fire is fanned by the wind. // Dhs_7.79 //

body.translated_text: Even immortals, overpowered by passion, fall:

children.translated_text: The immortals, overpowered by passion, always intent on sense-objects,
fall from the celestial world, deceived by delusion and passion. // Dhs_7.80 //
They enjoy sense-objects there, their minds absorbed therein,

children.text: na ca vindanti yad duḥkhaṃ viprayogo bhaviṣyati // Dhs_7.81 //
children.translated_text: and they do not perceive the suffering that separation will bring. // Dhs_7.81 //

body.translated_text: The suffering born of separation is indeed most tormenting:

children.translated_text: That which was divine happiness at first, endowed with the five qualities of pleasure,
does not equal even a sixteenth part of the suffering born of separation. // Dhs_7.82 //
That destruction of desires is indeed experienced by people.

children.text: satṛṣṇasya tathā tṛptiḥ kāmebhyo naiva jāyate // Dhs_7.83 //
children.translated_text: And for one who has craving, satisfaction never arises from desires. // Dhs_7.83 //

body.translated_text: The suffering of one who pursues desires never finds peace:

children.translated_text: For one whose mind is careless, always pursuing desires,
the suffering that follows through long nights never ceases. // Dhs_7.84 //
The fool is guarded hastily; he is awakened only through calamity.

children.text: paścāttu vyasane prāpte jānīte yasya tat phalam // Dhs_7.85 //
children.translated_text: Afterward, when calamity has arrived, he knows whose fruit that is. // Dhs_7.85 //
These desires are pleasant in taste but supremely terrible.
These messengers of hell roam about, causing harm. // Dhs_7.86 //

body.translated_text: Those burned by the fire of sense-objects go to hell:

children.translated_text: That mortal who trusts in them is despised by the eye of wisdom.

children.text: viṣayāgnirabhratulyaḥ sa yāti narakaṃ naraḥ // Dhs_7.87 //
children.translated_text: The fire of sense-objects, like a cloud, takes that man to hell. // Dhs_7.87 //
Of little taste and little heart, always deceiving men,
like a <s>gandharva</s> city (mirage), desires are pleasant in taste. // Dhs_7.88 //

body.translated_text: Even gods deluded by sense-objects go to lower realms:

children.translated_text: Like the glow of a lamp, covered again and again by ash,

children.text: na ca bindatyamanaso devā viṣayamohitāḥ // Dhs_7.89 //
children.translated_text: the gods, deluded by sense-objects, do not perceive with inattentive minds. // Dhs_7.89 //
Always rushing after sense-objects, always subject to desire,

children.text: na vidanti mahad duḥkhaṃ yadavaśyaṃ bhaviṣyati // Dhs_7.90 //
children.translated_text: they do not know the great suffering that will inevitably come. // Dhs_7.90 //
In whose mind the thought arises, "Desires are delightful" —

children.text: sa paścād vyasane prāpte mūḍho 'sau vipralapyate // Dhs_7.91 //
children.translated_text: that fool, afterward when calamity arrives, laments. // Dhs_7.91 //
For one blinded by the intoxication of desire and deluded by sense-objects,
there is no eternal happiness — which is the highest of all pleasures. // Dhs_7.92 //

body.translated_text: Compared to inner spiritual happiness, sensual pleasure is most inferior:

children.text: yacca kāmasukhaṃ loke yacca tṛṣṇodbhavaṃ sukham /
children.translated_text: Whatever sensual happiness exists in the world, and whatever happiness born of craving,
this does not equal even a sixteenth part of one inner spiritual happiness. // Dhs_7.93 //

body.translated_text: One who desires never enjoys happiness:

children.text: na sukhī vartate tāvadya yasya kāmo hṛdi sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: As long as desire is established in the heart, one does not dwell in happiness.
Such a one, deserving of all suffering, runs after hells. // Dhs_7.94 //
There is no satisfaction from desires, even with a hundred enjoyments for men.

children.text: yatra saukhyaṃ na tatrāsti tṛptirviṣayasevinām // Dhs_7.95 //
children.translated_text: Where there is no happiness, there is no satisfaction for those who resort to sense-objects. // Dhs_7.95 //

children.text: sevyamānāḥ sadā kāmā vardhante ca muhurmuhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Desires, when constantly indulged, grow again and again.

children.text: te vardhitā viṣasamā bhavanti vinipātinaḥ // Dhs_7.96 //
children.translated_text: Having grown, they become like poison and cause downfall. // Dhs_7.96 //
Skilled in calamity, terrible, always causing downfall —

children.text: na ca teṣāṃ parityāgaṃ kurvanti viṣayotsavāḥ // Dhs_7.97 //
children.translated_text: yet those celebrating sense-objects do not make their abandonment. // Dhs_7.97 //
For the ocean of sight, there is no satisfaction through forms.
Likewise, with pleasant and delightful things, there is no satisfaction of taste. // Dhs_7.98 //
Even with fragrances, the nose never attains satisfaction.

children.text: sparśāḥ sammukhasaṃsparśāḥ sevyante naiva tṛpyate // Dhs_7.99 //
children.translated_text: Touches are experienced face to face, yet one is never satisfied. // Dhs_7.99 //

children.text: śabdaiḥ kāntaiḥ sumadhuraiḥ śrotrameti na tarpaṇam /
children.translated_text: With sweet, melodious sounds, the ear never reaches fullness.

children.text: mano 'pi tṛptiviśvastaṃ vardhamānaṃ na tṛpyati // Dhs_7.100 //
children.translated_text: Even the mind, trusting in satisfaction, while growing, is never satisfied. // Dhs_7.100 //

body.translated_text: The senses cause one to fall into the realms of desire:

children.translated_text: The six senses, fickle and ungoverned, turned toward pleasure,
always wander about, robbed, in the many realms of desire. // Dhs_7.101 //

children.text: na tṛptirasti devānāṃ gajānāṃ vai tṛṇairyathā /
children.translated_text: There is no satisfaction for the gods, just as elephants are never satisfied with grass.

children.text: analasya svabhāvo 'yaṃ tasya tṛptirna vidyate // Dhs_7.102 //
children.translated_text: This is the nature of fire — there is no satisfaction for it. // Dhs_7.102 //
These six fierce fires, inflamed by the wind of thought,
always wander about, robbed, in the many realms of desire. // Dhs_7.103 //

body.translated_text: Burned by the senses, they go to hell:

children.text: tairayaṃ dahyate loko na ca vindatyabuddhimān /
children.translated_text: By these the world is burned, yet the unintelligent one does not perceive it.

children.text: āsvādabhadrakā hayete narakasya ca hetavaḥ // Dhs_7.104 //
children.translated_text: These are pleasant in taste but are causes of hell. // Dhs_7.104 //

body.translated_text: One deluded by desire is cheated of happiness:

children.translated_text: Desires are the greed of sense-objects, licking like serpents.

children.text: vilocanavaro hayeṣa na ca kāmairvimohitaḥ // Dhs_7.105 //
children.translated_text: The best of sight is this one who is not deluded by desires. // Dhs_7.105 //

body.translated_text: A man subject to desire is more foolish than one without eyes:

children.translated_text: Desire follows one who pursues happiness, running after hells.

children.text: na netrahīno narake pātyate satkriyānvitaḥ // Dhs_7.106 //
children.translated_text: One without eyes, endowed with good conduct, is not cast into hell. // Dhs_7.106 //

children.text: tasmād varaṃ vicakṣuḥ syānna tu kāmavaśo naraḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is better to be without eyes than to be a man subject to desire.
The fools, incapable of being deceived, are deceived by desires that cause harm. // Dhs_7.107 //

body.translated_text: For those who pursue desires, knowledge and understanding are difficult to obtain:

children.translated_text: Not becoming disenchanted with desires, deluded by their own minds,

children.text: na jñānaṃ nāpi vijñānaṃ vidyate kāmacāriṇām // Dhs_7.108 //
children.translated_text: there is neither knowledge nor understanding for those who pursue desires. // Dhs_7.108 //

body.translated_text: Desire leads to the abode of death:

children.translated_text: Having killed the suffering born of desire, yet again subject to desire —
those desires that appear as friends, like <s>kimpāka</s> fruits,

children.text: nayanti mṛtyubhavanaṃ durgatīśca punaḥ punaḥ // Dhs_7.109 //
children.translated_text: lead to the abode of death and to lower realms again and again. // Dhs_7.109 //
Just as the water of rivers does not return,

children.text: tathā saukhyagataṃ nṛṇāṃ sarvathā na vivartate // Dhs_7.110 //
children.translated_text: so the happiness that has gone from men never returns at all. // Dhs_7.110 //
In the enjoyments of forests and groves, with many pleasures obtained,

children.text: yo na tṛpyati kāmeṣu sa naro 'dhamagāmikaḥ // Dhs_7.111 //
children.translated_text: one who is not satisfied with desires — that man goes to the lowest state. // Dhs_7.111 //
A being destroyed by heedlessness, intent on the taste of desire,

children.text: rūpeṣu rakṣyate nityaṃ pariṇāme ca vidyate // Dhs_7.112 //
children.translated_text: is always guarded by forms and is found in transformation. // Dhs_7.112 //
Those that are of the nature of dense shade, mixed with karma —

children.text: tāni caiva kathaṃ devāḥ śakṣyante kāmagocare // Dhs_7.113 //
children.translated_text: how will those gods be able in the realm of desire? // Dhs_7.113 //

body.translated_text: Desires should never be pursued:

body.text: yadi nityā bhaveyurna kāmāste syurviṣopamāḥ // Dhs_7.114 //
body.translated_text: If desires were permanent, they would not be like poison. // Dhs_7.114 //
Craving for desire is the cause of suffering:

children.text: tathāpi kāmatṛṣṇā yā na sā jāti vilakṣaṇā /
children.translated_text: Moreover, that craving for desire is not different in birth.

children.text: prāgeva nityaṃ duḥkhāya śūnyamātmānameva ca // Dhs_7.115 //
children.translated_text: It always leads to suffering, and the self itself is empty. // Dhs_7.115 //
How do the unwise guard themselves in those painful fruitions?
The foolish and dull-witted are guarded by the taste of desires.
They do not understand the danger, which is like <s>kimpāka</s> fruit. // Dhs_7.116 //
This person, bound by form, sound, and the rest, distorted by craving,
is helplessly kindled always, deluded by the fruit of bad karma. // Dhs_7.117 //
Having tasted desires that are like poison-fruit,

children.text: tṛṣṇayā tṛptamanasaḥ patanti narake punaḥ // Dhs_7.118 //
children.translated_text: men whose minds are satisfied by craving fall again into hell. // Dhs_7.118 //
Just as rain pours down and rivers grow,
so by the rain of desires, the fire of the gods grows. // Dhs_7.119 //

body.translated_text: There is no end to the happiness of desire:

children.translated_text: Even a fish born in water is seen to be afflicted by thirst.

children.text: evaṃ sukhābhivṛddhā ca na vitṛpyati devatā // Dhs_7.120 //
children.translated_text: Thus a god, though increased in happiness, is never satisfied. // Dhs_7.120 //

children.text: ākāśasya yathā nānto vidyate nāpi saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as there is no end of space, without doubt,

children.text: evaṃ kāmeṣu nāstyantaḥ kāmināṃ nāsti saṃkṣayaḥ // Dhs_7.121 //
children.translated_text: so there is no end of desires for the desirous, no exhaustion for them. // Dhs_7.121 //
For the ocean with its garlands of waves, unsatisfied by water and the rest —

children.text: na tu kāmairatṛptasya tṛptirasti kathañcana // Dhs_7.122 //
children.translated_text: but for one unsatisfied with desires, there is never any satisfaction. // Dhs_7.122 //
The foolish gods are not satisfied with unobtained sense objects;
they are not satisfied with sense objects, being devoted to yearning for pleasure. // Dhs_7.123 //

body.translated_text: Desires are for torment, not for peace

children.translated_text: When intense calamity has arrived, even while falling in many ways,

children.text: tapyate viṣaye tasmāt paraṃ kāmo na śakyate // Dhs_7.124 //
children.translated_text: one is burned by sense objects; therefore desire cannot be surpassed. // Dhs_7.124 //
Seeing these people, desires, treacherous destroyers of trust,

children.text: tyajanti vyasane prāptā vipadyante hi te narāḥ // Dhs_7.125 //
children.translated_text: abandon them when calamity arrives — for those people come to ruin. // Dhs_7.125 //
There is no happiness for the unsatisfied, and one is not satisfied by sense objects;

children.text: ye vā tṛiptikarā dṛṣṭāstān buddhvā (tu) vivarjayet // Dhs_7.126 //
children.translated_text: those seen to bring satisfaction — having understood them, one should abandon them. // Dhs_7.126 //

body.translated_text: Having abandoned sense objects, one should cultivate peace

children.translated_text: Peace is always the root of happiness; sense objects are considered unhappy;
therefore, gods who desire the happiness of peace should avoid the serpents of sense objects. // Dhs_7.127 //
Killing, bondage, disease, and the like — great danger comes from sense objects;
here in <s>saṃsāra</s>, confusion arises from sense objects alone. // Dhs_7.128 //
Unions ending in separation, by the hundreds and thousands,

children.text: jātau jātau sadā dṛṣṭāḥ saugataistattvadarśibhiḥ // Dhs_7.129 //
children.translated_text: are always seen in birth after birth by the followers of the <s>Sugata</s> (Buddha), the seers of reality. // Dhs_7.129 //

body.translated_text: The <s>saṃsāra</s> of manifold pleasures is of the nature of sense objects

children.translated_text: The <s>saṃsāra</s> of manifold pleasures indeed exists within sense objects;

children.text: viṣayaiśca bhavet sarva jātau jātau prajāyate // Dhs_7.130 //
children.translated_text: through sense objects, everything arises in birth after birth. // Dhs_7.130 //
Painful, unwanted, and unable to be endured by an undeluded mind —
yet those blinded by delusion, whose understanding is undeveloped, serve them again. // Dhs_7.131 //

body.translated_text: Those who serve the enemy of sense objects are foolish

children.translated_text: A person always avoids an enemy out of fear of deception;

children.text: viṣayāḥ śatrubhūtā hi na vaśyante kathañcana // Dhs_7.132 //
children.translated_text: sense objects, being like enemies, are never subdued in any way. // Dhs_7.132 //

children.text: kāmabaddhāḥ sadā mohabāliśā vā bhavanti te /
children.translated_text: Those bound by desires are always foolish in their delusion;

children.text: na tyajanti kathaṃ mūḍhā mohitāḥ svena karmaṇā // Dhs_7.133 //
children.translated_text: how do the deluded not abandon them — deluded by their own <s>karma</s>? // Dhs_7.133 //
Just as someone, out of fear of fire, still serves fire,
so one deluded by sense objects serves sense objects. // Dhs_7.134 //
Just as a snare tied with sinews may appear charming,
so this snare charming with sense objects is supremely cruel. // Dhs_7.135 //

body.translated_text: Sensual happiness leads to destruction

children.translated_text: Just as the taste of the <s>kiṃpāka</s> (bitter fruit) is sweet at first, of great potency,

children.text: paścād bhavati nāśāya sukhaṃ tadvadidaṃ nṛṇām // Dhs_7.136 //
children.translated_text: yet afterward leads to destruction — so too is this happiness for people. // Dhs_7.136 //
Just as a moth, maddened by delusion, reaches the flame of a lamp

children.text: patate dahyate caiva tathedaṃ sukhamiṣyate // Dhs_7.137 //
children.translated_text: and falls and is burned — so too is this happiness considered. // Dhs_7.137 //
Just as children, not knowing, through desire for the pleasure of a beautiful body,

children.text: spṛśanti jvalanaṃ tadvat sukhametad bhaviṣyati // Dhs_7.138 //
children.translated_text: touch fire — so too will this happiness be. // Dhs_7.138 //

body.translated_text: The destruction of craving alone gives rise to happiness

children.translated_text: Just as a lovely forest deer, tormented by thirst, runs toward a mirage,

children.text: na ca tṛṣṇāvighāto 'sya tadidaṃ sukhamiṣyate // Dhs_7.139 //
children.translated_text: yet there is no cessation of his thirst — so too is this happiness considered. // Dhs_7.139 //

children.text: na tṛptā na ca tṛpyanti na ca tṛptirbhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: They were not satisfied, they are not satisfied, and they will not be satisfied

children.text: viṣayaiḥ sarvadevānāṃ tasmāt kāmo na śāntaye // Dhs_7.140 //
children.translated_text: by sense objects — for all the gods; therefore desire does not lead to peace. // Dhs_7.140 //

body.translated_text: Those heedless through sense objects experience suffering

children.translated_text: Desires give happiness in the present but do not bring good in the end;
the gods, colored by sense objects, always have distracted minds. // Dhs_7.141 //
For one heedless through manifold pleasures and deceived by sense objects,

children.text: samprāpte mṛtyukāle ca na śamāyāsya vidyate // Dhs_7.142 //
children.translated_text: when the time of death arrives, there is no peace for him. // Dhs_7.142 //
Death approaches gradually, and that is evident;
for the gods, stricken by sense objects, whose minds are attached to desires. // Dhs_7.143 //

body.translated_text: Desires bring harm

children.text: jānīyādadya me devā yad duḥkhaṃ viprayogajam /
children.translated_text: If the gods know today what suffering arises from separation,

children.text: muhūrtamapi kāmeṣu na kuryāt tatra saṃsthitim // Dhs_7.144 //
children.translated_text: they would not remain even for a moment in desires. // Dhs_7.144 //

body.translated_text: Burned by the fire of passion, one is born deluded

children.translated_text: Desires are impermanent, dangerous to the self, and always cause harm;
yet time serves again those deluded by them. // Dhs_7.145 //
The gods, deluded, are constantly burned by the fire of passion;

children.text: dahyamānāḥ punastattvaṃ praśaṃsanti punaḥ punaḥ // Dhs_7.146 //
children.translated_text: while being burned, they praise that very reality again and again. // Dhs_7.146 //

body.translated_text: Deluded by sense objects, they always wander like a chariot wheel

children.text: viṣayeṣu na rakṣyante teṣāṃ duḥkhamiva sthitam /
children.translated_text: They are not protected in sense objects — suffering stands as if established for them;
this entire triple world revolves like a chariot wheel. // Dhs_7.147 //

body.translated_text: Desires are like a <s>Gandharva</s> city

children.text: sattvā avidyayā mugdhā nityaṃ duḥkhasya bhoginaḥ /
children.translated_text: Beings, deluded by ignorance, are always experiencers of suffering;
desires are declared equal to lightning and a spinning firebrand;
like a <s>Gandharva</s> city in a dream, they are deceptive. // Dhs_7.148 //

body.translated_text: One with the notion of the five aggregates remains suffering

children.translated_text: In what is impermanent, suffering, and empty, the self-possessed should not place the mind;

children.text: pañcaskandhāsuraiḥ proktaḥ śubhai riktaḥ svabhāvataḥ // Dhs_7.149 //
children.translated_text: the five <s>skandhas</s>, declared by the <s>asuras</s> to be auspicious, are empty by nature. // Dhs_7.149 //

children.text: anyathā viṣavad vijñaḥ kāmeṣu ca prasahyate /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, the wise one who endures desires as poison —

children.text: sa budhaḥ pāragaḥ śāntaḥ sattvānāmanukampakaḥ // Dhs_7.150 //
children.translated_text: he is the enlightened one, who has gone beyond, peaceful, compassionate toward beings. // Dhs_7.150 //

children.text: hitvā kleśamayaṃ pāśaṃ nirvāṇasyāntike sthitaḥ // Dhs_7.151 //
children.translated_text: Having abandoned the noose of afflictions, one stands near <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_7.151 //

body.translated_text: One directed toward <s>Nirvāṇa</s> indeed attains peace from the faults
Talk of peace is vain for one distracted by desires

children.translated_text: For one who delights in the conduct of desires, even though not prevailing in faults —
for one whose mind is distracted, how will there be peace? // Dhs_7.152 //
See how the distracted mind runs after sense objects;
one distracted from the path of the true Dharma is reborn in the hells. // Dhs_7.153 //
What use are desires, resembling lightning, for one who has failed and fallen short?
Resembling <s>kiṃpāka</s> fruit, poison, weapons, and fire — they are causes of suffering. // Dhs_7.154 //

body.translated_text: The fire of desire increases through the serving of sense objects

children.text: yathā yathā hi sevyante vardhante te tathā tathā /
children.translated_text: The more they are served, the more they increase;
they bring no satisfaction — they are the causes of burning like fire. // Dhs_7.155 //
Only by abandoning desires do people enjoy happiness
Those gods who, frightened by the fault of burning, desire happiness —
having abandoned inauspicious desires, then happiness will come. // Dhs_7.156 //

body.translated_text: Desires are fickle like strands of lightning

children.text: vañcayitvā janaṃ mūḍhaṃ śāṭī kṛtyeva bandhanam /
children.translated_text: Having deceived foolish people, as if effecting bondage with a cloth,

children.text: pratyayo netracapalaḥ kāmā vidyud guṇopamāḥ // Dhs_7.157 //
children.translated_text: these occasions, flickering to the eye — desires are like strands of lightning. // Dhs_7.157 //
Again and again, desires are served by those with the thirst of desire;

children.text: te rāgavahninā dagdhā dāhād dāhamavāpnuyāt // Dhs_7.158 //
children.translated_text: they, burned by the fire of passion, would obtain burning from burning. // Dhs_7.158 //
Most extremely deluded are those gods who are deluded by desire,

children.text: athavā ye na gacchanti yatsukhāt sukhamuttamam // Dhs_7.159 //
children.translated_text: or those who do not go from that happiness to the supreme happiness. // Dhs_7.159 //

children.text: nirvāṇagāmino nāsti vinā muktyā kutaḥ sukham? /
children.translated_text: Without liberation there is no happiness for one going to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>;

children.text: tasmāt kāmānna seveta kaṣṭaḥ kāmasamāgamaḥ // Dhs_7.160 //
children.translated_text: therefore one should not serve desires — the encounter with desire is painful. // Dhs_7.160 //
The senses of one who serves passion are not satisfied by sense objects;

children.text: atṛptau ca kutaḥ śarma sarvathā sampraveśate // Dhs_7.161 //
children.translated_text: and when there is no satisfaction, how can happiness enter in any way? // Dhs_7.161 //
One who knows the foremost from both — from <s>saṃsāra</s> and the ocean of suffering —
abandons evil desires gone to the domain of craving. // Dhs_7.162 //

body.translated_text: The arising and passing of desires should be rightly observed

children.translated_text: These mountain peaks, lovely with various trees —
dwelling upon them, one contemplates the arising and passing of desires. // Dhs_7.163 //

body.translated_text: One should accomplish what is desired through morality and faith

children.text: na kāmabandhanestṛptāḥ kāmajaṃ nidhanaṃ hi tat /
children.translated_text: Those satisfied with the bonds of desire — for that is destruction born of desire;
without morality and faith, by which what is desired is obtained, the cause of inauspiciousness arises;
this destruction born of desire is the guide to the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>. // Dhs_7.164 //

body.translated_text: Having abandoned evils, the happiness-bringing path of peace should be cultivated

children.translated_text: Where the bond free from desire is called the forest,

children.text: yatra bhāsayate pāpād yatra śāntiḥ sukhāvahā /
children.translated_text: where one shines free from evil, where peace brings happiness —

children.text: tat kevalaṃ mahājñānaṃ kathyate nidhanaṃ dhanam // Dhs_7.165 //
children.translated_text: that alone is called the great knowledge, the treasure of destruction. // Dhs_7.165 //

body.translated_text: One freed from desire and craving attains the auspicious

children.text: ye prasaktā na kāmeṣu tṛṣṇayā na pralobhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who are not attached to desires, not seduced by craving —

children.text: te śivaṃ sthānamāpannā na kāmāgnipraveśakāḥ // Dhs_7.166 //
children.translated_text: they have attained the auspicious state, not entering the fire of desire. // Dhs_7.166 //

body.translated_text: The unsatisfied perish indeed

children.text: tṛptirnāsti sadā kāmairna kāmāḥ śāntaye smṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: There is never satisfaction through desires; desires are not remembered as leading to peace;
accompanied by craving as a companion, they blaze like fire. // Dhs_7.167 //
The unsatisfied perish — people, gods, and <s>nāgas</s> alike;

children.text: te kevalaṃ praṇaṣṭā hi narakāgni pradarśakāḥ // Dhs_7.168 //
children.translated_text: they are utterly destroyed, displaying the fire of hell. // Dhs_7.168 //

body.translated_text: For one deluded by craving, death becomes the lord

children.translated_text: For one afflicted by thoughts, deceived by sense objects,

children.text: tṛṣṇayā mohitasyaiṣa mṛtyū rājā bhaviṣyati // Dhs_7.169 //
children.translated_text: deluded by craving — this death will become the king. // Dhs_7.169 //

body.translated_text: Those attached to desires do not distinguish the wholesome from the unwholesome

children.translated_text: Among those who are attached to the enjoyment of desires, the wholesome and unwholesome are not found;
all people are deluded by sense objects called desire. // Dhs_7.170 //

body.translated_text: Those who follow the power of desire are bound by sense objects alone

children.translated_text: Those gods of deluded minds are dragged by sense objects alone;

children.text: ye (tu) buddhaguṇairyuktā na te kāmavaśānugāḥ // Dhs_7.171 //
children.translated_text: but those endowed with the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> do not follow the power of desire. // Dhs_7.171 //

body.translated_text: Definition of 'the steadfast one'

children.translated_text: Among present desires, especially those with faults,

children.text: yo na muhyati saukhyeṣu sa 'dhīra' iti kathyate // Dhs_7.172 //
children.translated_text: one who is not deluded by pleasures — that one is called 'the steadfast.' // Dhs_7.172 //

body.translated_text: He describes the condition of gods who have fallen into desire

children.translated_text: Into desires resembling variegated dream-bodies, resembling a garland of flames,
equal to a <s>Gandharva</s> city — the gods have fallen. // Dhs_7.173 //
Into desires that are productive of craving and that effect destruction at the end —

children.text: kāntāreṣu viśāleṣu kāmeṣu patitāḥ surāḥ // Dhs_7.174 //
children.translated_text: into vast wildernesses — the gods have fallen. // Dhs_7.174 //
Into desires that are fleeting, split in three, resembling the rush of a river,
fickle and extremely difficult to traverse — the gods have fallen. // Dhs_7.175 //
Into desires unstable like the moon in water stirred by the wind,
in the worlds of the restless wheel — the gods have fallen. // Dhs_7.176 //
Into desires equal to the wheel of lightning-creepers and to a mirage,
essenceless like foam — the gods have fallen. // Dhs_7.177 //
Into desires equal to the core of a plantain tree, resembling an elephant's ear,
like the rush of river waves — the gods have fallen. // Dhs_7.178 //
Into desires equal to the fruit of <s>kiṃpāka</s>, of a nature resembling fire,
resembling the rays of illusion — the gods have fallen. // Dhs_7.179 //

body.translated_text: Desire should be avoided with the goad of knowledge

children.translated_text: Sense objects are warded off by the goad of knowledge by the seers of reality —
those unrestrained, fickle, intense, considered to be the cause of all misfortune. // Dhs_7.180 //

body.translated_text: Sense objects alone are the causes of falling into hell

children.translated_text: The hope for sense objects of the deluded, whose minds are carried away by intention —
this noose of death approaches, binding with the hope of life. // Dhs_7.181 //
Desires cook in hell the light-minded living being;

children.text: na ca vindanti mūḍhā ye mohena parivañcitāḥ // Dhs_7.182 //
children.translated_text: the deluded who are deceived by delusion do not perceive this. // Dhs_7.182 //
All sense objects are fickle, like a <s>Gandharva</s> city;
these, which roll toward suffering, are the five causes of hell. // Dhs_7.183 //

body.translated_text: Passion born of intention causes one to fall into hell

children.translated_text: From intention is born passion; from passion, anger arises;
a person overwhelmed by anger serves the hells. // Dhs_7.184 //

body.translated_text: Having first abandoned desire, one should strive for the attainment of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>

children.text: tasmāt kāmaṃ parityajya krodhaṃ nirvāsya paṇḍitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, having abandoned desire, having banished anger, the wise one,

children.text: mohaṃ cāpi parityajya nirvāṇābhimukho bhavet // Dhs_7.185 //
children.translated_text: having also abandoned delusion, should turn toward <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_7.185 //

body.translated_text: For those on the path to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, desire should be avoided like an enemy

children.text: śatruvad viṣayā jñeyā nirvāṇaṃ caiva mitravat /
children.translated_text: Sense objects should be known as enemies, and <s>Nirvāṇa</s> as a friend;
a person who has rested from sense objects attains <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_7.186 //

body.translated_text: One unstained by the defilements of desire attains spotless radiance

children.translated_text: Without greed, unstained by the defilements of desire, whose faults are abandoned, whose craving for speech is destroyed —

children.text: saṃkṣīṇadoṣo vimalaprakāśaḥ prayāti śāntiṃ svaphalopabhogī // Dhs_7.187 //
children.translated_text: With faults extinguished and of stainless radiance, he attains peace, enjoying his own fruits. // Dhs_7.187 //
He who has extracted himself from the mire of desires, free from fault,
always seeking the happiness of all beings —
he, stainless, freed from the unpeaceful mind,
attains the bliss of <s>nirvāṇa</s> with force. // Dhs_7.188 //

body.translated_text: One who desires happiness attains peace only by completely abandoning desires
Thus ends the seventh chapter, on Loathing Desires.
(8) Chapter on Craving (<s>Tṛṣṇā</s>)
The fire of craving is itself a hell

children.translated_text: The fire of craving, blazing for the crossing of existence, is called cold;
the fire in hell is hellish, but the fire of craving [pervades] the three realms. // Dhs_8.1 //
Comparable to the cosmic fire is this fire born in hell;
a fire full of many flames, arising from the cause of craving. // Dhs_8.2 //
Through the exhaustion of karma, sinners are freed from hell;
but those who follow the power of craving burn in the three realms. // Dhs_8.3 //
In the beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>, the fire of craving is the greatest binder;
the fire of craving is therefore hell — not the fire born in hell. // Dhs_8.4 //

body.translated_text: The fire of craving burns the body and mind

children.translated_text: The hellish fire causes supreme burning of the limbs;

children.text: śārīraṃ mānasaṃ dāhaṃ tṛṣṇāgniḥ kurute nṛṇām // Dhs_8.5 //
children.translated_text: but the fire of craving causes both physical and mental burning in humans. // Dhs_8.5 //

body.translated_text: The fire of craving is superior to ordinary fire

children.translated_text: Therefore the fire arising from the cause of craving is distinguished;
the hellish fire is unequal, but the fire of craving is remembered as far greater. // Dhs_8.6 //

body.translated_text: This fire arises in the three times

children.translated_text: Going to three places, having three causes, illuminating three kinds of karma,
arising in the three times — thus the fire of craving is to be known as supreme. // Dhs_8.7 //

body.translated_text: The fire of craving always burns everywhere

children.translated_text: The fire of desire burns in heaven; the fire of hatred burns in the animal realm;

children.text: mohāgnirdahyate pāpe tṛṣṇāgniḥ sarvadā sthitaḥ // Dhs_8.8 //
children.translated_text: the fire of delusion burns in the realm of sin; the fire of craving persists everywhere. // Dhs_8.8 //

body.translated_text: Examination of the true nature of the fire of craving

children.translated_text: With smoke-like arrows of pride and jealousy, born of intention with wealth as fuel,
the fire of greed burns the world — not the fire born of desire [alone]. // Dhs_8.9 //
The fire of craving grows only through the indulgence of sense objects

children.text: lobhāśīviṣadaṣṭā ye teṣāṃ śarma na vidyate /
children.translated_text: For those bitten by the venomous serpent of greed, there is no peace;

children.text: sevito bhāvito lobho bhūya evābhivardhate // Dhs_8.10 //
children.translated_text: greed, when served and cultivated, only grows further. // Dhs_8.10 //

body.translated_text: There is no enemy on earth equal to greed

children.translated_text: Just as fire, obtaining fuel, grows in manifold ways,
fire can be contained, but the fire of greed cannot. // Dhs_8.11 //
The world revolves like a wheel, deceived by greed;

children.text: anādinidhane loke nāsti lobhasamo ripuḥ // Dhs_8.12 //
children.translated_text: in this world without beginning or end, there is no enemy equal to greed. // Dhs_8.12 //
Deceived by greed, they enter the ocean waters;
they enter the thicket of war, dense with the clash of weapons. // Dhs_8.13 //
For the sake of greed, kings destroy one another;
brandishing fearsome swords and weapons, they fight out of thirst for wealth. // Dhs_8.14 //
Those freed from the poison of craving, free from the embers of greed,

children.text: samaloṣṭakāñcanā ye nirvāṇasyāntike hi te // Dhs_8.15 //
children.translated_text: for whom a clod of earth and gold are equal — they are near <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_8.15 //

body.translated_text: The fire of greed is the most dangerous of all

children.translated_text: He who is exceedingly unworthy is burned by the greed for wealth;
fire is not as dangerous as where the fire of greed operates. // Dhs_8.16 //

body.translated_text: Without the pacification of greed, talk of <s>nirvāṇa</s> is vain

children.translated_text: The wise one should forcefully destroy them through the effort of uprooting greed;
for one whose greed is unquenched, <s>nirvāṇa</s> stands far away. // Dhs_8.17 //

body.translated_text: One who abandons the pleasures of existence does not experience existential suffering

children.translated_text: Those people who do not welcome the delight that craves for existence —

children.text: na teṣāṃ bhavajaṃ duḥkhaṃ svapne samupavidyate // Dhs_8.18 //
children.translated_text: for them, suffering born of existence is not found even in dreams. // Dhs_8.18 //

children.text: tṛṣṇābaddhān janān mṛtyuḥ śambūka iva karṣati
children.translated_text: Death drags people bound by craving like a turtle drags [fish]
Just as a turtle drags fish caught in a net,
so death drags beings bound by craving. // Dhs_8.19 //

body.translated_text: The poison of craving never lets go anywhere

children.translated_text: Just as a deer struck by poisoned arrows — wherever it runs,

children.text: tatra tatra viṣaṃ yāti tathā tṛṣṇāviṣaṃ nṛṇām // Dhs_8.20 //
children.translated_text: the poison follows there — so too is the poison of craving for humans. // Dhs_8.20 //
Like the course of a river flowing with its current, pursuing its movement,
so it burns fools like fire burns dry kindling. // Dhs_8.21 //
Sense objects are pleasing at first encounter but like fire in their ripening;

children.text: tasmāt tṛṣṇā vimoktavyā yadi saukhyaṃ hi rocate // Dhs_8.22 //
children.translated_text: therefore craving should be released if happiness is desired. // Dhs_8.22 //
Just as fish that have swallowed a hook follow the power of death,

children.text: tathā prataptā viṣayān paridhāvanti duḥkhitāḥ // Dhs_8.23 //
children.translated_text: so too, tormented ones, chasing after sense objects, remain in suffering. // Dhs_8.23 //

body.translated_text: The fire of craving is greater even than hell

children.translated_text: Hell and its hellish [torments] are great, established by craving;
mortals who live off the wives of others fall to destruction. // Dhs_8.24 //

body.translated_text: Even a sage, impelled by craving, experiences suffering

children.translated_text: The sage, impelled by craving that arises as an affliction of the mind's activity,
born of the six senses, burns with sense objects as fuel. // Dhs_8.25 //

body.translated_text: The fire of craving burns even the gods

children.translated_text: The fire of craving burns a god; the bodily fire never does;
enveloped in happiness, delighting in happiness, they are deceived by happiness. // Dhs_8.26 //
One deceived by craving does not even perceive the fall
Those deceived by craving do not perceive the fall;
the entire <s>saṃsāra</s>, covered by craving, is full of wreaths of flame. // Dhs_8.27 //
People who have come under the power of the fire of craving go to evil destinies;
the heavenly world is surrounded on all sides by the fires of craving. // Dhs_8.28 //

body.translated_text: The fire of craving always grows

children.translated_text: The helpless one, attached, brought under the power of sensual enjoyments, is burned;

children.text: yathā yathendhanaṃ prāpya jvalanaṃ saṃpravardhate // Dhs_8.29 //
children.translated_text: just as fire grows upon obtaining fuel, // Dhs_8.29 //

children.text: tathā tathā sukhaṃ prāpya tṛṣṇāgnirvardhate nṛṇām /
children.translated_text: so too, upon obtaining happiness, the fire of craving grows in humans;
like fire on wood, it burns and blazes, transforming the person. // Dhs_8.30 //
The fire of craving burns the world and cannot be avoided;

children.text: ye viśālāṃ nadīṃ tīrṇā saṅkalpakṛtabhairavīm // Dhs_8.31 //
children.translated_text: those who have crossed the vast river, made terrible by intention — // Dhs_8.31 //

body.translated_text: One free from the noose of craving attains supreme peace

children.text: te gatāḥ paramāṃ śāntiṃ yān hi tṛṣṇā na bādhate /
children.translated_text: they have gone to supreme peace, those whom craving does not afflict;
freed from the noose of craving, free from the fault of attachment. // Dhs_8.32 //
Freed from the stain of sin, their sorrow gone — they are the wise ones;
for thousands of billions of <s>kalpas</s>, people have been deceived by craving. // Dhs_8.33 //

body.translated_text: The world, deceived by craving, serves craving itself

children.translated_text: Those who have come under the power of illusion and delusion do not abandon sense objects;
the world, deceived by craving, serves craving itself. // Dhs_8.34 //
Just as a thirsty person drinks salt water,
the creature is not satisfied by it and dries up repeatedly. // Dhs_8.35 //

body.translated_text: One should not serve craving, which brings suffering

children.translated_text: The lowest person, afflicted by craving, exerts himself only in sense objects;

children.text: tasmāt tṛṣṇāṃ na seveta sā hi tṛṣṇā durāsadā // Dhs_8.36 //
children.translated_text: therefore one should not serve craving, for that craving is difficult to overcome. // Dhs_8.36 //

body.translated_text: One subject to craving is never liberated

children.translated_text: A person subject to craving is never freed from <s>saṃsāra</s>;

children.text: anuttamāni saukhyāni bhuktvā deveṣu jantavaḥ // Dhs_8.37 //
children.translated_text: having enjoyed the highest pleasures among the gods, creatures // Dhs_8.37 //

body.translated_text: Those dragged by the noose of craving fall into hell

children.translated_text: dragged by the noose of craving, fall into hell again;
devoid of independence and good fortune, full of perpetual suffering and bitterness. // Dhs_8.38 //

body.translated_text: Through craving, satisfaction never comes

children.translated_text: One liberated from the service of craving reaches the true path;
but for one who has craving, how will there be satisfaction in sense objects? // Dhs_8.39 //
True contentment belongs to the embodied being who is free from craving, whose sorrow is gone;

children.text: evaṃ vitarkavihitāḥ pramādena ca vañcitāḥ // Dhs_8.40 //
children.translated_text: thus, those ensnared by discursive thought are deceived by heedlessness. // Dhs_8.40 //

body.translated_text: Even gods go to hell through craving

children.text: tṛṣṇayāḥ toṣitā devāḥ patanti narakaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Gods, gratified by craving, fall into hell again;

children.text: viḍambaneyaṃ paramā yatsurā narakaṃ gatāḥ // Dhs_8.41 //
children.translated_text: this is the supreme mockery — that the gods have gone to hell. // Dhs_8.41 //
Having become supreme players, they come under the power of desire;
beings with deluded minds are not alarmed by <s>saṃsāra</s>. // Dhs_8.42 //

body.translated_text: Through craving, one arrives at a state more painful than suffering

children.translated_text: Those deceived by craving go from suffering to greater suffering;

children.text: yathā yathā sukhasyāptirvardhate jālinī tathā // Dhs_8.43 //
children.translated_text: the more happiness is obtained, the more the ensnarer (craving) grows. // Dhs_8.43 //
One burned by the ensnaring fire is dragged into the hells;

children.text: satṛṣṇasya vitarkā ye teṣāṃ saṃkhyā na vidyate // Dhs_8.44 //
children.translated_text: the discursive thoughts of one who has craving are innumerable. // Dhs_8.44 //

body.translated_text: Those going toward sense objects through craving enter the very mouth of death

children.translated_text: The king of death drags away those who do not reflect with reflection;
subject to discursive thought and desire, they go toward the sense objects of craving. // Dhs_8.45 //

body.translated_text: Those intoxicated by the taste of desire, pursuing sense objects, remain in suffering

children.translated_text: Seeing one who enjoys happiness — the wise do not consider it so,
for those creatures intoxicated by the taste of desire, who seek sense objects — // Dhs_8.46 //

body.translated_text: Embodied beings are burned by craving

children.text: jālinī bādhate nityaṃ yathā badhnanti dehinaḥ /
children.translated_text: The ensnarer always afflicts and binds embodied beings;
this fivefold support — that is not what is burned by craving. // Dhs_8.47 //

body.translated_text: Those freed from craving become pure

children.translated_text: Those freed from craving, pure, do not go to the city of sin;
those of crooked intention, arising from the dust of the three faults, [do]. // Dhs_8.48 //

body.translated_text: Through craving, people fall revolving in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>

children.translated_text: Deep as the waters of heedlessness, attended upon by passion for women,
with sounds of song and music, and restless from drinking liquor — // Dhs_8.49 //
all with concealed sense objects, their minds tossed like waves,

children.text: tṛṣṇānadīṣu viṣame vahanti na ca gocare // Dhs_8.50 //
children.translated_text: they flow in the perilous rivers of craving, but not in the [right] domain. // Dhs_8.50 //

children.text: gāhante te ca sammūḍhāḥ surā rāgeṇa vañcitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those deluded gods, deceived by passion, plunge in;
born of the fuel of the three faults, driven by the wind of heedlessness. // Dhs_8.51 //

children.text: tṛṣṇānalaḥ suragaṇān dahate na ca te viduḥ /
children.translated_text: The fire of craving burns the hosts of gods, yet they do not know it;

children.text: na kṣaṇo nāpi hi lavo na muhūrta kathañcana // Dhs_8.52 //
children.translated_text: not for a moment, not for an instant, not for even a short while // Dhs_8.52 //
is there anything not experienced by gods subject to craving;
this ground of craving is the limit, nourished by the waters of discursive thought. // Dhs_8.53 //

body.translated_text: One burned by the serpent of craving comes under the power of time

children.translated_text: Wherein the helpless gods, following the power of desire, play —
with the fierce, creeping poison of craving of the mind and the rest — // Dhs_8.54 //
bitten by the five-headed [serpent], why do you lament in vain?
This vast river of craving arises from five fords. // Dhs_8.55 //
Always scattered by the magic net of craving and delusion,

children.text: tathā prapañcitā devā yathā na śubhabhāginaḥ // Dhs_8.56 //
children.translated_text: the gods are so deluded that they become non-partakers of merit. // Dhs_8.56 //

body.translated_text: The fire of craving, sprinkled with the ghee of sense objects, only grows

children.translated_text: The senses are never satisfied by desires in any way;

children.text: saṃvardhate tathā tṛṣṇā ghṛtasikto yathānalaḥ // Dhs_8.57 //
children.translated_text: craving grows just as fire grows when sprinkled with ghee. // Dhs_8.57 //

body.translated_text: Through craving, people wander in various births

children.translated_text: This ensnarer, destroyer of the world, with its manifold pleasures,
always causing people to wander in hell, the hungry-ghost realm, and the animal realm. // Dhs_8.58 //

body.translated_text: One free from craving, freed from bondage, attains the supreme destination

children.translated_text: Foolish people cling to the swing between death and rebirth;
but those of good conduct and free from craving have gone to the supreme destination. // Dhs_8.59 //
The wise, freed from bondage, their sorrow and anguish gone,

children.text: sukhaṃ prāpnuvanti nityaṃ ye na tṛṣṇāvaśānugāḥ /
children.translated_text: always attain happiness — those who do not follow the power of craving;

children.text: janmaduḥkhamayaiḥ pāśairna te vidhyanti sūrayaḥ // Dhs_8.60 //
children.translated_text: the wise are not pierced by the fetters made of the suffering of birth. // Dhs_8.60 //

body.translated_text: The release from craving leads to knowledge

children.translated_text: Those whose minds in all states are directed toward knowledge,

children.text: animitte mano yeṣāṃ visṛṣṭā ye ca tṛṣṇayā /
children.translated_text: whose minds are set on the signless, who have released craving —

children.text: te vītamalakāntārāḥ pāraṃ prāptāḥ sukhodayam // Dhs_8.61 //
children.translated_text: they, having passed through the wilderness of defilements, have reached the far shore, the arising of happiness. // Dhs_8.61 //

body.translated_text: Those intoxicated by craving and delusion wander from existence to existence

children.translated_text: Those who are intoxicated by craving and delusion, and likewise by the pleasures of delight —

children.text: mohitāste devagaṇā bhramiṣyanti bhave bhave // Dhs_8.62 //
children.translated_text: those deluded hosts of gods will wander from existence to existence. // Dhs_8.62 //

body.translated_text: Craving torments day and night

children.translated_text: Those whose conduct is base, who steal others' minds,
Who are full of ignorance, who always long for burning —

children.text: na rātrau na divā teṣāṃ hṛdayaṃ suprasīdati // Dhs_8.63 //
children.translated_text: Neither by night nor by day does their heart find peace. // Dhs_8.63 //

body.translated_text: Those overcome by greed become like smoldering chaff-fire

children.translated_text: For those whose minds are overcome by greed, who long for others' wealth —
Those who are like smoldering chaff-fire should not be trusted by nature. // Dhs_8.64 //

body.translated_text: Fear is proper from the serpent of sense-object-fuel

children.text: bibheti hi naraḥ sarvaḥ sarpādiva viṣendhanāt /
children.translated_text: For every person fears a serpent whose fuel is poison;
Those people are greatly overcome by greed and sense objects. // Dhs_8.65 //

body.translated_text: Those enslaved by craving obtain various births

children.text: te mṛtā narakaṃ yānti pretayoniṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Having died, they go to hell and likewise to the realm of hungry ghosts;
And even when freed from that, from hell, they face fire again. // Dhs_8.66 //

body.translated_text: Those who long are always sharers of suffering

children.translated_text: For five hundred births, these remain as those who long;
Pale, with wretched faces, always sharers of suffering —
All humans become so, their minds overcome by greed. // Dhs_8.67 //

body.translated_text: Those endowed with discernment attain the supreme destination

children.translated_text: Those who have abandoned greed, who always long for knowledge,

children.text: buddhimantaḥ sadā santaḥ te gatāḥ paramāṃ gatim /
children.translated_text: Wise, always peaceful — they have gone to the supreme destination;
People whose hearts are set on <s>nirvāṇa</s>, free from greed and delusion always. // Dhs_8.68 //

body.translated_text: The downfall of one drawn by greed

children.translated_text: For one bitten by the poisonous serpent of greed, downfall is certainly established;

children.text: kriyamāṇo dhruvaṃ loko vardhate sa muhurmuhuḥ // Dhs_8.69 //
children.translated_text: The world being so acted upon, that greed grows again and again. // Dhs_8.69 //
Just as fire increases when given dry fuel,
So beings delighting in craving for wealth are devoted to the acquisition of wealth. // Dhs_8.70 //
When the time of death has arisen, they helplessly abandon their wealth;

children.text: yacca tatsambhavaṃ yogāt tat sarva na vinaśyati // Dhs_8.71 //
children.translated_text: But whatever arises from that connection through effort — all that does not perish. // Dhs_8.71 //

body.translated_text: The greedy soul goes to terrible hell

children.text: tena vittena lobhātmā nīyate narakaṃ bhṛśam /
children.translated_text: By that wealth the greedy soul is led forcefully to hell;

children.text: anyaistadbhujyate vittaṃ sa tu pāpena lipyate // Dhs_8.72 //
children.translated_text: Others enjoy that wealth, but he is stained by sin. // Dhs_8.72 //
They go to terrible hell and are burned by remorse;

children.text: anartho hyartharūpeṇa sukharūpeṇa vā sukham // Dhs_8.73 //
children.translated_text: For misfortune appears in the guise of fortune, and suffering in the guise of happiness. // Dhs_8.73 //

body.translated_text: The wise one should abandon greed

children.translated_text: This greed dwells in the heart disguised as a friend, though it is an enemy;

children.text: na lobhaṃ saṃśrayet prājño lobhāgnirdahyate sadā // Dhs_8.74 //
children.translated_text: The wise one should not resort to greed — one is always burned by the fire of greed. // Dhs_8.74 //

body.translated_text: Those burned by greed become hell-bound

children.translated_text: Beings severely burned by it afterward become hell-bound;
For these possessions are common to all the world, devoid of happiness. // Dhs_8.75 //

body.translated_text: Liberation from the fear of craving alone is beneficial

children.translated_text: For whose sake is sin committed by the dull-witted?
For one liberated from the fear of craving, who is without expectations in every way, // Dhs_8.76 //
For the steadfast wise one free from longing, the state is eternally established;

children.text: sampattau dhābate loko vipattau nāvabudhyate // Dhs_8.77 //
children.translated_text: The world rushes in prosperity, but does not understand in adversity. // Dhs_8.77 //

body.translated_text: Prosperity ends in decline

children.text: vipadantā hi sampattiḥ kṣayāntaṃ divasaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: For prosperity ends in misfortune, like a day ending in decline;

children.text: yathā tiṣṭhati sampattiḥ vipattiḥ pāpikā tathā // Dhs_8.78 //
children.translated_text: As long as prosperity lasts, so too does wicked misfortune. // Dhs_8.78 //

body.translated_text: Through enjoyment of desires, even gods go to hell

children.translated_text: One unsatisfied with desires is burned by craving;

children.text: yasyeṣṭāḥ sampado nityaṃ sukhaṃ cābhimataṃ sadā // Dhs_8.79 //
children.translated_text: One whose cherished fortunes and desired happiness are ever present — // Dhs_8.79 //

children.text: jani nāśayate tāsāṃ tṛṣṇā naṣṭā sukhāvahā /
children.translated_text: Birth destroys those; craving, once destroyed, would bring happiness;

children.text: te devā narakaṃ yānti kāmabhogaistathārpitāḥ // Dhs_8.80 //
children.translated_text: Those gods, thus devoted to the enjoyment of desires, go to hell. // Dhs_8.80 //
All that is the doing of fire — thus declare the <s>Tathāgatas</s>;

children.text: manuṣyā yacca narakaṃ prayā(nti) śataśastathā // Dhs_8.81 //
children.translated_text: And humans too go to hell by the hundreds likewise. // Dhs_8.81 //

body.translated_text: The greatly deluded do not perceive the passing of life

children.translated_text: The conduct of that broad-eyed woman — the wise know it well;

children.text: vimohitā na vindanti tvaritaṃ svalpajīvitam // Dhs_8.82 //
children.translated_text: Yet the deluded do not perceive the swiftly passing, brief life. // Dhs_8.82 //

body.translated_text: Through craving, meritorious deeds perish

children.text: sukṛtāni ca naśyanti tṛṣṇā naiva vinaśyati /
children.translated_text: Meritorious deeds perish, but craving never perishes;

children.text: bhave bhave gatā satvāḥ na vindanti śubhāśubham // Dhs_8.83 //
children.translated_text: Beings, passing from existence to existence, do not perceive the wholesome and unwholesome. // Dhs_8.83 //
That which the gods enjoy is indeed the fruit of the wholesome;
Likewise the unhappiness born of downfall is seen as the fruit of the unwholesome. // Dhs_8.84 //

body.translated_text: Those who have abandoned the wholesome and unwholesome are free from old age and death

children.translated_text: Those who have abandoned both wholesome and unwholesome, free from the fault of attachment —

children.text: te gatāḥ paramaṃ sthānaṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitam // Dhs_8.85 //
children.translated_text: They have gone to the supreme state, free from old age and death. // Dhs_8.85 //

body.translated_text: A person surrounded by the river of craving understands nothing

children.translated_text: That wheel of existence with five spokes, preceded by the hub of craving,
Surrounded by the river of passion — the world does not understand. // Dhs_8.86 //
One should know that the vortex of faults is deeper, filled with the crocodiles of mental fabrication;

children.text: tṛṣṇānadī viśāleyaṃ na ca loko 'vabudhyate // Dhs_8.87 //
children.translated_text: This broad river of craving — the world does not understand. // Dhs_8.87 //

body.translated_text: Craving is a deceiver in all three times

children.translated_text: In the three times craving is a deceiver, always producing ignorance;

children.text: na tasyāṃ viśvased dhīmān saṃsārabandhanā hi sā // Dhs_8.88 //
children.translated_text: The wise one should not trust in it, for it is the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s>. // Dhs_8.88 //

body.translated_text: Craving is the bondage of the world

children.translated_text: It appears as a friend in time, but cuts like an enemy;

children.text: na tasyāṃ viśvaset prājñaḥ sā hi lokasya bandhanam // Dhs_8.89 //
children.translated_text: The wise one should not trust in it, for it is the bondage of the world. // Dhs_8.89 //
One can cut bonds of iron or wood,

children.text: na tṛṣṇābandhanaṃ chettuṃ nityaṃ kāmagaveṣibhiḥ // Dhs_8.90 //
children.translated_text: But the bond of craving cannot be cut by those who always seek desires. // Dhs_8.90 //
One who desires the breaking of this bond, who desires imperishable happiness —
Let him be freed from craving, endowed with wisdom and wealth-making. // Dhs_8.91 //

body.translated_text: The tree of craving should be cut down by knowledge

children.translated_text: The light of knowledge is the light of happiness; craving's darkness is declared as suffering;
Therefore the wise one, taking his stand in the light, dispels the darkness. // Dhs_8.92 //
With the sharp sword of knowledge, one cuts down the tree of craving;
That person, whose tree is cut down, attains unsurpassed happiness. // Dhs_8.93 //
For this river, abundant in faults, agitated with waterfalls —
The wise one, without abandoning the fault-guides, does not free himself from existence. // Dhs_8.94 //

body.translated_text: Relying on the boat of wisdom, one crosses to the far shore of the river of craving

children.translated_text: The river of craving, flowing in three streams, with the difficult vortex of heedlessness —
Relying on the boat of wisdom, they cross to the far shore, free from affliction. // Dhs_8.95 //
The great umbrella of great desire, by which fools are brought;
Therefore this great desire should be slain by you with the eye of knowledge. // Dhs_8.96 //

body.translated_text: Great desire itself is a wound in the heart

children.translated_text: The severe wound of great desire arises in the heart of one in whom it dwells;

children.text: na rātrau na divā tasya sukhaṃ bhavati lobhinaḥ // Dhs_8.97 //
children.translated_text: Neither by night nor by day does the greedy one have happiness. // Dhs_8.97 //
Not born in mere mental fabrication, stirred by the wind of craving,
The fire of the affliction of great desire burns the hearts of people. // Dhs_8.98 //

body.translated_text: Through greed, people act to their own detriment

children.translated_text: A person whose mind is enveloped by greed, of frivolous mind,
Abandons even the essentials of life through craving for wealth. // Dhs_8.99 //

children.text: pāpāni hi ca karmāṇi kurvanti puruṣāḥ kṣitau /
children.translated_text: People on earth commit sinful deeds;

children.text: dhanalābhena tat sarva pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ // Dhs_8.100 //
children.translated_text: All that is due to the acquisition of wealth — so the sages declare. // Dhs_8.100 //

children.text: ye sāhasaṃ na kurvanti viśanti jvalanaṃ ca yat /
children.translated_text: Those violent deeds they would not commit, and the fire they enter —
All that, through the fault of greed, they do to their own detriment. // Dhs_8.101 //
Weapons, storms, and various sufferings everywhere —

children.text: viśanti (vai) narā mūḍhā lobhastatra hi kāraṇam // Dhs_8.102 //
children.translated_text: Deluded people enter into them; greed is the cause therein. // Dhs_8.102 //
The fire of the mind dwelling in the heart always belongs to those of great desire;
Through having few desires, peace of heart comes to the one who gains. // Dhs_8.103 //
Just as fire increases with fuel alone,

children.text: tathā vahvicchatāṃ nṛṇāṃ dhanairvṛddhiḥ prajāyate // Dhs_8.104 //
children.translated_text: So for people of great desire, increase comes through wealth. // Dhs_8.104 //

body.translated_text: Having few desires is itself happiness

children.translated_text: Kings, though satisfied with wealth in <s>koṭis</s>, have gone to destruction;

children.text: yāsyanti cānye nidhanaṃ tasmādalpecchatā sukham // Dhs_8.105 //
children.translated_text: Others too will go to destruction — therefore having few desires is happiness. // Dhs_8.105 //

body.translated_text: Only one free from craving attains happiness

children.translated_text: Great desire is suffering for people — such is the characteristic of happiness and suffering;
It should be abandoned by every effort — thus say the examiners;

children.text: eṣa panthāḥ śivaḥ śreṣṭho yena tṛṣṇā vaśīkṛtā // Dhs_8.106 //
children.translated_text: This is the auspicious, supreme path — the one by which craving is mastered. // Dhs_8.106 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the eighth chapter on Craving (<s>Tṛṣṇāvarga</s>). //
(9) Chapter on Revulsion from Women (<s>Strījugupsāvarga</s>)
Women are the root of misfortune

children.translated_text: Women are the root of sin and of the destruction of wealth in every way;

children.text: svahite ye na niratāḥ kutasteṣāṃ bhavet sukham // Dhs_9.1 //
children.translated_text: For those who are not devoted to their own welfare, how can there be happiness? // Dhs_9.1 //
Devoted to harmful deeds, full of deceit and jealousy, women
Are established for the destruction of both worlds for men. // Dhs_9.2 //
Always skilled in passion, always speaking sweet words,

children.text: anyacca hṛdaye tāsāṃ kathayantyanyadeva vā // Dhs_9.3 //
children.translated_text: But in their hearts they have one thing, and they speak quite another. // Dhs_9.3 //
Sweet at first contact, subtle, with diamond hearts in their ripening —
They do not remember kindness through gratitude, being of frivolous mind. // Dhs_9.4 //

body.translated_text: Women have hearts of lightning-nature, supremely fickle

children.translated_text: Having destroyed a hundred beloved ones, they remember a single disliked one;
Women, with hearts of lightning-nature, are the grounds of sin. // Dhs_9.5 //

body.translated_text: Demonstration that women are agents of destruction

children.translated_text: Men of crooked minds, because of women, desire destruction;

children.text: strīvināśo vināśo drāgiha loke paratra ca // Dhs_9.6 //
children.translated_text: The destruction caused by women is swift destruction — in this world and the next. // Dhs_9.6 //

body.translated_text: The very sight of women burns like fire

children.translated_text: Thus all sense objects — but the sight of a woman is the foremost one here;
Overpowering all sense objects, the blazing fire of women is great. // Dhs_9.7 //

body.translated_text: Examination of revulsion from women, preceded by demonstration of women's faults

children.translated_text: From contact too comes separation, from remembrance and from speaking too;
This fire arising from the burning of women is an inner conflagration. // Dhs_9.8 //

children.text: rāgeṇa saha jāyante nityaṃ vai dāruṇāḥ striyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Women are born fierce together with passion always,

children.text: dānena saha jāyante yathā loke hutāśanāḥ // Dhs_9.9 //
children.translated_text: Just as fires in the world are born together with their offering. // Dhs_9.9 //

children.text: na bhavet tādṛśo dāho yo 'yaṃ vahnisamudbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: There would not be such burning as that which arises from fire,

children.text: yādṛśaḥ strīmado hyasti dehināṃ hṛdayodbhavaḥ // Dhs_9.10 //
children.translated_text: As the intoxication of women that arises in the hearts of embodied beings. // Dhs_9.10 //
For the destruction of the entire world, for the annihilation of all dharmas —

children.text: hetavo narakasyaitāḥ striyaḥ proktā maharṣibhiḥ // Dhs_9.11 //
children.translated_text: Women have been declared by the great sages as causes of hell. // Dhs_9.11 //
Sweet and forgiving in speech, but like poison in their hearts;

children.text: anavasthitasauhārdā nāsāṃ kaścit priyo naraḥ // Dhs_9.12 //
children.translated_text: Of unsteady affection — no man is truly dear to them. // Dhs_9.12 //
In one moment one is dear to them, in another moment one is disliked;
Of unsteady affection, fickle, and momentary in nature. // Dhs_9.13 //
Skilled in the arts of deception, always devoted to their own purposes,
Always with minds set on union, always devoted to pride. // Dhs_9.14 //
For gods and for humans — <s>piśācas</s>, serpents, and <s>rākṣasas</s>

children.text: na bandhabhūtā yādṛśyaḥ striyaḥ kālaviṣopamāḥ // Dhs_9.15 //
children.translated_text: Are not such bonds as women, who are like the poison of time. // Dhs_9.15 //

children.text: nopakāraṃ smarantyetā na kuśalaṃ nāpi vikramam /
children.translated_text: They remember neither kindness, nor skill, nor valor;
Of unsteady mind, women are like the force of the wind. // Dhs_9.16 //

children.text: bhavanti sampado yatra rakṣyante yatra yoṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Where there are fortunes, there women are guarded;

children.text: vyasaneṣu viraktāstu tyajanti puruṣaṃ dhruvam // Dhs_9.17 //
children.translated_text: But in times of calamity, indifferent, they certainly abandon a man. // Dhs_9.17 //

children.text: yaṃ yaṃ gacchanti puruṣaṃ rakṣyante tatra yoṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: To whatever man they go, there women are guarded;

children.text: śīghraṃ śīghraṃ naraṃ hyetāstyajanti puruṣaṃ sthitam // Dhs_9.18 //
children.translated_text: But these women quickly, very quickly abandon the man who remains. // Dhs_9.18 //

children.text: yathā hi bhramarī puṣpaṃ śuṣkaṃ tyajati sarvadā /
children.translated_text: Just as a bee always abandons a dried flower,

children.text: tathā vittena rahitaṃ puruṣaṃ tyajati priyā // Dhs_9.19 //
children.translated_text: So a beloved woman abandons a man deprived of wealth. // Dhs_9.19 //
With sword-like hearts, cruel, fickle, veiled in darkness —

children.text: striyaḥ puruṣanāśāya jātāḥ kenāpi hetunā // Dhs_9.20 //
children.translated_text: Women are born for the destruction of men, through some cause or other. // Dhs_9.20 //

children.text: devānāṃ bandhanaṃ nāma yathā strībandhanaṃ matam /
children.translated_text: What is called the bondage of the gods — that is considered the bondage of women. /
Those bound by the bondage of women fall into hell again. // Dhs_9.21 //

children.text: etadagraṃ hi rāgāṇāṃ yo rāgaḥ strīsamudbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is the foremost of passions — the passion born of women;
the fire afterwards burns one whose mind is consumed by passion for women. // Dhs_9.22 //
Even deeds that are evident, a man struck down by passions

children.text: na vetti mūḍhahṛdayaḥ strīrāgeṇa vimohitaḥ // Dhs_9.23 //
children.translated_text: does not recognize, deluded in heart, bewildered by passion for women. // Dhs_9.23 //

children.text: viśvāsya viṣaye puruṣaṃ bad dhvā priyamanekaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having inspired trust in a man through sense objects, having bound the beloved one in many ways,
they abandon him at the loss of wealth, just as snakes shed their skin. // Dhs_9.24 //
Women maintained by all means, guarded in every way —

children.text: na śakyāḥ svavaśīkarttuṃ striyaḥ paramadāruṇāḥ // Dhs_9.25 //
children.translated_text: supremely terrible women cannot be brought under one's own control. // Dhs_9.25 //
Of these women of every nature, of fickle minds —

children.text: na yāyājjātu viśvāsaṃ pumān dhīreṇa cetasā // Dhs_9.26 //
children.translated_text: a wise-minded man should never place trust in them. // Dhs_9.26 //
Those mortals who are governed by women, always seeking desires —
their last sight will be in the heavenly world. // Dhs_9.27 //
Deceived on all sides by the five-fold music,

children.text: vindanti vyasane duḥkhaṃ yadavaśyaṃ bhaviṣyati // Dhs_9.28 //
children.translated_text: they find suffering in calamity, which will inevitably come. // Dhs_9.28 //
These are those fickle women for whom you have developed passion;

children.text: tā bhavantaṃ parityajya punaranyaṃ tato gatāḥ // Dhs_9.29 //
children.translated_text: they, having abandoned you, have gone elsewhere. // Dhs_9.29 //
For the nature of those women is twofold, their constant companion:

children.text: bhūyo 'bhiyanti puruṣaṃ vyasaneṣu tyajanti ca // Dhs_9.30 //
children.translated_text: they approach a man again and again, and abandon him in adversities. // Dhs_9.30 //
Like deer, they bewitch a man deluded by passion;

children.text: paścāt (tu) vyasane prāpte tyajanti laghucetasaḥ // Dhs_9.31 //
children.translated_text: but afterward, when adversity strikes, those of fickle minds abandon him. // Dhs_9.31 //

children.text: nopakāraṃ na satkāraṃ na priyāṇi na santatim /
children.translated_text: Neither kindness, nor respect, nor affection, nor lineage
do fierce women remember when adversity is at hand. // Dhs_9.32 //

children.text: mlānaṃ puṣpaṃ yathā tyaktvā bhramaro 'nyatra dhāvati /
children.translated_text: Just as a bee, leaving a withered flower, hastens elsewhere,

children.text: tathā hi vyasane prāpte tyajanti khalu yoṣitaḥ // Dhs_9.33 //
children.translated_text: so too do women abandon one when adversity strikes. // Dhs_9.33 //
Without regard for friendship, fickle, and fond of conflict —

children.text: bhavanti yoṣitaḥ sarvā viṣamiśraṃ yathā madhu // Dhs_9.34 //
children.translated_text: all women are like honey mixed with poison. // Dhs_9.34 //
They bewitch men through desires and especially through words;

children.text: na teṣāṃ viśvaseddhīmān puruṣo dhīramānasaḥ // Dhs_9.35 //
children.translated_text: a wise man of firm mind should not trust in them. // Dhs_9.35 //

children.text: ābhirvimohitāḥ kiṃ vā raṃjitāḥ puruṣāḥ svataḥ /
children.translated_text: Are men bewitched by them, or captivated of their own accord?

children.text: na kurvanti hitaṃ vākyaṃ yathā muṣṇikagāmikam // Dhs_9.36 //
children.translated_text: They do not follow beneficial words, like those who walk the thieves' path. // Dhs_9.36 //
<s>Devas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, humans, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>piśācas</s> (goblins), <s>nāgas</s> (serpents), and <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons) —
women, being like conjurers, deceive them all especially. // Dhs_9.37 //
