This is the foremost of all snares — that which is made of women, firm;

children.text: anena baddhāḥ puruṣā bhramanti bhavacārake // Dhs_9.38 //
children.translated_text: bound by this, men wander in the course of existence. // Dhs_9.38 //

children.text: na kaścit pāśapāśo 'yaṃ hṛtpāśo yoṣitaḥ param /
children.translated_text: No noose or snare equals this — the heart's noose of women is supreme;
bound by the bonds of the heart's noose, men are deluded by suffering. // Dhs_9.39 //
A noose can be burned and cut, but the noose made of women cannot be burned;
it follows one who goes to hells, the realm of <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), and animal births. // Dhs_9.40 //

children.text: mūrtimān badhyate kāyaḥ pāśena mahatā tathā /
children.translated_text: The material body is bound by a great noose,

children.text: amūrtigaṃ cittamidaṃ strīpāśena tu badhyate // Dhs_9.41 //
children.translated_text: but this immaterial mind is bound by the noose of women. // Dhs_9.41 //
No other noose is seen by which women bind —
the bondage made of women, great and immeasurable, should be recognized. // Dhs_9.42 //
By this noose, charming at first sight but always leading to suffering,

children.text: pāśena baddhāḥ puruṣā na mucyante bhavārṇavāt // Dhs_9.43 //
children.translated_text: men, once bound, are not freed from the ocean of existence. // Dhs_9.43 //

children.text: ṣaḍindriyāṇi badhnāti pāśo yaḥ strīmayo mahān /
children.translated_text: The great noose made of women binds the six sense faculties;

children.text: pāśastu kāyamevaikaṃ kaścit badhnāti vā na vā // Dhs_9.44 //
children.translated_text: whereas some other noose may or may not bind the body alone. // Dhs_9.44 //

children.text: bandhanaṃ na dṛḍhaṃ hīdaṃ mokṣavārya ṣaḍāyasam /
children.translated_text: This bondage of iron and the six senses is not firm, and can be liberated;
but for a man of dull understanding whose mind is attached to enjoyment — // Dhs_9.45 //
bound in those extensive fields of action by the mechanism of sinews,
equipped with a sharp blood-stained sword, he has come here for the purpose of death. // Dhs_9.46 //

body.translated_text: The evil qualities of women:

children.translated_text: In deception, fraud, and trickery, they are especially impetuous;
fickle among those of wandering minds, bewildered in every moment and limb — // Dhs_9.47 //
confused by bewildering words and by the sounds of ornaments,

children.text: haranti puruṣaṃ kṣipraṃ vañcanākuśalāḥ striyaḥ // Dhs_9.48 //
children.translated_text: women, skilled in deception, quickly carry men away. // Dhs_9.48 //

children.text: nānāvidheṣu puṣpeṣu yathā carati ṣaṭ padaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a bee moves among various flowers,
so do these fickle women among various mortals. // Dhs_9.49 //
Just as a bee, having drunk the nectar, goes to another flower,

children.text: tathā puruṣamāpīyaḥ prayānti rabhasaṃ striyaḥ // Dhs_9.50 //
children.translated_text: so women, having drained a man, depart swiftly. // Dhs_9.50 //
Skilled in extracting wealth, always angry and formidable,

children.text: vañcayitvā naraṃ śīghramanyatra saṃprayānti tāḥ // Dhs_9.51 //
children.translated_text: having quickly deceived a man, they proceed elsewhere. // Dhs_9.51 //
With weapons of deceitful illusion, comparable to <s>kālakūṭa</s> poison,
women, destroyers of men, are established in cunning. // Dhs_9.52 //

children.text: vāyvākāśānalā yadvan na śaktā grathituṃ naraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as wind, sky, and fire cannot be bound by men,
so women cannot be guarded by men through a hundred means. // Dhs_9.53 //
Women are the supreme cause of misfortune, disease, death,

children.text: hetubhūtāḥ paraṃ nāryo mokṣacaryābadhasya ca // Dhs_9.54 //
children.translated_text: and of evil deeds — and of obstruction to the practice of liberation. // Dhs_9.54 //
That in the world people of many kinds fall into wicked evil deeds —

children.text: (patanti) manujā loke tatra hetuḥ parastriyaḥ // Dhs_9.55 //
children.translated_text: the cause of that is other men's women. // Dhs_9.55 //
Neither in childhood, nor in youth, nor in old age does it subside —

children.text: cāpalyaṃ sahajaṃ strīṇāṃ bhāskarasya yathā prabhā // Dhs_9.56 //
children.translated_text: the fickleness innate in women, like the radiance of the sun. // Dhs_9.56 //
Their friendship is impermanent, like sparks of blazing flames;

children.text: vairañca śāśvataṃ tāsāmaśmanāṃ ca yathā vraṇaiḥ // Dhs_9.57 //
children.translated_text: and their enmity is eternal, like wounds from stones. // Dhs_9.57 //
They lose passion for one bereft of wealth and become attached to one with wealth;
women exist only so long as there is wealth — when wealth is gone, where are the women? // Dhs_9.58 //
Neither through service, nor through gifts, nor through various kindnesses

children.text: svīkarttuṃ na striyaḥ śakyāḥ jvalanopamacetasaḥ // Dhs_9.59 //
children.translated_text: can women be won over — they whose minds are like blazing fire. // Dhs_9.59 //
The more a man is accommodating and does their bidding,

children.text: tathā tathā striyastasya vañcanākuśalāḥ param // Dhs_9.60 //
children.translated_text: the more those women are supremely skilled at deceiving him. // Dhs_9.60 //

children.text: puṣpacchatro yathā sarpo bhasmacchatro yathā nalaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a serpent is hidden beneath flowers, just as embers are hidden beneath ashes,

children.text: rūpacchannaṃ tathā cittamāsāṃ bhavati yoṣitām // Dhs_9.61 //
children.translated_text: so the minds of these women are hidden beneath their beauty. // Dhs_9.61 //

children.text: viṣavṛkṣe yathā puṣpaṃ dṛṣṭiramyaṃ na śāntaye /
children.translated_text: Just as a flower on a poison-tree is pleasing to the eye but not for peace,
women, being equal to poison-trees, should be completely avoided. // Dhs_9.62 //
A man who desires the sight of women and is devoted to sense objects

children.text: naro na sukhabhogāya (haya) smilloke na cāpare // Dhs_9.63 //
children.translated_text: finds no happiness in this world or the next. // Dhs_9.63 //

children.text: nāgninā na ca śastreṇa na balena na jantubhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Neither by fire, nor by weapons, nor by force, nor by creatures —

children.text: strīmayaṃ bandhanaṃ hetuḥ śakyate na durāsadam // Dhs_9.64 //
children.translated_text: the bondage made of women, the irresistible cause, cannot be overcome. // Dhs_9.64 //
This net of faults, this thread made of women, moves upon the earth;
a wise man who is free from women is honored in this world. // Dhs_9.65 //
Just as spirits do not help people in producing their own <s>karma</s>,

children.text: tathā striyo hi rakṣanti viṣamārtha tyajanti ca // Dhs_9.66 //
children.translated_text: so women protect in favorable times but abandon in adversity. // Dhs_9.66 //
Seeing a god whose wealth and fortune have departed, abandoned by his own <s>karma</s>,

children.text: devaṃ samīkṣya capalāḥ striyo naiva prabhāvikāḥ // Dhs_9.67 //
children.translated_text: fickle women have no power at all. // Dhs_9.67 //

body.translated_text: The happiness from women is momentary and fragile:

children.translated_text: This happiness that has been attained and established is momentary and fragile;

children.text: catvāryetāni duḥkhāni sevitāni nṛbhiḥ sadā // Dhs_9.68 //
children.translated_text: these four sufferings are always indulged in by people. // Dhs_9.68 //

body.translated_text: Women are like poison and fire:

children.translated_text: Therefore those should be avoided, for they are like poison and fire;

children.text: yaḥ kaściccapalo janturyaśca doṣodbhavaḥ sadā // Dhs_9.69 //
children.translated_text: whatever creature is fickle, that is always the source of faults. // Dhs_9.69 //
Therefore, women who have entered in are fond of their purpose;

children.text: na sūryastamaso heturnāgniḥ śītasya kāraṇam // Dhs_9.70 //
children.translated_text: the sun is not the cause of darkness, nor is fire the cause of cold. // Dhs_9.70 //
Not even a little friendship endures in the hearts of women;

children.text: yathā sthirā bhūmiriyaṃ yathā vāyuḥ sadā calaḥ // Dhs_9.71 //
children.translated_text: just as this earth is stable, just as wind is always moving — // Dhs_9.71 //

body.translated_text: Women remember only faults:

children.text: tathā strīṇāṃ kṛtaṃ nāsti doṣamayyaḥ sadā smṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: thus women have no gratitude; they are always remembered as full of faults;

children.text: ciraprayatnāḥ puruṣaiḥ lobhitā bahuśaḥ striyaḥ // Dhs_9.72 //
children.translated_text: women, courted by men with long effort and many times, // Dhs_9.72 //

children.text: tyajanti vyasane prāpte śuṣkaṃ sara ivāśugāḥ /
children.translated_text: abandon them when adversity strikes, like swift-flowing streams leaving a dry lake.

children.text: nordhvagāḥ sarito dṛṣṭā nāśmano gatiriṣyate // Dhs_9.73 //
children.translated_text: Rivers flowing upward have not been seen, nor is the movement of stones desired; // Dhs_9.73 //

children.text: girīṇāṃ gamanaṃ nāsti strīṇāṃ naivāsti sauhṛdam /
children.translated_text: mountains do not move, and women have no friendship;

children.text: vapukarti sadā nṛṇāṃ dharmārthayaśasāṃ tathā // Dhs_9.74 //
children.translated_text: they always destroy the appearance, Dharma, purpose, and fame of men. // Dhs_9.74 //
They are the source of the net of misfortune and the origin of faults;

children.text: bhaved vajramayī mṛdvī tyajed (rātrau yathā) ravim // Dhs_9.75 //
children.translated_text: one would be as hard as diamond yet soft — one would abandon the sun at night. // Dhs_9.75 //
A woman does not abandon what cannot be accomplished, especially expectation of birth;
neither through courteous conduct, gifts, sweet words, nor entreaties // Dhs_9.76 //
can women be won over — they whose minds are like blazing fire;

children.text: sukheṣu samatāṃ yānti vyasaneṣu tyajanti ca // Dhs_9.77 //
children.translated_text: they share equality in happiness but abandon in adversities. // Dhs_9.77 //
Having forgotten kindnesses, they remember a single fault;
having enjoyed much happiness in forests, groves, and mountains — // Dhs_9.78 //

body.translated_text: Women are the bondage of the world:

children.text: saṃprāpte vyasane tīvre striya paribhavanti hi /
children.translated_text: when severe adversity strikes, women treat one with contempt;
women are the bondage of the world, ever increasing in deception. // Dhs_9.79 //
The lowest of all downfalls, and the manifold abode of faults —
they bring the whole world under their control through craving, for the world's destruction. // Dhs_9.80 //
This bondage of women, great and unbearable, is thus established —

children.text: yadidaṃ bandhanaṃ loke kāmarāgamayaṃ mahat // Dhs_9.81 //
children.translated_text: this great bondage in the world, made of desire and passion. // Dhs_9.81 //

body.translated_text: Avoidance of women alone is conducive to welfare:

children.translated_text: Through other effort and investigation, this is ascertained;
those women bring under control through the arrows of desire in many ways. // Dhs_9.82 //

children.text: svalpaiḥ parājitaṃ kṛtvā kāmasya vaśagāḥ striyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having defeated with trifles, women are subject to desire;
those of lightning-like fickle minds, whose domains are passion, jealousy, and deceit — // Dhs_9.83 //
those whose sources are greed and pride should not be trusted in any way;
sharp as weapons and fire, whose nature is the noose of desire — // Dhs_9.84 //
dangerous as the fall into one's own abyss, whose minds are deep as equal —
whose minds are given to harming others through deception and conjury — // Dhs_9.85 //
whose nature is equal to untimely death, thunderbolt, fire, and <s>kālakūṭa</s> poison —
delighting in the manifold accumulation of faults — // Dhs_9.86 //

children.text: yadi śīlalavaḥ kaścit strīṇāṃ manasi vartate /
children.translated_text: if even a trace of virtue exists in the minds of women,

children.text: cireṇa dahate vahniḥ sa spṛṣṭāḥ pavaneritaḥ // Dhs_9.87 //
children.translated_text: the fire, touched and fanned by the wind, burns it up in time. // Dhs_9.87 //
The fire burns merely at the sight of women, just upon being aroused;

children.text: tasmāt striyo vivarjyāḥ syuḥ yadicchet sukhamuttamam // Dhs_9.88 //
children.translated_text: therefore, women should be avoided if one desires supreme happiness. // Dhs_9.88 //

children.text: etat sarva paraṃ loke nārīṇāṃ varjanaṃ sadā /
children.translated_text: This is the supreme thing in the world — always avoiding women;
one who desires prosperity for oneself should guard against the cause of the net of chance. // Dhs_9.89 //

children.text: ya icchati nivṛttiṃ tu sa naraḥ strīṃ vivarjayet /
children.translated_text: A man who desires renunciation should avoid women;
one attached to pleasure, and likewise to wealth, lazy, fickle, and dishonest, // Dhs_9.90 //

children.text: pāpasevī sumṛṣṭāśī naro bhadraṃ na paśyati /
children.translated_text: a man given to evil, eating dainty food — such a person does not see what is good.

children.text: udyukto vīryavān dhīro dhārmikaḥ strīṃ vivarjayet /
children.translated_text: Vigorous, endowed with energy, firm, righteous — one should avoid women;

children.text: dakṣo hetuphalaśraddho naraḥ kalyāṇavān bhavet // Dhs_9.91 //
children.translated_text: a man who has faith in causes and their fruits, skilled and endowed with virtue, will be blessed. // Dhs_9.91 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the ninth chapter, the chapter on abhorrence of women. //
(10) The Chapter on Abhorrence of Intoxicants.
Demonstration of the description of the defects of drinking intoxicants:

children.text: madyapānaṃ na seveta madyaṃ hi viṣamuttamam /
children.translated_text: One should not indulge in drinking intoxicants, for intoxicants are the supreme poison;
wholesome dharmas perish through the indulgence in drinking intoxicants. // Dhs_10.1 //

children.text: yaḥ sevate sadā madyaṃ tasya buddhirasaṃsthitā /
children.translated_text: One who always indulges in intoxicants — that one's understanding is unsteady;

children.text: balabuddhī na dharmo 'sti tasmānmadyaṃ vivarjayet // Dhs_10.2 //
children.translated_text: for one of enfeebled understanding there is no Dharma; therefore one should avoid intoxicants. // Dhs_10.2 //
The supreme of all destructions — intoxicants have been declared by the wise. /

children.text: tasmānmadyaṃ na seveta (madyaṃ) nāśayate naram // Dhs_10.3 //
children.translated_text: Therefore one should not resort to intoxicants — intoxicants destroy a person. // Dhs_10.3 //
Undesirable, evil dharmas arise from the consumption of intoxicants.
Therefore, one should abandon the drinking of intoxicants like poison. // Dhs_10.4 //
Causing loss of wealth, producing evil, supremely causing indolence —

children.text: madyapānasthitā doṣāḥ tasmāt tat parivarjayet // Dhs_10.5 //
children.translated_text: these are the faults established in drinking intoxicants; therefore one should abandon it. // Dhs_10.5 //
Intoxicants inflame passion, and likewise anger.
They are the supreme inflamer of delusion — therefore one should abandon intoxicants. // Dhs_10.6 //
Intoxicants are the root of misfortune, of laughter, and of hell,
the cause of the destruction of all faculties — purposeless indeed. // Dhs_10.7 //
Of excessive elation, of grief, and of fear,
of verbal faults, of extreme recklessness, and of harshness — it is the abode. // Dhs_10.8 //
Men whose minds are overthrown by intoxicants are equal to animals.

children.text: kāryākārya na vindanti tasmānmadyaṃ vivarjayet // Dhs_10.9 //
children.translated_text: They do not know what should and should not be done — therefore one should abandon intoxicants. // Dhs_10.9 //

children.text: madyakṣipto hi puruṣo jīvannapi mṛto mataḥ /
children.translated_text: A man overthrown by intoxicants, though living, is considered dead.

children.text: ya icchejjīvitaṃ saukhyaṃ sa madyaṃ varjayet sadā // Dhs_10.10 //
children.translated_text: One who desires a happy life should always avoid intoxicants. // Dhs_10.10 //

body.translated_text: Intoxicants are the abode of all faults:

children.translated_text: Intoxicants are the abode of all faults, always producing all misfortune,
a stairway to all evils, a great dwelling of darkness. // Dhs_10.11 //

body.translated_text: Through intoxicants one falls to the <s>preta</s>-world or to hell:

children.text: madyena narakaṃ yānti pretalokaṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Through intoxicants men go to hell and likewise to the <s>preta</s>-world.

children.text: tiryakṣu yānti puruṣā madyadoṣeṇa vañcitāḥ // Dhs_10.12 //
children.translated_text: Men go to animal realms, deceived by the fault of intoxicants. // Dhs_10.12 //
Intoxicants are more poisonous than poison, more hellish than hell.

children.text: vyādhīnāṃ ca paraṃ vyādhirmadyamuktaṃ manīṣibhiḥ // Dhs_10.13 //
children.translated_text: The supreme disease of all diseases — so intoxicants are called by the wise. // Dhs_10.13 //

body.translated_text: Demonstration of the harm of intoxicants:

children.translated_text: For the destruction of intellect and faculties, for the loss of the jewel of dharma,
that supreme excess — intoxicants — is for the obstruction of celibacy. // Dhs_10.14 //
Through intoxicants, even kings with the eye of scripture come to disgrace.

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ prākṛtā martyā madyapānavilambitāḥ // Dhs_10.15 //
children.translated_text: How much more ordinary mortals, delayed by the drinking of intoxicants! // Dhs_10.15 //

body.translated_text: The destructive nature of intoxicants:

children.translated_text: An axe to all dharmas, supremely destructive of modesty —
intoxicants, when resorted to by mortals, are destined for destruction. // Dhs_10.16 //

body.translated_text: Through intoxicants, one becomes void of discrimination between knowledge and ignorance:

children.text: na jñānaṃ nāpi vijñānaṃ na kāryāṇi na ca kriyām /
children.translated_text: Neither knowledge, nor understanding, nor duties, nor actions

children.text: jānīte puruṣaḥ sarva madyena hṛtacetasā // Dhs_10.17 //
children.translated_text: does a person know at all, with his mind stolen by intoxicants. // Dhs_10.17 //

body.translated_text: The consumption of intoxicants brings about torment:

children.translated_text: Suddenly a being is scorched, suddenly tormented,
and suddenly becomes sinful — one who resorts to intoxicants. // Dhs_10.18 //

body.translated_text: Intoxicants generate bewilderment of intellect:

children.translated_text: Generating bewilderment of intellect, destroying both worlds,
a fire to the dharmas of liberation — intoxicants alone are established as such. // Dhs_10.19 //

body.translated_text: Intoxicants are like <s>kimpāka</s> fruit:

children.text: abhyāse madhuraṃ madyaṃ vipāke paramaṃ kaṭu /
children.translated_text: Sweet in practice, intoxicants are supremely bitter in maturation.
More poisonous than <s>kimpāka</s> fruit — so intoxicants are called by the discerning. // Dhs_10.20 //

body.translated_text: Intoxicants are a means to hell:

children.text: na madye viśvaseddhīmān naraṃ vakṣyati māmiti /
children.translated_text: A wise man should not trust intoxicants, saying "It will carry me."
Cool to the touch, hot in maturation, intoxicants lead to hell. // Dhs_10.21 //

children.text: sampattau vyasanaṃ madyaṃ devānāṃ tu viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: Intoxicants are a calamity in prosperity, especially for the gods.

children.text: yathā yathā sukhā prītistannāśe vyasanaṃ tathā // Dhs_10.22 //
children.translated_text: The greater the happy pleasure, the greater the calamity at its destruction. // Dhs_10.22 //
Beings, mad with the intoxication of drinking, subject to delusion,
drink this beverage that is the very embodiment of delusion, through thirst for taste. // Dhs_10.23 //

children.text: madyaṃ mohamayaṃ pāna pītvā kālena coditāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having drunk this beverage made of delusion, impelled by time,

children.text: nākāt pratyakṣanarakaṃ tasmāt madyaṃ na saṃspṛśet // Dhs_10.24 //
children.translated_text: they go from heaven directly to hell — therefore one should not touch intoxicants. // Dhs_10.24 //

body.translated_text: From seeing and drinking, intoxicants generate delusion:

children.text: darśanāt sparśanāt pānāta madyaṃ mohayate naram /
children.translated_text: By seeing, by touching, and by drinking, intoxicants delude a person.

children.text: tasmāt sa madyapānaṃ ca dūrataḥ parivarjayet // Dhs_10.25 //
children.translated_text: Therefore one should avoid intoxicant-drinking from afar. // Dhs_10.25 //
From seeing arises greed; from touching arises the sensation of fragrance.
From fragrance arises desire for taste, and from tasting arises the lowest mentality. // Dhs_10.26 //

body.translated_text: Even the wise fall through the consumption of intoxicants:

children.translated_text: The wise call it not merely one among the worst deposits,
but for the negation of name and form — thus intoxicants are resorted to. // Dhs_10.27 //

body.translated_text: An indication of the fruit of drinking intoxicants:

children.translated_text: It makes the speech wander, the brain, and the eyes are mere noise.
Confused, of deranged judgment, the fool understands nothing. // Dhs_10.28 //

body.translated_text: Even women mock the drinker of intoxicants:

children.translated_text: Even women mock this man fallen on the ground,

children.text: niśceṣṭaṃ kāṣṭhasadṛśaṃ niścalaṃ patitaṃ bhuvi // Dhs_10.29 //
children.translated_text: motionless like a log, immobile, fallen on the ground. // Dhs_10.29 //

body.translated_text: Drinking intoxicants is worse than death:

children.translated_text: For a respectable person, drinking intoxicants is proclaimed as death.
Worse than <s>hālāhala</s> poison, worse than imprisonment — that is it. // Dhs_10.30 //

body.translated_text: Abstaining from intoxicants brings about welfare:

children.translated_text: Thirty-six dangers are established from the drinking of intoxicants.

children.text: tasmādādīnavo jñeyaḥ sa hi tad varjayet sadā // Dhs_10.31 //
children.translated_text: Therefore the danger should be known, and one should always avoid it. // Dhs_10.31 //

body.translated_text: Drinking intoxicants defiles even a learned being:

children.translated_text: For one well-born and learned, it is a great defilement.
It quickly makes a being who is like a <s>kāśa</s> flower into one of little worth. // Dhs_10.32 //

body.translated_text: One burned by the fire of sense-objects becomes devoid of knowing right from wrong:

children.translated_text: For those sunk in heedlessness, delighted by sense-objects,
additionally by intoxicant-drinking, which bewilders the mind, // Dhs_10.33 //
for one burned by the fire of sense-objects, not knowing what should and should not be done,
how much more so for the drinking of intoxicants obtained in forests and groves! // Dhs_10.34 //

body.translated_text: The drinking of intoxicants leads to delusion and sin:

children.translated_text: Intoxicants are pleasant in taste but terrible in maturation.
The sinful fruit of maturation leads to birth in hells. // Dhs_10.35 //

children.text: pītaṃ janayate mohaṃ mohāt pāpeṣu rakṣyate /
children.translated_text: When drunk, it generates delusion; from delusion one is guarded in sins.
The fool with an impassioned heart runs after hells. // Dhs_10.36 //

body.translated_text: The drinking of intoxicants accomplishes the lowest state:

children.translated_text: It generates elation at first, but the utmost wretchedness in maturation.

children.text: tṛṭ chedaṃ kurute cāsau paścāddāhaṃ sudāruṇam // Dhs_10.37 //
children.translated_text: It creates thirst and cutting, and afterward a supremely terrible burning. // Dhs_10.37 //
It destroys the intellect first, afterward it destroys happiness.

children.text: tasmāt sa puruṣo dhīro yo madyaṃ nānusevate // Dhs_10.38 //
children.translated_text: Therefore that man is wise who does not resort to intoxicants. // Dhs_10.38 //

body.translated_text: Those who resort to intoxicants become like birds:

children.translated_text: Men who resort to intoxicants go like birds.
Equally generating delusion, intoxicants are the great poison of delusion. // Dhs_10.39 //

body.translated_text: Those deluded reach lower realms:

children.translated_text: Those who have seen intoxicants as poison — they have seen the supreme state.

children.text: yaistu tad virasaṃ pītaṃ pītaṃ tāmra (ka) lohitam // Dhs_10.40 //
children.translated_text: But those who have drunk it tasteless — they have drunk what is coppery and red. // Dhs_10.40 //
One who, deluded, performs irreversible deeds,
possessed by the drinking of intoxicants — he goes to lower realms in the end. // Dhs_10.41 //

body.translated_text: Destruction comes to those who resort to drinking intoxicants:

children.translated_text: All sins in one — the resorting to intoxicant-drinking,
for it destroys the mind-root and restraint. // Dhs_10.42 //

body.translated_text: The drinker of intoxicants becomes one whose dharma is lost:

children.text: naikāṅgitā hi cittasya na dharmāṇāṃ vicāraṇā /
children.translated_text: There is neither one-pointedness of mind nor reflection on dharmas
for a monk who is devoted to evil through the consumption of intoxicants. // Dhs_10.43 //
One whose mind is overthrown by intoxicants is a killer of the wholesome.

children.text: naṣṭadharmasya sattvasya nāyaṃ loko na cāparaḥ // Dhs_10.44 //
children.translated_text: For a being whose dharma is lost, there is neither this world nor the next. // Dhs_10.44 //

children.text: īryyāpathaṃ na jānāti na kālaṃ nāpi deśanām /
children.translated_text: He does not know proper conduct, nor time, nor instruction.

children.text: saddharmato viruddhaśca tucchaṃ kimapi bhāṣate // Dhs_10.45 //
children.translated_text: Opposed to the true dharma, he speaks something trivial. // Dhs_10.45 //

children.text: svayaṃ tāvanna jānāti kimidaṃ kathyate mayā /
children.translated_text: He himself does not know: "What is this I am saying?"
How will he discern verbal harshness and ugliness in another? // Dhs_10.46 //
He comes to disgrace before the world and declines from dharma.
Destruction is seen by men from resorting to the fire of intoxicants. // Dhs_10.47 //

body.translated_text: Drinking intoxicants produces contempt:

children.translated_text: In the past there is destruction, in the present among friends,
in the future among the despised — intoxicants destroy in all three times. // Dhs_10.48 //

body.translated_text: Intoxicants are indeed a corrupter of dharma:

children.translated_text: For the destruction of name and form, for the destruction of the minds of embodied beings,
generating arising faults — intoxicants corrupt dharma. // Dhs_10.49 //

body.translated_text: Abstaining from intoxicants is for dharma; drinking leads not to death:

children.translated_text: Composed, righteous in dharma, those who abstain from intoxicants —

children.text: te yānti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yatra mṛtyurna vidyate // Dhs_10.50 //
children.translated_text: they go to the supreme state where death does not exist. // Dhs_10.50 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the tenth chapter on the abhorrence of intoxicants. //
Now the second declaration:
(Mind, speech, and action, and evil bondage,
hell, <s>preta</s>-realm, animal realm, hunger, and indolence — these are the ten.) //
(11) Chapter on Mind:
The mind operates like a king:

children.translated_text: Unfathomable, uneven, intense, pervading all beings, great —

children.text: cittaṃ sarvasya jagato rājavat sampravartate // Dhs_11.1 //
children.translated_text: the mind of the entire world operates like a king. // Dhs_11.1 //

body.translated_text: Those who master the mind and know it attain the supreme destination:

children.translated_text: Invisible now is the fear, the karma, the unstable ones destined for hell.

children.text: ye cittadhāriṇastajjñāste gatāḥ paramāṃ gatim // Dhs_11.2 //
children.translated_text: Those who master the mind and know it — they have gone to the supreme destination. // Dhs_11.2 //
This leads to exaltation, this leads to lower realms.
This very thing, pure from beginning to end, attains <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_11.3 //

children.text: manaḥ pūrvamaṅgamā dharmā manaḥ śreṣṭhā manomayāḥ /
children.translated_text: Dharmas are preceded by mind, mind is their chief, they are mind-made.

children.text: manasā suprasannena bhāṣate vā karoti vā // Dhs_11.4 //
children.translated_text: With a well-clarified mind, one speaks or acts. // Dhs_11.4 //

body.translated_text: For one subject to the mind, the mind always follows:

children.text: yo na cittasya vaśagaścittaṃ tasyāntagaṃ sadā /
children.translated_text: One who is not subject to the mind — the mind always reaches its end for him.

children.text: sa nirṇāśayati kleśān tamaḥ sūryodayo yathā // Dhs_11.5 //
children.translated_text: He destroys the defilements, as sunrise destroys darkness. // Dhs_11.5 //

body.translated_text: Those burned by the mind go to destruction:

children.text: cittaṃ śatruḥ paraṃ śatrurna śatruraparaḥ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: The mind is the supreme enemy — no other enemy is known.

children.text: cittadagdhāḥ sadā sattvāḥ kāladagdhā yathā jaḍāḥ // Dhs_11.6 //
children.translated_text: Beings burned by the mind are always like the dull burned by time. // Dhs_11.6 //
One who has come under the power of the mind, foolish, deluded, with uncontrolled senses —

children.text: tena duḥkhe samo nāsti nirvāṇaṃ tasya dūrataḥ // Dhs_11.7 //
children.translated_text: there is no one equal to him in suffering; <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is far from him. // Dhs_11.7 //

body.translated_text: One subject to the mind reaches hell:

children.translated_text: No other enemy can be averted — the mind does not hide.
This binds a person in the dominion of king <s>Yama</s>. // Dhs_11.8 //

children.text: viṣayeṣu ratā nityaṃ na sa dharmaḥ kathañcana /
children.translated_text: One always delighting in sense-objects — that is in no way dharma.
Confused on the path of the true dharma, one is led to great hell. // Dhs_11.9 //
The mind, supreme and difficult to tame, is the ultimate fire of evil ones.

children.text: durdāntaṃ śīghragantṛ ca narakaṃ nayate dhruvam // Dhs_11.10 //
children.translated_text: Untamed and swift-going, it surely leads to hell. // Dhs_11.10 //

children.text: ye cittasya vaśaṃ yātā yātāste narakaṃ purā /
children.translated_text: Those who have gone under the power of the mind — they have gone to hell before.

children.text: yaistu tad vāryate śīghraṃ na te duḥkhānugāminaḥ // Dhs_11.11 //
children.translated_text: But those who quickly restrain it — they are not followers of suffering. // Dhs_11.11 //

body.translated_text: Happiness and suffering arise in accordance with the mind:

children.translated_text: As the mind of men is, so is the result.
For the doer of good, wholesome; for the doer of evil, evil. // Dhs_11.12 //

children.text: cittāyattaṃ bhavet karma karmāyattaṃ mano bhavet /
children.translated_text: Karma depends on the mind; the mind depends on karma.
Arising from mind and karma, <s>saṃsāra</s> is proclaimed. // Dhs_11.13 //

children.text: duṣṭena cetasā karma yaḥ karoti pumāniha /
children.translated_text: Whatever karma a man performs here with a corrupt mind,

children.text: pacyate narake tena jālinyā sa viḍambitaḥ // Dhs_11.14 //
children.translated_text: he is cooked in hell by that, mocked by a net. // Dhs_11.14 //

body.translated_text: Mind-karma is <s>saṃsāra</s> thus:

children.translated_text: Evil depends on the mind — <s>saṃsāra</s> is proclaimed.
This arises from the condition of mind, born from cause and condition. // Dhs_11.15 //
Beings deceived by the mind, having come under the power of evil,
go to hell from evil, from the great fear of the chain of causes. // Dhs_11.16 //

children.text: na bhavet cittavaśago 'pi tu dharmavaśo bhavet
children.translated_text: One should not be subject to the mind but rather subject to dharma:

children.text: na gacchet cittavaśatāṃ gacched dharmavaśe sadā /
children.translated_text: One should not go under the power of the mind; one should always go under the power of dharma.

children.text: dharmacārī sukhī nityaṃ pāpacārī na śarmabhāk // Dhs_11.17 //
children.translated_text: One who practices the Dharma is always happy; one who practices evil is not a partaker of happiness. // Dhs_11.17 //

body.translated_text: All fruit depends on the mind

children.text: cittāyattā kriyā sarvā cittāyattaṃ phalaṃ smṛtam /
children.translated_text: All action depends on the mind; all fruit is said to depend on the mind;

children.text: vicittaṃ hi phalaṃ cittaṃ tathā phalamadhismṛtam // Dhs_11.18 //
children.translated_text: the mind produces variegated fruit, and thus the fruit is remembered. // Dhs_11.18 //
Everything is conceived by the mind; the world follows the arising of the mind;

children.text: na hi tad vidyate sthānaṃ yanna cittavaśānugam // Dhs_11.19 //
children.translated_text: there is no place that does not follow the power of the mind. // Dhs_11.19 //

body.translated_text: The wholesome is a means to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>

children.translated_text: The root of both liberation and bondage is considered the supreme cause;
by the wholesome, a being is freed; by the unwholesome, one is quickly bound. // Dhs_11.20 //
Those subject to the mind never attain <s>Nirvāṇa</s>
Beings, deluded by the net, have come under the power of the mind;

children.text: nirvāṇaṃ nāpi gacchanti jātyandhā iva satpatham // Dhs_11.21 //
children.translated_text: they do not attain <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, like the blind-born not finding the good path. // Dhs_11.21 //

children.text: pañcendriyāṇi jitavān pāpaṃ bhuṅkte na karhicit /
children.translated_text: One who has conquered the five senses never tastes evil;

children.text: ekacittaṃ tathā karma kurute vividhe bhave // Dhs_11.22 //
children.translated_text: with a single-pointed mind, one performs <s>karma</s> in various existences. // Dhs_11.22 //
Just as the mind, brilliant with five colors, is praised as a spectacle,

children.text: pañcendriyavicitraṃ hi tathā karma bhave bhavet // Dhs_11.23 //
children.translated_text: so <s>karma</s>, variegated with the five senses, manifests in existence after existence. // Dhs_11.23 //

body.translated_text: The mind as creator becomes manifold

children.translated_text: A person, having the mind as creator, becomes manifold through the visible;

children.text: cittaṃ cittakaraṃ śūnyaṃ sarvathā naiva dṛśyate // Dhs_11.24 //
children.translated_text: the mind, the maker of the mind, is empty — it is never seen in any way. // Dhs_11.24 //

body.translated_text: The mind performs both beautiful and ugly <s>karma</s>

children.translated_text: Just as both beautiful and ugly paintings are made on a wall,

children.text: śobhanāśobhanaṃ karma tathā cittaṃ karoti hi // Dhs_11.25 //
children.translated_text: so the mind indeed performs both beautiful and ugly <s>karma</s>. // Dhs_11.25 //

body.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> follows the mind

children.text: divārātrau yathā cittaṃ sthitaṃ bhavati citragam /
children.translated_text: Day and night, just as the mind abides moving toward the variegated,

children.text: divārātrau tathā karma bhave samanuvartate // Dhs_11.26 //
children.translated_text: day and night, <s>karma</s> likewise follows in existence. // Dhs_11.26 //
People who have not performed wholesome <s>karma</s>, following the movement of the mind,
fall helplessly into evil, deceived by the enemy of the mind. // Dhs_11.27 //
This mind, the maker of <s>karma</s>, wherever it is employed,

children.text: caracittena mahatā taccittaṃ ca karotyayam // Dhs_11.28 //
children.translated_text: with its great restless mind, it performs that <s>karma</s>. // Dhs_11.28 //
By the distinction of transformation, wherever it is directed,

children.text: preṣyante tatra cittena tridhā tu gaticāriṇaḥ // Dhs_11.29 //
children.translated_text: beings traversing the three destinies are dispatched there by the mind. // Dhs_11.29 //

body.translated_text: Taming the mind brings happiness

children.translated_text: All actions of beings proceed under the mind's control;

children.text: tasmāccittaṃ sadā dāntaṃ nayate padamacyutam // Dhs_11.30 //
children.translated_text: therefore a mind always tamed leads to the imperishable state. // Dhs_11.30 //
Of the mind, unbearable, fickle, falling wherever it goes —

children.text: cittasya damanaṃ sādhu cittaṃ dāntaṃ sukhāvaham // Dhs_11.31 //
children.translated_text: the taming of the mind is good; a tamed mind brings happiness. // Dhs_11.31 //

children.text: yena cittaṃ sadā dāntaṃ tena doṣāḥ sadā jitāḥ /
children.translated_text: By one whose mind is always tamed, faults are always conquered;

children.text: jitadoṣasya dhīrasya duḥkhaṃ naiva prapadyate // Dhs_11.32 //
children.translated_text: for the steadfast one whose faults are conquered, suffering never approaches. // Dhs_11.32 //

body.translated_text: The fickle activity of the mind itself is suffering

children.text: yacca svakaṃ bhaved duḥkhaṃ yacca duḥkhaṃ paratra ca /
children.translated_text: Whatever suffering is one's own, and whatever suffering exists elsewhere —
all that is the fickle activity of the unbearable mind. // Dhs_11.33 //

body.translated_text: The mind alone is the lord of all

children.translated_text: Of gods, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>nāgas</s>, of <s>piśācas</s>, serpent-demons, and <s>rākṣasas</s> —

children.text: prabhurekaḥ paraṃ cittaṃ rājā(hi)tribhavasya tat // Dhs_11.34 //
children.translated_text: the mind is the sole supreme lord; it is the king of the three existences. // Dhs_11.34 //

body.translated_text: One whose mind wanders experiences suffering

children.translated_text: The mind leads one to the gods; the mind leads one to the human realm;

children.text: cittaṃ nayatyapāye(ṣu) cittaṃ bhrāmayati prajāḥ // Dhs_11.35 //
children.translated_text: the mind leads one to the lower realms; the mind causes beings to wander. // Dhs_11.35 //
For one whose mind has wandered, who is lost, deluded by sense objects,
burned by craving — the most extreme suffering stands established. // Dhs_11.36 //

body.translated_text: From taming the mind, the experience of happiness arises

children.translated_text: Ever wandering alone, ever deluded, unbearable, of great power,
ever tearing apart, ever visible, fickle, swift-moving — // Dhs_11.37 //

children.text: evaṃ vidhaṃ hi ye cittaṃ damayanti manīṣiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: those wise ones who tame such a mind —

children.text: te mārabandhanātītāḥ pāraṃ prāptāḥ sukhodayam // Dhs_11.38 //
children.translated_text: they have passed beyond the bonds of <s>Māra</s> and reached the far shore, the arising of happiness. // Dhs_11.38 //

body.translated_text: The fickle mind is fashioned for hell

children.translated_text: Crooked with intentions, fierce, unfathomable, and fickle —
the mind, abiding in darkness, though bright, is fashioned for hell. // Dhs_11.39 //

body.translated_text: One freed from faults attains the imperishable state

children.translated_text: That very mind, freed from faults, not following the power of sense objects,
unstained by evil dharmas, leads to the imperishable state. // Dhs_11.40 //

body.translated_text: A pure mind engages in pure action

children.text: hetupratyayajaṃ cittaṃ yogavāhi paraṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: The mind, born from causes and conditions, is the supreme bearer of yoga;
through the power of transformation, it quickly engages accordingly. // Dhs_11.41 //

body.translated_text: When not under the mind's control, <s>karma</s> becomes unstable

children.text: ekaṃ karoti karmāṇi vividhāni calaṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: Alone, it performs various actions, and it is unstable;

children.text: ekānekaṃ caraṃ sūkṣmaṃ kṣaṇādūrdhva na tiṣṭhati // Dhs_11.42 //
children.translated_text: moving as one or many, subtle — it does not remain beyond a moment. // Dhs_11.42 //

body.translated_text: Demonstration of the illusion-like nature of <s>saṃsāra</s>

children.translated_text: Always difficult to understand, always without a body —

children.text: ko 'sau nayati lokāntamatha kena ca gacchati // Dhs_11.43 //
children.translated_text: who is that which leads to the world's end, and by what does it go? // Dhs_11.43 //
And having gone, where does the maker of bodily <s>karma</s> abide?

children.text: dṛśyāni tasya karmāṇi sañcayo na ca dṛśyate // Dhs_11.44 //
children.translated_text: Its actions are visible, but its accumulation is not visible. // Dhs_11.44 //

children.text: damanaṃ duṣkaraṃ tasya yasya bhūtirna vidyate /
children.translated_text: Difficult is the taming of that whose nature is not found;

children.text: sarvasattvagataṃ ghoraṃ laghukāri ca cākṣuṣam // Dhs_11.45 //
children.translated_text: terrible, pervading all beings, quick to act, and visible. // Dhs_11.45 //
Worse than evil is seen — this is like illusion;
more meritorious than merit is seen — one who has resorted to the right path. // Dhs_11.46 //

body.translated_text: Establishing the illusion-like nature

children.text: na gatirjñāyate tasya gamanaṃ naiva dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Its destination is not known; its going is never seen;

children.text: nīyate ca kṣataṃ sarva jātyuttarasamāni ca // Dhs_11.47 //
children.translated_text: yet all that is wounded is carried away — things equal to successive births. // Dhs_11.47 //

children.text: śastreṇa chidyate nedaṃ jvalanena ca dahayate /
children.translated_text: It is not cut by a weapon nor burned by fire;

children.text: chidyate dahyate caiva janaḥ sarvamacakṣuṣā // Dhs_11.48 //
children.translated_text: yet people, entirely blind, are cut and burned by it. // Dhs_11.48 //

children.text: dṛḍhaṃ yat karmarajjvādi naraṃ badhnāti duḥkhitam /
children.translated_text: The strong rope of <s>karma</s> and the like binds a person in suffering;

children.text: jātyantarasahastrāṇi nayate na ca dṛśyate // Dhs_11.49 //
children.translated_text: it carries one through thousands of successive births and is never seen. // Dhs_11.49 //

body.translated_text: A tamed mind alone brings happiness

children.text: muhūrtena śubhaṃ bhūtaṃ muhūrtenāśubhaṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: In a moment it becomes wholesome; in a moment it becomes unwholesome;
fashioned by the wholesome and unwholesome, the tamed mind brings happiness. // Dhs_11.50 //
Excessively greedy for sense objects produced through the six doors,

children.text: cittaṃ nayati lokāntaṃ vyasanaṃ na ca budhyate // Dhs_11.51 //
children.translated_text: the mind leads to the world's end — and calamity is not perceived. // Dhs_11.51 //

body.translated_text: For one whose mind is clear and inclined toward welfare, there is unsurpassed happiness

children.text: viprasannaṃ yathā toyaṃ viprasannaṃ yathā nabhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as clear water, just as a clear sky,

children.text: viprasannaṃ tathā cittaṃ nīyate sukhamuttamam // Dhs_11.52 //
children.translated_text: so a clear mind is led to unsurpassed happiness. // Dhs_11.52 //
People are seen to be exceptional through the arising of the domain of thought;
they become companions of the king that is the mind, like citizens. // Dhs_11.53 //

body.translated_text: The restless mind causes one to go through the destinies of <s>saṃsāra</s>

children.translated_text: Where the mind runs, there the ignorant run;
led by mutual force, they wander in the ocean of the three existences. // Dhs_11.54 //

body.translated_text: Through a distinguished mind, the supreme destiny arises

children.translated_text: The distinction of the mind among existences and the distinction of <s>karma</s> —
for one devoid of the quality of <s>karma</s>, no distinction is obtained. // Dhs_11.55 //

body.translated_text: Praise of one whose mind is well-composed

children.translated_text: One whose mind is well-composed always perceives the Dharma;
he does not come under the power of faults, like the divine dispeller of darkness. // Dhs_11.56 //

body.translated_text: Even a householder with right view attains <s>Nirvāṇa</s>

children.translated_text: One whose intense right view abides in the mind —

children.text: gṛhastho 'pi sa me jñeyo muktaḥ saṃsārabandhanāt // Dhs_11.57 //
children.translated_text: even a householder should be known by me as liberated from the bonds of <s>saṃsāra</s>. // Dhs_11.57 //

body.translated_text: The wise go to the realm of the gods

children.translated_text: That which is auspicious and pure — then by a fault one is obstructed;

children.text: vijño (na) malamāpnoti devaloke sa jāyate // Dhs_11.58 //
children.translated_text: the wise one does not obtain defilement and is born in the realm of the gods. // Dhs_11.58 //

body.translated_text: Those with disciplined minds become goers to happiness

children.translated_text: The mind, fickle at the doors of sense objects, flowing crookedly like a river —

children.text: yairvinītamidaṃ cittaṃ te surāḥ śubhabhāginaḥ // Dhs_11.59 //
children.translated_text: those who have disciplined this mind, those gods are partakers of the good. // Dhs_11.59 //

body.translated_text: The path of <s>adharma</s> does not lead to the auspicious

children.translated_text: People who have resorted to the path of <s>adharma</s>, following the power of evil,

children.text: ciraṃ bhramanti saṃsāre cittena parikheditāḥ // Dhs_11.60 //
children.translated_text: wander long in <s>saṃsāra</s>, wearied by the mind. // Dhs_11.60 //

body.translated_text: The mind changes moment by moment

children.translated_text: Moment by moment, this mind transforms in many ways;
fickle by light nature, resembling illusion and <s>Gandharvas</s>. // Dhs_11.61 //

body.translated_text: One with a restless mind becomes bound

children.translated_text: The binding of that is desired, approved by knowledge and discrimination;
of far-reaching movement and great velocity, it runs about in many ways. // Dhs_11.62 //

body.translated_text: One who holds the mind with steadfastness enjoys happiness

children.translated_text: The mind, always being carried away toward sense objects, difficult to approach —

children.text: sandhārayati yo dhṛtyā sa dhīraḥ pāragāmikaḥ // Dhs_11.63 //
children.translated_text: one who holds it with steadfastness, that steadfast one goes to the far shore. // Dhs_11.63 //
The steadfast wise one who holds the mind, confused by ignorance and delusion,

children.text: sandhārayati yo dhīmān sa loke paṇḍito naraḥ // Dhs_11.64 //
children.translated_text: turned toward sense objects — that person is a wise one in the world. // Dhs_11.64 //

body.translated_text: A wholesome mind obstructs desire

children.text: yo yathā kurute cittaṃ tathā kāmān sa paśyati /
children.translated_text: As one directs the mind, so one perceives desires;
by the wholesome, there is the calming of desire; by the unwholesome, its increase. // Dhs_11.65 //
One whose mind is unpeaceful obtains suffering
The peaceful-minded one overcomes desires here as if they were poisoned arrows;

children.text: apraśāntamatiḥ sarpamaṇivat tān sa paśyati // Dhs_11.66 //
children.translated_text: one whose mind is unpeaceful sees them as a snake's jewel. // Dhs_11.66 //

body.translated_text: One subject to the mind does not attain a good destiny

children.translated_text: The senses and the objects of the senses come under the mind's control;
through the union with the mind, transformation proceeds. // Dhs_11.67 //

body.translated_text: Praise of the steadfast one

children.translated_text: Through the distinction of that very one, the steadfast one awakens;

children.text: rūpasāmānyato dṛṣṭaṃ pariṇāmaḥ kathaṃ pṛthak // Dhs_11.68 //
children.translated_text: seen generally in form — how is transformation different? // Dhs_11.68 //

body.translated_text: Exposition of the nature of the mind

children.translated_text: All, just as form, are sense objects as causes of the mind;

children.text: cittaṃ dāntaṃ sadā śāntaṃ doṣamiśravigarhitam // Dhs_11.69 //
children.translated_text: the mind, always tamed, is peaceful; mixed with faults, it is censured. // Dhs_11.69 //
Just as one grain of rice is of different kinds in husk and form,

children.text: saṃśleṣo yāti nānātvaṃ tathācittaṃ pravartate // Dhs_11.70 //
children.translated_text: so the union goes to diversity — thus the mind operates. // Dhs_11.70 //

children.text: kriyāṃ hi tatra kurute yatra (cittaṃ) pradhāvati /
children.translated_text: It performs action in that direction where the mind runs;
the conveyance of the mind is that speech — this world proceeds accordingly. // Dhs_11.71 //
From sense objects, the wandering mind, of extreme velocity and great power —

children.text: cittaṃ(śānta)karaṃ dāntaṃ śivaṃ bhavati dehinām // Dhs_11.72 //
children.translated_text: the mind, tamed and made peaceful, becomes auspicious for beings. // Dhs_11.72 //

body.translated_text: Through a tamed mind, the seeing of reality occurs

children.translated_text: With that untamed, swift mind, which dwells in all evil,

children.text: bhrāmyate tribhavaḥ sarvaḥ na ca tattvaṃ sa paśyati // Dhs_11.73 //
children.translated_text: the entire three realms wander — and it does not see reality. // Dhs_11.73 //

body.translated_text: The world, tossed about by the battle of the wind, wanders in <s>saṃsāra</s>

children.translated_text: Just as the ocean whirls, tossed about by the battle of the wind,
so this world, yoked with the lord that is the mind, always wanders. // Dhs_11.74 //

body.translated_text: A wholesome mind increases happiness

children.translated_text: The mind led toward the good is directed toward the good alone;
and so, following after good conduct, one enjoys those states where it runs. // Dhs_11.75 //

body.translated_text: The mind, a bearer of yoga, obtains conditions

children.translated_text: The mind of people is a bearer of yoga, equal to wind and water;

children.text: pratyayaśca yathā labhyastathā tat paridhāvati // Dhs_11.76 //
children.translated_text: as it obtains conditions, so it runs about. // Dhs_11.76 //

body.translated_text: The mind runs and revolves

children.translated_text: The mind runs swiftly and revolves swiftly;
swiftly it leads one, lord of the gods, to the realms of the gods and the earthly realms. // Dhs_11.77 //

body.translated_text: The agency of the mind

children.translated_text: The agency of all dharmas, the sustaining of all <s>karma</s>,
the leadership of all <s>karma</s> — this is characterized as mind-ness. // Dhs_11.78 //

body.translated_text: One should not trust the mind

children.translated_text: One should never trust the mind, which always strikes through openings,
which is difficult to obtain, difficult to control, and especially fickle. // Dhs_11.79 //

body.translated_text: Description of the mind's movement

children.translated_text: In a moment it goes to the wholesome; in a moment it goes to the unwholesome.

children.text: bhavatyavyākṛtaṃ śīghraṃ gatirasya na vidyate // Dhs_11.80 //
children.translated_text: it becomes indeterminate; its course swiftly is not found. // Dhs_11.80 //
Its extension is not known; its going indeed does not exist;

children.text: abhūtaḥ sambhavastasya bhūtvā ca pratigacchati // Dhs_11.81 //
children.translated_text: its arising is from the non-existent, and having come into being, it returns. // Dhs_11.81 //

body.translated_text: The mind is without form

children.text: nākāro vidyate tasya sañcayo 'pi na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Its form is not found, nor is there any accumulation of it;

children.text: grahaṇaṃ tasya naivāsti niḥśarīrasya sarvataḥ // Dhs_11.82 //
children.translated_text: there is no grasping of it at all, for it is entirely bodiless. // Dhs_11.82 //

body.translated_text: Description of the operation of conditions

children.translated_text: Through the conjunction of causes and conditions, having been obtained, it arises again;
like a jewel-and-moon condition, fire is known as a condition. // Dhs_11.83 //

body.translated_text: The mind runs toward the sense faculties, form, and the rest

children.translated_text: Just so, consciousness arises in dependence on the sense faculties, form, and the rest;
the mind of the individual is not known — it is observed only in conjunction. // Dhs_11.84 //

body.translated_text: The mind is difficult to restrain

children.text: tadevaṃ viṣayaṃ matvā durnivārya ca sarvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus understood its domain, and that it is difficult to restrain from all sides,
one should resort to the intention of the true Dharma, never to desires. // Dhs_11.85 //

body.translated_text: The mind is exceedingly fickle

children.translated_text: Fierce, exceedingly fickle, intense, unbearable, and of great power —

children.text: cittaṃ karoti karmāṇi yanna paśyanti bāliśāḥ // Dhs_11.86 //
children.translated_text: the mind performs actions that the foolish do not see. // Dhs_11.86 //

body.translated_text: The mind sets suffering in motion

children.translated_text: The mind is the cause of all actions from existence to existence;

children.text: bhavet pravartakaṃ duḥkhaṃ yena dhāvati bāliśaḥ // Dhs_11.87 //
children.translated_text: it would set suffering in motion, by which the foolish one runs about. // Dhs_11.87 //

body.translated_text: A fault of the mind is indeed a great fault

children.text: vātādayo na doṣāḥ syurdoṣā rāgādayo matāḥ /
children.translated_text: Wind and the like are not faults; faults are considered to be desire and the rest;
through wind and the like, a human is not reborn in the lower realms. // Dhs_11.88 //
A fault of the mind is a great fault, always revealing what is sinful;
therefore, the supreme refuge from those [faults] is not [the cure for] wind and other [physical ailments] here. // Dhs_11.89 //

body.translated_text: The mind that follows desire becomes corrupted

children.translated_text: Wind and the like perish with the destruction of the body of embodied beings;
but desire and the like do not perish even in hundreds of lifetimes. // Dhs_11.90 //

children.text: tasmād rāgasya vaśagaṃ na vidheyaṃ kadācana /
children.translated_text: Therefore one should never allow the mind to be subject to desire;

children.text: ābhyantikaṃ paraṃ śreyaḥ prāpyate rāgasaṅkramāt // Dhs_11.91 //
children.translated_text: the inner, supreme good is obtained by crossing over desire. // Dhs_11.91 //

body.translated_text: The mind itself becomes the physician

children.text: yaścittavaidyaḥ sa bhiṣag na śarīrabhiṣag bhṛśam /
children.translated_text: The physician of the mind is a true healer, not so much the physician of the body;

children.text: manaścikitsako jñeyo na tathā laukiko mataḥ // Dhs_11.92 //
children.translated_text: one should be known as a physician of the mind — not so the worldly one. // Dhs_11.92 //

body.translated_text: Burned by the actions of one's own mind, one falls into hell

children.text: karmacintyaṃ samaṃ cintyaṃ na cittena prapadyate /
children.translated_text: One should reflect equally on karma and reflection; one does not fall through the mind alone;
burned by the actions of one's own mind, one runs toward the hells. // Dhs_11.93 //

body.translated_text: Only through meditation does the mind become pure

children.translated_text: The good of one whose mind is equanimous is found nowhere else;
the deluded one, who should guard the heart, runs after what has departed. // Dhs_11.94 //

body.translated_text: One subject to the mind obtains suffering

children.text: dhyānād dhyeyena kūṭena yaḥ pumān vanamāśritaḥ /
children.translated_text: The person who resorts to the forest through meditation and its object, the peak —

children.text: taṃ muktvā cittakaḥ so 'yaṃ saṃprahṛṣyati bāliśaḥ // Dhs_11.95 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned that, this foolish mind-follower rejoices. // Dhs_11.95 //
Those fools bound by the noose of the mind, pursuing the actions of the mind,

children.text: nīyante hyavaśā ghoraṃ narakaṃ karmamohitā // Dhs_11.96 //
children.translated_text: are led helplessly to terrible hell, deluded by karma. // Dhs_11.96 //

body.translated_text: Examination of the mind's diversity

children.text: sucittamapi yaccitaṃ na taccittaṃ satāṃ matam /
children.translated_text: Even a well-placed mind — that is not considered to be the mind by the good;
the karma-mind, the great mind, is variegated across the three realms. // Dhs_11.97 //
Beings wander in the five destinies through variegated means;

children.text: tat sarva karmasācivyaṃ citrakartṛ vicitritam // Dhs_11.98 //
children.translated_text: all that is the assistance of karma — variegated by the variegated maker. // Dhs_11.98 //

body.translated_text: One subject to the mind becomes bound

children.translated_text: By the variegated maker — the mind — this mass of karma is variegated;

children.text: yena sarvamidaṃ baddhaṃ jagad bhramati mohitam // Dhs_11.99 //
children.translated_text: by which this entire world is bound and wanders, deluded. // Dhs_11.99 //
The mind is destroyed by rain, heat, dust, and smoke for earth-rulers;
in thousands of billions of <s>kalpas</s>, the variegated mind is destroyed. // Dhs_11.100 //
The earth passes away and even the ocean dries up;

children.text: cittenāpi kṛtaṃ citraṃ tasyānubhavane sthite // Dhs_11.101 //
children.translated_text: but the variegated [karma] created by the mind remains for its experience. // Dhs_11.101 //

body.translated_text: When the mind is heedless, various destinies arise

children.translated_text: Entering various destinies, following various karma,
subject to various minds, beings wander in the five destinies. // Dhs_11.102 //
The mind of foolish people runs toward sense objects;

children.text: na cinotyaśubhaṃ karma yena dhāvati durgatim // Dhs_11.103 //
children.translated_text: it accumulates unwholesome karma by which one runs to evil destinies. // Dhs_11.103 //

body.translated_text: The fickle mind is always perilous

children.text: tasmāccittaṃ sadā rakṣyaṃ cañcalaṃ viṣamaṃ kharam /
children.translated_text: Therefore the mind should always be guarded — fickle, perilous, and harsh,
always attached to sense objects, enveloped by the poison of craving. // Dhs_11.104 //

body.translated_text: The mind attached to sense objects casts one into calamity

children.translated_text: This [mind] runs toward sense objects and does not perceive calamity;

children.text: paścāttu vyasane prāpte phalaṃ vindati karmaṇaḥ // Dhs_11.105 //
children.translated_text: later, when calamity has arrived, one reaps the fruit of karma. // Dhs_11.105 //

body.translated_text: One whose mind is concentrated enjoys happiness

children.translated_text: One who has fear of the lower realms — his mind is concentrated;
with a concentrated mind, he obtains happiness after happiness. // Dhs_11.106 //

body.translated_text: One who has conquered the mind obtains happiness

children.translated_text: Perilous, fickle, intense, unbearable, and of great power —

children.text: yaiścittaṃ nirjitaṃ dhīraiste loke sukhino matāḥ // Dhs_11.107 //
children.translated_text: those wise ones who have conquered the mind are considered happy in the world. // Dhs_11.107 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the eleventh chapter, on the Mind. //
(12) Chapter on Speech (<s>Vāgvarga</s>)
One who desires <s>nirvāṇa</s> should avoid harsh speech

children.text: pāruṣyaṃ varjayet dhīmān samyagvāg bhīrato bhavet /
children.translated_text: The wise one should avoid harsh speech and be fearful of right speech;
the being who delights in sweetness stands near <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_12.1 //
Always examining one's speech, one should speak, and should avoid what is impure;

children.text: vāṅmanenābhibhūtā ye te yānti narakaṃ narāḥ // Dhs_12.2 //
children.translated_text: those people who are overpowered by speech and mind go to hell. // Dhs_12.2 //
For the embodied being who has transgressed the one dharma of false speech,
who has crossed the boundary — there is no sin that cannot be done here. // Dhs_12.3 //

body.translated_text: False speech should not be employed

children.translated_text: One should not speak false speech, which produces all [negative] conditions;

children.text: yathā badhyati saṃsāre sugatiṃ naiva paśyati // Dhs_12.4 //
children.translated_text: by which one is bound in <s>saṃsāra</s> and never sees a good destination. // Dhs_12.4 //
It creates distrust in the good and generates universal hatred;
the wilderness of all non-dharmas — false speech proceeds [from it]. // Dhs_12.5 //
For every mortal born, an axe is born in the mouth;

children.text: paścāt chinattyātmānaṃ vācā durbhāṣitaṃ vadan // Dhs_12.6 //
children.translated_text: later it cuts oneself — the one who speaks ill-spoken words. // Dhs_12.6 //
It is the banner of all ill deeds, the mother of all sins;

children.text: tamasāṃ yonirekā sā yāṃ vācaṃ bhāṣate mṛṣā // Dhs_12.7 //
children.translated_text: it is the single source of darkness — the word spoken falsely. // Dhs_12.7 //
People devoid of truth are bereft of all goodness;

children.text: tṛṇavad yānti loke 'smin pratyapāyeṣu duḥkhitāḥ // Dhs_12.8 //
children.translated_text: they go like grass in this world, suffering in the lower realms. // Dhs_12.8 //
The wise one should not speak falsehood; speaking falsehood is terrible;
even one who seems happy with foul-smelling [deeds] is scorched by remorse. // Dhs_12.9 //

body.translated_text: The greatness of truth

children.text: satyaṃ ca na vivarjeta tasya dharmo na vidyate /
children.translated_text: One should never abandon truth; for one without truth, there is no dharma;
for one who has turned away from the Dharma, suffering of many kinds remains. // Dhs_12.10 //

body.translated_text: Truth is the lamp of all dharmas

children.translated_text: Truth is the lamp of all dharmas, dear to the good like a jewel;

children.text: svargasya ca paraṃ vartma satyamuktaṃ gatajvaraiḥ // Dhs_12.11 //
children.translated_text: truth is the supreme path to heaven — so declare those free from fever. // Dhs_12.11 //

children.text: satyaṃ na hi divaṃ yāti mokṣasyāsatyavādinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Truth does not go to heaven for the speaker of falsehood who seeks liberation;

children.text: satyahīnā hi puruṣāḥ paśutulyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ // Dhs_12.12 //
children.translated_text: people devoid of truth are declared equal to animals. // Dhs_12.12 //
The lowest of the low are those for whom truth does not exist;

children.text: satyaṃ dharmasya sopānaṃ jyotiṣāmākaro mahān // Dhs_12.13 //
children.translated_text: truth is the stairway of the Dharma, the great mine of luminaries. // Dhs_12.13 //
It is the path of the dharmas of liberation, the supreme wealth among riches,
and protection from sinners — so truth is declared by the wise. // Dhs_12.14 //

body.translated_text: Speech adorned with truth is the ornament of ornaments

children.translated_text: The supreme light of lights, the eye even of those who have eyes —

children.text: draviṇena vinā satyaṃ bhūṣaṇasyāpi bhūṣaṇam // Dhs_12.15 //
children.translated_text: without wealth, truth is the ornament even of ornaments. // Dhs_12.15 //
Truth is an incomparable treasure, unassailable, accomplishing all;

children.text: gacchanti (satyā yiṇaḥ) puruṣāḥ paramāṃ gatim // Dhs_12.16 //
children.translated_text: people who resort to truth go to the supreme destination. // Dhs_12.16 //
A king adorned with various ornaments does not shine as much

children.text: satyena bhūṣito dhīmān śobhate devavad yathā // Dhs_12.17 //
children.translated_text: as the wise one adorned with truth shines, like a god. // Dhs_12.17 //

children.text: na mātā na pitā cātha mitrāṇi na ca bāndhavāḥ /
children.translated_text: Neither mother nor father, neither friends nor kinsmen —

children.text: trāṇamevaṃ yathā śrutvā tasmāt satyaparo bhavet // Dhs_12.18 //
children.translated_text: none protects as much as hearing [the Dharma]; therefore one should be devoted to truth. // Dhs_12.18 //

body.translated_text: Censure of falsehood

children.translated_text: The supreme fire among fires, the supreme poison among poisons,
and the stairway to the lower realms — thus is falsehood proclaimed. // Dhs_12.19 //
A person should conduct falsehood as having the touch of poison and fire;

children.text: anṛtena hi yo deva dagdhaityabhidhīyate // Dhs_12.20 //
children.translated_text: for a god who is burned by falsehood — so it is declared. // Dhs_12.20 //

body.translated_text: Truth and falsehood are mutually opposed

children.translated_text: Therefore, with all effort, a person should not speak falsehood;

children.text: sarva bhayādikaṃ kaṣṭamanṛtaṃ kīrtitaṃ budhaiḥ // Dhs_12.21 //
children.translated_text: falsehood is declared by the wise as the worst of all fears and calamities. // Dhs_12.21 //
The supreme fire among fires could burn even the ocean;
how much more so the speaker of falsehood, who is like wood and a clod of earth! // Dhs_12.22 //

children.text: satyaṃ tyaktvā mṛṣāvādaṃ yo naraḥ pratipadyate /
children.translated_text: The person who, abandoning truth, resorts to false speech —

children.text: ratnaṃ tyaktvā sa pāpātmā pāṣāṇaṃ pratipadyate // Dhs_12.23 //
children.translated_text: that sinful soul, abandoning a jewel, resorts to a stone. // Dhs_12.23 //

children.text: yasyātmā na bhavet dviṣṭo yasya vā narakaṃ priyam /
children.translated_text: One whose own self is not hateful to him, or for whom hell is pleasing —

children.text: mṛṣāvādaṃ svadehāgnim abuddhiḥ sa niṣevate // Dhs_12.24 //
children.translated_text: that unintelligent one resorts to false speech, the fire of one's own body. // Dhs_12.24 //

body.translated_text: This truthful speech is always the ornament of all embodied beings;

body.text: satyaṃ tyaktvā mṛṣāvāde kasmād yānti kubuddhayaḥ // Dhs_12.25 //
body.translated_text: having abandoned truth, why do those of evil understanding resort to false speech? // Dhs_12.25 //

children.translated_text: Truth is the foremost of virtues; falsehood is remembered as [the foremost] of faults;

children.text: guṇāṃstyaktvā kathaṃ mūḍho doṣeṣu paridhāvati // Dhs_12.26 //
children.translated_text: how does the deluded one, abandoning virtues, run after faults? // Dhs_12.26 //
False speech is proclaimed to be the seed of all suffering;

children.text: tathā satyaṃ sukhasyaiva tasmānnānṛtako bhavet // Dhs_12.27 //
children.translated_text: likewise, truth is [the seed] of happiness — therefore one should not be a liar. // Dhs_12.27 //

children.text: satyavādī hi puruṣaḥ priyaḥ sarvasya dehinaḥ /
children.translated_text: A truth-speaking person is dear to every embodied being;
a liar is an eye-affliction — therefore one should not be a liar. // Dhs_12.28 //
People who speak the truth are always esteemed as godlike;
but the deluded people of false minds are like denizens of hell. // Dhs_12.29 //
Truth is supreme among auspicious things; falsehood likewise among faults;
the person who avoids faults and is averse to [spiritual] virtues is the best among persons. // Dhs_12.30 //
Arising from happiness, resulting in happiness, it ripens with happiness;
one obtains truth with happiness — truth which leads to <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_12.31 //
Arising from suffering, bearing bitter fruit, it ripens with suffering;

children.text: anṛtaṃ sarvaduḥkhāntaṃ kaḥ pumān na vivarjayet // Dhs_12.32 //
children.translated_text: falsehood ends in all suffering — what person would not avoid it? // Dhs_12.32 //

children.text: nānyadeśāgataṃ satyaṃ nānyasmāt prārthyate hi tat /
children.translated_text: Truth does not come from another land, nor is it sought from another;
truth is the supreme among all <s>tīrthas</s> (sacred fords) — not enveloped in the waters of a <s>tīrtha</s>. // Dhs_12.33 //

children.text: dīpānāṃ ca paro dīpaḥ satyaṃ buddhena deśitam /
children.translated_text: The supreme lamp among lamps — truth was taught by the <s>Buddha</s>;

children.text: auṣadhānāṃ paraṃ tacca sadā duḥkhaniṣūdanam // Dhs_12.34 //
children.translated_text: and it is the supreme among medicines, always destroying suffering. // Dhs_12.34 //
Both nectar and poison are situated on the tongue of human beings;

children.text: amṛtaṃ satyamityuktaṃ viṣaṃ tūktaṃ mṛṣāvacaḥ // Dhs_12.35 //
children.translated_text: truth is declared to be the nectar; false speech is declared to be the poison. // Dhs_12.35 //
One for whom falsehood is cherished — truth is firmly established for him [elsewhere];
and one for whom poison is desired — false speech would be his choice. // Dhs_12.36 //
Through poison, destruction is certain; through false speech, it is certain;

children.text: mṛtavat sa pumānasti yo mithyātvabhibhāṣate // Dhs_12.37 //
children.translated_text: that person who speaks falsely is as good as dead. // Dhs_12.37 //

children.text: nātmano hi hitaṃ pathyaṃ (para)sya na kathañcana /
children.translated_text: It is not beneficial or wholesome for oneself, nor for another in any way;

children.text: paścāttu paraduḥkhāya tat kathaṃ sevyate nṛbhiḥ // Dhs_12.38 //
children.translated_text: later it leads to suffering for others — so how is it served by people? // Dhs_12.38 //
In every land I have seen thousands of births and deaths;
the supreme [truth] would produce thousands, but false speech would destroy [them]. // Dhs_12.39 //
The extraction of noble birth, the ornament of the twice-born,
the vision of the path of liberation — this is called truth. // Dhs_12.40 //
The river of craving, the army of <s>Māra</s> — through truth and through actions of the good,
truth is declared as supreme, as formerly, as the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s>. // Dhs_12.41 //
In this world without beginning or end, people have gone to the far shore of craving;

children.text: nāstyatrāṇaṃ yathā satyamiti dharmavido viduḥ // Dhs_12.42 //
children.translated_text: There is no refuge — this is the truth, as those who know the Dharma understand. // Dhs_12.42 //

body.translated_text: The noose of covetousness should not be pursued

children.text: satyavadhyā sadā kleśā vajravadhyā yathā nagāḥ /
children.translated_text: Defilements are truly to be slain, just as mountains are slain by the thunderbolt;

children.text: hatā(ste) puruṣā (jñeyā ye ') bhidhyā parivañcitāḥ // Dhs_12.43 //
children.translated_text: Those people who are deceived by covetousness should be known as slain. // Dhs_12.43 //
This mind, equal to another's mind, is deceived by form and the rest;

children.text: abhidhyāmānasaṃ pāśaṃ sevitaṃ na vicakṣaṇaiḥ // Dhs_12.44 //
children.translated_text: The noose of covetous thought has not been pursued by the discerning. // Dhs_12.44 //
The unaltered self is burned like a lamp fed with oil;
For one whose mind is burned by covetousness, no cause is apprehended. // Dhs_12.45 //

body.translated_text: Ill-will only deludes beings
Since that should always be avoided — that which produces the bitter taste of poison;
Beings deluded by ill-will, whose minds are always absorbed in it — // Dhs_12.46 //

children.translated_text: They do not attain peace, like serpents dwelling in holes.

children.text: atha kūrasvabhāvā ye vyāpādaparamā narāḥ // Dhs_12.47 //
children.translated_text: And those who are of cruel nature, those people supreme in ill-will — // Dhs_12.47 //

children.text: na teṣāṃ vidyate saukhyamādityena yathā tamaḥ /
children.translated_text: For them there is no happiness, as there is no darkness for the sun.

children.text: na dharme nārthanikaro na dharmā na ca bāndhavāḥ // Dhs_12.48 //
children.translated_text: Neither Dharma, nor accumulation of wealth, nor dharmas, nor kinsmen // Dhs_12.48 //
Protect all those people whose minds are struck by ill-will.

children.text: tamasāmākaro hyeṣa vyāpāda iha kathyate // Dhs_12.49 //
children.translated_text: This ill-will is declared here as a mine of darkness. // Dhs_12.49 //
Ill-will (<s>vyāpāda</s>) is proclaimed as that which destroys the progenitor;

children.text: avyāpādaḥ paraṃ śreyo na vyāpādaḥ kathañcana // Dhs_12.50 //
children.translated_text: Non-ill-will is the supreme good — never ill-will. // Dhs_12.50 //

children.text: avyāpādaparā ye tu te yānti padamacyutam /
children.translated_text: Those who are devoted to non-ill-will go to the imperishable state.
One who is certainly a speaker of untruth, a speaker of non-Dharma, is not righteous. // Dhs_12.51 //

children.text: sa cauraḥ sarvalokasya na cauraḥ prākṛtaḥ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: He is a thief of the whole world; an ordinary thief is not so considered.

children.text: dharmavādī naro yastu carate dharmameva yaḥ // Dhs_12.52 //
children.translated_text: But that man who speaks the Dharma, who practices the Dharma — // Dhs_12.52 //

children.text: sa yāti śāśvataṃ sthānaṃ yatra gatvā na śocyate /
children.translated_text: He goes to the eternal abode, having gone where there is no sorrow.
A man afflicted by false speech is proclaimed as worldly; // Dhs_12.53 //

children.text: lokottaraiḥ kalpaśataiḥ kadācit kathyate na vā /
children.translated_text: By the supramundane, in a hundred <s>kalpas</s>, he may sometimes be spoken of or not.

children.text: tasmāt lokottaraṃ vākyaṃ laukikaṃ na kathañcana // Dhs_12.54 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, supramundane speech — worldly speech never. // Dhs_12.54 //
Worldly speech, seen as bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s>, is like poison;
One attached to craving is always freed from merit — this is certain. // Dhs_12.55 //
A supramundane person is declared blessed by the learned.

children.text: hitaṃ tattvaṃ ca yo mūḍho na gṛhṇāti gurorvacaḥ // Dhs_12.56 //
children.translated_text: The fool who does not accept the beneficial and truthful words of the teacher — // Dhs_12.56 //

body.translated_text: The truthful speaker is always honored by the gods

children.text: sa paścād vyasane prāpte tapyate svena cetasā /
children.translated_text: He later, when calamity has arrived, is tormented by his own mind.

children.text: satyavādī sadā dānto devatābhiḥ puraskṛtaḥ // Dhs_12.57 //
children.translated_text: The truthful speaker, always self-controlled, is honored by the gods; // Dhs_12.57 //

children.text: priyo bhavati lokasya paścād deveṣu modati /
children.translated_text: He becomes dear to the world and later rejoices among the gods.
He becomes dear to the world and later grows by his own inner nature;

children.text: darśanīyaṃ mukhaṃ cāsya devalokeṣu jāyate // Dhs_12.58 //
children.translated_text: His face becomes beautiful, and he is born in the heavenly worlds. // Dhs_12.58 //
A man who speaks untruth is a calamity for all beings;
Resembling a mass of darkness, though living he is equal to the dead. // Dhs_12.59 //
How does the tongue not fall out, which delights in the ornament of words,

children.text: mṛṣā vadati yo vācaṃ sadbhūtaguṇanāśikām // Dhs_12.60 //
children.translated_text: Of one who speaks false speech that destroys true virtues? // Dhs_12.60 //
In the mouth dwells a serpent, in the mouth dwells fruitlessness,
In the mouth blazes fire — for one who speaks falsely with words. // Dhs_12.61 //
The tongue is bound by nooses that are the foremost causes of hell;

children.text: chettā ca dharmahetūnāṃ mṛṣāvādaḥ pravartate // Dhs_12.62 //
children.translated_text: False speech proceeds as the cutter of the causes of Dharma. // Dhs_12.62 //

children.text: na tasya mātā na pitā buddho nāpi samvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: He has no mother, no father, no Buddha, nor restraint —

children.text: yaḥ pāpabuddhiḥ patito mṛṣāvādaṃ prabhāṣateḥ // Dhs_12.63 //
children.translated_text: One of evil mind who, having fallen, utters false speech. // Dhs_12.63 //
Without cause he comes to insignificance and is revolving in the six realms;

children.text: mucyate devatābhiśca yo vācaṃ bhāṣate mṛṣā // Dhs_12.64 //
children.translated_text: He is abandoned by the gods — one who speaks false words. // Dhs_12.64 //
For one whose speech is unrestrained, who is angry without reflection,
Who is fickle and of little fortune — endless suffering is established. // Dhs_12.65 //
Even seeing another's suffering, a being who is a calamity to beings,
One who knows it as another's misfortune — that person goes to hell. // Dhs_12.66 //

body.text: ye yathāvādino marttyā na ca tatkāriṇaḥ sadā // Dhs_12.67 //
body.translated_text: Those mortals who speak in one way but never act accordingly. // Dhs_12.67 //
Truth itself is the stairway to heaven and <s>nirvāṇa</s>

children.translated_text: Truth is the stairway to heaven, and it is indeed the door to <s>nirvāṇa</s>;

children.text: tasmāt satyaparo nityaṃ nityaṃ dharmagatiḥ smṛtiḥ // Dhs_12.68 //
children.translated_text: Therefore one should always be devoted to truth, always intent on the path of Dharma with mindfulness. // Dhs_12.68 //

body.translated_text: One should not speak falsehood

children.translated_text: The best of men proceeds to the abode free from sorrow and old age;
The wise one should avoid falsehood, which is condemned by the seers of truth. // Dhs_12.69 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the twelfth chapter on Speech (<s>Vāgvarga</s>). //
(13) Chapter on Action (<s>Karmavarga</s>)
The experience of the fruits of wholesome and unwholesome actions

children.translated_text: The certainty of the fruits of wholesome and unwholesome actions —

children.text: bhujyate sukṛtaṃ sarva karmabaddhā hi dehinaḥ // Dhs_13.1 //
children.translated_text: All meritorious deeds are experienced, for embodied beings are bound by <s>karma</s>. // Dhs_13.1 //
Whatever action is undertaken is experienced by those who do it —
By a deluded mind and pride, a dweller in the city of craving. // Dhs_13.2 //

body.translated_text: One alone experiences the fruit

children.translated_text: Together with many companions one commits sinful deeds;

children.text: ekākī karmaṇastasya phalaṃ bhuṅkte bhave bhave // Dhs_13.3 //
children.translated_text: But alone one experiences the fruit of that action, in existence after existence. // Dhs_13.3 //
There is no separation from actions, even by all one's own people and kinsmen;
The wholesome and unwholesome follow the one departing to the other world. // Dhs_13.4 //
Where merits go, their fragrance follows there;
Likewise, wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s> follows the one who departs.
Heirs to the fruits of their own actions, beings are yoked by <s>karma</s> through their vital breath. // Dhs_13.5 //

body.translated_text: Through meritorious deeds, one goes to the heavenly realm

children.translated_text: Through meritorious deeds, one goes to the heavenly realms; through misdeeds, one goes below;
Whatever suffering, born as the fruit of action, arises with a bitter origin — // Dhs_13.6 //
The comparison for it, formidable, arises in the three realms;

children.text: tridoṣajaṃ tricittotthaṃ triṣu dhātuṣu pacyate // Dhs_13.7 //
children.translated_text: Born of the three poisons, arising from the three minds, it ripens in the three realms. // Dhs_13.7 //
The ripening of that action is observed in the three realms;
It arises from the aggregate of causes and conditions, and that is its measure. // Dhs_13.8 //

body.translated_text: No one else experiences the fruit of action done by another

children.translated_text: For sin committed by one is not ripened by another;

children.text: sukarmaphaladāyādaḥ prāṇināṃ sarva eva hi // Dhs_13.9 //
children.translated_text: Every living being is indeed an heir to the fruit of good action. // Dhs_13.9 //

body.text: pūrvoktānāṃ trividhānāṃ svasya kṛta eva vipāko bhavati
body.translated_text: Of the previously mentioned three types of action, the ripening is only of one's own doing

children.translated_text: Of this threefold action, the ripening is not of another's;
