The forty ripen terribly. // Dhs_13.10 //

body.translated_text: Description of the fruits of action

children.translated_text: One alone commits actions and one alone experiences the fruit;
One alone crosses dangers, and another is born as a companion. // Dhs_13.11 //

children.text: jalāpekṣī jano yastu kurute karma duṣkṛtam /
children.translated_text: A person, desiring water, commits sinful deeds;

children.text: na jano janaśatānāṃ bhuṅkte hi vyañjanaṃ (kvacit) // Dhs_13.12 //
children.translated_text: No person enjoys the food of a hundred persons anywhere. // Dhs_13.12 //

children.text: na hyanyena kṛtaṃ karma saṅkrāmatyaparasya tat /
children.translated_text: For action committed by one does not transfer to another;
I do not consider it without beginning or end, neither in this world nor by others. // Dhs_13.13 //
One by whom misconduct has been committed, tasting suffering born of happiness,

children.text: tena carati saṃsāre prerite karmavāyunā // Dhs_13.14 //
children.translated_text: That one wanders in <s>saṃsāra</s>, driven by the wind of <s>karma</s>. // Dhs_13.14 //

body.translated_text: For whom does Dharma increase?

children.translated_text: For one who has not examined the truth, whose mind is confused —
The whole Dharma increases, charming though veiled by dharmas. // Dhs_13.15 //

body.translated_text: Who goes to hell?

children.translated_text: Beings deceived by the mind, deluded by the mind —
The sinful ones go to hell, heading from darkness to deeper darkness. // Dhs_13.16 //
In <s>saṃsāra</s> veiled by darkness, the teaching of the Buddha is hard to find;

children.text: duḥkhād duḥkhataraṃ yānti yebhyaḥ dharmo na rocate // Dhs_13.17 //
children.translated_text: Those for whom the Dharma does not please go from suffering to greater suffering. // Dhs_13.17 //
In beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>, beings are covered by the net of <s>karma</s>;
One is born and sustained by the cause of the fruits of one's own actions. // Dhs_13.18 //
Gods are born in hell, and hell-beings likewise;

children.text: manuṣyāḥ pretaviṣaye narakaṃ vā prayānti hi // Dhs_13.19 //
children.translated_text: Humans go to the realm of hungry ghosts, or indeed go to hell. // Dhs_13.19 //

body.translated_text: Happiness comes only through good deeds

children.text: anyonyaprabhavaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ duḥkhaṃ vā yadi vā sukham /
children.translated_text: It is seen that suffering and happiness arise from one another;
In birth produced by the dharma of defilements, that is committed by the offender. // Dhs_13.20 //
Innumerable actions are always committed by beings in <s>saṃsāra</s>;

children.text: tatra śakyaṃ budhairgantuṃ varjayitvā tathāgataiḥ // Dhs_13.21 //
children.translated_text: Therein, the wise can navigate, except for the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. // Dhs_13.21 //

children.text: nādharmasya phalaṃ sādhu viparītaṃ na pacyate /
children.translated_text: The fruit of non-dharma is not good; the opposite does not ripen;

children.text: hetoḥ sadṛśatā dṛṣṭā jalasya vividhasya vai // Dhs_13.22 //
children.translated_text: Similarity of cause is seen, like that of various kinds of water. // Dhs_13.22 //

children.text: sādṛśyasya hetuphalaṃ viparītaṃ na jātu hi /
children.translated_text: The causal fruit of similarity is never the opposite;
For conditioned, formless things, the cause is the arising of conditions. // Dhs_13.23 //

body.translated_text: All fruits of action have a cause

children.text: nāhetukaṃ phalaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ narake tu viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: No causeless fruit is seen, especially in hell;
Connected with the aggregate of causes, it ripens in the hells. // Dhs_13.24 //
For those who are firmly committed to sin and certainly bound for evil,
The connection of fruit with action ripens in the hells. // Dhs_13.25 //

children.text: deśānāṃ prati kālaṃ tu yat karma (vi)nivartate /
children.translated_text: But whatever action ceases in due time in various regions,

children.text: tasya neṣṭaṃ phalaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ tattvamārgavidarśakaiḥ // Dhs_13.26 //
children.translated_text: Its undesired fruit is seen by the revealers of the path of truth. // Dhs_13.26 //

body.translated_text: Illustrated by examples: the fruit is indeed dependent on action

children.text: dīpādhīnā prabhā yadvat karmādhīnaṃ phalaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Just as radiance depends on a lamp, so does the fruit depend on action;

children.text: anyo 'nyaphalasambhūtaḥ saṃskṛtaḥ sarva eva hi // Dhs_13.27 //
children.translated_text: All conditioned things are indeed born from the fruit of one another. // Dhs_13.27 //

body.translated_text: Affirmation of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>)

children.translated_text: They are seen as having mutual causes, as being subject to mutual control;
Through the connection of similarity, they are seen by the seers of truth. // Dhs_13.28 //
The connection of causeless fruits is not established by <s>Īśvara</s> and the like;
Conditioned dharmas have been taught by the seers of truth. // Dhs_13.29 //
In beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>, arising from causes and conditions,

children.text: sādṛśyaṃ karmaṇā dṛṣṭaṃ viparītaṃ na kalpyate // Dhs_13.30 //
children.translated_text: Similarity with action is seen — the opposite is not to be imagined. // Dhs_13.30 //

body.translated_text: The nature of the Buddha

children.translated_text: Beings therein are subject to <s>karma</s>, born from the cause of <s>karma</s>;
One who knows the truth of the fruits of <s>karma</s> — that one is called a Buddha. // Dhs_13.31 //

body.translated_text: For whom is peace not found?

children.translated_text: Those who are opposed to the path and the non-path, deluded regarding the Buddha's teaching —

children.text: (na) teṣāṃ vidyate śāntirādityasya tamo yathā // Dhs_13.32 //
children.translated_text: For them peace is not found, just as darkness is not found before the sun. // Dhs_13.32 //

body.translated_text: Happiness depends on action

children.translated_text: Happiness is seen to depend on action, and the mind depends on happiness;
The mind understands dharmas — those who investigate with discernment. // Dhs_13.33 //

body.translated_text: The fruit of good conduct

children.translated_text: All conditioned things are impermanent, like water bubbles;

children.text: tasmāt sucaritaṃ karma loke martya paratra ca // Dhs_13.34 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, good conduct in the world of mortals and beyond. // Dhs_13.34 //

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ karmaphalaṃ loke dṛṣṭā eva vicitratā /
children.translated_text: The fruit of action is seen in the world; diversity itself is seen;
For one whose supreme concern is heedlessness, the self is certainly not dear. // Dhs_13.35 //
By the exceedingly strong rope of <s>karma</s>, deeply fastened and hard to release,

children.text: baddhā bālā na gacchanti nirvāṇapuramuttamam // Dhs_13.36 //
children.translated_text: The foolish, being bound, do not go to the supreme city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_13.36 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the thirteenth chapter on Action (<s>Karmavarga</s>). //
(14) Chapter on Fetters (<s>Saṃyojanavarga</s>)
Through knowledge, attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s>

children.translated_text: Having cut them with the weapon of knowledge, freed and without fever,

children.text: prayānti nirvṛttiṃ dhanyā yatra jñānyeva vidyate // Dhs_14.1 //
children.translated_text: The blessed ones proceed to liberation, where knowledge alone exists. // Dhs_14.1 //

children.text: sadṛśaṃ hi phalaṃ hetoḥ kathayanti manīṣiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: The sages declare that the fruit is similar to the cause;

children.text: hetorasadṛśaṃ naiva phalaṃ pacati dehinām // Dhs_14.2 //
children.translated_text: A fruit dissimilar to the cause never ripens for embodied beings. // Dhs_14.2 //
Bound by causes and conditions, connected to the conditions of birth —

children.text: yathā baddhā hi saṃsāre pramucyante (na)dehinaḥ // Dhs_14.3 //
children.translated_text: Thus bound in <s>saṃsāra</s>, embodied beings are not freed. // Dhs_14.3 //

body.translated_text: The means to supreme peace

children.text: tāṃ viśliṣya susambaddhāṃ gāḍhāṃ durviṣehāṃ parām /
children.translated_text: Having separated from that which is well-joined, firm, unbearable, and supreme,

children.text: gacchanti paramāṃ śānti yatra duḥkhaṃ na vidyate // Dhs_14.4 //
children.translated_text: They go to supreme peace, where suffering is not found. // Dhs_14.4 //
A creature is certainly determined by <s>karma</s>; by <s>karma</s> it is ripened. /
Accessible indeed — yet in <s>saṃsāra</s>, happiness is truly not found. // Dhs_14.5 //
For beings of deluded minds who are afflicted by suffering within suffering,

children.text: sanmārgadeśiko nāsti yo 'smād duḥkhāt pramocayet // Dhs_14.6 //
children.translated_text: there is no guide to the right path who would free them from this suffering. // Dhs_14.6 //

children.text: ye na dharmaparā nityaṃ ye na satyaparāḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: Those who are not always devoted to Dharma, who are not always devoted to truth,

children.text: ye ca yoniratā nityaṃ teṣāṃ duḥkhaṃ na hīyate // Dhs_14.7 //
children.translated_text: and who are always attached to birth — their suffering does not diminish. // Dhs_14.7 //

body.translated_text: Dharma brings happiness in this world and the next:

children.translated_text: Like a mother, like a father, like a friend, like a kinsman always —

children.text: dharmo vai deśito buddhairiha loke paratra ca // Dhs_14.8 //
children.translated_text: the Dharma has been taught by the Buddhas, in this world and the next. // Dhs_14.8 //
Beings established in the three destinies, come under the power of the three poisons,
having the course of the three realms, always fallen in the triple world — // Dhs_14.9 //
those subject to the reach of the three <s>karmas</s>, and those devoted to women, drink, and the like —

children.text: na bhavānmuktigatikāḥ syurbhūmau vicaranti te // Dhs_14.10 //
children.translated_text: they will not have the course of liberation from existence; they wander on the earth. // Dhs_14.10 //

body.translated_text: For whom does suffering not exist?

children.translated_text: Those who do not become heedless regarding the Three Jewels, and who are under the guidance of the three awakenings,

children.text: tridṛṣṭivarjakā ye tu teṣāṃ duḥkhaṃ na vidyate // Dhs_14.11 //
children.translated_text: and those who abandon the three wrong views — for them suffering does not exist. // Dhs_14.11 //
Attached to abiding in the three times, fever-free, seers of truth,
content with deeds done in the three portions, free from grief, heading toward cessation — // Dhs_14.12 //
those who are endowed with the three groups and who investigate the three <s>karmas</s> —

children.text: na te vatsyanti saṃsāre vītadoṣā gatajvarāḥ // Dhs_14.13 //
children.translated_text: they will not dwell in <s>saṃsāra</s>, free from faults and free from fever. // Dhs_14.13 //
Those who know the procedure of the path and the non-path, who contemplate existence and non-existence,

children.text: maitrībhāvaviviktā ye te yānti paramāṃ gatim // Dhs_14.14 //
children.translated_text: those who are distinguished by the cultivation of loving-kindness — they go to the supreme destination. // Dhs_14.14 //

body.translated_text: Whom should a person honor?

children.translated_text: With an undisturbed mind and with a clear heart,

children.text: sarvadā dharmavaśagān dhīrān viprān bhajennaraḥ // Dhs_14.15 //
children.translated_text: a person should always honor the wise and learned who are devoted to the Dharma. // Dhs_14.15 //
Those who have taken refuge in truth alone, having abandoned the impurity of the mind through mindfulness,

children.text: bhāvābhilāṣād viratā muktā niḥsaṃśayaṃ hi te // Dhs_14.16 //
children.translated_text: who have ceased from longing for existence — they are liberated, without doubt. // Dhs_14.16 //
Always bound by suffering and happiness, deceived in many ways,

children.text: narā nidhanatāṃ yānti prāṇino mohavañcitāḥ // Dhs_14.17 //
children.translated_text: people go to death — living beings deceived by delusion. // Dhs_14.17 //

body.translated_text: Through which bad qualities is heaven not attained?

children.translated_text: Shamelessness, lack of moral dread, laziness, and bad companionship —

children.text: naitāni nākabījāni tebhyo rajyenna paṇḍitaḥ // Dhs_14.18 //
children.translated_text: these are not the seeds of heaven; the wise should not be attached to them. // Dhs_14.18 //
Those who are always shameless, lacking moral dread, and following evil —

children.text: naraḥ prapātāt patati sa paścāt pratibudhyate // Dhs_14.19 //
children.translated_text: a person falls from the precipice, and only afterward awakens. // Dhs_14.19 //

body.translated_text: Those seized by anger, jealousy, and fear do not go to heaven:

children.translated_text: Anger, jealousy, torpor, and sloth, and a mind of faithlessness —

children.text: mohaśokabhayagrastā na svarga prabhavanti te // Dhs_14.20 //
children.translated_text: those seized by delusion, grief, and fear are not capable of reaching heaven. // Dhs_14.20 //
Drinking intoxicants, taking life, wrong views, and covetousness,
ill-will and cruel deeds — these are the causes of the instruments of destruction. // Dhs_14.21 //

body.translated_text: The fruit of wrong views is evil:

children.text: adarśanaṃ paraṃ śreyo na kudṛṣṭiḥ kathañcana /
children.translated_text: Not seeing what is truly beneficial, wrong views in any form —

children.text: kudarśanena saṃmūḍhāḥ prayānti narakaṃ narāḥ // Dhs_14.22 //
children.translated_text: people deluded by wrong seeing proceed to hell. // Dhs_14.22 //
Seeing what is not a cause as a cause, people always seeing the impermanent as permanent —

children.text: prayānti narakaṃ tīvraṃ mithyāvādena vañcitāḥ // Dhs_14.23 //
children.translated_text: they proceed to terrible hell, deceived by false speech. // Dhs_14.23 //
With painful brilliance, those devoted to wrong seeing,
conceited about their wisdom, delude other people. // Dhs_14.24 //
They fall indeed into the great ocean of the thicket of the darkness of delusion;

children.text: loke prakṛtiduḥkhe 'smin hetubhūtā hi te janāḥ // Dhs_14.25 //
children.translated_text: in this world of inherent suffering, those people are indeed the cause. // Dhs_14.25 //
The wise speak of the heating and casting of arrows;

children.text: cittatā yā tudatyante sarvataḥ kleśaparvataḥ // Dhs_14.26 //
children.translated_text: the mind is pierced from all sides by the mountain of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). // Dhs_14.26 //

children.text: kleśanāgād vimokṣo yo yasya jñānapuraḥ saraḥ /
children.translated_text: Liberation from the elephant of afflictions, whose forerunner is the lake of knowledge,
is attained by persons who see the truth, by forms free from attachment. // Dhs_14.27 //
This world, seduced by the understanding of each other,

children.text: na yāti paramāṃ śāntiṃ yatra mithyā na kathyate // Dhs_14.28 //
children.translated_text: does not reach the supreme peace where falsehood is not spoken. // Dhs_14.28 //

body.translated_text: The causes of hell:

children.translated_text: Restlessness, association with evil, laziness, and covetousness,

children.text: hetavo narakasyaite śīlasya hi vivarjanam // Dhs_14.29 //
children.translated_text: these are the causes of hell — and the avoidance of morality. // Dhs_14.29 //
Constant drinking of intoxicants, violence, coveting others' spouses,

children.text: lobhaḥ kūrā matiścaiva hetavo narakasya te // Dhs_14.30 //
children.translated_text: greed, and cruel intention — these are the causes of hell. // Dhs_14.30 //

body.translated_text: The causes of destruction:

children.translated_text: Slander, association with evil, wrong views, lack of restraint,

children.text: cāpalyaṃ manasaścaiva nāśayanti naraṃ sadā // Dhs_14.31 //
children.translated_text: and fickleness of the mind — these always destroy a person. // Dhs_14.31 //
Ignorance together with harshness, false speech and conceit —

children.text: na sukhāya bhavantyete asmiṃlloke na cāpare // Dhs_14.32 //
children.translated_text: these do not lead to happiness in this world or the next. // Dhs_14.32 //

body.translated_text: Who should be avoided?

children.text: yadyasau bhramati prāyo lokesmin kinna cāpare /
children.translated_text: If one mostly wanders in this world, why not the next?

children.text: yadyasambhrāmite loke ye ca duḥkhe nimajjati // Dhs_14.33 //
children.translated_text: Those who in an unshaken world sink into suffering — // Dhs_14.33 //
the <s>Tathāgatas</s> declare that to be the doing of ignorance.
False pride and excessive pride should be completely avoided;

children.text: parivarjyāḥ sadā hyete duḥkhavṛkṣasya hetavaḥ // Dhs_14.34 //
children.translated_text: these should always be avoided, for they are the causes of the tree of suffering. // Dhs_14.34 //
The wise, supremely generous, always delighting in the destruction of afflictions,
having cut all that bondage, go to the unfailing state —
beneficial at beginning, middle, and end, in this world and not in the other. // Dhs_14.35 //

body.translated_text: Through the cultivation of faults, destruction occurs:

children.translated_text: The cultivation of faults is seen to be the instigator of ignorance;

children.text: varjanīyāḥ sadā kleśāḥ sevyaṃ jñānamanuttamam // Dhs_14.36 //
children.translated_text: afflictions should always be avoided; supreme knowledge should be cultivated. // Dhs_14.36 //

body.translated_text: Through knowledge, liberation occurs:

children.translated_text: Through knowledge, liberation occurs — and not through afflictions, it is said here;

children.text: jñānāgninā hi dahayante kleśakāṣṭhā na śeṣataḥ // Dhs_14.37 //
children.translated_text: for by the fire of knowledge, the fuel of afflictions is burned without remainder. // Dhs_14.37 //

body.translated_text: Knowledge made of desire generates afflictions:

children.text: kleśaiḥ kimartha saṃruddhā jālinī viṣa(yai) ratā /
children.translated_text: Why are those ensnared by afflictions, the net delighting in sense objects?
Again, knowledge made of desire is an obstruction to the eye. // Dhs_14.38 //

body.translated_text: Censure of passion:

children.translated_text: By the medicine-food of the words of the Perfectly Awakened One, the commander-in-chief of the true Dharma
extinguishes and condemns the army of passion. // Dhs_14.39 //

body.translated_text: Auspicious speech should be employed:

children.translated_text: When auspicious speech has been uttered, it should be determined with effort;
for the four perversions shine forth like bubbles,
and the eight worldly dharmas likewise destroy the entire world. // Dhs_14.40 //

body.translated_text: The raft of knowledge is capable of crossing:

children.translated_text: The rivers born from the net of craving are difficult to cross with hundreds of discursive thoughts;

children.text: jñānaplavaṃ samāruhya taranti munayaḥ śivāḥ // Dhs_14.41 //
children.translated_text: having mounted the raft of knowledge, the auspicious sages cross over. // Dhs_14.41 //

body.translated_text: For whom does liberation not exist?

children.text: mūḍhā ye bhūtamanaso narāḥ kāmasya sevinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those deluded men of corrupted minds, who are servants of desire,

children.text: sadā ca pañcabhiḥ sthānairmuktisteṣāṃ na vidyate // Dhs_14.42 //
children.translated_text: always in the five stations — liberation does not exist for them. // Dhs_14.42 //
The fire that is kindled by improper mental attention
is countered by the rains of proper mental attention. // Dhs_14.43 //

body.translated_text: How can the blindness born of ignorance be removed?

children.translated_text: The blindness of people, long-standing and born of ignorance —

children.text: tadalpakāle jātena pradīpena na paśyati // Dhs_14.44 //
children.translated_text: a lamp produced in a short time does not illuminate it. // Dhs_14.44 //

body.translated_text: By the light of knowledge, the three poisons are destroyed:

children.translated_text: Those deluded by passion, of weak intelligence, ripen in hell;
but the knowledgeable do not perish, as they are going to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>;

children.text: trayo do(ṣā) vinaśyanti jñānalokena dehinām // Dhs_14.45 //
children.translated_text: the three poisons are destroyed by the light of knowledge for embodied beings. // Dhs_14.45 //
Therefore one should delight in complete knowledge, morality, and patience;

children.text: amūḍhānāṃ praṇaśyanti trayo doṣāḥ śarīriṇām // Dhs_14.46 //
children.translated_text: for those who are undeluded, the three poisons of embodied beings perish. // Dhs_14.46 //
By the fire of knowledge, the slow-witted, with the great splendor of affliction-fuel,
those emaciated by disease, dwelling in the domain of beds and wrappings — // Dhs_14.47 //

children.text: yatra yāti paraṃ vedaṃ manomohamayaṃ phalam /
children.translated_text: where the supreme fruition of the mind's delusion goes,
where manifold sufferings and manifold destinies are experienced — // Dhs_14.48 //
by the groups of five, beings are constantly — this is the doing of delusion;

children.text: trayo vā nirjitā doṣā yairidaṃ dahyate jagat // Dhs_14.49 //
children.translated_text: the three poisons by which this world is burned are conquered. // Dhs_14.49 //

body.translated_text: Through the practice of knowledge, happiness arises:

children.translated_text: Having extinguished that fire through the practice of knowledge, one becomes happy;
therefore, one should always burn the mountain of afflictions with the fire of knowledge;
for one whose mountain of afflictions has been burned, the state of happiness is established. // Dhs_14.50 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, the chapter on fetters. //
(15) The Chapter on Evil.
One who is ignorant of the fruit of evil obtains torment:

children.translated_text: The bitter fruit of evil being done should be known;

children.text: yo na jānāti mūḍhātmā paścāt sa paritapyate // Dhs_15.1 //
children.translated_text: one who, deluded in soul, does not know it is afterward tormented. // Dhs_15.1 //
A person obtains the fruit of all evil <s>karma</s>;

children.text: tasmāt pāpaṃ na seveta yadīcchet sukhamātmanaḥ // Dhs_15.2 //
children.translated_text: therefore one should not pursue evil, if one desires happiness for oneself. // Dhs_15.2 //
Even from a little, the most terrible hell — for one of evil mind;

children.text: muktyartha (tāni) pāpāni bhūyo mohavaśaṃ gatāḥ // Dhs_15.3 //
children.translated_text: for the sake of liberation from those evils, those who have gone under the power of delusion again — // Dhs_15.3 //
one should not trust in the smallness of evil that leads to hell;

children.text: alpena vahninā śaile dahayante sarvato drumāḥ // Dhs_15.4 //
children.translated_text: by a small fire on a mountain, all trees are burned. // Dhs_15.4 //

body.translated_text: There is no enemy equal to evil:

children.translated_text: Through evil one goes to hell, through evil one is burned;

children.text: pāpena naiti nirvāṇaṃ nāsti pāpasamo ripuḥ // Dhs_15.5 //
children.translated_text: through evil one does not attain <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — there is no enemy equal to evil. // Dhs_15.5 //

children.text: pāpācāro hi puruṣo na kvacit sukhamedhate /
children.translated_text: A person of evil conduct never flourishes in happiness;
therefore one should not pursue evil, if one desires happiness for oneself. // Dhs_15.6 //
Applauding the good is difficult for one on the evil path;
beings who commit evil deeds rejoice, being of fickle minds. // Dhs_15.7 //
Afterward the ripening is bitter — the torment of one of small understanding;
whence is the fruit of <s>karma</s> seen for one of emaciated body? // Dhs_15.8 //

children.text: tasmāt pāpaṃ na kurvīta kaṣṭā pāpasya vedanā /
children.translated_text: Therefore one should not commit evil — the sensation of evil is painful;

children.text: pāpaṃ pāpavipākaṃ ca pāpināṃ pacyate dhruvam // Dhs_15.9 //
children.translated_text: evil and the ripening of evil surely ripen for the evildoer. // Dhs_15.9 //

children.text: na hi pāpaṃ na pāpasya tasmāt pāpaṃ vivarjayet /
children.translated_text: For evil does not remain without its evil consequence; therefore one should avoid evil;

children.text: parivarjitapāpasya na pāpād bhayamasti hi // Dhs_15.10 //
children.translated_text: for one who has avoided evil, there is no fear from evil. // Dhs_15.10 //

children.text: svakṛtaṃ bādhate pāpaṃ parīkṣyaṃ naiva bhujyate /
children.translated_text: Self-made evil afflicts one; what is not examined is not experienced;

children.text: kalyāṇasya phalaṃ sādhu kaṣṭaṃ pāpasya pacyate // Dhs_15.11 //
children.translated_text: the fruit of virtue is good; the fruit of evil ripens painfully. // Dhs_15.11 //

children.text: kṛtvā tu puruṣaḥ pāpaṃ kalyāṇaṃ nānusevate /
children.translated_text: A person who has committed evil does not pursue virtue;

children.text: na śastrāgniprapātebhyo duḥkhaṃ syāt tādṛśaṃ nṛṇām // Dhs_15.12 //
children.translated_text: there is no suffering for people from weapons, fire, and precipices comparable to that. // Dhs_15.12 //
Just as wrongly pursued evil is reckoned among evils,
so for one who has avoided evil, who always has a virtuous mind — // Dhs_15.13 //

body.translated_text: <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is not far from the peaceful <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk):

children.translated_text: For an embodied being of peaceful speech, <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is not far away;

children.text: tīvrāt tīvrataraṃ yānti narāḥ kukṛtakāriṇaḥ // Dhs_15.14 //
children.translated_text: people who are evildoers go from severe to more severe. // Dhs_15.14 //
People who are doers of good go from happiness to greater happiness;

children.text: na hi tīvrasya pāpasya sukhaṃ phalamavāpyate // Dhs_15.15 //
children.translated_text: for the fruit of severe evil is not happiness that is obtained. // Dhs_15.15 //

children.text: sukhasya vā phala tīvraṃ viparītaṃ na pacyate /
children.translated_text: Nor does the fruit of happiness ripen severely in the opposite way;

children.text: anādimati saṃsāre sukṛtānāṃ phalaṃ sukham // Dhs_15.16 //
children.translated_text: in beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>, the fruit of good deeds is happiness. // Dhs_15.16 //

children.text: karmaṇāṃ sukṛtānāṃ ca tathā duḥkhaphalaṃ smṛtam /
children.translated_text: Of good deeds, likewise, the fruit of suffering is remembered;

children.text: pāpaṃ pāpānugaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ śubhasya ca śubhaṃ tathā // Dhs_15.17 //
children.translated_text: evil is seen to follow evil, and good follows good likewise. // Dhs_15.17 //

body.translated_text: The evildoer is reborn in hells:

children.translated_text: One of evil conduct, a hater of the good, is reborn in hells;
but for one who has avoided evil, who always has a virtuous mind — // Dhs_15.18 //
<s>Nirvāṇa</s> is within hand's reach — unseen, yet that is pure;
dharmas that are beneficial at beginning, middle, and end always give rise to happiness. // Dhs_15.19 //

body.translated_text: Therefore one should avoid evil:

children.translated_text: The fruit of evil <s>karma</s> is bitter at beginning, middle, and end;

children.text: tasmāt pāpaṃ sadā varjyamālambyañca śubhaṃ sadā // Dhs_15.20 //
children.translated_text: therefore evil should always be avoided, and one should always take hold of the good. // Dhs_15.20 //

body.translated_text: For one who has avoided evil, happiness is always established;

children.translated_text: in beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>, people are burned by evils again;

children.text: khedaṃ kasmānna gacchanti bālā mohavaśānugāḥ // Dhs_15.21 //
children.translated_text: why do fools, subject to the power of delusion, not feel distress? // Dhs_15.21 //
Evil is sweet at first but in ripening resembles fire. /
But a man who does evil is despised by the whole world.

children.text: śubhakārī sadā śāntastasmāt pāpaṃ vivarjayet // Dhs_15.22 //
children.translated_text: One who does good is always peaceful — therefore one should abandon evil. // Dhs_15.22 //
Abandonment of evil by the wise who show the truth:
Undesirable, harmful — seen in maturation as bitterly painful —

children.text: pāpaṃ pāpavipākaṃ ca tasmād dhīmān vivarjayet // Dhs_15.23 //
children.translated_text: evil and its evil fruition — therefore the wise one should abandon them. // Dhs_15.23 //

children.text: asti pāpaṃ dhruvaṃ pāpe pāpamasti na pātakam /
children.translated_text: There is certainly evil in evil; there is evil, not just sin.
Evil conduct leads to exhaustion; compassion leads to the ease of mind. // Dhs_15.24 //
Evil always resorts to evil; dharma likewise resorts to dharma.
This is declared and proclaimed by the wise who show the truth. // Dhs_15.25 //

body.translated_text: Those free from evil attain the supreme happiness:

children.text: acetanā dhruvaṃ bālā yeṣāṃ duścaritaṃ priyam /
children.translated_text: The foolish are certainly senseless — those for whom misconduct is dear.
But those who have abandoned evil go to the supreme destination. // Dhs_15.26 //
Exceedingly terrible in deception, certainly leading to evil —

children.text: mānuṣyaṃ durlabhaṃ prāpya yasya pāpaṃ priyaṃ bahu // Dhs_15.27 //
children.translated_text: having attained the rare human birth, one for whom evil is much beloved. // Dhs_15.27 //

body.translated_text: The difference in maturation of good and evil fruits:

children.text: pāpād virajyate yastu śubhe vātīva rajyate /
children.translated_text: One who becomes dispassionate toward evil or is excessively attached to good,

children.text: sa sukhāt sukhamāpnoti nivṛttiṃ vā prayāti hi // Dhs_15.28 //
children.translated_text: he attains happiness from happiness, or indeed goes to cessation. // Dhs_15.28 //
That man is fortunate who resorts to good deeds.

children.text: sa tvadhanyatamo loke yaḥ pāpamupasevate // Dhs_15.29 //
children.translated_text: But the most unfortunate in the world is one who resorts to evil. // Dhs_15.29 //
Ending in destruction at the beginning, middle, and end, despised by the good,
evil is seen to follow evil — it is destined for hell. // Dhs_15.30 //
One who does good attains happiness and goes to the divine world:
One who does good deeds and has controlled senses shines exceedingly in the world.

children.text: kāyasya bhedāt satataṃ devaloke sa jāyate // Dhs_15.31 //
children.translated_text: At the breaking up of the body, he is always born in the divine world. // Dhs_15.31 //

body.translated_text: The maturation of evil is supremely terrible:

children.translated_text: The fruit of wrongdoing is said to be wrongdoing that follows after.
Likewise the fruit of good deeds is seen to ripen in happiness.
Like a seed whose transformation is swift, the maturation is supremely terrible. // Dhs_15.32 //

children.text: nimittaṃ sadṛśaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ phalaṃ pāpasya karmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: The sign is seen to correspond to the fruit of evil karma.
A being is dragged by evil to lower realms as by fish-hooks. // Dhs_15.33 //
A fish may be freed from hooks, but evil is not freed from evil.

children.text: dina pīḍāpi pāpasya sarvathā duḥkhakārikā // Dhs_15.34 //
children.translated_text: Even the daily affliction of evil is entirely suffering-producing. // Dhs_15.34 //

children.text: amedhyasya yathā gandhaḥ pratikūlo hi dehinām /
children.translated_text: Just as the smell of excrement is repugnant to embodied beings,

children.text: śubhasya vāsanā ramyā vipraṇaṣṭasya durgatau // Dhs_15.35 //
children.translated_text: so the impression of good is pleasant — when it is destroyed, one goes to lower realms. // Dhs_15.35 //

children.text: vileṣu vāsanaṃ yadvat puṣpe naṣṭe pradṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Just as the scent in flowers appears even when the flower is destroyed,
so this evildoer moves about, always subject to the power of desire. // Dhs_15.36 //

body.translated_text: Who are the practitioners of good?

children.translated_text: One who is always lazy and untruthful does not deserve welfare.

children.text: anantā rajanī teṣāṃ (yeṣāṃ) pāpe sthitaṃ manaḥ // Dhs_15.37 //
children.translated_text: The night is endless for those whose minds are fixed in evil. // Dhs_15.37 //

children.text: prabhātaṃ rajanī teṣāṃ yeṣāṃ pāpe sthirā matiḥ /
children.translated_text: The night has dawned for those whose minds are firm in evil.
Non-envious, possessed of welfare, such men are practitioners of good. // Dhs_15.38 //

body.translated_text: One with little evil attains happiness:

children.text: ye na pāpātmano bhūtāste nityaṃ koṭacāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who are not evil-natured beings — they always walk on the summit.

children.text: alpabhārā yathā nāvā plavate na nimajjati // Dhs_15.39 //
children.translated_text: Like a lightly-laden boat, they float and do not sink. // Dhs_15.39 //

body.translated_text: From association with an evil friend comes suffering:

children.translated_text: Likewise a person with little evil floats and does not sink.

children.text: na pāpamitrasaṃsargāt puruṣaḥ sukhavān bhavet // Dhs_15.40 //
children.translated_text: A person cannot become happy through association with an evil friend. // Dhs_15.40 //
Having encountered an evil friend, one becomes consumed by all fire.

children.text: karmārambha vidhijño yo nityaṃ sūkṣmārtha (darśakaḥ) // Dhs_15.41 //
children.translated_text: But one who knows the method of undertaking action, always seeing subtle meaning, // Dhs_15.41 //

children.text: nāsau limpati pāpena paṅkena gaganaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: is not stained by evil, as the sky is not by mud.

children.text: aśrutaṃ puruṣaḥ śṛṇvan śrutañcāpi bhaved dṛḍham // Dhs_15.42 //
children.translated_text: A person hearing what is unheard, and what is heard becomes firm. // Dhs_15.42 //

body.translated_text: The mark of the wise:

children.text: pāpaṃ ca varjayed dhīmān pretya deveṣu jāyate /
children.translated_text: The wise one avoids evil and after death is born among the gods.
The discernment of qualities and faults — this is the mark of the wise. // Dhs_15.43 //

body.translated_text: The mark of the fool:

children.translated_text: Non-discernment of qualities and faults — this is the mark of the fool.

children.text: guṇeṣu guṇasañcāro doṣeṣu ca tathaiva ca // Dhs_15.44 //
children.translated_text: Moving among qualities as qualities, and among faults likewise. // Dhs_15.44 //

body.translated_text: The marks of the fool and the non-fool:

children.translated_text: One who always knows the truth of faults and qualities becomes a partaker of grief.
A man who does evil stands like an enemy to himself. // Dhs_15.45 //
Likewise, a man who does good proceeds like a friend.
This immortal one proceeds to the dark realms of hell. // Dhs_15.46 //
One whose intellect delights in evil, always intent on sense-objects,
fickle in the pleasure-garden of sense-objects, always following after passion — // Dhs_15.47 //
for a person whose intellect is not in dharmas, who is a partaker of suffering,
from the cause of great suffering's end, united with fire — // Dhs_15.48 //
we all, our evil exhausted, have come again to this world.
The fruit of good deeds is excellent, adorned with many virtues. // Dhs_15.49 //
The fruit of wrongdoing is suffering, said to be deceptive.

children.text: te vayaṃ sukhaduḥkhābhyāṃ bhūyāma bhavasaṅkaṭe // Dhs_15.50 //
children.translated_text: May we, through happiness and suffering, exist in the straits of existence. // Dhs_15.50 //
Whirled about by the wind of karma, like the waves of the ocean —

children.text: kṛtaṃ pāpeṣvamanasaḥ pāpaiḥ rakṣanti ye janāḥ // Dhs_15.51 //
children.translated_text: those who guard people from evils with inattentive minds regarding evils, // Dhs_15.51 //
they, of unwholesome conduct, go to hell because of that.

children.text: tasmāttu narakānmuktāḥ te gacchanti triviṣṭapam // Dhs_15.52 //
children.translated_text: But freed from those hells, they go to heaven. // Dhs_15.52 //
Not remembering that suffering, again subject to desire,
this mind becomes hardened, swinging with the swings of happiness and unhappiness. // Dhs_15.53 //

children.text: viyogo 'yaṃ parīghāto na ca duḥkhairna vidyate /
children.translated_text: There is this separation, this destruction — and it is not without suffering.
Connected with the wives of others, deceived by the senses, // Dhs_15.54 //

body.translated_text: subject to the noose of craving, one wanders in <s>saṃsāra</s>:

children.translated_text: A being wanders in <s>saṃsāra</s>, subject to the noose of craving.
From hell to the <s>preta</s>-world, from the <s>preta</s>-world to animal realms, // Dhs_15.55 //
from animal realms to the heavenly world, from heaven again to human birth.
Whirled about by a single karma, the world revolves like a wheel. // Dhs_15.56 //

body.translated_text: Everything is suffering:

children.translated_text: They do not come under the power of weariness, having come under the power of habit.

children.text: rakṣanti nākabhuvanaṃ virajyante tathā sukhaiḥ // Dhs_15.57 //
children.translated_text: They guard the heavenly world and become dispassionate toward pleasures. // Dhs_15.57 //
Whirled about by happiness from happiness, the wanderers wander.
Thousands of <s>padmas</s>, hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>padmas</s> of suffering — // Dhs_15.58 //

children.text: (tāni) duḥkhāni bhuṅktāni na ca kliśyanti bāliśāḥ /
children.translated_text: they experience those sufferings, yet the foolish are not distressed.

children.text: na sukhaṃ vidyate loke sarvaduḥkhaiḥ pariplutam // Dhs_15.59 //
children.translated_text: There is no happiness in the world — all is engulfed by suffering. // Dhs_15.59 //

body.translated_text: There is a cause of suffering:

children.translated_text: Living beings afflicted by delusion do not feel alarm.

children.text: duḥkhena khidyate bālo duḥkhahetau ca vartate // Dhs_15.60 //
children.translated_text: The fool is troubled by suffering yet continues in its cause. // Dhs_15.60 //

children.text: hetau śataphalaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ bījaṃ prati yathā phalaiḥ /
children.translated_text: In the cause, a hundredfold fruit is seen — as fruit is to seed.
Living beings, bound by the whip of happiness and suffering, following the three existences, // Dhs_15.61 //
do not go to the supreme security, free from all suffering.

children.text: smaryate (hi) yadā duḥkhaṃ tadā vidhyati dehinam // Dhs_15.62 //
children.translated_text: When suffering is remembered, then it pierces the embodied one. // Dhs_15.62 //
But when suffering is forgotten, they act without distress.

children.text: nārakaṃ tu sadā duḥkhaṃ smṛtaṃ bhavati dehibhiḥ // Dhs_15.63 //
children.translated_text: The suffering of hell is always remembered by embodied beings. // Dhs_15.63 //
Then this dark happiness stands by inference.

children.text: tadeva viditaṃ matvā jagat sarva samanvitam // Dhs_15.64 //
children.translated_text: Knowing that very thing to be understood, the entire world is pervaded by it. // Dhs_15.64 //
Let the intellect be set on what is beneficial, turned away from faults.
Life passes, fickle in its momentary authority. // Dhs_15.65 //
And karmas are exhausted — therefore one should be devoted to what is beneficial.

children.text: cittavegaṃ manaḥ sarva jīvitaṃ veti vartate // Dhs_15.66 //
children.translated_text: All mental velocity, life passes and moves on. // Dhs_15.66 //

body.translated_text: The wise one does not fear future suffering:

children.translated_text: Therefore a discerning person should not do evil for the sake of livelihood.

children.text: anāgatasya duḥkhasya na vibheti mahājanaḥ // Dhs_15.67 //
children.translated_text: The great person does not fear future suffering. // Dhs_15.67 //
By which his evil ripens — fallen under the power of delusion-evil —
deluded by evil dharmas, unwholesome, devoid of the bright. // Dhs_15.68 //

body.translated_text: The fool, through the power of evil, goes to hell:

children.text: nīyate narakaṃ mūḍho yatra pāpaṃ vipacyate /
children.translated_text: The fool is led to hell where evil ripens.

children.text: yasya pāpād bhayaṃ nāsti sa pāpaṃ kurute bahu // Dhs_15.69 //
children.translated_text: One who has no fear of evil does much evil. // Dhs_15.69 //
Burned by endless evil, he afterward reaches hell.
Just as even a minute spark of fire suffices for burning. // Dhs_15.70 //

body.translated_text: Those free from evil desire happiness:

children.translated_text: Through various evils too, the unintelligent go to hell.
Therefore fearlessness of evil should be practiced by one who desires happiness. // Dhs_15.71 //
Violence, false speech, unchastity — these further produce happiness.
Shamelessness, unconscientiousness, restlessness, association with evil friends — // Dhs_15.72 //

body.translated_text: Evil is like poison and fire:

children.translated_text: These are indeed like poison and fire — one should guard against them with effort.

children.text: duḥkhaṃ hi māradharmo 'yaṃ sukhaṃ dharmasamantataḥ // Dhs_15.73 //
children.translated_text: For this is the dharma of <s>Māra</s>, which is suffering; happiness is dharma on all sides. // Dhs_15.73 //

body.translated_text: The marks of happiness and suffering:

children.translated_text: The wise who know the truth know the marks of happiness and suffering.

children.text: satyaṃ dānaṃ tathā kṣāntiḥ sadā cāpāpamitratā /
children.translated_text: Truth, giving, and patience, and always non-association with evil friends,
loving-kindness always toward those oppressed — this is the way to heaven. // Dhs_15.74 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the fifteenth chapter on evil. //
(16) Chapter on Hells:
The eight hell-fires:

children.translated_text: Having done evil deeds, beings who live crookedly —

children.text: yā gatiḥ pretya gacchantī tānapāyān (hi me) śṛṇu // Dhs_16.1 //
children.translated_text: the destination to which they go after death — hear from me about those lower realms. // Dhs_16.1 //

children.text: sañjīvaṃ kāmasūtraṃ ca sampātaṃ dvau ca rauravau /
children.translated_text: <s>Sañjīva</s>, <s>Kāmasūtra</s>, <s>Sampāta</s>, and the two <s>Raurvas</s>,
<s>Tamopara</s>, <s>Mahācitra</s>, <s>Patana</s>, and <s>Pratāpana</s> — // Dhs_16.2 //
these are the eight hells, declared to be hard to cross,
filled with terrible karma, each causing disturbance. // Dhs_16.3 //

body.translated_text: The terrifying nature of the hell-fires:

children.translated_text: With four sectors and four gates, divided and measured in portions,
surrounded by iron walls, afflicted with iron. // Dhs_16.4 //
The ground is of heated iron, blazing, radiating intense heat,
burning for many hundreds of <s>yojanas</s> with its own flame exceedingly. // Dhs_16.5 //
Terrible, subduing desire, full of flames, difficult to approach,
hair-raising in their form — they declare them to be painful and terrifying. // Dhs_16.6 //

body.translated_text: Those who have fallen into hell are exceedingly tormented:

children.translated_text: They fall into hell, feet upward, faces downward —
those who slander sages, the restrained, and ascetics. // Dhs_16.7 //

children.text: te punastatra pacyante taptāmbhasi kṛtā iva /
children.translated_text: They are then cooked there like things placed in boiling water.

children.text: krandamānā divārātrau, nagā vāteritā iva // Dhs_16.8 //
children.translated_text: Crying out day and night, like trees shaken by the wind, // Dhs_16.8 //
they emit great cries, tormented by intense sufferings.

children.text: sarvā diśaśca dhāvanti nārakaiḥ puruṣairdrutāḥ // Dhs_16.9 //
children.translated_text: They run in all directions, driven by the men of hell. // Dhs_16.9 //
A person, having deluded regarding meaning through wrong views, covered by the noose of delusion,
reaches terrible hell, enveloped by the ocean of causes. // Dhs_16.10 //
A person whose all is burned by wrong views, the lowest of men,

children.text: tathā baddho 'sti narake mānināṃ ghorakāraṇam // Dhs_16.11 //
children.translated_text: is thus bound in hell — the terrible reason for the proud. // Dhs_16.11 //
Those persons of dull intellect who have come under the power of wrong views —

children.text: te sarve narakaṃ yānti cittairhi parivañcitāḥ // Dhs_16.12 //
children.translated_text: they all go to hell, deceived by their minds. // Dhs_16.12 //

body.translated_text: The fruit of evil deeds:

children.translated_text: Whatever evil was done by you formerly, following the mind's inclination —
you experience its fruit, O fool — you shall obtain the supreme maturation. // Dhs_16.13 //
Stealing goods and coveting the wives of others —
beings are always diminished, deceived by their own minds. // Dhs_16.14 //
You have come under the power of that karma-fruition alone.

children.text: kiṃ krandasi svayaṃ kṛtvā kukarma puruṣādhama! // Dhs_16.15 //
children.translated_text: Why do you cry, having done evil karma yourself, O lowest of men! // Dhs_16.15 //

children.text: ye narāḥ kukṛtaṃ kṛtvā pañcatvaṃ yāntyamedhasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those dull-witted men who, having done evil deeds, go to death —

children.text: yeṣāṃ tu niṣphalaṃ janma bījamuptaṃ yathoṣare // Dhs_16.16 //
children.translated_text: those whose birth is fruitless, like seed sown in barren ground. // Dhs_16.16 //
One who serves desires mixed with little sweetness and bitter in fruition,

children.text: sevate yastvasau mūḍhaḥ sa yāti tamaso tamaḥ // Dhs_16.17 //
children.translated_text: that fool goes from darkness to darkness. // Dhs_16.17 //
What have you done, O fool, desiring the happiness of sons and wives?
You will burn alone in hell, deceived by the fruit of your own <s>karma</s>. // Dhs_16.18 //

body.translated_text: For whom is life difficult?

children.translated_text: A person subject to the power of sons and wives serves what is difficult;

children.text: sa yāti narakatvaṃ (ca) pāpaṃ tadanubhūyate // Dhs_16.19 //
children.translated_text: he goes to the state of hell, and evil is experienced. // Dhs_16.19 //

children.text: na dārā na sutā nārtha na mitrāṇi kathañcana /
children.translated_text: Neither wives, nor sons, nor wealth, nor friends in any way
protect one when the time of death has arrived. // Dhs_16.20 //
For those whose minds are defiled, deceived by craving —
how can there be companionship for them? Why do you torment yourself? // Dhs_16.21 //
You have been carried away by former sense objects, deceived by craving;

children.text: kiṃ krandasi svayaṃ kṛtvā kukṛtaṃ mūḍhacetanaḥ // Dhs_16.22 //
children.translated_text: why do you weep, having yourself committed evil, O deluded one? // Dhs_16.22 //

children.text: na tathāgnirna śastrāṇi na viṣaṃ nārayaḥ sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Neither fire, nor weapons, nor poison, nor enemies standing ready

children.text: bādhate puruṣaṃ loke yathā duṣkṛtyamātmajam // Dhs_16.23 //
children.translated_text: harm a person in the world as much as one's own evil deed. // Dhs_16.23 //

body.translated_text: The wheel of existence is like the nest-dwelling of birds

children.text: digbhāge hi yathā gatvā saṃśrayante vanaspatīn /
children.translated_text: Just as birds, having gone to the directions, take shelter in trees,
and then at the appointed time depart — so too is the assembly of living beings. // Dhs_16.24 //
Having destroyed another's property and transgressed against the world,

children.text: kiṃ karotyaśubhaṃ karma mohena parivañcitaḥ // Dhs_16.25 //
children.translated_text: what does one do with unwholesome <s>karma</s>, deceived by delusion? // Dhs_16.25 //

children.text: yena yāti parāṃ śāntiṃ yena yātyasurālayam /
children.translated_text: By which one goes to supreme peace, or by which one goes to the abode of <s>asuras</s> —

children.text: tatra hetuḥ paraṃ mohastamasāmapi yat tamaḥ // Dhs_16.26 //
children.translated_text: therein the supreme cause is delusion, which is the darkness of darknesses. // Dhs_16.26 //

body.translated_text: Evil done for the sake of family causes one to fall into hell

children.translated_text: Dragged to the abode of hell by nooses made of sons and wives —
that for whose sake evil is committed by you who are deceived in mind. // Dhs_16.27 //
Friends, sons, parents — what use are relatives and kinsmen
for whose sake evil was committed by you of dull understanding? // Dhs_16.28 //

children.text: nūnamātmā na te kānto babhūva narabhūmiṣu /
children.translated_text: Surely your own self was not dear to you in human births,

children.text: yena tvayā kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ putrārthena narādhamaḥ // Dhs_16.29 //
children.translated_text: since you committed evil for the sake of your sons, O lowest of men! // Dhs_16.29 //
One who has committed evil before and does not repent afterward —

children.text: sa yāti narakaṃ ghoraṃ putrakāraṇavañcitaḥ // Dhs_16.30 //
children.translated_text: he goes to a terrible hell, deceived by the excuse of children. // Dhs_16.30 //

body.translated_text: The fruit of evil <s>karma</s>

children.text: kiṃ kariṣyanti putrāste kiṃ dārāḥ kiṃ ca bāndhavāḥ /
children.translated_text: What will your sons do? What will your wives? What will your kinsmen?
You will burn in the beginningless hell — that fire drives you through <s>karma</s>. // Dhs_16.31 //
Having yourself committed unwholesome <s>karma</s> that gives rise to unhappiness — O blameless one,
you are tormented — even vainly supported — afterward deceived by delusion. // Dhs_16.32 //
Following passion and hatred, deceived by delusion,

children.text: aghaṃ prayānti te sarve putradārasukhārthinaḥ // Dhs_16.33 //
children.translated_text: all those desiring the happiness of sons and wives go to misfortune. // Dhs_16.33 //
Burned by both internal and external fire,
burned by suffering in hell through evil <s>karma</s>. // Dhs_16.34 //

children.text: vaśaṃ prāptāḥ svacittasya sarva eva viḍambitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having come under the power of one's own mind, all are completely mocked;

children.text: kiṃ krandasi vṛthā nāde vahninā paritāpitaḥ // Dhs_16.35 //
children.translated_text: why do you weep in vain, O wretch, tormented by fire? // Dhs_16.35 //

body.translated_text: The fruit that follows evil is seen

children.translated_text: Now, if you think you have committed evil actions —

children.text: durmate tatra mā kranda kiṃ vṛthā paridevase // Dhs_16.36 //
children.translated_text: O evil-minded one, do not weep there! Why do you lament in vain? // Dhs_16.36 //
The fool is protected in evils; one is protected in causes that are impure;
the fruit that follows evil is seen, born from causes and conditions. // Dhs_16.37 //

children.text: kasmānna sevito dharmaḥ pāpañca nahi varjitam /
children.translated_text: Why was the Dharma not served? And why was evil not avoided?

children.text: pāpād bahiśca puruṣo narakaṃ naiva paśyati // Dhs_16.38 //
children.translated_text: A person who is outside evil does not see hell at all. // Dhs_16.38 //

children.text: yo na vindanti mūḍhātmā phalaṃ pāpasya karttṛkam /
children.translated_text: The deluded one who does not perceive the fruit of committing evil —

children.text: so 'vaśyaṃ labhate doṣān kathaṃ bhokṣyasi durmate // Dhs_16.39 //
children.translated_text: he will certainly obtain the faults. How will you endure, O evil-minded one? // Dhs_16.39 //
Deceived by evil before, one is burned by evil;

children.text: na kariṣyasi pāpāni tvaduḥkhenaiva yāsyasi // Dhs_16.40 //
children.translated_text: you will not commit evils — for you will go through your own suffering alone. // Dhs_16.40 //
You have committed evils, never anything wholesome;

children.text: pāpena dahyate tasmādaśubhe na manaḥ kṛthāḥ // Dhs_16.41 //
children.translated_text: therefore you are burned by evil — do not set your mind on the unwholesome. // Dhs_16.41 //

body.translated_text: What is more suffering than suffering?

children.translated_text: There is no suffering greater than this — that one serves evil;

children.text: tasmāt pāpaṃ na seveta yadi duḥkhaṃ na vāñchasi // Dhs_16.42 //
children.translated_text: therefore one should not serve evil if one does not desire suffering. // Dhs_16.42 //

body.translated_text: The frank speech of family members

children.translated_text: In his inner heart is an image, but peace is not found;
we are objects of compassion, yet compassion is not in our hearts. // Dhs_16.43 //
Whatever much evil was done by you, covered by delusion —

children.text: tad vaḥ pradhāvate gāḍhaṃ na ca ye tatra hetavaḥ // Dhs_16.44 //
children.translated_text: that pursues you intensely, yet we are not the causes therein. // Dhs_16.44 //

children.text: śīlaṃ na rakṣitaṃ mūḍha pāpaṃ ca bahu sañcitam /
children.translated_text: Morality was not guarded, O fool, and much evil was accumulated;
this is the fruit of the evil that has arisen, now at hand. // Dhs_16.45 //

children.text: na vayaṃ kāraṇaṃ tatra yūyameva hi kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: We are not the cause therein — you yourselves are the cause;

children.text: yaḥ pāpaṃ kurute karma sa hetustasya karmaṇaḥ // Dhs_16.46 //
children.translated_text: one who commits evil <s>karma</s> is the cause of that <s>karma</s>. // Dhs_16.46 //
Whatever evil was committed by you, mocked by the curse of craving —

children.text: tad vo prapadyate ghoraṃ kimasmān paribhāṣata // Dhs_16.47 //
children.translated_text: that terrible thing approaches you. Why do you abuse us? // Dhs_16.47 //

children.text: nākṛtaṃ pacyate pāpaṃ na pāpaṃ syādahetukam /
children.translated_text: Evil that was not committed does not ripen; nor would there be evil without a cause;

children.text: yena yaddhi kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tasya tat paripacyate // Dhs_16.48 //
children.translated_text: whatever evil was committed by whomever — that ripens for him. // Dhs_16.48 //

body.translated_text: The sinner goes to hell

children.translated_text: So you, devoid of right action, deceived by drinking liquor,

children.text: patitā narake tīvre kiṃ vṛthā paritapyatha // Dhs_16.49 //
children.translated_text: have fallen into a terrible hell — why do you torment yourselves in vain? // Dhs_16.49 //
You who were devoted to desires have come to a terrible hell;

children.text: kāraṇeṣvapi tīvreṣu kiṃ tathā paritapyatha // Dhs_16.50 //
children.translated_text: even amid intense torments, why do you thus torment yourselves? // Dhs_16.50 //
When evil deeds were committed by you, deluded by desire,

children.text: tadā kasmānna nikṛṣṭaṃ kimadya paritapyatha // Dhs_16.51 //
children.translated_text: why then was it not considered base? Why do you now torment yourselves? // Dhs_16.51 //
Hell has been taught as the cause of false speech;

children.text: heturvai sevitaṃ pūrva niṣphalaṃ paridevatha // Dhs_16.52 //
children.translated_text: the cause was indeed served before — you lament in vain. // Dhs_16.52 //
Truth is not obtained by wealth, nor is it attained through difficulty;

children.text: tasmāt satyaṃ parityajya mṛṣāvādeṣu rajyase // Dhs_16.53 //
children.translated_text: therefore, having abandoned truth, you delight in false speech. // Dhs_16.53 //
In the past, evil was cherished by you of deluded mind;
the evil deed committed by you — the misdeed — ripens. // Dhs_16.54 //
When evil is exhausted, one is freed — hell is not found;
wailing people are never freed in any way. // Dhs_16.55 //

body.translated_text: The doer of evil experiences the fruit himself

children.text: kiṃ krandatha vṛthā mūḍhā vañcitāḥ svena karmaṇā /
children.translated_text: Why do you fools weep in vain, deceived by your own <s>karma</s>?

children.text: muñcitā vañcitā bālā vṛthā krandantyabuddhayaḥ // Dhs_16.56 //
children.translated_text: Released but deceived, the foolish ones of no understanding weep in vain. // Dhs_16.56 //
By those harmful in the guise of helpers, by enemies in the guise of friends,

children.text: vipralabdho 'si bho martya! gacchannasi mahat tamaḥ // Dhs_16.57 //
children.translated_text: you have been deceived, O mortal! You are going to the great darkness. // Dhs_16.57 //

children.text: nānyaḥ śatruryathā karma duṣkṛtaṃ tava pāpakam /
children.translated_text: There is no enemy like your own evil, wicked <s>karma</s>;
by threefold <s>karma</s>, you are led to the abode of <s>Yama</s>. // Dhs_16.58 //
Why are you then so foolish, deceived by those called 'sons'?

children.text: na dānādiṣu buddhistaiḥ kṛtā (te) mohavañcitā // Dhs_16.59 //
children.translated_text: No understanding about giving and the like was given by those deceived by delusion. // Dhs_16.59 //
From this world to the next world, like a snake on the back of enemies,
the first enemy among enemies, the demonstrator of all evil. // Dhs_16.60 //
Resembling poison, fire, and weapons! You yourself committed the evil deed;
the <s>karma</s> committed by you — you yourself will experience it. // Dhs_16.61 //

children.text: yasya śāntaṃ sadā cittaṃ viṣayairyo na hanyate /
children.translated_text: One whose mind is always peaceful, who is not destroyed by sense objects —
such ones do not go to this condition. Do you not see this? // Dhs_16.62 //

children.text: narakasya dhvaniṃ śrutvā kathaṃ krandasi durmate! /
children.translated_text: Having heard the sound of hell, why do you weep, O evil-minded one?

children.text: kiṃ punaryatra vahnistvāṃ dhakṣyati śuṣkakāṣṭhavat // Dhs_16.63 //
children.translated_text: What then when the fire will burn you like dry wood? // Dhs_16.63 //

children.text: na dagdhā vahninā ye ca dagdhāste kukṛtaiḥ svakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those not burned by fire — but they are burned by their own evil deeds;

children.text: vahnistu śāmyate kvāpi duṣkṛtāgnirna śāmyati // Dhs_16.64 //
children.translated_text: fire is extinguished somewhere, but the fire of evil deeds is never extinguished. // Dhs_16.64 //
Fire does not reach the world's end, nor does a person touched by fire die;

children.text: kukṛtāgnimayaṃ pāpaṃ yad dhakṣyati hi tattvataḥ // Dhs_16.65 //
children.translated_text: but the evil made of the fire of evil deeds — that truly burns. // Dhs_16.65 //

children.text: kukṛtāgnividagdhā ye te dagdhā narake narāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those burned by the fire of evil deeds — those people are burned in hell;

children.text: pāpāgnivarjitā ye tu na teṣāṃ narakodayaḥ /
children.translated_text: but those free from the fire of evil — for them there is no arising of hell.

children.text: yadyātmanaḥ priyo nityaṃ vibheṣi narakād yadi // Dhs_16.66 //
children.translated_text: If the self is always dear to you, if you fear hell — // Dhs_16.66 //

children.text: vivarjaya svapāpāni tato duḥkhaṃ na yāsyasi /
children.translated_text: abandon your evil deeds, and then you will not go to suffering.
Those who always follow the power of delusion go into the realm of evil. // Dhs_16.67 //
You arrive at a terrible hell — why do you shed tears?

children.text: duḥkhaṃ duḥkhavipākaṃ ca duḥkhāntagamanaṃ tathā // Dhs_16.68 //
children.translated_text: Suffering, the fruition of suffering, and the going to the end of suffering — // Dhs_16.68 //
well-done <s>karma</s>, beautiful at beginning, middle, and end, ripens;

children.text: nātra loke tvayāpāpaṃ yatkṛtaṃ sukṛtaṃ (muhuḥ) // Dhs_16.69 //
children.translated_text: the evil that was committed by you in this world — not the good deeds many times over. // Dhs_16.69 //
You will now experience the fruit of that intense ripening;
the resemblance of cause and condition — the opposite is not conceived. // Dhs_16.70 //

children.text: hetuḥ kṛto yathā pūrva tathā phalamavāpsyasi /
children.translated_text: As the cause was made before, so you will obtain the fruit;

children.text: yathā tava tathānyeṣāṃ prāṇarakṣā prayatnataḥ // Dhs_16.71 //
children.translated_text: as for you, so for others — protection of life should be made with effort. // Dhs_16.71 //
Why were killings committed by you, follower of evil?
The wealth that was earned by people through the sacrifice of life — // Dhs_16.72 //
that <s>karma</s>, arising from its fruition, which was earned by you;

children.text: sarveṣāṃ dayitā dārāḥ prāṇebhyo 'pi garīyasaḥ // Dhs_16.73 //
children.translated_text: wives are dear to all, more weighty than life itself. // Dhs_16.73 //
Why then, dyed with passion, have you done harm?
The supreme corruption of the dharmas, generating delusion of the intellect — // Dhs_16.74 //
the drinking of the Dharma should be done by you, avoiding unwholesome <s>karma</s>;
that which arises from the poison of the tongue, causing all to lose trust — // Dhs_16.75 //
the evil of false speech should be avoided by you along with unwholesome <s>karma</s>.
Since you were attached to these five types of conduct — // Dhs_16.76 //

children.text: tasmāt saṃmukṣya mā rodi kiṃ vṛthā paridevase /
children.translated_text: therefore wipe away your tears and do not weep! Why do you lament in vain?

children.text: viṣayaṃ pāpakā dharmā yasmānnu parivañcitaḥ // Dhs_16.77 //
children.translated_text: Since you were deceived by evil dharmas and sense objects — // Dhs_16.77 //
therefore you arrive at a great hell, crowded with garlands of flame.

children.text: etat tṛṣṇāgninā sarva pradīptaṃ bhuvanatrayam // Dhs_16.78 //
children.translated_text: This entire triple world is set ablaze by the fire of craving. // Dhs_16.78 //

body.translated_text: One should be attentive in the practice of the Dharma

children.translated_text: Having seen the Dharma but not practiced it — why do you now torment yourself?

children.text: (śrutvā) te madhuraṃ cittaṃ kāmamandirakaṃ vacaḥ // Dhs_16.79 //
children.translated_text: Having heard your sweet mind, the words that are the mansion of desire — // Dhs_16.79 //
when great evil was uttered, the fruit thereof has come;

children.text: sa kṛtvā pāpakaṃ karma niyatā pāpavedanā // Dhs_16.80 //
children.translated_text: having committed evil <s>karma</s>, painful sensation is certain. // Dhs_16.80 //
Pitiable, crippled, wretched — why do you now torment yourself?
Through the exhaustion of <s>karma</s>, evildoers are freed from hell. // Dhs_16.81 //
Wailing and sinking, they are never freed in any way;

children.text: aniṣṭaṃ pāpakaṃ karma kṛtvā rogavaśe sthitāḥ // Dhs_16.82 //
children.translated_text: having committed undesirable, evil <s>karma</s>, they remain subject to disease. // Dhs_16.82 //

body.translated_text: The ignorant practice the unwholesome

children.text: paridevati yo mūḍho vṛthā sa paridevati /
children.translated_text: The fool who laments — he laments in vain;
one who knows the future fruit delights in present good. // Dhs_16.83 //
He does not wail in hell as you repent;

children.text: mayā kṛtāni karmāṇi phaladāni mamaiva hi // Dhs_16.84 //
children.translated_text: the <s>karma</s> done by me — they are indeed fruit-bearing for me alone. // Dhs_16.84 //
Burned by the enemy of disease, one has afterward come to hell;
the unwholesome ground of heedlessness for a being burned by passion. // Dhs_16.85 //
Bound by that noose, I have come to this terrible condition;

children.text: durācāraratānāṃ tu nṛṇāmasya phalaṃ kaṭu // Dhs_16.86 //
children.translated_text: for people who delight in evil conduct, the fruit of this is bitter. // Dhs_16.86 //
I am afflicted by ignorance — what I myself made is experienced by me;
I have come under the power of merciless, terrible evils. // Dhs_16.87 //

body.translated_text: How might there be liberation?

children.translated_text: How indeed might there be liberation from this ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> full of suffering?

children.text: duḥkhād duḥkhataraṃ karma mayedaṃ paripacyate // Dhs_16.88 //
children.translated_text: This <s>karma</s>, more suffering than suffering, ripens for me. // Dhs_16.88 //

children.text: sukhāvāptiṃ na paśyāmi kṣemaṃ vā narakasya me /
children.translated_text: I do not see the attainment of happiness or safety from hell for me.

children.text: jīvalokādahaṃ bhraṣṭo abuddha iva mārgataḥ // Dhs_16.89 //
children.translated_text: I have fallen from the world of the living, like one who has lost the path! // Dhs_16.89 //
This living being, become helpless, is surrounded by the distorted;
all the intermediate space is ceaselessly full of wreaths of flame. // Dhs_16.90 //
The directions and the three heavens and the earth are uninterrupted;
wretched, wandering in ignorance, suffering — I perceive no dwelling. // Dhs_16.91 //
For one tormented by razor-sharp blades, the face of the king is most terrifying;
for one being swept into the wilderness, devoid of any companion,

children.text: trātāraṃ nāvagacchāmi yo 'smād duḥkhāt pramocayet // Dhs_16.92 //
children.translated_text: I find no protector who would free me from this suffering. // Dhs_16.92 //
Powerless, helpless, suffering, scorched by fire —
I am led away, helpless, somewhere, bound by fetters on my arms. // Dhs_16.93 //

children.text: na vārthā nāpi mitrāṇi na putrā na ca yoṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Neither wealth, nor friends, nor sons, nor women

children.text: trāyante vyasanādasmāt kṛtaghnā bata te mama // Dhs_16.94 //
children.translated_text: protect me from this calamity — ungrateful, alas, are they to me! // Dhs_16.94 //

body.translated_text: For those who practice non-dharma, there is no refuge anywhere

children.translated_text: For one without joy, there is no happiness — I grasp suffering in every way;
for one bound by the noose of death, no refuge is perceived. // Dhs_16.95 //

children.text: saṃkruddhā iva te, krūrā bhaviṣyanti samantataḥ /
children.translated_text: They will be as if enraged, cruel, on all sides;

children.text: nirānandā diśaḥ sarvā vyālaiśca parivāritā // Dhs_16.96 //
children.translated_text: all the directions are joyless and surrounded by serpents. // Dhs_16.96 //
I would fall into hell by the very nature of my sin;

children.text: yacca yaccehaṃ paśyāmi jaṅgamaṃ sthāvaraṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: and whatever I see here — whether moving or stationary —

children.text: tat sarva vyākulaṃ caiva vahninā paridīpitam // Dhs_16.97 //
children.translated_text: all that is agitated and ablaze with fire. // Dhs_16.97 //
I find no refuge; I am without any companion;

children.text: ghore tamasi majjāsi sāgare ca hṛtaplavaḥ // Dhs_16.98 //
children.translated_text: you sink in terrible darkness and in the ocean, your raft lost. // Dhs_16.98 //
I cannot see the sky, the constellations, planets, and stars;
all this is reversed, surrounded by darkness. // Dhs_16.99 //
All the five senses are completely ceased;

children.text: krakacaistu tadā sarva śarīraṃ paripāṭayate // Dhs_16.100 //
children.translated_text: then with saws, the entire body is split apart. // Dhs_16.100 //
I find no refuge; desire will become bondage;
the masses of suffering increase on all sides. // Dhs_16.101 //
Again and again, the sensations born of the body intensify;
and sufferings increase, and one is without any companion. // Dhs_16.102 //

children.text: samīkṣya karmajaṃ nityaṃ dhyeyo hetuḥ punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having examined the karma-born [consequences] always, one should reflect on the cause again and again;
the elders speak firmly of happiness arising from the fruits of one's own karma. // Dhs_16.103 //

children.text: yat pūrva karaṇīyaṃ te tatpaścāt paricintyase /
children.translated_text: What should have been done before, you now contemplate after;
having been deceived by delusion before, why do you grieve now?

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ pāpakartturyaḥ kaṭukaṃ paripacyate // Dhs_16.104 //
children.translated_text: And for the evildoer, what more [can be said] — the bitter [fruit] ripens. // Dhs_16.104 //
Your suffering will arise from many causes of suffering;

children.text: trāṇaṃ naiva (ca) yatrāsti vinā karmaparikṣayāt // Dhs_16.105 //
children.translated_text: where there is no protection at all — except from the exhaustion of karma. // Dhs_16.105 //
Thus, through the destruction of truth, by the messengers of <s>Yama</s>, in many ways,
one is led to terrible hell, gone under the power of the noose of karma. // Dhs_16.106 //
Four-cornered, with four doors, divided into sections and measured,

children.text: pacyate yatra vivaśā nārakeyā hyanekaśaḥ // Dhs_16.107 //
children.translated_text: where the helpless hell-dwellers are cooked in manifold ways. // Dhs_16.107 //
By means of division, the many things you have said,
the defilement of the dharmas of beings — this fruit has come of that. // Dhs_16.108 //

body.translated_text: Those who practice slander go to hell

children.translated_text: They are always reduced to ashes by friends, one's own people, and kinsmen;
their intention is corrupted — slander, condemned by the good. // Dhs_16.109 //

children.text: tasmānna carito dharmaḥ paiśunyaṃ ca na varjitam /
children.translated_text: Therefore the Dharma was not practiced and slander was not avoided;

children.text: paiśunyaṃ saphalaṃ bhuktvā kimadya paritapyase // Dhs_16.110 //
children.translated_text: having enjoyed the fruit of slander, why do you grieve now? // Dhs_16.110 //
Released from the bow of the tongue, sharp, perilously risen —
harsh speech is seen as such — alas! such is its fruit! // Dhs_16.111 //
The being given to supreme harsh speech has come to terrible hell;
it has come from your tongue for your [undoing] — why do you now lament? // Dhs_16.112 //
A fire with thousandfold intensity, self-arising from the heart,
a fire of hunger and thirst, completely burns up the wind. // Dhs_16.113 //

body.translated_text: The interval of harsh speech and that of hell

children.translated_text: The distance between snow and fire, and that between <s>Meru</s> and a mustard seed —

children.text: tadantaraṃ jihvayoktyā narake jvalanasya ca // Dhs_16.114 //
children.translated_text: such is the distance between the utterance of the tongue and the fire of hell. // Dhs_16.114 //
The fire born of hell is found nowhere else;
but the fire of hunger and thirst is found even among the gods. // Dhs_16.115 //
For whatever reason the hellish fire is fierce,

children.text: na tathā sa prabhavati yathā vahnistadudbhavaḥ // Dhs_16.116 //
children.translated_text: it does not prevail as much as the fire born from that [speech]. // Dhs_16.116 //
Bound in earlier and later [statements], meaningless and incoherent,
what you boldly spoke — this is the fruit that has come of it. // Dhs_16.117 //

children.text: pareṣāṃ sampadaṃ dṛṣṭvā mama syāditi cintitam /
children.translated_text: Having seen the prosperity of others, you thought: 'Let that be mine' —
the fruit has come of the poison that arose as covetousness. // Dhs_16.118 //
You have been burned by the fire of hostility, O lowest of men!

children.text: dahanād dahanaṃ prāpto tapyase ca vikatthyase // Dhs_16.119 //
children.translated_text: Having arrived at burning from burning, you are scorched and you boast. // Dhs_16.119 //
Through the supreme delusion of hostility, for rebirth in hell,
you are bound by this very rope — O man, you cry out! // Dhs_16.120 //
You have been dragged by hostility and have come to terrible hell;
through the exhaustion of karma there will be liberation, and you will be freed from hell. // Dhs_16.121 //

body.translated_text: Speaking of non-dharma indeed burns

children.translated_text: Non-dharma in the form of dharma, sin in the form of the good —

children.text: yat tvayā kathitaṃ pūrva tat tvāṃ dahati nānalaḥ // Dhs_16.122 //
children.translated_text: what was formerly spoken by you — that, not fire, burns you. // Dhs_16.122 //
How, for those whose truth is destroyed, who desire neither dharma nor non-dharma,

children.text: deśitaṃ vivaraṃ pāpaṃ niyataṃ pāpagāmikam // Dhs_16.123 //
children.translated_text: is the sinful opening taught, which necessarily leads to sin? // Dhs_16.123 //
The dharma you abandoned, and the good people you censured,
what you acquired and cultivated — that now ripens for you. // Dhs_16.124 //
With the sense domain of craving, through the force of delusion always,

children.text: yataḥ sadharmavinayaiḥ kiṃ tathā paridevase // Dhs_16.125 //
children.translated_text: since [you did not heed] the disciplines of the true Dharma — why do you now thus lament? // Dhs_16.125 //
He would be ever an evildoer, gone under the power of the noose of delusion;

children.text: ki tapyase rodiṣi ca karma kṛtvā sudāruṇam // Dhs_16.126 //
children.translated_text: why are you scorched and why do you weep, having done terribly harsh karma? // Dhs_16.126 //
For one always deluded about causes and conditions regarding dharma and non-dharma,

children.text: prāpto 'si narakaṃ ghoraṃ nārakāgraṃ sudāruṇam // Dhs_16.127 //
children.translated_text: you have arrived at terrible hell, the supremely dreadful summit of hell. // Dhs_16.127 //

body.translated_text: Those who follow the power of desires go to hell

children.translated_text: By desires conjoined, by which no [proper] effort is made —
merit becomes tasteless karma — this fruit has arrived. // Dhs_16.128 //
Having exhausted through heedlessness, with a mind attached to happiness,

children.text: sukṛta narakaṃ yānti devāḥ kāmavaśānugāḥ // Dhs_16.129 //
children.translated_text: their merit, the gods go to hell, following the power of desires. // Dhs_16.129 //

body.translated_text: Those who slander the noble ones go to hell

children.text: āryāpavādakā ye ca ye ca karmaphaladviṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who slander the noble ones, and those who hate the fruits of karma —

children.text: te mṛtvā narakaṃ yānti ye ca mithyāvinītakāḥ // Dhs_16.130 //
children.translated_text: having died, they go to hell, and those who are falsely disciplined. // Dhs_16.130 //

body.translated_text: Dharma-deceivers are indeed hell-bound

children.translated_text: Those who sin in the maternal home, and others who are Dharma-deceivers —

children.text: teṣāmiṣṭakarā loke narakasya ca gāminaḥ // Dhs_16.131 //
children.translated_text: they who gratify the desired in the world are goers to hell. // Dhs_16.131 //

body.translated_text: Those devoted to sin experience suffering

children.text: ye cānye sukhasaṃsaktā nityaṃ pāparatā narāḥ /
children.translated_text: And those other people who are always attached to pleasure and devoted to sin —

children.text: duḥkhād duḥkhaṃ tu te yānti cittena parivañcitāḥ // Dhs_16.132 //
children.translated_text: they go from suffering to suffering, deceived by their own minds. // Dhs_16.132 //

body.translated_text: Blameworthy deeds cast one into hell

children.translated_text: Therefore one should never set one's mind on blameworthy deeds;
inferior, blameworthy deeds cast one into hell. // Dhs_16.133 //

body.translated_text: Therefore wholesome actions should be performed
One should always perform wholesome actions, with aspirations bound to the benefit of others;

body.text: (hitaḥ sadaivaṃ narakasya rodhī) / sevyo 'pavargo daśadharma eṣaḥ // Dhs_16.134 //
body.translated_text: always beneficial, a barrier against hell — this tenfold dharma of liberation should be served. // Dhs_16.134 //
// Thus ends the sixteenth chapter, on Hell. //
(17) Chapter on Hungry Ghosts (<s>Preta</s>)
How can there be happiness for the non-giver?
How can there be peace for the undisciplined? What fruit for the unsown?

body.text: adīpikā prabhā nāsti adānasya kutaḥ sukham // Dhs_17.1 //
body.translated_text: There is no light without a lamp; how can there be happiness for the non-giver? // Dhs_17.1 //

children.translated_text: Indeed there is no peace of heart for the embodied being whose sight is painful;

children.text: dānena virahāt tadvat sukhaṃ pretairna labhyate // Dhs_17.2 //
children.translated_text: likewise, through the absence of giving, happiness is not obtained by the hungry ghosts. // Dhs_17.2 //

body.translated_text: The evildoer goes to the world of hungry ghosts

children.text: yaṃ pretya pretalokasya triloke ca yathādhamāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having died, in the world of hungry ghosts, and in the three worlds as the lowest —
the fruit made by stinginess, wandering about in supreme distress. // Dhs_17.3 //

children.text: na dātrā labhyate kiñcit kṛtanāśo na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Nothing is obtained from a giver; the destruction of what is done is not found;
beings are experiencers of the fruits of their own karma, enjoyers of karma. // Dhs_17.4 //
By your misdeeds, you are burned, established in the worlds of the dead;
here you are ablaze with the fire of hunger and thirst. // Dhs_17.5 //
When will there be a domain of happiness for us?

children.text: paridāhāt kadā cāsmāt parimokṣo bhaviṣyati // Dhs_17.6 //
children.translated_text: When will there be liberation from this burning? // Dhs_17.6 //

body.translated_text: One deprived of the path and non-path lives only in suffering

children.translated_text: I am bereft of path and non-path; the fruit of karma is unknown;
the fire of hunger and thirst is unknown, [yet its] manifestation is evident. // Dhs_17.7 //
With faces [covered by] the darkness of defilements, without hope, their livelihood abandoned,

children.text: tvaksnāyujālabaddhāḥ sma jīvāmo bata duḥkhitāḥ // Dhs_17.8 //
children.translated_text: bound by nets of skin and sinew — alas, we live in suffering! // Dhs_17.8 //

children.text: na trātā sarvato 'smākaṃ hanta kṛcchragatā vayam /
children.translated_text: There is no protector for us anywhere; alas, we have reached hardship;

children.text: utpanneṣu manuṣyeṣu khaṇḍitāḥ svena karmaṇā // Dhs_17.9 //
children.translated_text: though born among humans, we are ruined by our own karma. // Dhs_17.9 //
Why was the Dharma not practiced, accumulated in the lamps of jewels?

children.text: yaḥ karoti śubhaṃ nityamaśubhaṃ na ca sarvadā // Dhs_17.10 //
children.translated_text: One who always does what is good and never what is not good — // Dhs_17.10 //
goes by the path of equanimous vision, resorting to the stairway to heaven;

children.text: yeṣāmarthe kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ kleśayan mānasaṃ bahu // Dhs_17.11 //
children.translated_text: for the sake of those for whom much sin was committed, afflicting the mind greatly. // Dhs_17.11 //

children.text: anena te gatāḥ sarve bhavānāṃ trāsane sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: By this, they have all departed; you stand in the terror of existences;
you are bound by severe bonds given by <s>Yama</s>, established [in suffering]. // Dhs_17.12 //

body.translated_text: Being dragged by the rope of sin, one experiences [the fruits of] one's own deeds

children.translated_text: You have arrived at the terrible world of <s>Yama</s>, the darkness hard to overcome;

children.text: ihopabhokṣyase karma yattvayā kukṛtaṃ kṛtam // Dhs_17.13 //
children.translated_text: here you will experience the karma — the misdeeds done by you. // Dhs_17.13 //

children.text: svakṛtaṃ bhujyate bāla! pareṣāṃ naiva bhujyate /
children.translated_text: One's own deeds are experienced, O fool! The deeds of others are never experienced;
this one is being dragged here by the most terrible rope of sin. // Dhs_17.14 //
The fall from fire, weapons, and poisons is not as bitter // Dhs_17.15 //

body.translated_text: The fire of the world of hungry ghosts is the great fire of hunger and thirst

children.translated_text: as the fall from the fire of hunger and thirst;

children.text: na kṣaṇo nāpi hi lavo na muhūrto na śarvarī // Dhs_17.16 //
children.translated_text: not a moment, not an instant, not a short while, not a night — // Dhs_17.16 //

body.translated_text: We are beset by suffering

children.translated_text: where there would be happiness, there is death; we are always enveloped in suffering;
having arrived at greater suffering from suffering, having served the cause of suffering. // Dhs_17.17 //
Perhaps there will be liberation from suffering; there will be an arising of happiness;

children.text: notsave dṛśyate toyaṃ taḍāgeṣu ca śuṣyati // Dhs_17.18 //
