children.translated_text: but no water is seen at a festival, and ponds dry up. // Dhs_17.18 //

body.translated_text: Examination of the true nature of the fruits of karma

children.translated_text: The rivers have reached destruction; how should we run to this collection?
We, with our waters dried up, together with mountains, forests, and groves — // Dhs_17.19 //
we wander about the earth, always longing for water;

children.text: te vayaṃ dagdhatanavaḥ kṣutpipāsāhatā narāḥ // Dhs_17.20 //
children.translated_text: we, with bodies burned, people struck by hunger and thirst. // Dhs_17.20 //
We find no refuge; alas, we have arrived at calamity;
tormented by vajra-toothed, extremely sharp [beasts], and by crows and owls. // Dhs_17.21 //
Being attacked, I see no refuge that gives happiness;
this is the reflection of that karma that has come upon us. // Dhs_17.22 //
As we have done the karma, so has this fruit arrived;
bound by the wind of karma and cooked by the thread of karma. // Dhs_17.23 //

body.translated_text: Without the exhaustion of karma, there is no liberation

children.translated_text: We see no escape except from the exhaustion of karma.

children.text: yasya pāpānyaniṣṭāni vahnivat tāni paśyati // Dhs_17.24 //
children.translated_text: one who sees those evils as undesirable, like fire. // Dhs_17.24 //

body.translated_text: What is the world of <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) like?

children.translated_text: One goes to the abode of <s>pretas</s>, enveloped by the fire of hunger and thirst;
again and again, the sensations born from hell intensify. // Dhs_17.25 //
We are like a mountain ablaze with garlands of flames;

children.text: jvalitaḥ śāmyate śailaḥ salilenaiva sarvathā // Dhs_17.26 //
children.translated_text: a burning mountain is extinguished entirely by water. // Dhs_17.26 //
But this fire, comparable to an ocean, is not extinguished in the slightest;
at what moment it arose, accompanied by the wind of craving — // Dhs_17.27 //
the fire of <s>karma</s> burns us, surrounding us on all sides;
we, the evildoers, are devoid of wholesome dharmas. // Dhs_17.28 //
Having arrived at this world of <s>pretas</s>, deluded by the fruits of heaven,
the fire consisting of hunger and thirst, and the second fire born of fire itself — // Dhs_17.29 //

body.translated_text: Through evil deeds alone, people with mace-like bodies go to the abode of <s>pretas</s>:

children.text: mudgarāśimayā(dārāḥ) na putrāḥ na ca bāndhavāḥ /
children.translated_text: With mace-like bodies — neither wives, nor sons, nor kinsmen;
'I have been deceived by my own mind, cheated by <s>karma</s>. // Dhs_17.30 //
I have arrived at the abode of <s>pretas</s>, abandoned by friends and relatives;

children.text: na dārāḥ nāpi mitrāṇi na putrāḥ nāpi bāndhavāḥ // Dhs_17.31 //
children.translated_text: there are no wives, no friends, no sons, no kinsmen.' // Dhs_17.31 //

body.translated_text: Description of the fruit of evil deeds:

children.translated_text: 'One is rescued by the noose of <s>karma</s>, being led by the powerful;

children.text: nānyastrātā yathā karma trividhaṃ bhujyate mayā // Dhs_17.32 //
children.translated_text: there is no other savior — I experience threefold <s>karma</s>.' // Dhs_17.32 //

children.text: dānaṃ śīlaṃ śrutaṃ cāpi trividhaṃ parikīrtitam /
children.translated_text: 'Giving, morality, and learning — the threefold has been proclaimed;
enveloped by the net of delusion, I committed evil deeds here.' // Dhs_17.33 //

body.translated_text: Through good deeds alone comes liberation from the world of <s>pretas</s>:

children.translated_text: 'The fruit that has come from <s>karma</s> that was the cause —

children.text: yadi mucyāmahe pāpāt pretalokād durāsadāt // Dhs_17.34 //
children.translated_text: if we may be freed from evil, from the irresistible world of <s>pretas</s> — // Dhs_17.34 //

body.translated_text: one should avoid inauspicious evil deeds:

children.text: na bhūyaḥ pāpakaṃ karma kariṣyāmi kathañcana /
children.translated_text: never again will I commit evil <s>karma</s> in any way;
hot, with hot ripening, causing great affliction —
one should avoid those inauspicious evil deeds here.' // Dhs_17.35 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, the chapter on <s>pretas</s>. //
(18) The Chapter on Animals.
One should never harm another:

children.translated_text: Devouring, mutual killing in existence, binding, and imprisonment —

children.text: tiryagyoniṃ samāsādya tasmād drohaṃ vivarjayet // Dhs_18.1 //
children.translated_text: arriving at animal birth, therefore one should avoid harming. // Dhs_18.1 //
Those whose minds are stricken by delusion, devoid of morality and giving,
are born in animal births — fools mocked by craving. // Dhs_18.2 //

children.text: gamyāgamyaṃ na vindanti bhakṣyābhakṣyaṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: They do not know what is proper and improper, what is edible and inedible;
outside of what should and should not be done, obscured from Dharma and non-Dharma. // Dhs_18.3 //
Deluded by old age of the five senses, following the noose of craving,
seized by anger, jealousy, and drunkenness — people who descend to animal births. // Dhs_18.4 //
Mortals are stricken by searching, gods are stricken by heedlessness,

children.text: kṣuttarṣavyasanāḥ pretāḥ kāraṇātte ca nārakāḥ // Dhs_18.5 //
children.translated_text: <s>pretas</s> suffer from hunger and thirst, and hell-beings are tormented by punishment. // Dhs_18.5 //

body.translated_text: Who are destined for animal birth?

children.translated_text: thus the world is troubled by those manifold various misfortunes. // Dhs_18.6 //

body.translated_text: Those given to mutual killing are destined for animal birth;
One stricken by jealousy should not commit evil:

children.text: na kuryāda duṣkṛtaṃ karma mātsaryopahataḥ param /
children.translated_text: One should not commit evil <s>karma</s> while stricken by supreme jealousy;
beings stricken by jealousy go to the realm of <s>pretas</s> and animals. // Dhs_18.7 //

body.translated_text: Whose birth is fruitful?

children.text: teṣāṃ hi saphalaṃ janma teṣāṃ buddhiravañcitā /
children.translated_text: Fruitful is the birth of those whose understanding is undeceived;

children.text: te ca pūjyāḥ sadā sadbhiryeṣāṃ dharme sadā matiḥ // Dhs_18.8 //
children.translated_text: and they should always be honored by the good — those whose mind is always on the Dharma. // Dhs_18.8 //

body.translated_text: Those mounted on the chariot of knowledge attain liberation:

children.translated_text: Thus the world, whose essence is <s>karma</s> made by the three faults, wanders in what is hard to fathom;

children.text: karoti yastasya ca śuddhasattvo 'vamānanāṃ jñānarathāvarūḍhaḥ // Dhs_18.9 //
children.translated_text: one of pure nature, mounted on the chariot of knowledge, shows contempt for it. // Dhs_18.9 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, the chapter on animals. //
(19) The Chapter on Hunger.
People afflicted by hunger commit unwholesome deeds:

children.translated_text: In <s>saṃsāra</s>, suffering mostly arises from the hunger of the triple realm;
afflicted by which, beings commit what is unwholesome for themselves. // Dhs_19.1 //
The fire within one's own body, when studying hunger, properly consumes;

children.text: śeṣo dahati lokān vai kalpānala iva drumān // Dhs_19.2 //
children.translated_text: the rest burns the worlds, like the fire at the end of the cosmic age burns trees. // Dhs_19.2 //
This supramundane fire follows one who goes;
it is not seen to self-extinguish even in hundreds of cosmic ages. // Dhs_19.3 //

children.text: nānalasya hi tadvīrya kṣudhāyā yādṛśaṃ balam /
children.translated_text: No fire has such power, such is the force of hunger;
this entire triple realm operates with respect to food. // Dhs_19.4 //
Various thoughts of human origin would bewitch the world;

children.text: tāḥ sarvā bhojanārthāya bhavanti tribhavārṇave // Dhs_19.5 //
children.translated_text: all those exist for the sake of food in the ocean of the triple existence. // Dhs_19.5 //

body.translated_text: Suffering is indescribable:

children.translated_text: For one abiding in the intermediate state, being dragged by <s>karmas</s>,

children.text: dīrghāgamasya yad duḥkhaṃ na tad varṇayituṃ kṣamam // Dhs_19.6 //
children.translated_text: the suffering of the long journey — that is not possible to describe. // Dhs_19.6 //
For one ablaze with the fuel of ignorance, burning with heat,

children.text: garbhasthasya hi yad duḥkha na tad varṇayituṃ kṣamam // Dhs_19.7 //
children.translated_text: the suffering of one dwelling in the womb — that is not possible to describe. // Dhs_19.7 //
For one greedy for the taste of food, whose mind is always set upon it,

children.text: yad duḥkhaṃ paragṛddhasya na ca varṇayituṃ kṣamam // Dhs_19.8 //
children.translated_text: the suffering of one greedy for another's — that is not possible to describe. // Dhs_19.8 //
For one firmly tormented in mind, or one whose heart is scorched by desire,

children.text: yad bhavatyadhikaṃ duḥkhaṃ na tad varṇayituṃ kṣamam // Dhs_19.9 //
children.translated_text: the excessive suffering that arises — that is not possible to describe. // Dhs_19.9 //
Association with the unloved, and constant sense objects —

children.text: praṇaṣṭe hṛdi yad duḥkhaṃ na tad varṇayituṃ kṣamam // Dhs_19.10 //
children.translated_text: the suffering in one's lost heart — that is not possible to describe. // Dhs_19.10 //
For one scorched by the poison of craving, whose nature is constant searching,

children.text: āmṛtyu yad bhave duḥkhaṃ na tad varṇayituṃ kṣamam // Dhs_19.11 //
children.translated_text: the suffering in existence until death — that is not possible to describe. // Dhs_19.11 //
Unceasing, manifold suffering born from bad companionship,

children.text: apāyajanakaṃ yasya na tad varṇayituṃ kṣamam // Dhs_19.12 //
children.translated_text: that which generates the lower realms — that is not possible to describe. // Dhs_19.12 //

children.text: vyasanaṃ putradārāṇāṃ yad dṛṣṭ(vā) hṛdi jāyate /
children.translated_text: The calamity of sons and wives — having seen which, what arises in the heart,

children.text: narakāṇāṃ mahāmārgo na tad varṇayituṃ kṣamam // Dhs_19.13 //
children.translated_text: the great highway to hells — that is not possible to describe. // Dhs_19.13 //
For one scorched by hunger and thirst, blazing with fire,

children.text: yad duḥkhaṃ naṣṭamanaso na tad varṇayituṃ kṣamam // Dhs_19.14 //
children.translated_text: the suffering of one whose mind is destroyed — that is not possible to describe. // Dhs_19.14 //
For one constantly despised by friends, relatives, and dear ones,

children.text: yad bhavecchokajaṃ duḥkhaṃ na tad varṇayituṃ kṣamam // Dhs_19.15 //
children.translated_text: the suffering born of grief — that is not possible to describe. // Dhs_19.15 //
Clinging to wife, unsteady, with an affectionate heart,

children.text: yad duḥkhaṃ jīrṇakāyasya na tad varṇayituṃ kṣamam // Dhs_19.16 //
children.translated_text: the suffering of one whose body is decayed — that is not possible to describe. // Dhs_19.16 //
For one being carried away by death from this world, from one's own vital essence,

children.text: yad duḥkhaṃ jāyate vṛttau na tad varṇayituṃ kṣamam // Dhs_19.17 //
children.translated_text: the suffering that arises in one's circumstances — that is not possible to describe. // Dhs_19.17 //

body.translated_text: Through giving, the unwholesome is destroyed:

children.text: yat kurvantyaśubhaṃ bālā yacca gacchati durgatim /
children.translated_text: Whatever unwholesome deeds fools commit, and whatever leads to the lower realms —
that is carried away by giving, the wise declare. // Dhs_19.18 //

body.translated_text: Therefore, the mind should be set on good deeds:

children.translated_text: Counter-evil deeds should always be avoided;
the mind should be set on good deeds, adorned with giving and morality. // Dhs_19.19 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, the chapter on hunger. //
(20) The Chapter on Laziness.
Through laziness, knowledge is lost:

children.translated_text: Laziness, excessive cunning, hypocrisy, and harshness —

children.text: niyātabhūmayo dṛṣṭā jñānasya ca vivarjanam // Dhs_20.1 //
children.translated_text: these are seen as the grounds of certainty regarding the avoidance of knowledge. // Dhs_20.1 //
And association with the wicked, and avoidance of the good,

children.text: nāśasya hetavaḥ śaktā mithyādarśanameva ca // Dhs_20.2 //
children.translated_text: and wrong views too — these are the powerful causes of destruction. // Dhs_20.2 //
Exertion at the wrong place and time, by one who does not know what should and should not be said —
these are grounds of misfortune, and trust in such things too. // Dhs_20.3 //

body.translated_text: Grounds of misfortune:

children.text: yena tena ca samprītiḥ yatra tatra ca bhojanam /
children.translated_text: Friendship with anyone and everyone, eating anywhere and everywhere,
produces frivolity in the end, and self-praise likewise. // Dhs_20.4 //
Loss of firmness, lapse of mindfulness, and conflict with the ruler —

children.text: akrāntamṛtyavo hyete krūratā manasi sthitā // Dhs_20.5 //
children.translated_text: these are deaths that have not arrived; cruelty is established in the mind. // Dhs_20.5 //
One who does not know the truth of action and its fruit, excluded from Dharma and non-Dharma,
a person freed from the good, whose intention is to go to the precipice — // Dhs_20.6 //
laziness, excessive sleep, and indulgence in taste —
these are declared to be sources of hatred of people, as well as harsh speech. // Dhs_20.7 //

body.translated_text: Greed is the cause of dishonor:

children.translated_text: Excessive greed, dishonor, excessive pride, and fickleness,
pursuit of desires while abandoning Dharma — these are the kindlers of delusion. // Dhs_20.8 //

body.translated_text: Laziness is the root of all faults:

children.translated_text: Laziness is declared to be the root of the three faults here;

children.text: vīryārambheṇa duṣyante doṣā manasi sambhavāḥ // Dhs_20.9 //
children.translated_text: through the undertaking of vigor, the faults that arise in the mind are destroyed. // Dhs_20.9 //
Through the undertaking of vigor, the fruit is inevitably enjoyed;
the fruit of <s>karma</s> begun in accordance with proper truth is seen. // Dhs_20.10 //
Of this threefold <s>karma</s>, the fruit is declared to be threefold;
determined by the three groups, it is the trident accompanying the three existences. // Dhs_20.11 //

body.translated_text: Those who indulge in laziness go to a bad destiny:

children.translated_text: One who is fierce and pursues evil, and who also indulges in laziness,
a hater of Dharma, cruel — runs along the wrong path. // Dhs_20.12 //

children.text: yasya tasya ca santuṣṭo yasya tasya prakupyati /
children.translated_text: Satisfied with anyone and everyone, angry at anyone and everyone,

children.text: yatra tatra ca saṃsakto sa mūḍha iti kathyate // Dhs_20.13 //
children.translated_text: attached to this and that — such a one is called deluded. // Dhs_20.13 //
Laziness of one's own mind, maddened by the poison of heedlessness,

children.text: prapātaṃ taṃ ca saṃrabdhamavisaṃvādakaṃ param // Dhs_20.14 //
children.translated_text: that precipice, furious and supremely unreliable — // Dhs_20.14 //
those who, in the undertaking of vigor, are free from the stain of great evil and laziness,
those who enjoy liberation — those people are sharers of happiness. // Dhs_20.15 //
Laziness is that which makes all dharmas ageless and deathless;

children.text: tena doṣeṇa mahatā narā duḥkhasya bhāginaḥ // Dhs_20.16 //
children.translated_text: through that great fault, people become sharers of suffering. // Dhs_20.16 //
It is a companion that welcomes pleasure; therefore one should avoid it;

children.text: tena viddho hi puruṣaḥ svadhistutyaḥ samantataḥ // Dhs_20.17 //
children.translated_text: for a person pierced by it is praised by one's own place on all sides. // Dhs_20.17 //
For the lazy one of small share, whose mind is carried away by delusion,

children.text: kutsitaḥ svajanaiḥ sarvairna gatirvidyate śivā // Dhs_20.18 //
children.translated_text: despised by all one's own people — no auspicious path is found. // Dhs_20.18 //

body.translated_text: One who delights in laziness becomes sinful:

children.translated_text: Association with the evil of laziness, as well as torpor and sloth —
these become great fears for the obstruction of the gate of liberation. // Dhs_20.19 //

body.translated_text: These are the mansions of suffering:
Shamelessness, lack of moral dread, restlessness, and bad companionship —

body.text: duḥkhasyaitāni harmyāṇi tebhyo rakṣennu paṇḍitaḥ // Dhs_20.20 //
body.translated_text: these are the mansions of suffering; the wise one should guard against them. // Dhs_20.20 //

children.translated_text: Those overcome by laziness, without undertaking, whose splendor has departed —

children.text: socchvāsamaraṇaṃ teṣāṃ jīvitaṃ cāpi niṣphalam // Dhs_20.21 //
children.translated_text: their death comes with a gasp, and their life too is fruitless. // Dhs_20.21 //
People stricken by laziness are not alive even while living;
this laziness is considered to be worse than death itself. // Dhs_20.22 //

body.translated_text: Only those who have begun vigor cross the ocean of existence:

children.translated_text: Those sunk in the mud of laziness are sunk in the expanse of suffering;

children.text: ārabdhavīryā ye puṃsaste tīrṇā bhavasāgarāt // Dhs_20.23 //
children.translated_text: those persons who have begun vigor have crossed from the ocean of existence. // Dhs_20.23 //
One who, from laziness, is of weak vigor and always delights in evil —

children.text: sa jīvamāno 'pi mṛto mṛtastu narakāya saḥ // Dhs_20.24 //
children.translated_text: even while living, that one is dead; and being dead, one goes to hell. // Dhs_20.24 //

body.translated_text: Laziness is the cause of people's destitution:

children.translated_text: Those destitute people, equal to animals, are sharers of suffering,

children.text: parapiṇḍāśino dīnāḥ kausīdyaṃ tatra kāraṇam // Dhs_20.25 //
children.translated_text: living on others' food, wretched — laziness is the cause of that. // Dhs_20.25 //
Mostly, for the lazy, for those living off others' wives,

children.text: ratābhilāṣo 'tyadhiko maithune ca sadā ratiḥ // Dhs_20.26 //
children.translated_text: the desire for enjoyment is excessive, and there is constant delight in sexual intercourse. // Dhs_20.26 //
They, empty of essential purpose, devoted solely to food,

children.text: mṛtyukāle samutpanne dahyante svena cetasā // Dhs_20.27 //
children.translated_text: when the time of death arises, are burned by their own minds. // Dhs_20.27 //

children.text: śītoṣṇaṃ ca sahantyete kṣutpipāse tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: These should endure cold and heat, hunger and thirst likewise;

children.text: gātrāntā ca kriyā kāryā yātrā dharmāya sarvadā // Dhs_20.28 //
children.translated_text: bodily exertion should be done — the practice always for the sake of Dharma. // Dhs_20.28 //

body.translated_text: Therefore the mind should not be set on laziness:

children.text: na kausīdye matiṃ kuryāt kuśīle śīlakāmukaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who desires good morality should not set the mind on laziness;

children.text: saṃsāre sīdati nityaṃ na ca duḥkhāt pramucyate // Dhs_20.29 //
children.translated_text: In <s>saṃsāra</s> one sinks forever and is not freed from suffering. // Dhs_20.29 //

body.translated_text: One endowed with laziness becomes deceived by the world

children.translated_text: Despised among the good, the lazy one is deceived by the world;

children.text: vañcitaśca bhavatyante śarmaṇo vā vimucyate // Dhs_20.30 //
children.translated_text: And being deceived, in the end he is deprived of well-being. // Dhs_20.30 //

body.translated_text: Through Dharma comes liberation

children.translated_text: Endowed with vigor, possessing mindfulness, always devoted to solitude,
Freed from evil dharmas, one attains liberation through effort. // Dhs_20.31 //

body.translated_text: One should not set the mind on evil deeds

children.text: evaṃvidhā duḥkhaparamparā hi, sattvaḥ kukarmeṣu (matiṃ) na kuryāt /
children.translated_text: Such indeed is the chain of suffering — a being should not set the mind on evil deeds;

children.text: loke tridoṣānalasampradīpte, kuryāt parāṃ śāntikṛpā mṛte na // Dhs_20.32 //
children.translated_text: In a world ablaze with the fire of the three poisons, one should strive for supreme peace — not through compassion for death alone. // Dhs_20.32 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the twentieth chapter on Laziness (<s>Kausīdyavarga</s>). //

children.text: cittañca vāk tathā karma saṃyojanantu pāpakam /
children.translated_text: Mind, speech, and action, and evil fetters —
Hell, hungry ghosts, animals, hunger, and laziness — know these as ten. //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the second <s>Udāna</s>. //
Now the third <s>Udāna</s>

children.translated_text: (Compassion, giving, morality, patience, vigor too,

children.text: dhyānaṃ prajñātha nirvāṇo mano bhikṣuśca te daśa // )
children.translated_text: Meditation, wisdom, and <s>nirvāṇa</s>, mind, and the monk — these are ten.)

body.translated_text: (21) Chapter on Compassion (<s>Karuṇāvarga</s>)
Compassion acts beneficially like a mother

children.translated_text: Compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>) toward all beings, acting beneficially like a mother —

children.text: yāṃ samāśritya puruṣāḥ prayānti sukhamuttamam // Dhs_21.1 //
children.translated_text: Relying on it, people proceed to supreme happiness. // Dhs_21.1 //
A person who seeks compassion, devoted to the welfare of all beings,

children.text: pūjanīyaḥ satāṃ yāti pretya svarge ca modate // Dhs_21.2 //
children.translated_text: Is worthy of worship by the good, and after death rejoices in heaven. // Dhs_21.2 //
The compassionate one, ever-turning, devoted to the welfare of all beings —

children.text: tamevaṃ puruṣaṃ nityaṃ praṇamanti divaukasaḥ // Dhs_21.3 //
children.translated_text: To that person, the celestial dwellers always bow down. // Dhs_21.3 //

body.translated_text: One endowed with compassion goes to the heavenly realm

children.translated_text: One who is virtuous and endowed with compassion goes to the heavenly realm;

children.text: kṛpānvitaḥ sa puruṣo candramā iva śobhate // Dhs_21.4 //
children.translated_text: That person endowed with compassion shines like the moon. // Dhs_21.4 //

body.translated_text: One who seeks happiness should cultivate compassion

children.translated_text: Beings take refuge in it, free from sorrow and free from anguish;
Therefore compassion should be cultivated with effort by one who seeks happiness. // Dhs_21.5 //

body.translated_text: Through compassion, fame increases

children.translated_text: One whose speech, body, and mind are adorned with compassion —

children.text: tasya mitramayā lokā bhavanti yaśasā vṛtāḥ // Dhs_21.6 //
children.translated_text: For that one, the worlds become full of friends, surrounded by fame. // Dhs_21.6 //

body.translated_text: The learned one moistened by compassion goes to <s>nirvāṇa</s>

children.translated_text: For the learned one moistened by compassion, who always has gentle faculties,
Who strives for right view — <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not far away. // Dhs_21.7 //

body.translated_text: Those adorned with compassion beautify the human world like gods

children.text: manuṣyaloke te devā ye kāruṇyena vibhūṣitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those in the human world who are adorned with compassion are gods;

children.text: kāruṇyena daridrā ye te daridrāḥ satāṃ matāḥ // Dhs_21.8 //
children.translated_text: Those who are poor in compassion — they are considered poor by the good. // Dhs_21.8 //

body.translated_text: Mortals of gentle disposition are virtuous

children.text: mṛdvāśayā hi ye martyāḥ sādhuvat kāñcanopamāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those mortals who are of gentle disposition, like gold among the virtuous,

children.text: kāruṇyamakṣayaṃ yeṣāṃ sadā manasi vartate // Dhs_21.9 //
children.translated_text: In whose minds imperishable compassion always dwells. // Dhs_21.9 //

body.translated_text: Who become devoted to the Dharma?

children.text: te ca sattvāḥ sadodyuktā nityaṃ dharmaparāyaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those beings, always diligent, always devoted to the Dharma,
Whose hearts are illuminated by the lamp of compassion. // Dhs_21.10 //

children.text: na rātrau na divā teṣāṃ dharmo hi vinivartate /
children.translated_text: Neither by night nor by day does the Dharma turn away from them,
Whose delight in compassion in all circumstances is esteemed. // Dhs_21.11 //

body.translated_text: Compassion is a cool mind

children.translated_text: A mind cooled by compassion, devoted to the welfare of all beings,

children.text: bhuktvā saukhyaṃ nirupamaṃ paścād gacchati nirvṛtim // Dhs_21.12 //
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed incomparable happiness, afterward goes to liberation. // Dhs_21.12 //

body.translated_text: Compassion is imperishable wealth

children.text: kāruṇyaṃ munibhiḥ śastaṃ kāruṇyaṃ nirmalaṃ saraḥ /
children.translated_text: Compassion is praised by sages; compassion is a pure lake;
Compassion is the destroyer of faults; compassion is imperishable wealth. // Dhs_21.13 //
The foremost ornament of virtues, the destroyer of all faults —

children.text: kāruṇyārdrā hi paramaṃ prayānti dhanamacyutam // Dhs_21.14 //
children.translated_text: Those moistened by compassion proceed to the supreme, imperishable wealth. // Dhs_21.14 //
Since compassion is wealth endowed with the milk of sweetness,

children.text: na dāhaḥ krodhajastasya hṛdaye sampravartate // Dhs_21.15 //
children.translated_text: The burning born of anger does not arise in that one's heart. // Dhs_21.15 //

body.translated_text: Boarding the boat of compassion, people cross the ocean of existence

children.translated_text: Boarding the boat of compassion, with delight and devotion to firmness,
One is tossed about in the ocean of existence with the great waves of the three poisons. // Dhs_21.16 //

body.translated_text: The definition of compassion

children.translated_text: The supreme non-dual ornament among virtues, without the mind —

children.text: sādhūnāṃ dayitaṃ nityaṃ kāruṇyamiti kathyate // Dhs_21.17 //
children.translated_text: That which is always dear to the virtuous is called compassion. // Dhs_21.17 //
One in whose heart gentleness is melted like gold —

children.text: sa jano hi tu kalpānte duḥkhādāśu vimucyate // Dhs_21.18 //
children.translated_text: That person is indeed quickly freed from suffering at the end of the <s>kalpa</s>. // Dhs_21.18 //

body.translated_text: For the compassionate one, blessings grow

children.translated_text: One whose mind has been made a vessel by gentleness on all sides —

children.text: śreyāṃsi tasya rohanti kedāra iva śālayaḥ // Dhs_21.19 //
children.translated_text: Blessings grow for that one, like rice in a paddy field. // Dhs_21.19 //
That imperishable treasure in the house of the mind, belonging to all embodied beings,
Banishes poverty from people — the great inner disposition. // Dhs_21.20 //
For one of sharp senses who is unpeaceful, who reflects and investigates,

children.text: viṣayeṣu pramattasya duḥkhaṃ naiva pradhāvati // Dhs_21.21 //
children.translated_text: Who is heedless in sense objects — suffering does not rush toward him. // Dhs_21.21 //
With a mind of friendliness always, showing sympathy and compassion to others —
Those who know the truth of causes and fruits are freed from the noose of suffering. // Dhs_21.22 //

children.text: na saṅkalpe mano yeṣāṃ ramate doṣavarjitam /
children.translated_text: Those whose minds do not delight in mental fabrication, free from faults —
They, freed from the fear of faults, go to the unsurpassed state. // Dhs_21.23 //
Endowed with the practice of patience, having friends and fearless from all sides,

children.text: priyo bhavati loke 'smin paścād deveṣu modate // Dhs_21.24 //
children.translated_text: One becomes dear in this world and afterward rejoices among the gods. // Dhs_21.24 //

body.translated_text: The jewel of compassion should always be cultivated

children.translated_text: Like a mother, like a father — those people are to the whole world

children.text: dayāratnaṃ sadā yeṣāṃ manasi sthitamuttamam // Dhs_21.25 //
children.translated_text: In whose minds the supreme jewel of compassion always abides. // Dhs_21.25 //

body.translated_text: Compassion itself is the root of happiness

children.text: sukhasya ca paraṃ mūlaṃ kṛpaiva parikīrtitā /
children.translated_text: Compassion is proclaimed as the supreme root of happiness;

children.text: (hṛdi) yasya kṛpā nāsti sa duḥkhī parikīrtyate // Dhs_21.26 //
children.translated_text: One in whose heart there is no compassion is declared to be suffering. // Dhs_21.26 //

body.translated_text: <s>Maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) alone brings happiness

children.translated_text: There is one truth that is supreme — <s>Brahman</s>; one unsurpassed good — <s>Śiva</s>;

children.text: ekavidyā paraṃ mātā maitrī caikā sukhāvahā // Dhs_21.27 //
children.translated_text: One supreme knowledge is the mother; and one <s>maitrī</s> brings happiness. // Dhs_21.27 //

body.translated_text: The non-violent alone are blessed

children.text: ahiṃsakāḥ sadā dhanyāḥ saddṛṣṭiḥ paramā śubhā /
children.translated_text: The non-violent are always blessed; right view is supremely auspicious;

children.text: etad ṛju sadā satyaṃ pāpānāṃ cāpi varjanam // Dhs_21.28 //
children.translated_text: This is always righteous truth — and the avoidance of sins. // Dhs_21.28 //

body.translated_text: The greatness of compassion

children.translated_text: Therefore, by men whose minds are stirred by compassion, there should be practiced
Giving, morality, patience, loving-kindness, and the pure cultivation of knowledge. // Dhs_21.29 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the twenty-first chapter on Compassion (<s>Karuṇāvarga</s>). //
(22) Chapter on Giving (<s>Dānavarga</s>)
Definition of pure and impure giving

children.translated_text: That giving which is endowed with twelve virtues and free from twelve impurities

children.text: dānaṃ bhavati śuddhaṃ tad viparītaṃ sakalmaṣam // Dhs_22.1 //
children.translated_text: Becomes pure giving; the opposite is defiled. // Dhs_22.1 //

body.translated_text: Those devoid of giving are the lowest of men

children.translated_text: For gods or for men, the supreme power of wealth is giving;

children.text: dānena rahitā pāde patanti puruṣādhamāḥ // Dhs_22.2 //
children.translated_text: Those lowest of men who are devoid of giving fall at one's feet. // Dhs_22.2 //
Stained by greed and miserliness, slaves to sons and wives,
People go to destruction, desiring only food. // Dhs_22.3 //
For the release from the knot of greed, for the destruction of the tree of begging,
For the destruction of the mass of darkness — giving is given here. // Dhs_22.4 //

body.translated_text: The giver goes to the next world

children.translated_text: One performs indestructible giving, and the giver too thereafter;
Like a signpost on the road, giving proceeds to the next world. // Dhs_22.5 //
People, having bathed in the water of giving, surrounded by the waves of morality,

children.text: jñānavistīrṇa(vimalaṃ) pāraṃ duḥkhasya yānti vai // Dhs_22.6 //
children.translated_text: Go indeed to the far shore of suffering, vast and pure with knowledge. // Dhs_22.6 //

body.translated_text: The three lamps that destroy faults

children.translated_text: Three lamps should be kindled by a person who desires welfare:

children.text: dānaṃ śīlaṃ tathā jñānamete doṣavināśakāḥ // Dhs_22.7 //
children.translated_text: Giving, morality, and knowledge — these are the destroyers of faults. // Dhs_22.7 //
Discolored by craving, in a foul-smelling pool agitated with the waves and fish of discursive thought,

children.text: duḥkhārṇave plutā hyete jñānaśīleṣu rakṣitāḥ // Dhs_22.8 //
children.translated_text: These beings, plunged into the ocean of suffering, are protected in knowledge and morality. // Dhs_22.8 //

body.translated_text: The medicine for defilements is giving, morality, and knowledge

children.translated_text: Three medicines are declared as destroyers of the disease of defilements:

children.text: dānaṃ śīlaṃ tathā jñānamete nityaṃ sukhāvahāḥ // Dhs_22.9 //
children.translated_text: Giving, morality, and knowledge — these always bring happiness. // Dhs_22.9 //
The mind, uneven with heedlessness, crooked with mental fabrication, and fickle,
Is bound by these three bonds beginning with knowledge, for people. // Dhs_22.10 //
Always scorched by the fires of faults, by which one is burned —
Having slain them through the practice of giving and knowledge, one goes to liberation. // Dhs_22.11 //

children.text: na dānajñāna śīleṣu yeṣāṃ sammiśritā matiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those beings whose minds are not blended with giving, knowledge, and morality —

children.text: te nityaduḥkhitāḥ sattvāḥ sukhaṃ teṣāṃ na vidyate // Dhs_22.12 //
children.translated_text: They are eternally suffering; no happiness exists for them. // Dhs_22.12 //

body.translated_text: Givers become free from the stain of miserliness

children.translated_text: Those whose happiness is ashamed by non-giving, deceived by the fault of the mind,

children.text: bhavanti vibudhāḥ hitvā tasmād dānaparo bhavet // Dhs_22.13 //
children.translated_text: Become wise ones, having abandoned it — therefore one should be devoted to giving. // Dhs_22.13 //
Endowed with the progressive excellence of giving, free from the stain of miserliness,
The gods become glad-hearted, devoted to play. // Dhs_22.14 //
The fire of the disease of hunger and thirst which rushes forth as the principal —

children.text: mātsarya vai phalaṃ sarva taduktaṃ tattvabuddhibhiḥ // Dhs_22.15 //
children.translated_text: All that is the fruit of miserliness — thus say those of truthful understanding. // Dhs_22.15 //

body.translated_text: Praise of giving

children.text: yo dadāti sukhaṃ tasya nīyate jāyate sukham /
children.translated_text: One who gives — happiness is led to that one; happiness is born;

children.text: sukhaṃ bhavati dānāddhi tasmād dānaṃ praśasyate // Dhs_22.16 //
children.translated_text: From giving indeed comes happiness — therefore giving is praised. // Dhs_22.16 //
Giving, which illuminates the world, follows one who departs;

children.text: gataṃ ca mantradānena yujyate bhadravatsalaiḥ // Dhs_22.17 //
children.translated_text: And that which has gone is joined through the giving of sacred words by those who love the good. // Dhs_22.17 //
This is a non-deceiving state — thus declared by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>;
And because of its non-deceiving nature, one should always be devoted to giving. // Dhs_22.18 //

body.translated_text: The giver crosses the ocean of existence

children.translated_text: Having conquered the enemy of miserliness, having made the mind endowed with good —

children.text: ye prayacchanti dānāni te taranti bhavārṇavam // Dhs_22.19 //
children.translated_text: Those who bestow gifts cross the ocean of existence. // Dhs_22.19 //
Through three kinds of decline, giving is threefold, earned in three ways;

children.text: tasya kṣatānvitasyaivaṃ phalaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ tricakṣuṣā // Dhs_22.20 //
children.translated_text: The fruit of that which is endowed with loss is thus seen by the three-eyed one. // Dhs_22.20 //

body.translated_text: What path brings happiness?

children.text: dānamādau sadā deyaṃ śīlaṃ labhyaṃ prayatnataḥ /
children.translated_text: Giving should always be given first; morality should be obtained through effort;

children.text: tṛṣṇā jñānena hantavyā mārga eṣa sukhāvahaḥ // Dhs_22.21 //
children.translated_text: Craving should be slain by knowledge — this is the path that brings happiness. // Dhs_22.21 //
Craving is impermanent, wicked, and harmful to the world;

children.text: na śakyaṃ tadvinā śreyaḥ prāptuṃ padamanuttamam // Dhs_22.22 //
children.translated_text: Without conquering it, one cannot attain the unsurpassed, supreme state. // Dhs_22.22 //

body.translated_text: The consequence of not giving

children.text: adāne na manaḥ kārya nityaṃ dānarato bhavet /
children.translated_text: One should not set the mind on not giving; one should always be devoted to giving;
Through not giving, one is burned by hunger and thirst in the realms of hungry ghosts. // Dhs_22.23 //

body.translated_text: Through giving, one should always guard morality

children.translated_text: Through giving, one becomes a king, a righteous wheel-turning monarch;

children.text: dānabhūmiṃ samāśritya śīlaṃ rakṣanti paṇḍitāḥ // Dhs_22.24 //
children.translated_text: Having taken the ground of giving as their basis, the wise guard morality. // Dhs_22.24 //
Even one of morality, knowing the right time, is freed from ignorance;
This path leading away from suffering has been praised by the foremost sages. // Dhs_22.25 //

children.text: taṃ viditvā mahāvīro nityaṃ dānarato bhavet /
children.translated_text: Having understood this, the great hero should always be devoted to giving;

children.text: adā(nā)dapi deveṣu devā hi na sukhā matāḥ // Dhs_22.26 //
children.translated_text: Even among gods, gods without giving are not considered happy. // Dhs_22.26 //

body.text: dānī yatra kutrāpi vasan sukhī bhavati
body.translated_text: The giver, wherever he dwells, becomes happy

children.translated_text: Mortals become sharers of happiness from the very forest of birth;
That is the fruit of giving cultivated by all beings with intention. // Dhs_22.27 //
Even when born among animals, they become sharers of happiness;

children.text: tatsarva dānajaṃ saukhyaṃ kathayanti manīṣiṇaḥ // Dhs_22.28 //
children.translated_text: All that happiness is born of giving — so the sages declare. // Dhs_22.28 //
That hungry ghosts in the realm of hungry ghosts become eaters of forms —

children.text: svayaṃ kṛtasya dānasya phalaṃ bhavati tādṛśam // Dhs_22.29 //
children.translated_text: Such is the fruit of giving done by oneself. // Dhs_22.29 //

body.translated_text: For one devoid of giving, a wretched state ensues

children.translated_text: One who does not give — hunger and thirst, by which embodied beings are burned,

children.text: sarvadā na tapastābhyāṃ phalaṃ bhavati śītalam // Dhs_22.30 //
children.translated_text: Through those austerities, the fruit is not at all cooling. // Dhs_22.30 //

body.translated_text: The heedless one at the time of death encounters burning

children.text: pūrva pramādacārī yo na dānādiṣu vartate /
children.translated_text: One who formerly practiced heedlessness and did not engage in giving and the rest —

children.text: sa paścānmṛtyusamaye dahyate svena cetasā // Dhs_22.31 //
children.translated_text: that one, at the time of death, is burned by his own mind. // Dhs_22.31 //

body.translated_text: The fruit of giving:

children.translated_text: Through giving one becomes beloved, and minds are also pleased.

children.text: paścād bhavati sa śrīmān dānasya phalamīdṛśam // Dhs_22.32 //
children.translated_text: Afterward one becomes prosperous — such is the fruit of giving. // Dhs_22.32 //
Where there is giving and other such things for the mind's enjoyment always,

children.text: tatra nirdhanataiṣā vā dayayā parirakṣitam // Dhs_22.33 //
children.translated_text: where there is destitution — that is protected by compassion. // Dhs_22.33 //

children.text: yad bhujyate sadā cittaṃ gurubhyaścāpi dīyate /
children.translated_text: What is always enjoyed by the mind and also given to teachers,

children.text: yad vanaṃ śobhanaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ viparītaṃ yathā tṛṇam // Dhs_22.34 //
children.translated_text: what beautiful forest is seen — the opposite is like grass. // Dhs_22.34 //
For beings who are always weak and afflicted, endowed with sight,
giving is a device without conceptualization — in this world and the next. // Dhs_22.35 //

body.translated_text: The fruit of giving in the human realm:

children.text: manuṣyabhūmau dānāni dattvā yānti śubhāṃ gatim /
children.translated_text: Having given gifts in the human realm, they go to a good destination.

children.text: na devā dānapatayaḥ phalabhūmirasau matā // Dhs_22.36 //
children.translated_text: Gods are not givers — that realm is considered the fruit-realm. // Dhs_22.36 //

body.translated_text: The greatness of karma:

children.translated_text: The human realm is the karma-realm; the divine abode is the fruit-realm.

children.text: karmāyattaṃ phalaṃ sarva na phalaṃ syādahetukam // Dhs_22.37 //
children.translated_text: All fruit depends on karma — there is no fruit without a cause. // Dhs_22.37 //

body.translated_text: Who is equal to the dead?

children.translated_text: One devoid of meditation and study, bereft of giving and morality,
though adorned with golden bracelets — though living, he is equal to the dead. // Dhs_22.38 //

children.text: sa jīvati hi loke 'smin yo dharmamanuvartate /
children.translated_text: He truly lives in this world who follows dharma.

children.text: dharmamūḍhaḥ sadā mūḍho jīvannapi mṛtaiḥ samaḥ // Dhs_22.39 //
children.translated_text: One confused about dharma, always confused — though living, he is equal to the dead. // Dhs_22.39 //

body.translated_text: The ignorant one is indeed a fool:

children.translated_text: Covered with human skin, the fool is an animal,
whose heart is not illuminated by the lamp of knowledge. // Dhs_22.40 //
A person exists to the extent that he follows morality.
A person fallen from morality is praiseworthy in all but powerless. // Dhs_22.41 //

body.translated_text: One devoid of giving has the form of a <s>preta</s>:

children.translated_text: Devoid of giving, heedless, of evil conduct, with uncontrolled senses —

children.text: nāsau martya iti jñeyaḥ preto vigrahavānayam // Dhs_22.42 //
children.translated_text: he should not be known as a mortal — he is a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost) with a body. // Dhs_22.42 //

body.translated_text: One devoid of knowledge is as good as dead:

children.translated_text: Devoid of knowledge and morality, bereft of the jewel of giving —
a person, though living, is called 'dead.' // Dhs_22.43 //

body.translated_text: Who is a god?

children.translated_text: Through giving, morality, austerity, and meditation, one endowed with vigor, mindfulness, and <s>samādhi</s>,

children.text: puruṣaḥ puruṣaireje devairapi sa vandyate // Dhs_22.44 //
children.translated_text: such a person shines among men — he is worshipped even by gods. // Dhs_22.44 //

children.text: guṇavāṃstu naro vandyaḥ nirguṇaḥ paśubhiḥ samaḥ /
children.translated_text: A virtuous person is worthy of worship; one without virtue is equal to animals.

children.text: guṇāguṇavidhijño yaḥ sa deva iti kathyate // Dhs_22.45 //
children.translated_text: One who knows the method of qualities and non-qualities — he is called a god. // Dhs_22.45 //

body.translated_text: Whose life is fruitful?

children.text: sujīvitaṃ bhavettasya yasya tyāge sthitaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Well-lived is the life of one whose mind is established in renunciation.

children.text: nahi tyāgavinirmuktaṃ jīvitaṃ jīvanaṃ matam // Dhs_22.46 //
children.translated_text: A life devoid of renunciation is not considered living. // Dhs_22.46 //

body.translated_text: Giving always brings happiness:

children.translated_text: For beings born in the five destinies, by their own karma,

children.text: mātṛvat pitṛvad dṛṣṭaṃ dānaṃ nityaṃ sukhāvaham // Dhs_22.47 //
children.translated_text: giving, seen as mother-like and father-like, always brings happiness. // Dhs_22.47 //

body.translated_text: Those delighting in giving are freed from the straits of existence:

children.translated_text: Having established this ground, a being should delight in giving.
Those always delighting in giving and morality are freed from the straits of existence. // Dhs_22.48 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the twenty-second chapter on giving. //
(23) Chapter on Morality:
Morality shines like the sun:

children.translated_text: Morality is the supreme wealth, like the sun among luminaries.

children.text: vihāya gacchati dhanaṃ śīlaṃ sthitamivāgrataḥ // Dhs_23.1 //
children.translated_text: Wealth departs, but morality remains as if standing before one. // Dhs_23.1 //
Through morality one goes to the heavens or to the realm of meditation.

children.text: nāsti śīlasamaṃ jyotirasmiṃlloke paratra ca // Dhs_23.2 //
children.translated_text: There is no light equal to morality — in this world and the next. // Dhs_23.2 //
By a small cause, one desiring heaven attains heaven.

children.text: tasmād duścaritaṃ hitvā nityaṃ sucarito bhavet // Dhs_23.3 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, having abandoned misconduct, one should always be of good conduct. // Dhs_23.3 //
Giving cultivated with intention, and morality well-guarded —
one is led to a heaven-granted state, endowed with the five qualities of pleasure. // Dhs_23.4 //

body.translated_text: Only through well-guarded morality can happiness be attained:

children.text: na mātā na pitā nārthā dayitā nāpi bāndhavāḥ /
children.translated_text: Neither mother, nor father, nor wealth, nor beloved, nor relatives —

children.text: na sukhā (ste) tathā dṛṣṭā yathā śīlaṃ surakṣitam // Dhs_23.5 //
children.translated_text: none are seen to bring such happiness as well-guarded morality. // Dhs_23.5 //

body.translated_text: A moral person attains happiness:

children.translated_text: Morality is protection here and hereafter; morality is the supreme path here.

children.text: śīlavān puruṣo nityaṃ sukhāt sukhamavāpnute // Dhs_23.6 //
children.translated_text: A moral person always attains happiness upon happiness. // Dhs_23.6 //
Those men of good conduct who practice giving and morality —

children.text: te yānti devasadanaṃ racitāḥ svena karmaṇā // Dhs_23.7 //
children.translated_text: they go to the abode of gods, fashioned by their own karma. // Dhs_23.7 //
Morality is an inexhaustible treasure; the happiness of morality is beyond reasoning.

children.text: śīlādhikā hi puruṣā nityaṃ sukhavihāriṇaḥ // Dhs_23.8 //
children.translated_text: Persons endowed with morality always dwell in happiness. // Dhs_23.8 //

children.text: śīlaṃ rakṣatu medhāvī yathā yānaṃ sukhatrayam /
children.translated_text: Let the wise one guard morality as a vehicle for the three happinesses —

children.text: praśaṃsāvṛttalābhaṃ ca pretya svarge ca modate // Dhs_23.9 //
children.translated_text: praise, wealth gained through conduct, and after death he rejoices in heaven. // Dhs_23.9 //

body.translated_text: The moral person attains <s>Nirvāṇa</s>:

children.text: śīlavān yo hi puruṣaḥ śīlamevāti sevate /
children.translated_text: A person who is moral and exceedingly devotes himself to morality —

children.text: sasukho nirvṛttiṃ yāti yatra mṛtyurna vidyate // Dhs_23.10 //
children.translated_text: he happily goes to cessation, where death does not exist. // Dhs_23.10 //
In this beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>, surrounded by craving, delusion, and the rest,
morality is ever a light — therefore morality should be pure. // Dhs_23.11 //
Morality is wealth that cannot be taken by kings, thieves, water, or the rest.

children.text: tasmācchīlaṃ sadā sevyaṃ dauḥśīlyaṃ ca vigarhitam // Dhs_23.12 //
children.translated_text: Therefore morality should always be cultivated, and immorality is despised. // Dhs_23.12 //
For a person who delights in morality, <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is near at hand.

children.text: śīlavān puruṣo dhanyaḥ śīlavāṃścāpi sevyate // Dhs_23.13 //
children.translated_text: A moral person is fortunate, and the moral person is sought out. // Dhs_23.13 //

children.text: ravivad bhrājate śīlaṃ dauḥśīlyaṃ caiva garhitam /
children.translated_text: Morality shines like the sun; immorality is despised.

children.text: nirmalaṃ vītakāntāraṃ nirjvaraṃ vītakāṅkṣi ca // Dhs_23.14 //
children.translated_text: Pure, beyond the wilderness, without fever, free from doubt, // Dhs_23.14 //
praised by the perfectly awakened ones, leading to the city of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: āyuryāti dhruvaṃ dhīmān nityaṃ śīlenaṃ vṛṃhitam // Dhs_23.15 //
children.translated_text: the wise one's life-span surely increases, always nourished by morality. // Dhs_23.15 //

body.translated_text: Those devoid of morality are equal to animals:

children.translated_text: One does not fear at the time of death, being protected by morality.
Morality is wholesome from beginning to end, a promoter of all happiness.

children.text: śīlavān puruṣo dhanyo dauḥśīlyābhirataḥ paśuḥ // Dhs_23.16 //
children.translated_text: A moral person is fortunate; one who delights in immorality is an animal. // Dhs_23.16 //
Persons devoid of morality never reach the shore.

children.text: kāryākārya na vindanti tasmācchīlaṃ samācaret // Dhs_23.17 //
children.translated_text: They do not know what should and should not be done — therefore one should practice morality. // Dhs_23.17 //

children.text: śīlavastreṇa ye channāste channāḥ puruṣā matāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those covered by the garment of morality — they are considered covered persons.

children.text: śīlena varjitā ye tu nagnāste paśubhiḥ samāḥ // Dhs_23.18 //
children.translated_text: But those devoid of morality are naked — equal to animals. // Dhs_23.18 //

body.translated_text: A moral person goes to heaven:

children.translated_text: A moral person goes to heaven as if to a garden.
The moral person who has arrived well is regarded there as a kinsman. // Dhs_23.19 //
Those of pure moral conduct, endowed with wholesome dharmas,
those people who are doers of good deeds go to the divine world. // Dhs_23.20 //

body.translated_text: Qualities nourished by morality increase:

children.text: yo na prārthayate kāmān śīlavān puruṣaḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: One who does not desire pleasures, a moral person always —
his qualities increase, nourished by morality. // Dhs_23.21 //

body.translated_text: Morality is the stairway to heaven:

children.translated_text: Morality is supremely precious and excellent, in this world and the next.

children.text: tasmāt prahāya traiguṇyaṃ śīlameva sadā caret // Dhs_23.22 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, having abandoned the three qualities of nature, one should always practice morality. // Dhs_23.22 //

children.text: devebhyo rocate taddhi trāṇaṃ śīlaṃ śubhānvitam /
children.translated_text: The gods delight in it — morality, endowed with the good, is a protection.
Cultivated, it is supremely fortunate, leading to the next world. // Dhs_23.23 //

body.text: śīlavān yadi jānīyāt phalaṃ śīlasya yādṛśam // Dhs_23.24 //
body.translated_text: If a moral person knew what kind of fruit morality bears, // Dhs_23.24 //

children.translated_text: he would take a sharp sword and cut the bonds of this self.
For that which is like a weapon, blameworthy, yet accompanied by happiness — // Dhs_23.25 //

body.translated_text: The fruit of morality has been shown by the <s>Sugata</s>:

children.translated_text: The pure fruit of morality has been shown by the <s>Sugata</s>.

children.text: ādau śastaṃ tathā madhye nidhane śastameva tat // Dhs_23.26 //
children.translated_text: Praised at the beginning, likewise in the middle, and praised at the end. // Dhs_23.26 //
The fruit of morality is vast — supreme happiness upon happiness.

children.text: śīlacaryā paraṃ saukhyaṃ dhanacaryā na tādṛśī // Dhs_23.27 //
children.translated_text: The practice of morality is the highest happiness — the practice of wealth is not like that. // Dhs_23.27 //

children.text: narā dhanena hīyante śīlena na kathañcana /
children.translated_text: Men decline through wealth, but never through morality.

children.text: śocate puruṣastena pṛthak vā tadvirājate // Dhs_23.28 //
children.translated_text: A person grieves on account of that, or shines separately from it. // Dhs_23.28 //
Therefore good is praised by the best of sages as leading everywhere.
Persons of good conduct go as if to a garden.
For them, equal to the divine world, it is the supreme source of pleasures. // Dhs_23.29 //

body.translated_text: For the sake of going to heaven, one should practice morality:

children.translated_text: Of well-practiced morality, even when consumed many times,
the fruit that ripens is heaven — therefore one should practice morality. // Dhs_23.30 //
Morality is the stairway to heaven, the source of happy cessation.

children.text: śīlavarjī hi puruṣo na kvacit sukhamedhate // Dhs_23.31 //
children.translated_text: A person who rejects morality never flourishes in happiness. // Dhs_23.31 //

body.translated_text: A moral person obtains innumerable happinesses:

children.translated_text: Having bathed in the clear water of morality, always scattered abroad,

children.text: snātvā gacchanti puruṣā devaloke ca nirvṛte /
children.translated_text: men go to the divine world and to cessation,
endowed with divine garlands, ornaments, and divine happinesses. // Dhs_23.32 //
One rejoices in the divine abode — all that has a wholesome cause.

children.text: asaṃkhyāni ca saukhyāni vardhamānāni sarvadā // Dhs_23.33 //
children.translated_text: Innumerable happinesses, always increasing, // Dhs_23.33 //
a person obtains all who follows morality.

children.text: śubhacārī sadā satyaḥ pūjyate so 'parājitaḥ // Dhs_23.34 //
children.translated_text: A practitioner of good, always truthful, is worshipped — he is unconquered. // Dhs_23.34 //

body.translated_text: Morality, which bestows many happinesses, should be practiced:

children.text: śubhena śobhate martyaḥ pūjyate rājabhiḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: A mortal shines through good and is always worshipped by kings.
A mortal shines through good — therefore one should practice morality. // Dhs_23.35 //
Generating many happinesses, giving reassurance to all,

children.text: śīlaṃ sucaritaṃ kārya duṣkṛtaṃ ca vivarjayet // Dhs_23.36 //
children.translated_text: morality should be well practiced, and evil conduct should be abandoned. // Dhs_23.36 //
Those who practice giving and morality, with minds set on heaven —

children.text: teṣāṃ sakalmaṣaṃ śīlaṃ viṣamiśraṃ yathaudanam // Dhs_23.37 //
children.translated_text: their morality, if tainted, is like food mixed with poison. // Dhs_23.37 //
Various kinds of morality, guarded in many ways,
ripen among the gods for the maturation of wholesome results. // Dhs_23.38 //
Having bathed in the clear waters of morality, always scattered,

children.text: snātvā gacchanti manujā devāṃścātyantikaṃ sukham // Dhs_23.39 //
children.translated_text: humans go to the gods and to ultimate happiness. // Dhs_23.39 //
Those of giving and morality, always tamed, delighting in the welfare of all beings,
endowed with knowledge and friendly minds — they have gone to the assembly of gods. // Dhs_23.40 //
Their faults destroyed, endowed with action, adorned with the jewel of morality,
having compassion for all beings — they are the wise ones in the divine worlds. // Dhs_23.41 //
Like pure gold, their stains and taints removed,

children.text: samyak karma susaṃlagnā devalokeṣu te budhāḥ // Dhs_23.42 //
children.translated_text: rightly engaged in action — they are the wise ones in the divine worlds. // Dhs_23.42 //
Having compassion for all beings, desiring the welfare of all beings,

children.text: sarvapāpaviraktā ye teṣāṃ vāsaḥ surālaye // Dhs_23.43 //
children.translated_text: those who are dispassionate toward all evil — their dwelling is in the divine abode. // Dhs_23.43 //
Those who guard morality day after day with good discrimination,

children.text: ahanyahani teṣāṃ hi sukhaṃ bhavati naikaśaḥ // Dhs_23.44 //
children.translated_text: for them day after day there are manifold happinesses. // Dhs_23.44 //

body.translated_text: Mounted on the steed of morality, they go to the divine abode:

children.translated_text: Mounted on the steed of morality, persons who contemplate truth
go to the divine abode, with manifold sports. // Dhs_23.45 //
The sports in the divine abode and the unsurpassed happiness —

children.text: tat samagrasya śīlasya phalamuktaṃ tathāgataiḥ // Dhs_23.46 //
children.translated_text: that is declared by the <s>Tathāgatas</s> to be the fruit of complete morality. // Dhs_23.46 //

body.translated_text: Divine happiness is born of morality alone:

children.translated_text: That the gods with divine garlands and ornaments, adorned with divine raiment,

children.text: krīḍanti vibudhāḥ sarve tatsarva śubhahetukam // Dhs_23.47 //
children.translated_text: all sport — all that has a wholesome cause. // Dhs_23.47 //
In lovely lotus-and-lily groves, adorned with forests and pleasure-groves,

children.text: svarge ramanti ye devāstat sarva śubhajaṃ phalam // Dhs_23.48 //
children.translated_text: the gods who rejoice in heaven — all that fruit is born of goodness. // Dhs_23.48 //
When they stand in the sky, adorned with divine jewels,
the stainless gods shine — that is the great fruit of morality. // Dhs_23.49 //
When in lovely forests, variegated and flowering,
the gods rejoice on mountain tops — that fruit is born of morality. // Dhs_23.50 //

children.text: svagṛhaṃ hi yathā martyāḥ praviśanti gatavyathāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as mortals enter their own homes free from distress,

children.text: tathā śīlasamācārāḥ prayānti tridivaṃ narāḥ // Dhs_23.51 //
children.translated_text: so men of moral conduct go to heaven. // Dhs_23.51 //
This is the best well-lived life — the guarding of morality.
The supreme death among deaths is the abandonment of morality. // Dhs_23.52 //

body.translated_text: Incomparable morality should be practiced

children.text: etān guṇān sadā matvā priyatvamapi cātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having always understood these qualities and the dearness of the self,

children.text: śīlaṃ surakṣitaṃ kārya dauḥśīlyaṃ ca vivarjayet // Dhs_23.53 //
children.translated_text: morality should be well-guarded and immorality should be avoided. // Dhs_23.53 //
One who always practices morality is subdued, patient, and of good appearance;
as if mounted on a stairway, one goes to the abode of bliss. // Dhs_23.54 //

body.translated_text: Crossing <s>saṃsāra</s> with morality as a raft

children.text: phalaṃ śīlasya tu sukhaṃ devalokeṣu pacyate /
children.translated_text: The fruit of morality is happiness, ripening in the realms of the gods;
with morality as a raft, they cross over <s>saṃsāra</s>. // Dhs_23.55 //
Those purified by the waters of morality, self-possessed, with steadfast minds,
worship the celestial beings here with flowers made of fine gold. // Dhs_23.56 //
Those whose minds are newly pure, always adorned by morality,

children.text: te yānti devasadanaṃ yatra saukhyamanantakam // Dhs_23.57 //
children.translated_text: they go to the abode of the gods, where happiness is endless. // Dhs_23.57 //
People who perform good deeds go from happiness to greater happiness;
they play in the abode of the gods, nourished by morality. // Dhs_23.58 //

body.translated_text: Having ascended the stairway of morality, they go to a good destination

children.translated_text: Having ascended the stairway of morality, nourished by knowledge,

children.text: narāḥ prayānti sugatiṃ jñānena ca parāyaṇā // Dhs_23.59 //
children.translated_text: people go to a good destination, with knowledge as their refuge. // Dhs_23.59 //
Whatever morality is guarded with a deeply serene mind —
the coolness and happiness of that morality is at hand. // Dhs_23.60 //

body.translated_text: The fruition of morality bestows happiness

children.translated_text: Of morality well-guarded and cultivated in many ways,
in its fruition, one becomes happy and attains <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_23.61 //

body.translated_text: Morality guards through skillful means; morality leads to a good assembly;

body.text: tasmācchīlaṃ sadā rakṣyaṃ pariṇāmo 'sya śītalaḥ // Dhs_23.62 //
body.translated_text: therefore morality should always be guarded — its fruition is cool. // Dhs_23.62 //

children.translated_text: When the time of death has arrived, one who has morality has no fear from anywhere;

children.text: na me durgatinā trāṇaṃ śīlaṃ hi trāṇamuttamam // Dhs_23.63 //
children.translated_text: a bad rebirth is not my refuge — morality indeed is the supreme refuge. // Dhs_23.63 //

body.translated_text: Of despicable morality, the fruition is despicable

children.translated_text: One whose morality is despicable, like a covering of mist and clouds —

children.text: sa kutsitena śīlena kutsito jāyate naraḥ // Dhs_23.64 //
children.translated_text: that person is born despicable through despicable morality. // Dhs_23.64 //

body.text: śīlavirahitaḥ mūḍho bhavati svargamapi na yāti
body.translated_text: One devoid of morality is foolish and does not go even to heaven

children.translated_text: This happiness obtained in the heavens by beings through the root of morality —

children.text: tṛṣṇākṣayo na bhavati sa paścāt paritapyate // Dhs_23.65 //
children.translated_text: the destruction of craving does not come, and one repents afterward. // Dhs_23.65 //
Therefore, for the moral one, morality itself always excels;

children.text: niḥśīlaḥ puruṣo mūḍho na svargamadhirohati // Dhs_23.66 //
children.translated_text: a person without morality, a fool, does not ascend to heaven. // Dhs_23.66 //
This divine happiness enjoyed, resembling the five desires,

children.text: tacchīlasya viśuddhasya prāpyate hi phalaṃ mahat // Dhs_23.67 //
children.translated_text: is the great fruit obtained of pure morality. // Dhs_23.67 //
The brilliance of this gold abiding in <s>Meru</s> mountain —
that brilliance is not worth a sixteenth part of the brilliance of morality. // Dhs_23.68 //
Always shining with morality, with the luster of refined gold,

children.text: saṃyuktāstridivaṃ yānti paṇḍitā svena karmaṇā // Dhs_23.69 //
children.translated_text: the wise go to heaven by their own <s>karma</s>. // Dhs_23.69 //

body.translated_text: The threefold fruit of threefold morality

children.translated_text: Of morality that is inferior, middling, and superior — threefold indeed —

children.text: phalaṃ hi trividhaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ hīnamadhyottamaṃ tathā // Dhs_23.70 //
children.translated_text: a threefold fruit is seen: inferior, middling, and supreme. // Dhs_23.70 //
Morality free from heedlessness, nourished by non-negligence,

children.text: nityaṃ tat sukhadaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ dharmateyaṃ vyavasthitā // Dhs_23.71 //
children.translated_text: is always seen as bestowing happiness — this is the established law. // Dhs_23.71 //

body.translated_text: By the radiance of morality, even a thousand suns are surpassed

children.text: śīlodbhavā yā vimalā prabhā bhavati dehinām /
children.translated_text: The spotless radiance born of morality for embodied beings —

children.text: na sā sūryasahastrasya saṃyuktasya bhaviṣyati // Dhs_23.72 //
children.translated_text: that will not be equaled by a thousand suns combined. // Dhs_23.72 //

children.text: śīlaṃ saptavidhaṃ ramyaṃ yo rakṣati narottamaḥ /
children.translated_text: The best of men who guards the sevenfold lovely morality

children.text: sa kāmaṃ bhuñjati phalaṃ sugatena ca deśitam // Dhs_23.73 //
children.translated_text: enjoys the fruit at will, as taught by the <s>Sugata</s>. // Dhs_23.73 //

body.translated_text: Without the practice of morality, they do not go to heaven

children.translated_text: Having resorted to the practice of morality, devoted to right view,

children.text: martyalokād divaṃ yānti na kaṣṭaṃ tapacāriṇaḥ // Dhs_23.74 //
children.translated_text: from the mortal world they go to heaven — not by painful austerities. // Dhs_23.74 //
That morality, cool in the touch of morality and cool in its fruition —

children.text: niṣevate sadāmūḍhaḥ sa paścāt paritapyate // Dhs_23.75 //
children.translated_text: the deluded one who always serves it repents afterward. // Dhs_23.75 //

body.translated_text: Through sevenfold morality, proximity to the gods is attained

children.translated_text: The sevenfold morality is blessed, the state of non-deception;

children.text: śīlena rakṣitaḥ puruṣo devānāmantikaṃ gataḥ // Dhs_23.76 //
children.translated_text: a person guarded by morality has gone to the presence of the gods. // Dhs_23.76 //

body.translated_text: Through morality, beautiful fruit is obtained

children.translated_text: Just as a bird with strong wings dispels the shade of its sweat,

children.text: tathā naro dṛḍhaḥ śīlairdevalokāya kalpyate // Dhs_23.77 //
children.translated_text: so a person firm in morality is fashioned for the realm of the gods. // Dhs_23.77 //

children.text: śrutimātraṃ ca (tacchīlaṃ) ramyād ramyataraṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: That morality, heard of even by name, is lovelier than the lovely;

children.text: labhate puruṣaḥ kartā phalaṃ śīlasya śobhanam // Dhs_23.78 //
children.translated_text: the person who practices it obtains the beautiful fruit of morality. // Dhs_23.78 //
The jewels of generosity, morality, and austerity, resorted to with the heart —

children.text: devatā vā manuṣyo vā labhate paramaṃ padam // Dhs_23.79 //
children.translated_text: whether a god or a human, one obtains the supreme state. // Dhs_23.79 //
People devoid of the Dharma are essenceless both within and without;

children.text: saṃsārāt phalakāṅkṣibhyaḥ saddharmo na (ca) rocate // Dhs_23.80 //
children.translated_text: for those desiring fruit from <s>saṃsāra</s>, the true Dharma does not please. // Dhs_23.80 //

children.text: antarbahiśca ye sārāste narā vastuto dṛḍhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who have essence within and without, those people are truly firm;
they are practitioners of the Dharma, peaceful, seeking the welfare of other beings. // Dhs_23.81 //

body.translated_text: The fragrance of the moral is unsurpassed

children.text: na ketakī campakapuṣpagandhā, tamālake nāgarucaśca gandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Neither the fragrance of <s>ketakī</s>, <s>campaka</s> flowers, <s>tamāla</s>, nor <s>nāgaruca</s> —

children.text: prayānti gandhā hiṃ yathā sureṇa, anuttaraḥ śīlavatāṃ sugandhaḥ // Dhs_23.82 //
children.translated_text: fragrances travel as if by the wind of the gods, but unsurpassed is the sweet fragrance of the moral. // Dhs_23.82 //

body.translated_text: Immorality should always be avoided

children.translated_text: Therefore morality should always be practiced by those rich in generosity, knowledge, and austerity;
and immorality should always be avoided — resembling poison, weapons, and fire. // Dhs_23.83 //

body.translated_text: Through morality alone one attains happiness

children.text: evaṃ surakṣitaṃ śīlaṃ narān nayati saṅgatim /
children.translated_text: Thus, morality well-guarded leads people to a good assembly;

children.text: na hi śīlādṛte kaścit padaṃ sukhamavāpnute // Dhs_23.84 //
children.translated_text: without morality, no one attains the state of happiness. // Dhs_23.84 //

body.translated_text: One should always practice morality equal to the qualities of the gods

children.translated_text: Therefore, understanding it as a quality of the gods, one should always practice morality;

children.text: na śīlasadṛśaṃ kiñcidanyat trāṇamihāsti vai // Dhs_23.85 //
children.translated_text: there is nothing equal to morality as a refuge here. // Dhs_23.85 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the twenty-third chapter on Morality //
(24) Chapter on Patience
A person is adorned only by the ornament of patience

children.translated_text: Live adorned by patience — not adorned by other riches;

children.text: dhanaṃ vinā samāyāti kṣāntiṃ naiva kathañcana // Dhs_24.1 //
children.translated_text: one may arrive without wealth, but never without patience. // Dhs_24.1 //
A patient person is dear to all beings;

children.text: pūjyate daivatairnityaṃ tasmāt kṣāntiḥ parantapa ! // Dhs_24.2 //
children.translated_text: one is always honored by the gods — therefore patience, O scorcher of foes! // Dhs_24.2 //

body.translated_text: A patient person is honored everywhere

children.translated_text: A patient person, free from all the faults of anger,

children.text: yaśasā pūjyate nityamiha loke paratra ca // Dhs_24.3 //
children.translated_text: is always honored by fame in this world and the next. // Dhs_24.3 //

body.translated_text: The wealth of patience is the most supreme

children.translated_text: Patience is wealth, morality is wealth, and it increases wisdom;

children.text: dhanānyanyāni śastāni na hitasya kathañcana // Dhs_24.4 //
children.translated_text: other praised riches are in no way beneficial. // Dhs_24.4 //

body.translated_text: Only the patient one is honored by the good

children.translated_text: One is constantly honored by the good and honored by fame;

children.text: kṣamāvān puruṣaḥ sarvastamāt kṣāntiparo bhavet // Dhs_24.5 //
children.translated_text: a patient person in all things — therefore one should be devoted to patience. // Dhs_24.5 //

body.translated_text: Patience alone is the medicine for the poison of anger

children.translated_text: Patience is considered the supreme medicine for this poison of anger;
anger not destroyed by patience arises for one's own misfortune. // Dhs_24.6 //
For those overcome by knowledge and morality, especially the foolish,
patience performs the counter-action, showing the path. // Dhs_24.7 //

body.translated_text: Only the patient are truly wealthy in the world

children.translated_text: Among those wandering in the five destinies, deprived of the wealth of the Dharma,

children.text: yeṣāṃ kṣāntimayaṃ dravyaṃ te loke dhaninaḥ smṛtāḥ // Dhs_24.8 //
children.translated_text: those whose treasure is made of patience — they are remembered as the wealthy in the world. // Dhs_24.8 //
In the wilderness of accumulated darkness, impassable through firm anger,

children.text: kṣāntyā yathā smṛtāḥ sadbhistaranti khula mānavāḥ // Dhs_24.9 //
children.translated_text: through patience, as the good remember, people indeed cross. // Dhs_24.9 //
The supreme patience is the guide for those whose study of the true Dharma is lost;
for those frightened by the fear of the lower realms, patience is said to be fearlessness. // Dhs_24.10 //

body.translated_text: Patience brings happiness to people

children.text: sukhāvahā sadā nṛṇāṃ duḥkhasya ca vighātikā /
children.translated_text: Always bringing happiness to people and destroying suffering,
always leading to safety, producing the quality of trust — // Dhs_24.11 //
it is the auspicious, blessed guide, free from the inauspicious,
the messenger of liberation for people, the destroyer of the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>. // Dhs_24.12 //

body.translated_text: Patience destroys the fire of hell and is the stairway to heaven

children.translated_text: It is the stairway to heaven, the destroyer of the fire of hell;

children.text: trāyate pretalokātsā tiryagyonau tathaiva ca // Dhs_24.13 //
children.translated_text: it saves from the world of the hungry ghosts and likewise from the animal realm. // Dhs_24.13 //

body.translated_text: Patience is the lamp of nectar on the right path

children.text: sā guṇaudhaiḥ sadā pūrṇā śivā bhavati dehinām /
children.translated_text: It is always full of floods of virtues, auspicious for beings;

children.text: sā praśaste sukhe prāpte kṣāntiḥ kāryā prayatnataḥ /
children.translated_text: it is praised when happiness is obtained — patience should be practiced with effort,
like a mother to the entire world, the lamp of nectar on the right path. // Dhs_24.14 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter on Patience //
(25) Chapter on Vigor
Endeavors undertaken with proper place and action succeed

children.translated_text: For one endowed with proper place and time, suited to the occasion of action,
the vigor begun in the right way bears its full fruit. // Dhs_25.1 //
Devoid of proper place and action, separated from <s>adharma</s>,
heaps of endeavors sink, deprived of vigor. // Dhs_25.2 //

body.translated_text: Those of aroused vigor attain liberation

children.translated_text: Through vigor aroused in meditation, the wise attain liberation;

children.text: bhavakṣipta ivākāro devaloke prayānti ca // Dhs_25.3 //
children.translated_text: as if their form were projected by existence, they also go to the realm of the gods. // Dhs_25.3 //
Those endeavors that are begun with vigor, by people strong and powerful —

children.text: tāni tāni prasiddhāni vipulāni bhavanti ca // Dhs_25.4 //
children.translated_text: each of those becomes accomplished and abundant. // Dhs_25.4 //

children.text: ye 'rthā lokottare siddhā ye ca lokeṣu sammatāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those aims that are accomplished in the supramundane, and those honored in the worldly —

children.text: te vīryeṇa prasādhyante vīryahīnā na jātu vai // Dhs_25.5 //
children.translated_text: they are accomplished through vigor; those devoid of vigor never succeed. // Dhs_25.5 //
A person of feeble vigor, of long-lasting effort but separated from the true Dharma,

children.text: naro viśati lokaṃ (ca) śaśāṅkamiva kalmaṣam // Dhs_25.6 //
children.translated_text: enters the world like the moon enters the stain. // Dhs_25.6 //

body.translated_text: Vigor bestows the supreme destination

children.translated_text: Not guarded by knowledge through the noble eightfold path,
the vigor of great enthusiasm goes to the supreme destination. // Dhs_25.7 //

body.translated_text: Awakening is attained through vigor

children.translated_text: Awakening is attained through vigor; the earth likewise through one's own vigor;
<s>Arhat</s>ship by the vigorous — therefore there is no course equal to fire. // Dhs_25.8 //

body.translated_text: For the attainment of the supreme station, the mind should be set on the exertion of vigor

children.text: tasmād devān guṇān matvā vīryavān niyatendriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, understanding the divine qualities, one of vigor and controlled senses
should set the mind on the exertion of vigor — there is nothing equal to vigor. // Dhs_25.9 //
A person desiring vigor, mindful, devoted to knowledge —
goes to the unsurpassed station, free from old age and death. // Dhs_25.10 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter on Vigor //
(26) Chapter on Meditation
Who is truly well?

children.translated_text: One whose mind is always unattached, who always dwells in meditation,
whose mind is always pure, who delights in one-pointedness — // Dhs_26.1 //

children.text: yasyaikāgrakaraṃ cittaṃ tasya doṣā na bādhakāḥ /
children.translated_text: one whose mind is single-pointed — faults do not afflict him;
he, freed from the fear of faults, is called 'one who is well.' // Dhs_26.2 //
The mind delighting in one-pointedness pursues seclusion;
freed from all speculation, one is called 'one who is well.' // Dhs_26.3 //

body.translated_text: He describes the one-pointedness of the mind

children.text: yasya cittaṃ dhruvaṃ śāntaṃ nirvāṇābhirataṃ sadā /
children.translated_text: One whose mind is firm, peaceful, always delighting in <s>Nirvāṇa</s> —

children.text: na tasyendriyajā doṣā bhavasya śubhahetavaḥ // Dhs_26.4 //
children.translated_text: for that one, faults born of the senses are not the auspicious causes of existence. // Dhs_26.4 //
Whatever happiness is produced by meditation, and whatever arises from <s>samādhi</s> —
all that becomes one-pointed of mind for the embodied being. // Dhs_26.5 //

body.translated_text: The ascetic enjoys supramundane happiness

children.text: ekārāmasya yatino yat sukhaṃ jāyate hṛdi /
children.translated_text: The happiness that arises in the heart of the ascetic who delights in one abode —

children.text: yat saukhyamativijñeyaṃ na saukhyaṃ laukikaṃ matam // Dhs_26.6 //
children.translated_text: that happiness is to be known as supremely transcendent; it is not considered worldly happiness. // Dhs_26.6 //

body.translated_text: What kind of mind attains peace?

children.translated_text: The mind that delights in one-pointedness, of purified form —
freed from the net of faults, attains peace. // Dhs_26.7 //

body.translated_text: With the water of knowledge, one extinguishes the fire of craving

children.translated_text: With single-pointed mind always, with the five senses withdrawn,

children.text: tṛṣṇāgninātivṛddhaṃ ca hanti jñānāmbhasā budhaḥ // Dhs_26.8 //
children.translated_text: the fire of craving, greatly grown, is extinguished by the wise with the water of knowledge. // Dhs_26.8 //
For him who is freed from craving, purified, and seeking happiness —

children.text: akṣayaṃ cāvyayaṃ caiva padaṃ hi sthitamagrataḥ // Dhs_26.9 //
children.translated_text: the imperishable and undecaying state stands before him. // Dhs_26.9 //

body.translated_text: The path leading to the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>

children.translated_text: Wherever the mind, crooked with discursive thought, arises,
it should be held by that <s>samādhi</s> united with a single object;
therefore this is the supreme path leading to the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_26.10 //

body.translated_text: The fruit of restraining the mind

children.translated_text: Foremost is this: having crushed the mind, one should destroy the host of enemies;

children.text: mano hīdaṃ vinirgṛhya (sa) vetti dhyānajairdṛḍhaiḥ // Dhs_26.11 //
children.translated_text: for, having fully restrained this mind, one knows firmly through the [attainments] born of meditation. // Dhs_26.11 //

body.translated_text: The incomparable happiness born of meditation

children.translated_text: Therein stand the best among people, the faithful and the wise;
they go to the supreme state, free from sorrow, with sins destroyed. // Dhs_26.12 //

children.text: yat sukhaṃ dhyānajaṃ bhāti kutastasyopamā parā // Dhs_26.13 //
children.translated_text: what comparison could there be for the happiness born of meditation that shines? // Dhs_26.13 //

body.translated_text: For the wise one who is free from sensory poison, contented, and free from passion —
Through meditations, the supreme state is attained

children.translated_text: This is the essence for the extremely wise, the <s>yogins</s> who go to the other shore;

children.text: yadevedaṃ manaḥ śrutvā prayānti padamacyutam // Dhs_26.14 //
children.translated_text: having heard this with the mind, they go to the imperishable state. // Dhs_26.14 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter, on Meditation. //
(27) Chapter on Wisdom (<s>Prajñā</s>)
<s>Prajñā</s> is beneficial like a mother

children.translated_text: <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom), following the Dharma, nourished by vigor,
united with the power of <s>samādhi</s> — like a mother, she acts for benefit. // Dhs_27.1 //

body.translated_text: <s>Prajñā</s> protects from the five destinies

children.text: sā hi santrāyate sarvān puruṣān gatipañcakāt /
children.translated_text: She indeed rescues all persons from the five destinies;

children.text: na mātā na pitā tatra gacchantamanugacchati // Dhs_27.2 //
children.translated_text: neither mother nor father follows one who is departing. // Dhs_27.2 //
Having ascended the peak of wisdom, the beautiful cavern of moral conduct,
adorned with knowledge, one sees all the faults of existence. // Dhs_27.3 //

body.translated_text: Through <s>samādhi</s>, one crosses the ocean of existence

children.translated_text: When the senses find that state apart from sense objects,
then, through <s>samādhi</s> and knowledge, one would cross the ocean of existence. // Dhs_27.4 //
Among generosity, moral conduct, austerity, and meditation, knowledge is called the foremost;
