children.text: apavargād yadā jñānaṃ jñānaśīle sukhāvahe // Dhs_27.5 //
children.translated_text: when knowledge comes from liberation, knowledge and moral conduct bring happiness. // Dhs_27.5 //
<s>Prajñā</s> is the eighth path taught by the <s>Tathāgata</s>
Supreme among visions, the utterly stainless <s>prajñā</s> is declared;

children.text: mārgāṇāṃ cāṣṭamo mārgaḥ śivaḥ proktastathāgataiḥ // Dhs_27.6 //
children.translated_text: and the eighth among paths, auspicious, is declared by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. // Dhs_27.6 //

body.translated_text: The power of wisdom is the most supreme

children.text: caturṇā caiva satyānāmagre dve tu prakīrtite /
children.translated_text: Of the four truths, two are proclaimed as foremost;

children.text: bālānāṃ ca sadā dṛṣṭaṃ prajñābalamihottamam // Dhs_27.7 //
children.translated_text: and for the foolish, the power of wisdom is always seen as supreme here. // Dhs_27.7 //

body.translated_text: The course of birth should be cut with the weapon of knowledge

children.translated_text: With the sharp weapon of knowledge, the difficult-to-overcome creeper should be cut;
the hosts of faults should be destroyed and the course of birth should be severed. // Dhs_27.8 //

body.translated_text: There is no kinsman greater than knowledge

children.translated_text: Knowledge is the supreme among nectars, the supreme treasure of welfare;

children.text: na jñānācca paraṃ bandhurna jñānāddhanamuttamam // Dhs_27.9 //
children.translated_text: there is no kinsman greater than knowledge, no wealth superior to knowledge. // Dhs_27.9 //

body.translated_text: Wisdom endowed with knowledge and moral conduct should be cultivated

children.translated_text: The elders endowed with knowledge and moral conduct, free from passion, free from desire —
the peaceful ones, who show the path of truth, should always be served. // Dhs_27.10 //

body.translated_text: One should split apart defilements and the rest with the weapon of wisdom

children.translated_text: With the sharp vajra of wisdom, and with the power of great fortune,
mounted on the great chariot of <s>yoga</s>, one should split apart the defilements and the rest. // Dhs_27.11 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter, on Wisdom. //
(28) Chapter on <s>Nirvāṇa</s>
The exhaustion of defilements is the path to <s>nirvāṇa</s>

children.translated_text: The wise declare supreme happiness from the exhaustion of defilements;
this is the path leading to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, as declared by the seers of truth. // Dhs_28.1 //
The <s>Tathāgatas</s> speak of that eternal, resorted-to state

children.text: yatra janma na mṛtyurna vidyate duḥkhasambhavaḥ // Dhs_28.2 //
children.translated_text: where there is no birth, no death, and no arising of suffering. // Dhs_28.2 //
Of the mighty one, the heedless one, the peaceful forest-dweller,
the uncovetous, the heroic — these are the glories of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_28.3 //

body.translated_text: One who is not heedless regarding sense objects attains <s>nirvāṇa</s> before long

children.translated_text: For one who has abandoned friends and enemies, who is free from attachment to existence,
who is not heedless regarding sense objects — <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not far away. // Dhs_28.4 //

body.translated_text: One who does good attains <s>nirvāṇa</s>

children.translated_text: For one devoted to meritorious deeds, who cultivates loving-kindness and compassion,
who is frightened by the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s> — <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not far away. // Dhs_28.5 //

body.translated_text: One free from laziness swiftly goes to <s>nirvāṇa</s>

children.translated_text: For one who knows the method for the exhaustion of defilements, and for him who [realizes] non-self —
and who is freed from laziness — <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not far away. // Dhs_28.6 //

body.translated_text: For one with controlled senses, who is peaceful, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is nearest

children.translated_text: For one who knows the method of the four truths, who cultivates the destruction of the three faults,
who has controlled senses and is peaceful — <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not far away. // Dhs_28.7 //
The sage freed from the fetters of happiness and suffering is called one who has gone to the other shore
One whose mind is not destroyed by the fetters of happiness and suffering,
freed from the fear of faults — that sage is called one who has gone to the other shore. // Dhs_28.8 //

body.translated_text: One who seeks the good attains <s>nirvāṇa</s>

children.translated_text: The person who fears the lower realms, who avoids the power of heedlessness,
who does good and seeks the good — he attains <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_28.9 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the twenty-eighth chapter, on <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. //
(29) Chapter on the Path (<s>Mārga</s>)
One who practices the fourfold noble [truths] goes to the other shore

children.text: satyāni catvāri śivāni tāni, subhāvitānyeva samīkṣya vidvān /
children.translated_text: Having well cultivated and examined those four truths, which are auspicious,

children.text: sucintako jātijarābhayebhyaḥ, pramucyaye pāramupaiti śāntaḥ // Dhs_29.1 //
children.translated_text: the wise one, reflecting well, is liberated from the fears of birth and old age, and, peaceful, reaches the other shore. // Dhs_29.1 //

body.translated_text: One attached to desires, bound by the enjoyments of existence, becomes [entrapped]

children.text: acintako yastu vibhūtabuddhiḥ kāmeṣu sakto bhavabhogabaddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: But the unreflective one, whose wisdom has perished, attached to desires, bound by the enjoyments of existence —

children.text: sa bandhanaiḥ kāmamayairnibaddho, na mucyate jātijarābhayebhyaḥ // Dhs_29.2 //
children.translated_text: he, bound by the bonds of desire, is not freed from the fears of birth and old age. // Dhs_29.2 //

body.translated_text: One who sees happiness in the ocean of existence goes to hell in the end

children.text: vicintya yo duḥkhamidaṃ viśālaṃ, na khedamāyāti bhavārṇavebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who, having reflected on this vast suffering, does not feel weariness from the ocean of existence —

children.text: sa kāmavāṇairnihato hi mūḍhaḥ, kaṣṭāmavasthāṃ narake 'pi yāti // Dhs_29.3 //
children.translated_text: he, the deluded one, struck by the arrows of desire, goes even to the terrible state of hell. // Dhs_29.3 //

children.text: ābhyantaraṃ kṣemasukhaṃ ca hitvā, kiṃ kāmabhogābhiratā hi bālāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having abandoned the inner happiness and security, why do fools delight in sensual enjoyments?

children.text: naite bijānanti bhayaṃ ca tīvramabhyeti mṛtyurjvalanaprakāśaḥ // Dhs_29.4 //
children.translated_text: These [fools] do not know the intense fear that approaches — death, blazing like fire. // Dhs_29.4 //

body.translated_text: What has been said by those who show the path of truth?

children.translated_text: This self is impermanent, suffering, empty, and devoid of an agent —
<s>saṃsāra</s> has been described by the Buddhas, the revealers of the path of truth. // Dhs_29.5 //
By that, all this truth-knowledge should be known in brief;
freed from knowledge and the knowable, a third is not found. // Dhs_29.6 //

body.translated_text: Who is the knower of the method of truth?

children.translated_text: One who knows the method of beginning and end, who knows the truth of the sixteen aspects,
who knows the method of upward movement, who is skilled in the truth of patience. // Dhs_29.7 //

body.translated_text: Only the knower of truth enters into the nature of dharmas

children.translated_text: The knower of the one dharma of the foremost world, the knower of the truth of the immediately-following [moment] —

children.text: sa dharmatāmanuviśed yathā (ca) na vikampate // Dhs_29.8 //
children.translated_text: he enters into the nature of dharmas (<s>dharmatā</s>) in such a way that he is not shaken. // Dhs_29.8 //
Freed from both means, he repeatedly destroys the destroyed;
the hero whose path to evil is destroyed is called a stream-enterer (<s>srotāpanna</s>). // Dhs_29.9 //
The streams of wholesome dharmas — the evil-going ones are worn away;
scorched by the fire of liberation, one thus becomes a stream-enterer. // Dhs_29.10 //
Born of tranquility, of great result, declared to be liberating from <s>saṃsāra</s>,
the happiness of the exhaustion of craving is seen as truly producing happiness. // Dhs_29.11 //

body.translated_text: Who is always happy?

children.translated_text: One whom craving does not bind, who is not mocked by discursive thoughts,
who has reached the other shore of existence — he is always happy. // Dhs_29.12 //

body.translated_text: The fourfold noble path arises from mutual fruition

children.translated_text: Arising from mutual fruition, it operates in every way;
that very thing should be known as the cause — the fourfold noble path. // Dhs_29.13 //
A person versed in the noble truths exists with certainty;

children.text: viṣayeṣu hi saṃghuṣṭaṃ jagad bhramati cakravat // Dhs_29.14 //
children.translated_text: but the world, proclaimed in sense objects, wanders like a wheel. // Dhs_29.14 //

body.translated_text: Which is the best path?

children.text: sa mārgo deśakaḥ śreṣṭho yo mārgo bhāṣitaḥ śivaḥ /
children.translated_text: That path which teaches, which is the best, which is the auspicious path that was spoken —

children.text: yena mārgeṇa prācīnā (dhruvaṃ) yātā manīṣiṇaḥ // Dhs_29.15 //
children.translated_text: the path by which the ancient wise ones have surely gone. // Dhs_29.15 //

body.translated_text: Only one who has gone to the Three Refuges lives happily

children.text: sujīvitaṃ bhavet tasya yasya buddhau sthitaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: His life is well-lived whose mind is established in the <s>Buddha</s>;

children.text: nahi buddhivinirmuktaṃ jīvitaṃ jīvitaṃ bhavet // Dhs_29.16 //
children.translated_text: for a life freed from the <s>Buddha</s> would not be a [real] life. // Dhs_29.16 //

children.text: sujīvitaṃ bhavet tasya yasya dharme sthitaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: His life is well-lived whose mind is established in the Dharma;

children.text: nahi dharmavinirmuktaṃ jīvitaṃ jīvitaṃ bhavet // Dhs_29.17 //
children.translated_text: for a life freed from the Dharma would not be a [real] life. // Dhs_29.17 //

children.text: sujīvitaṃ bhavet tasya yasya saṅghe sthitaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: His life is well-lived whose mind is established in the <s>Saṃgha</s>;

children.text: nahi saṅghavinirmuktaṃ jīvitaṃ jīvitaṃ bhavet // Dhs_29.18 //
children.translated_text: for a life freed from the <s>Saṃgha</s> would not be a [real] life. // Dhs_29.18 //

body.translated_text: For whom is life well-lived?

children.text: sujīvitaṃ bhavet tasya yasya satye sthitaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: His life is well-lived whose mind is established in truth;

children.text: nahi satyavinirmuktaṃ jīvitaṃ jīvitaṃ bhavet // Dhs_29.19 //
children.translated_text: for a life freed from truth would not be a [real] life. // Dhs_29.19 //

children.text: sujīvitaṃ bhavet tasya yasya mārge sthitaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: His life is well-lived whose mind is established on the path;

children.text: nahi mārgavinirmuktaṃ jīvitaṃ jīvitaṃ bhavet // Dhs_29.20 //
children.translated_text: for a life freed from the path would not be a [real] life. // Dhs_29.20 //
One whose wisdom is always established in going to <s>nirvāṇa</s> —

children.text: sa doṣādeva nirmukto na devaḥ krīḍati svayam // Dhs_29.21 //
children.translated_text: he is freed from faults entirely; a god does not play by himself. // Dhs_29.21 //

body.translated_text: What kind of play produces happiness?

children.translated_text: That play which pervades existence, always with a single-pointed mind —

children.text: sā sukhodbhāvikā krīḍā na krīḍā rāgakārikā // Dhs_29.22 //
children.translated_text: that play produces happiness; not the play that produces passion. // Dhs_29.22 //

body.translated_text: By which path does one find the auspicious state?

children.translated_text: When happiness and the rest, the truths, are found here by the self-disciplined one,

children.text: tadā kṣemaṃ śivaṃ sthānaṃ prāpnoti puruṣottamaḥ // Dhs_29.23 //
children.translated_text: then the best among persons attains the secure and auspicious state. // Dhs_29.23 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter, on the Path. //
(30) Chapter on the Monk (<s>Bhikṣu</s>)
The ideal monk is a guide showing the world's path

children.text: yo hinasti na bhūtāni mitravettā sadākṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who does not harm beings, who knows friendship, who is always imperishable —
like a father to all beings, the world regards him. // Dhs_30.1 //
Abstaining from taking what is not given, always possessed of knowledge, with senses conquered,
with peaceful bodily action, one who has crossed the passage of existence. // Dhs_30.2 //
It is not to be drawn in a picture, nor is it to be perceived by the eye;
one whose desires are destroyed, who has seen the truth — such a one is called liberated. // Dhs_30.3 //
For whom a clod of earth, a stone, and gold are equal; whose sorrow is gone; who is concentrated;

children.text: na kleśoragasampṛktaḥ sa saukhyaṃ dhruvamāpnuyāt // Dhs_30.4 //
children.translated_text: who is not afflicted by the serpent of defilements — he would certainly attain happiness. // Dhs_30.4 //

body.translated_text: Who is [truly] a monk?

children.translated_text: One for whom gain and loss, profit and non-profit are equal,

children.text: sukhaduḥkhasamāyuktaḥ bhikṣuḥ sa khalu kathyate // Dhs_30.5 //
children.translated_text: who is equanimous in happiness and suffering — he is truly called a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk). // Dhs_30.5 //
One who has abandoned friends and enemies, whose mind is equanimous, whose senses are conquered,

children.text: vibheti yo na viṣayaiḥ vijñeyastādṛśo yatiḥ // Dhs_30.6 //
children.translated_text: who does not fear sense objects — such an ascetic (<s>yati</s>) should be known. // Dhs_30.6 //

body.translated_text: One who is averse to sense objects attains <s>nirvāṇa</s>

children.translated_text: The wise one, whose anguish is gone, is averse to sense objects because of their perilousness;

children.text: na tasya dūre nirvāṇaṃ samyaksambuddhadeśitam // Dhs_30.7 //
children.translated_text: for him, <s>nirvāṇa</s>, as taught by the Perfectly Awakened One, is not far away. // Dhs_30.7 //
The knower of the truth of arising and passing away, of right view, uncovetous —
like the <s>Himavān</s>, having gone forth, he is the cause of liberation from <s>saṃsāra</s>. // Dhs_30.8 //
For whom grass and sandalwood are equal, whose mass of craving for garments is equanimous —
he is not afflicted by the craving for silk-patched robes. // Dhs_30.9 //
Contented with gain and honor, contented with beds of grass,

children.text: vahnivallābhasatkāraṃ yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati // Dhs_30.10 //
children.translated_text: one who sees gain and honor as fire — he truly sees. // Dhs_30.10 //

body.translated_text: The monk-dharmas taught by the <s>Buddha</s>

children.text: vāhyate yo na viṣayaistṛṇanadyā na vāhayate /
children.translated_text: One who is not carried away by sense objects, not swept by the river of grass,
who knows the truth of the fruits of his own karma — that monk is taught by the <s>Buddha</s>. // Dhs_30.11 //

children.text: nātītaṃ śocate yo hi buddhayā (caiva) gataspṛhaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who does not grieve over the past and has abandoned longing through wisdom,
who is engaged in the activity of the present — that one's understanding is not stained. // Dhs_30.12 //

children.text: nirvāṇe (ca) matiryasya dharme nityaṃ sthitā bhavet /
children.translated_text: One whose mind regarding <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is always established in the Dharma —

children.text: na vartate sa saṃsāre śukladharmasamāvṛtaḥ // Dhs_30.13 //
children.translated_text: that one does not move in <s>saṃsāra</s>, being enveloped in wholesome dharmas. // Dhs_30.13 //
One whose mind is not made turbid by the fire-like nature of knowledge,

children.text: dāruvadviṣayā yasya tasya duḥkhaṃ na vidyate // Dhs_30.14 //
children.translated_text: for whom sense objects are like wood — for that one suffering does not exist. // Dhs_30.14 //
One whose senses are under control, and who is subject to the senses —

children.text: hriyate yaḥ pumarthaino nikaṣastādṛśo muniḥ // Dhs_30.15 //
children.translated_text: the person who is carried away by the faults of human endeavor — such is the <s>muni</s> (sage) as a touchstone. // Dhs_30.15 //
One whose mind is like that of the good, who is patient and pleasant to behold —

children.text: prahlādayati cetāṃsi sa nṛṇāṃ śaśivanmuniḥ // Dhs_30.16 //
children.translated_text: that <s>muni</s>, like the moon, gladdens the hearts of people. // Dhs_30.16 //
One who delights in the dawn and does not cling to mansion-tops,
who is content with rag-robes — such a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) should delight in alms. // Dhs_30.17 //
Peaceful, restrained, firm in wisdom, truly knowing happiness and suffering —

children.text: sa yātyuttamamadhvānaṃ yatra gatvā na śocati // Dhs_30.18 //
children.translated_text: that one goes on the supreme journey, where having gone, one does not grieve. // Dhs_30.18 //
One whose transgressions are straightforward, always devoted to meditation,

children.text: prākṛtaiśca malai(rhīnaḥ) sa yogī satyavartmani // Dhs_30.19 //
children.translated_text: and free from ordinary stains — that <s>yogin</s> is on the path of truth. // Dhs_30.19 //
One who subdues all the senses, who delights in the welfare of all beings,

children.text: śānto dāntendriyaḥ svastho bhikṣurbhavati tādṛśaḥ // Dhs_30.20 //
children.translated_text: peaceful, with restrained senses, at ease — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.20 //
Mounted on the chariot of the six senses, repelling the enemy of passion,

children.text: prajñādhīraḥ kriyāvān yaḥ sa śāntipadamaśnute // Dhs_30.21 //
children.translated_text: firm in wisdom and active in deeds — that one attains the state of peace. // Dhs_30.21 //
Dwelling in the forest, content, sleeping on the ground, composed —
one shakes off evil dharmas as the sky shakes off life-giving rain-clouds. // Dhs_30.22 //
One whose bodily action is good, delighting in good conduct,
with true vision, skilled in action, destroying the instruments of <s>Māra</s> (the tempter). // Dhs_30.23 //

body.translated_text: A compassionate <s>bhikṣu</s> stands on the path to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>:

children.translated_text: One should not obstruct the virtuous mind that has gone beyond passion and is without attachment;
a <s>bhikṣu</s> rich in compassion, with loving-kindness, stands on the path leading out. // Dhs_30.24 //
One for whom sense objects such as form are not desired as causes of bondage —

children.text: sa yāti paramāṃ śāntiṃ yatra gatvā na śocyate // Dhs_30.25 //
children.translated_text: that one goes to supreme peace, where having gone, one is not grieved for. // Dhs_30.25 //
One who knows the truth of causes and conditions, who has determined the subtle meaning,
who delights in the stream of liberation — is not stained by craving. // Dhs_30.26 //
One who does not take up unwholesome <s>karma</s>, always delighting in wholesome <s>karma</s> —
such a <s>yogin</s> becomes of stainless course like the rays of the moon. // Dhs_30.27 //
Burning up evil dharmas like fire burns dry fuel,
one shines in the three worlds, freed from misfortune and gone beyond distress. // Dhs_30.28 //

children.text: mokṣe 'sti yasya tu mano na saṃsāre kathañcana /
children.translated_text: One whose mind is in liberation and nowhere in <s>saṃsāra</s> —

children.text: nāsau badhnāti saṃsāre muktaḥ pakṣī yathāmbare // Dhs_30.29 //
children.translated_text: that one is not bound in <s>saṃsāra</s>, like a bird freed in the sky. // Dhs_30.29 //
One who knows the truth of the arising of sensations, who is certain of the fruit of sensations —

children.text: sa mukta iti vijñeyastattvavid ṛtavāṃśca saḥ // Dhs_30.30 //
children.translated_text: that one should be known as liberated, a knower of truth, and truthful. // Dhs_30.30 //
Even so, that one is not stained by happiness or suffering, whether refined or unrefined;

children.text: dīptaṃ paśyati saṃsāraṃ yaḥ sa yogī satāṃ mataḥ // Dhs_30.31 //
children.translated_text: one who sees <s>saṃsāra</s> as blazing — that <s>yogin</s> is esteemed by the good. // Dhs_30.31 //

body.translated_text: What kind of person becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>?

children.translated_text: One whose understanding is always undeluded, always devoted to the Dharma,
delighting in the conduct of a <s>bhikṣu</s> — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.32 //
One who has no satisfaction in parks for seeing, but delights in seeing the good,
who has left behind the stain of household life — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.33 //
One who does not watch dancing and singing, but again examines the truth,
who is guarded in cremation grounds — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.34 //
One who takes alms-food at most once a day, who longs for nothing else,
content with filling only a third of the belly — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.35 //
One who avoids the finest garments and delights in rag-robes,
whose dwelling and food are free — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.36 //

children.text: karmāṇyārabhate yo na nirāśaḥ sa ca karmasu /
children.translated_text: One who does not undertake worldly activities and is without expectation in actions,
restrained yet not ceasing — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.37 //
One freed from the tip of the body's concerns, free from the darkness of delusion,
unstained by evil dharmas — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.38 //
One who has gone beyond all dispositions, who has abandoned all dispositions,
who is freed from all dispositions — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.39 //
Standing before <s>Nirvāṇa</s> through the noble eightfold path —
this is indeed the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of all purposes — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.40 //
One of peaceful senses, firm understanding, free from the ripening of desire,
one-pointedly established in mind — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.41 //
One who knows the traversal of the stages, who demonstrates the truth of the stages,

children.text: bhūmeḥ parāparajño yo bhikṣurbhavati tādṛśaḥ // Dhs_30.42 //
children.translated_text: who knows the higher and lower of the stages — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.42 //
One who duly knows all dharmas — those that arise and do not arise,

children.text: jānīte vidhivat sarvān bhikṣurbhavati tādṛśaḥ // Dhs_30.43 //
children.translated_text: and those arising from causes and conditions — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.43 //
Celibate, knowledgeable of the seasons, free from torpor and sloth,
alert as the cosmic age, skilled on the earth — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.44 //
One who abides in calm and insight, and who delights in the four <s>dhyānas</s>,
who rejoices in the grove of one's abode — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.45 //
Like the shadow that always follows a bird in the sky,
one who lives in accord with the true Dharma — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.46 //
One who destroys <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and secondary afflictions, who sees impartially and is endowed with goodness,
who knows the method of mindfulness of breathing — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.47 //
One who knows the method of sequential progression, who knows <s>yoga</s> and sees the truth,
who knows the method of the near and far shores — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.48 //

children.text: yo na hṛṣyati harṣeṣu bhayeṣu na bibheti ca /
children.translated_text: One who does not rejoice in moments of joy, and does not fear in moments of fear,
freed from agitation born of joy and fear — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.49 //
One who knows the truth of birth and death, honored by gods and <s>asuras</s>,
who knows the higher and lower among beings — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.50 //
One who is satisfied with merely a patchwork robe and does not cling to accumulations,

children.text: alpeccho brahmacārī yo bhikṣurbhavati tādṛśaḥ // Dhs_30.51 //
children.translated_text: of few desires and celibate — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.51 //

children.text: ekāśī vṛkṣamūle yaḥ sadā dhyānaṃ samīhate /
children.translated_text: One who eats alone at the root of a tree, always aspiring to meditation,
free from gain and honor — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.52 //
One whose affections are equanimity and compassion, free from the faults of liberation,
who has burned all faults and possessions — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.53 //
And not for the sight of <s>bhikṣus</s> who are weak in vigor and lazy —
one who does not delight in other practices — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.54 //
A <s>bhikṣu</s> who delights in laziness does not deserve what is beneficial:
A <s>bhikṣu</s> is not one who indulges in bedding and seats — so the Buddha has declared;
one who delights in laziness does not deserve what is beneficial. // Dhs_30.55 //

children.text: kleśānāṃ mūlapākaṃ hi kausīdyaṃ yasya vidyate /
children.translated_text: For one in whom laziness exists as the root-ripening of afflictions,

children.text: tasya duḥkhaṃ mahāghoraṃ saṃsāre sampravartate // Dhs_30.56 //
children.translated_text: the most terrible suffering operates in <s>saṃsāra</s>. // Dhs_30.56 //

children.text: kausīdyameva yasyāsti tasya dharmo na vidyate /
children.translated_text: For one who has only laziness, the Dharma does not exist;

children.text: kevalaṃ vastramātreṇa 'bhikṣuḥ' sa iti kathyate // Dhs_30.57 //
children.translated_text: merely by wearing a garment, one is called a '<s>bhikṣu</s>.' // Dhs_30.57 //

body.translated_text: Such a one does not become a <s>bhikṣu</s>:

children.translated_text: One who has no delight in study, who does not quickly guard through meditation —
merely by wearing a garment, such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s> in appearance. // Dhs_30.58 //
One who delights in the monastery but is not devoted to the domain of Dharma,
whose mind is greedy for women and intoxicants — such one is not a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.59 //
One whose mind is always in various evil deeds —

children.text: sa bhikṣurdeśito buddhaiḥ na bhoktā svakagocare // Dhs_30.60 //
children.translated_text: that <s>bhikṣu</s>, as taught by the Buddhas, is not an enjoyer in his own domain. // Dhs_30.60 //
Better is the poison of a venomous serpent, and even copper has been spoken of —
the evil food consumed by those of utterly bad morality is worse. // Dhs_30.61 //

children.text: yo hi nārhati piṇḍāya nāsau piṇḍāya kalpate /
children.translated_text: One who is not worthy of alms-food — that one is not fit for alms;

children.text: yasya piṇḍikṛtāḥ kleśāḥ sarpā iva vileśayāḥ // Dhs_30.62 //
children.translated_text: one for whom afflictions are made into balls, like serpents in their lairs — // Dhs_30.62 //
that <s>bhikṣu</s> should be one who eats alms, not one devoted to the sight of women;

children.text: bandhakaṃ yadi cātmānaṃ kṛtvā paraśubhakṣatim // Dhs_30.63 //
children.translated_text: if one makes oneself a bondage-maker, subject to the destruction by another's axe — // Dhs_30.63 //

body.translated_text: The true nature of a <s>bhikṣu</s> with evil qualities:

children.translated_text: How is that <s>bhikṣu</s> to be known who corrupts the jewel of the <s>Saṃgha</s>?

children.text: yasyeṣṭā lābhasatkārā viṣayā yasya sammatāḥ // Dhs_30.64 //
children.translated_text: One for whom gain and honor are desired, for whom sense objects are approved, // Dhs_30.64 //
one who longs for the sight of women — that one is neither a <s>bhikṣu</s> nor a householder;
one who freely approaches the courts of kings, who drinks intoxicants and is wrathful — // Dhs_30.65 //
such a <s>bhikṣu</s> always deceives donors, does he not, with his mind;
those who, taking offerings, resort to the doors of kings,

children.text: saṃrabdhā gṛhibhiḥ sārdha yathā nāgā vanāśritāḥ // Dhs_30.66 //
children.translated_text: contentious with householders, like elephants resorting to forests — // Dhs_30.66 //
therefore they nourish only those, gathered by the wind of jealousy;

children.text: putradārān parityajya ye śāntā ratnamāśritāḥ // Dhs_30.67 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned sons and wives, those peaceful ones who have taken refuge in the jewel — // Dhs_30.67 //

body.translated_text: The greatness of the virtues of a <s>bhikṣu</s>:

children.translated_text: A <s>bhikṣu</s> who abandons faults, who is a seer of the truth of what exists,
who knows the truth of the aggregates beginning with form — always strives for liberation. // Dhs_30.68 //
through the awakening to the characteristics of truth, one would attain the imperishable state. // Dhs_30.69 //

body.translated_text: One who delights in the awakening to the Dharma, who dwells in the grove of meditation —

children.translated_text: One who always delights in the grove of loving-kindness, who is diligent in the domain of Dharma,
who knows the truth of the characteristics of truth — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.70 //
One whose understanding is properly directed, who is not destroyed by desire and anger —
that one should be known as a <s>bhikṣu</s>; the opposite is otherwise. // Dhs_30.71 //
Firm toward all beings, peaceful, free from all attachment,
freed from all bondage — such a <s>bhikṣu</s> becomes a knower of truth. // Dhs_30.72 //
One who in action is not destroyed by the objects of knowledge,

children.text: nirmalaḥ syāt kanakavat santuṣṭo bhikṣurucyate // Dhs_30.73 //
children.translated_text: who would be stainless like gold, content — that one is called a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.73 //
One whose mind does not follow attachment in the pleasant and unpleasant,
who knows the method of intentions, free from all evil — // Dhs_30.74 //
of conduct uncorrupted by others, endowed with the morality of Dharma, with conquered senses,
of undiminished courage, wise — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.75 //
One whose mind always delights in the teachings and in the knowledge of their meaning,

children.text: na pānabhojanarataḥ sa bhikṣuḥ śāntamānasaḥ // Dhs_30.76 //
children.translated_text: who does not delight in drink and food — that <s>bhikṣu</s> is of peaceful mind. // Dhs_30.76 //

body.translated_text: The delineation of the true nature of a <s>bhikṣu</s>:

children.translated_text: In forest and wilderness dwellings, in cremation grounds, on a bed of grass —

children.text: ramate yasya tu mano bhikṣurbhavati tādṛśaḥ // Dhs_30.77 //
children.translated_text: one whose mind delights — such one becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.77 //
One who knows the truth of the <s>karma</s> of faults, who knows the fruit thoroughly,
who knows the truth of causes and conditions — that <s>bhikṣu</s> would be free from defilement. // Dhs_30.78 //
One who has destroyed the wilderness of sin, whose faults are destroyed, whose senses are conquered,
who knows the method of rebirth — that <s>bhikṣu</s> of peaceful mind is remembered. // Dhs_30.79 //
One does not become elated in a joyful heart, nor does one become angry at blame;
deep as the ocean in profundity — such a practitioner is called a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // Dhs_30.80 //
Distinctive, of firm understanding, speaking on subtle matters, not greedy,

children.text: kāmavādī samo dakṣaḥ sa bhikṣuḥ śānta ucyate // Dhs_30.81 //
children.translated_text: speaking of desires yet impartial and skilled — that <s>bhikṣu</s> is called peaceful. // Dhs_30.81 //
One who knows the truth of the causes pertaining to the desire realm, and likewise in the form realm,

children.text: āruṣyeṣu ca tattvajñaḥ śāstrā bhikṣuḥ sa ucyate // Dhs_30.82 //
children.translated_text: and in the formless realms — that <s>bhikṣu</s> is called a teacher. // Dhs_30.82 //
Not attached to worldly gossip, always engaged in destroying the faults of enemies,

children.text: viṣavad yasya viṣayāḥ sa bhikṣurdeśito budhaiḥ // Dhs_30.83 //
children.translated_text: for whom sense objects are like poison — that <s>bhikṣu</s> has been taught by the wise. // Dhs_30.83 //
One whose mind regarding desires is always pure —
that <s>bhikṣu</s> of liberated mind is freed from the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s>. // Dhs_30.84 //
Skilled in the works of meditation and study, for whom laziness is far away — /

children.text: hitakārī ca sattvānām āraṇyo bhikṣurucyate // Dhs_30.85 //
children.translated_text: One who acts for the welfare of beings — that monk is called a forest-dweller. // Dhs_30.85 //
One who has the intelligence for question and answer, is inspired, with senses conquered —

children.text: sa dharmaḥ kathito jñeyo viparītastṛṇaiḥ samaḥ // Dhs_30.86 //
children.translated_text: That should be known as the Dharma taught; the opposite is equal to grass. // Dhs_30.86 //

body.translated_text: What kind of monk is praised in the Buddha's teaching?

children.translated_text: One who never wearies in body, mind, and vigor,

children.text: sarvakṛtyakaro jñeyo yaḥ saṅghāya ca tatparaḥ // Dhs_30.87 //
children.translated_text: Who accomplishes all duties and is devoted to the <s>Saṅgha</s> — he should be known. // Dhs_30.87 //

children.text: na parārtha na lobhārtha yaśo 'rtha kurute na tu /
children.translated_text: He acts not for another's sake, not for the sake of greed, nor for fame;

children.text: saṅghakārye matiryasya sa muktaḥ sarvabandhanaiḥ // Dhs_30.88 //
children.translated_text: One whose mind is set on the work of the <s>Saṅgha</s> — he is freed from all bonds. // Dhs_30.88 //

children.text: na svargārtha matiryasya lābhārtha yaśase na vā /
children.translated_text: One whose mind is not set on the sake of heaven, nor for gain, nor for fame,

children.text: nirvāṇārtha kriyā sarvā sa bhikṣuḥ srota ucyate // Dhs_30.89 //
children.translated_text: Whose every action is for the sake of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — that monk is called a stream. // Dhs_30.89 //
Always abstaining from evil, always devoted to good deeds,

children.text: na pāpamitrasaṃsargī bhikṣuḥ syād buddhaśāsane // Dhs_30.90 //
children.translated_text: Not associating with evil friends — such should a monk be in the Buddha's teaching. // Dhs_30.90 //
For one whose mind is cultivated with <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), who is skilled and of upright mind,
Who is devoted to the training precepts — <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not far away. // Dhs_30.91 //
For one who is subject to old age and death, who is turned away from <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: dhyāne 'pi na pramattasya nirvāṇaṃ nātidūrataḥ // Dhs_30.92 //
children.translated_text: Who is not heedless even in meditation — <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not far away. // Dhs_30.92 //
For one who knows the method of impermanence, who acts upon emptiness,
Who knows the method of the excellence of meditation — <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not far away. // Dhs_30.93 //
Bold is he, but this foremost thief — the monk who is unrestrained,
Who inwardly oozes like a fine garment but is outwardly covered in the robe. // Dhs_30.94 //

body.translated_text: A monk empty of Dharma and Discipline would indeed become a sharer of suffering

children.translated_text: Just as a heap made of effort is all without pith and weak,

children.text: evaṃ sañcarati rikto vitatho bhikṣuvādikaḥ // Dhs_30.95 //
children.translated_text: So wanders one who is empty — a false bearer of the name of monk. // Dhs_30.95 //
That hell-bound immoral one, expelled from the jewel of the <s>Saṅgha</s>,
At the breaking up of the body is led to hell, deceived by his own mind. // Dhs_30.96 //

children.text: vañcito dharmavinayād yāti tat svena karmaṇā /
children.translated_text: Deceived and departed from the Dharma and Discipline, he goes by his own <s>karma</s>;
Stained and bound by darkness, he will become a sharer of suffering. // Dhs_30.97 //
Uncovered by the splendor of the good, naked, despised by the virtuous,

children.text: nayate narakaṃ ghoraṃ yathā dharmabahiṣkṛtaḥ // Dhs_30.98 //
children.translated_text: He is led to terrible hell, as one expelled from the Dharma. // Dhs_30.98 //
An accumulation of the unbeautiful, the door of suffering left uncovered,
The intense bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s> — this is called immorality. // Dhs_30.99 //

children.text: asaṃvareṇa yo dagdhaḥ sa dagdho vahninā bhṛśam /
children.translated_text: One who is burned by non-restraint is burned by fire severely;

children.text: tasya saṃvarakṣīṇasya vinipāto dhruvaṃ sthitaḥ // Dhs_30.100 //
children.translated_text: For one whose restraint is destroyed, downfall is certainly established. // Dhs_30.100 //

body.translated_text: Even a monk who acts wrongly goes to hell

children.translated_text: With a mind established in restraint, one restrains oneself by one's own conduct;
But mounting upon deluded conduct, one prepares oneself for hell. // Dhs_30.101 //

children.text: aśubhaṃ vardhate tasya divārātrau ca sarvataḥ /
children.translated_text: The unwholesome grows for that one, day and night, on all sides,

children.text: yasya śīlamayaṃ ratnaṃ dauḥśīlyena nivāritam // Dhs_30.102 //
children.translated_text: Whose jewel of morality has been obstructed by immorality. // Dhs_30.102 //
For one who is empty of Dharma, hollow, and covered by darkness,

children.text: vidyate 'saṃvarastasya yo na śaucāya kalpate // Dhs_30.103 //
children.translated_text: Non-restraint exists in that one who is not fit for purity. // Dhs_30.103 //
The noose of non-restraint, defiled and avoided by the good,

children.text: ākarṣati sa duḥśīlān pāpiṣṭhān śīlavarjitān // Dhs_30.104 //
children.translated_text: Drags along the immoral, the most sinful, those devoid of morality. // Dhs_30.104 //
Non-restraints, immoralities, and association with the sinful —
These are the messengers of hell, and also the servants of desires. // Dhs_30.105 //
For one born of non-restraint, especially one who is fickle,
Who is engaged in sinful deeds — hell is not far away. // Dhs_30.106 //
Why do these not understand that the fruit is similar to the action?
Deluded by evil understanding, fools rushing to destruction. // Dhs_30.107 //
Day by day grow the inaccessible rivers of sin,
With fickle garlands of waves of suffering, carrying away the most sinful people. // Dhs_30.108 //

children.text: na teṣāṃ sukaraṃ janma na teṣāṃ sukaraṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Birth is not easy for them, nor is the mind easy for them —

children.text: aśīlāḥ puruṣā ye vā śukladharmavivarjitāḥ // Dhs_30.109 //
children.translated_text: Those persons who are immoral, devoid of bright dharmas. // Dhs_30.109 //

body.translated_text: The Dharma is the highest, auspicious path

children.text: atyuccaśca śubho mārgaḥ sa 'dharma' iti kathyate /
children.translated_text: That which is highest, the auspicious path — it is called 'Dharma';

children.text: taṃ prāpyamanujaḥ śīghraṃ prayāti padamacyutam // Dhs_30.110 //
children.translated_text: Having attained it, a person quickly proceeds to the imperishable state. // Dhs_30.110 //
From that, objections are overcome by those who are powerful and happy;

children.text: saṃvarasya sadā dāsāsteṣāṃ duḥkhaṃ na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Those who are always servants of restraint — for them suffering is not found.
For this supreme immorality defiles people. // Dhs_30.111 //
Those who have fallen from the stages of training are sharers of hell;

children.text: evaṃ jñātvā naraḥ sarva saṃvaraṃ pratipadyate // Dhs_30.112 //
children.translated_text: Knowing this, every person should undertake restraint. // Dhs_30.112 //

body.translated_text: A monk of wholesome dharmas attains <s>nirvāṇa</s> before long

children.translated_text: Restraint is indeed the bridge over the entire ocean of existence;
For one whose pure livelihood is purified, whose peaceful speech is matched by action, // Dhs_30.113 //
For the meditator who is liberated — <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not far away.
For the bearer of the yoke, the non-heedless, the dweller in cremation grounds and forests, // Dhs_30.114 //
<s>Nirvāṇa</s> is not far away for one who always sleeps on the ground,
On a bed of dust, wearing a hanging garment, a single worn-out robe. // Dhs_30.115 //
Content with fruits and roots, that happy one is born of the Buddha;

children.text: vipramuktasya kāmebhyaḥ santoṣo hītarasya ca // Dhs_30.116 //
children.translated_text: For one freed from desires, and for one of contentment also, // Dhs_30.116 //
For one whose mind is freed from attachment — <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not far away.

children.text: kuhakāmalamuktasya rajo vā tasya tāyinaḥ // Dhs_30.117 //
children.translated_text: For one freed from the stain of deceit, or for that protector from passion, // Dhs_30.117 //
For one whose mind is like space — <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not far away.
The wandering in existence, bound with many fettered steps, should be known. // Dhs_30.118 //
The destroyer of the holy life, causing suffering on the path to <s>nirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: sevyate yā janairnityaṃ prākṛtaiḥ śīlavarjitaiḥ // Dhs_30.119 //
children.translated_text: Which is always pursued by ordinary people devoid of morality — // Dhs_30.119 //
That should be constantly avoided by meditators and seers of truth;
It alone is the root of weakness, the destroyer of mental attention. // Dhs_30.120 //
The destroyer of the holy life, the indicator of hell,
The one who causes falling from the path to heaven, the drainer of the ocean of suffering. // Dhs_30.121 //
The messenger of the realm of hungry ghosts, causing falls into animal births —

children.text: nāmnā saṅgaṇikā sevā saṃsāre bandhamātṛkā // Dhs_30.122 //
children.translated_text: By name it is called socializing (<s>saṅgaṇikā</s>), the mother of bondage in <s>saṃsāra</s>. // Dhs_30.122 //
The power of meditation and study — that should always be avoided by monks;
One who is freed from meditation and study, always delighting in signs, // Dhs_30.123 //

body.translated_text: Another's dharma is fearful

children.translated_text: Is devoid of auspicious dharmas and heads toward evil.

children.text: svadharma yaḥ parityajya paradharmeṣu rajyate // Dhs_30.124 //
children.translated_text: One who abandons one's own dharma and delights in another's dharmas, // Dhs_30.124 //
Fallen from both dharmas, prepares for downfall.

children.text: svagṛhaṃ yaḥ parityajya paraveśyāni tiṣṭhati // Dhs_30.125 //
children.translated_text: One who abandons one's own house and dwells in another's lodgings, // Dhs_30.125 //

children.text: sadāyaṃ lāghavaṃ yāti nidhanaṃ cāśu gacchati /
children.translated_text: Always comes to insignificance and quickly goes to destruction.

children.text: tathā yo vimatirbhūto vidvanmānī janecchayā // Dhs_30.126 //
children.translated_text: Likewise one who, becoming doubtful, proud of learning, following people's desires, // Dhs_30.126 //
Having ceased from one's own dharma, engages in another's dharmas.
His disposition is toward non-dharma, one who subsists by wearing another's insignia — // Dhs_30.127 //
This ghost, smeared with worthless learning, is tormented in sins;
Having taken his stand at the edge of fame, he engages in sinful deeds. // Dhs_30.128 //

body.translated_text: He is not called a monk here

children.text: śaśvat sa patito dṛṣṭaḥ śāsanāntāt pravartate /
children.translated_text: He is always seen as fallen, operating outside the teaching.
Free from desire in sensual conduct, without delight, a renunciant,

body.translated_text: Of vigorous effort, contented, meditative — that one is called a monk here. // Dhs_30.129 //

children.translated_text: But one attached to desires, always concerned with food and dwelling,
Covered in the ochre robe, shaven — that one is not called a monk here. // Dhs_30.130 //
One who interprets signs, who ponders the courses of stars,
Who is diligent in the service of kings — that one is not called a monk here. // Dhs_30.131 //
One who performs medical practices and likewise compiles texts,

children.text: saṅkīrṇā dinacaryā ca kurvan bhikṣuḥ praṇaśyati // Dhs_30.132 //
children.translated_text: Whose daily routine is mixed — that monk is destroyed. // Dhs_30.132 //
One who hates meditation and study, who delights in socializing,

children.text: lobhasatkāralābhaṃ ca kurvan bhikṣuḥ praṇaśyati // Dhs_30.133 //
children.translated_text: Who seeks profit through offerings and gain — that monk is destroyed. // Dhs_30.133 //
One attached to gold and minerals, who delights in many friends,
Who longs for others' gains — that monk falls from the teaching. // Dhs_30.134 //
Free from attachment to austerity, not a servant of evil groups,

children.text: saktūdakena santuṣṭaḥ sa bhikṣurniṣṭhuraḥ smṛtaḥ // Dhs_30.135 //
children.translated_text: Content with barley-water — that monk is remembered as austere. // Dhs_30.135 //

body.translated_text: Who is a pure monk?

children.translated_text: One who abandons all incoming sense objects, regarding them as fire,
Purified of faults, like a gem — that one is called a pure monk here. // Dhs_30.136 //
One who is purified within and without, adorned with knowledge and the rest,
Active, with the garment of morality and faith — that one is called a monk. // Dhs_30.137 //
One who has transcended the dharma of greed, standing firm like <s>Meru</s>,
Dear to all the world, peaceful, gone beyond — that one is called a monk. // Dhs_30.138 //
One who stays only three nights anywhere, who sits on a grass cushion,
Who frequents mountain caves — that one is called a liberated monk. // Dhs_30.139 //
One who fears evil, who is untouched, restrained and well-restrained,

children.text: jñānasevī sthiraḥ śānta ekākī bhikṣurucyate // Dhs_30.140 //
children.translated_text: Who pursues knowledge, firm, peaceful, solitary — that one is called a monk. // Dhs_30.140 //
Immovable, of pleasant speech, having avoided evil friends,
Unattached to all activities, liberated — that one is called a monk here. // Dhs_30.141 //

body.translated_text: Service of kings is service of false ochre-robed words

children.translated_text: Service of kings is censured for a monk who is a forest-dweller;
Such false service of ochre-robed words is the livelihood of a thief of death. // Dhs_30.142 //

children.text: na hi rājasevako bhikṣuryaḥ sevyo devatairapi /
children.translated_text: For a monk who serves kings is not worthy of worship even by gods;
One mingled with the flow of harm is a great servant of impurity. // Dhs_30.143 //

body.translated_text: Service of kings does not befit a monk

children.translated_text: For one who is pure, free from disease, free from desire, embodied,
Frightened by the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s> — the service of kings does not befit him. // Dhs_30.144 //
In forests, wilderness, and cremation grounds, in pools, on mountain ground,

children.text: prāntabhūmiṣu grāmasya sthitaḥ bhikṣuḥ praśobhate // Dhs_30.145 //
children.translated_text: In the outskirts of a village, standing there — a monk shines. // Dhs_30.145 //
In forests, wilderness, and cremation grounds — a monk, not through the service of kings.
One freed from meditation and study, eating morsels of food —
He should be known as not a monk, having a mind equal to a <s>piśāca</s> (demon). // Dhs_30.146 //
For the sages declare that from meditation comes pure happiness;

children.text: na tatsukhātsukhaṃ cānyadasti loke kathañcana // Dhs_30.147 //
children.translated_text: There is no other happiness in the world comparable to that happiness. // Dhs_30.147 //
That lowest of men who, having abandoned that supreme happiness of meditation,

children.text: raseṣu ramate bālastena mūḍho vihanyate // Dhs_30.148 //
children.translated_text: Delights in tastes like a fool — that deluded one is defeated. // Dhs_30.148 //
For one led astray by sense objects, whose mind is always absorbed in them,
Unwholesome dharmas increase, which drag one down in the next world. // Dhs_30.149 //

body.translated_text: A self-knowing monk attains <s>nirvāṇa</s>

children.translated_text: One who is humble regarding oneself, who questions teachers,
A monk of vigorous effort — he attains <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_30.150 //
He speaks only to the extent that he has learned;
One who knows himself, humble in pride — that monk becomes a knower of truth. // Dhs_30.151 //
One free from honor and dishonor, discerning the path and the non-path,

children.text: svaparārthavidhijño yaḥ sa tuṣṭo bhikṣurucyate // Dhs_30.152 //
children.translated_text: Who knows the method of benefiting self and others — that contented one is called a monk. // Dhs_30.152 //

body.translated_text: Whence comes peace for the proud?

children.translated_text: For the proud one, of cruel mind, fickle, and of small understanding,
Gone after gain and honor — whence will peace come? // Dhs_30.153 //
For one endowed with serene conduct, who pursues the range of knowledge,
Who is frightened by the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s> — renunciation is considered fruitful. // Dhs_30.154 //
One whose understanding does not let go regarding the nature of self and other,

children.text: na karmaṇyavipāke ca mārgāmārge tathaiva ca // Dhs_30.155 //
children.translated_text: Nor regarding action and its ripening, nor regarding the path and the non-path — // Dhs_30.155 //
A monk afflicted by attachment to dwelling does not find happiness
For one separated from good conduct, who is indifferent to happiness and suffering —
A monk ruined by dwelling is seen by others as childish. // Dhs_30.156 //
He becomes light as straw and declines from his own purpose.
A monk ruined by dwelling stands in a depleted forest. // Dhs_30.157 //
The mind does not engage in meditation, study, or duties.
A monk ruined by dwelling is intent on gathering people. // Dhs_30.158 //
For one whose mind is distracted by accumulation, life passes away.

children.text: kṣiṇoti retasaṃ svasya jīvitaṃ naiva gacchati // Dhs_30.159 //
children.translated_text: He exhausts his own vitality, yet life does not proceed. // Dhs_30.159 //

body.translated_text: Who goes to lower realms?

children.text: na ca vindati yat kṛtvā sukhamanyatra bhujyate /
children.translated_text: He does not find that, having done which, happiness is enjoyed elsewhere.
A monk ruined by dwelling, intent on gathering people,

children.text: pāpāni yāti nityaṃ sa tena gacchati durgatim // Dhs_30.160 //
children.translated_text: always goes toward evil — thereby he goes to lower realms. // Dhs_30.160 //

body.translated_text: The greatness of the ascetic dharma:

children.translated_text: For one whose mind is without expectation, who is without hope,
freed from all attachment — the ascetic life is considered fruitful. // Dhs_30.161 //
For one who always dwells in meditation among mountain caves and trees,
wholesome knowledge becomes clear, free from immorality. // Dhs_30.162 //

body.translated_text: Whose life is fruitful?

children.translated_text: Freed from all attachment, not deceived by sense-objects —
such a monk should be known as fruitful, like fire with dry fuel. // Dhs_30.163 //

body.translated_text: Praise of the monk who delights in <s>Nirvāṇa</s>:

children.translated_text: One who delights in <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, frightened of the ocean of existence,

children.text: bhikṣurbhavati śuddhātmā na nivāsena karhicit // Dhs_30.164 //
children.translated_text: a monk of pure self — never through dwelling. // Dhs_30.164 //

body.translated_text: Craving alone causes misfortune:

children.text: lobhamoheṣu ye śaktāste śaktā tṛṣṇayā sadā /
children.translated_text: Those who are attached to greed and delusion are always attached by craving.

children.text: tṛṣṇābandhanabaddhānāṃ nāyaṃ loko na cāparaḥ // Dhs_30.165 //
children.translated_text: For those bound by the bonds of craving, there is neither this world nor the next. // Dhs_30.165 //

body.translated_text: One who knows dharma does not reach lower realms:

children.translated_text: One whose mind is unattached to wrong deeds always,

children.text: apakṣapātī dharmajño na sa gacchati durgatim // Dhs_30.166 //
children.translated_text: impartial, knowing dharma — he does not go to lower realms. // Dhs_30.166 //

body.translated_text: Who is called a sage?

children.translated_text: One whose mind is not at all stained by the mud of faults,
dwelling alone in solitude, without hope — he is called a sage. // Dhs_30.167 //
Liberated, of stainless conduct, whose taints and defilements have ceased,

children.text: mukto yo viṣayaiḥ sarvairāraṇyo munirucyate // Dhs_30.168 //
children.translated_text: freed from all sense-objects, a forest-dweller — he is called a sage. // Dhs_30.168 //
One who never feels disgust from worldly dharmas,
equal-minded in happiness and suffering, stainless — he is called a sage. // Dhs_30.169 //
Contentment is the supreme dharma, always free from desire,
free from disease, living austerely, pure — he is called a sage here. // Dhs_30.170 //
One who does not form attachment wherever he goes,
walking alone, firm of mind, active — he is called a sage. // Dhs_30.171 //
One who knows the truth of the fruits of all good and evil deeds,
who renounces both good and evil — he is called a sage in the world. // Dhs_30.172 //
Striving for the destruction of faults, remembered as always going beyond desire,
knowing the truth of arising and passing away, wise — he is called a sage. // Dhs_30.173 //
The best among those who know place and time, speaking non-duality, with controlled senses,
frightened of the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>, peaceful — he is called a sage. // Dhs_30.174 //

body.translated_text: Which monk attains <s>Nirvāṇa</s>?

children.translated_text: A monk who dwells alone, with the five senses withdrawn,
knowing the truth of the marks of the body — he attains <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_30.175 //
A monk of vigor, truthful speech, always free from faults —
he attains <s>Nirvāṇa</s> as if going to a garden for play. // Dhs_30.176 //

body.translated_text: Be one of wholesome dharma:

children.text: dagdhe kleśe vayaṃ dagdhā vanaṃ dagdhaṃ yathāgninā /
children.translated_text: When defilements are burned, we are burned — as a forest is burned by fire.

children.text: kalyāṇadharme saṃraktā na raktā kāmabhojane // Dhs_30.177 //
children.translated_text: Devoted to wholesome dharma, not devoted to the enjoyment of desires. // Dhs_30.177 //

body.translated_text: Through deception people become deceivers:

children.translated_text: Those who are always eager to obtain, always devoted to their own people —

children.text: māyayā vañcakā (ye tu) mūḍhāste dharmavartmani // Dhs_30.178 //
children.translated_text: those who are deceivers through deception — they are fools on the path of dharma. // Dhs_30.178 //

body.translated_text: The mind should be engaged in wholesome action:

children.translated_text: Forests are delightful — there the mind rejoices.

children.text: ramante vītarāgāste na tu kāmagaveṣiṇaḥ // Dhs_30.179 //
children.translated_text: Those free from passion rejoice there — but not those who seek desires. // Dhs_30.179 //
One who is devoted to conversation, attached to sense-objects and craving,

children.text: na yāsyati puraṃ śāntaṃ yo ca mṛtyuṃ na vindati // Dhs_30.180 //
children.translated_text: will not go to the peaceful city — one who does not perceive death. // Dhs_30.180 //

body.translated_text: Be one who speaks non-duality:

children.translated_text: One whose mind is utterly peaceful, always devoted to meditation,
wholesome at the beginning, middle, and end, always in the domain of non-duality. // Dhs_30.181 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the thirtieth chapter on monks. //

children.translated_text: Compassion, giving, morality, patience, vigor,

children.text: dhyānaṃ prajñātha nirvāṇo mano bhikṣuśca te daśa //
children.translated_text: meditation, wisdom, and <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, mind, and monks — these are the ten. //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the third declaration. //
Now the fourth declaration:

children.translated_text: (Endowed with merit, divine happiness, friendship, praise of kings,
true dharma, mindfulness, and extensiveness — this collection is compiled.) //

body.translated_text: (31) Chapter on Merit:
Praise of merit:

children.text: ramaṇīyāni puṇyāni phalaṃ teṣāṃ paraṃ śubham /
children.translated_text: Merits are delightful; their fruit is supremely good.

children.text: tasmāt kuruta puṇyāni nāsti puṇyasamaṃ dhanam // Dhs_31.1 //
children.translated_text: Therefore do meritorious deeds — there is no wealth equal to merit. // Dhs_31.1 //
Merit is an inexhaustible treasure; merit is the unsurpassed jewel.

children.text: pradīpasadṛśaṃ puṇyaṃ mātṛvat pitṛvat sadā // Dhs_31.2 //
children.translated_text: Merit is like a lamp, always like a mother and father. // Dhs_31.2 //

children.text: puṇyaṃ kṛtvā gatā devāḥ puṇyaṃ nayati sadgatim /
children.translated_text: Having done merit, gods have gone; merit leads to a good destination.

children.text: puṇyaṃ kṛtvā narā loke modante tridive hi (te) // Dhs_31.3 //
children.translated_text: Having done merit, men in the world rejoice in heaven. // Dhs_31.3 //

body.translated_text: Merit is the supreme happiness:

children.text: puṇyādhikā hi puruṣā bhavanti sukhinaḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: Persons endowed with merit are always happy.

children.text: tasmāt kuruta puṇyāni nāsti puṇyasamaṃ sukham // Dhs_31.4 //
children.translated_text: Therefore do meritorious deeds — there is no happiness equal to merit. // Dhs_31.4 //

children.text: puṇyaṃ kṛtvā gatā devāḥ puṇyapriyadhanasya ca /
children.translated_text: Having done merit, gods have gone; for one whose wealth is beloved merit,

children.text: hetubhūtaṃ sadā dṛṣṭaṃ tasmāt puṇyaṃ paraṃ sukham // Dhs_31.5 //
children.translated_text: it is always seen as the cause — therefore merit is the supreme happiness. // Dhs_31.5 //

body.translated_text: Without merit, happiness is impossible:

children.translated_text: Merit is always seen as supreme, following like a shadow.

children.text: tasmāt sukhaṃ paraṃ puṇyaṃ nāsti puṇyādṛte sukham // Dhs_31.6 //
children.translated_text: Therefore merit is the supreme happiness — without merit there is no happiness. // Dhs_31.6 //

body.translated_text: The difference in the fruits of merit and demerit:

children.translated_text: Gods who have crossed beyond merit fall again, following good deeds.
The world has the fruits of merit and demerit — therefore one should practice merit. // Dhs_31.7 //

body.translated_text: Condemnation of demerit:

children.translated_text: Those devoid of merit, untamed, always going to lower realms —

children.text: kutasteṣāṃ sukhaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ sikatāsu yathā ghṛtam // Dhs_31.8 //
children.translated_text: where is happiness seen for them? Like butter in sand! // Dhs_31.8 //
Deceived by wealth, foolish, deprived of merit —

children.text: na teṣāṃ vidyate śarma duḥkhaṃ teṣāmanuttaram // Dhs_31.9 //
children.translated_text: there is no happiness for them; their suffering is unsurpassed. // Dhs_31.9 //

body.translated_text: Through the power of merit, one goes to the divine world:

children.text: mānuṣyaṃ sukṛtaṃ hyetat kṛte bhavati dehinaḥ /
children.translated_text: This human birth is indeed well-made; for the embodied one, this comes from doing good.
By that karma-fruition, one is born in the heavenly worlds. // Dhs_31.10 //

children.text: priyo bhavati yasyātmā yasya saukhye sthitā matiḥ /
children.translated_text: One who holds himself dear, whose mind is established in happiness —
let him do great merit for the sake of birth in the divine world. // Dhs_31.11 //

body.translated_text: Only a person who practices dharma attains happiness:

children.translated_text: A person who practices dharma attains happiness upon happiness.
Pure, he quickly attains the supreme peace.
Therefore do meritorious deeds — that which is always accumulative. // Dhs_31.12 //

body.translated_text: A doer of merit enjoys imperishable happiness:

children.text: puṇyakārī sadā dānto padaṃ gacchati cāvyayam /
children.translated_text: A doer of merit, always restrained, goes to the imperishable state.
Merits are delightful and should be done in many ways. // Dhs_31.13 //

body.translated_text: The variety of merit and the desirability of dharma:

children.text: vicitraṃ hi kṛtaṃ puṇyaṃ vicitraṃ paripacyate /
children.translated_text: Various merit done ripens in various ways.
For the world of the living, where dharma and adharma predominate everywhere —

children.text: śamatrāṇo yathā dharmastasmād dharmarato bhavet // Dhs_31.14 //
children.translated_text: dharma is a protection of peace — therefore one should delight in dharma. // Dhs_31.14 //

body.translated_text: One who practices adharma attains suffering:

children.text: yo (hi) dharma parityajya ramate kukṛte naraḥ /
children.translated_text: One who, having abandoned dharma, delights in wrongdoing —

children.text: tasya duṣkṛtadagdhasya duḥkhaṃ bhavati nityaśaḥ // Dhs_31.15 //
children.translated_text: for him, burned by wrongdoing, there is always suffering. // Dhs_31.15 //

body.translated_text: The mind should be set on dharma alone:

children.translated_text: As long as death has not arrived, as long as there is complete reflection,
the mind should be set on dharma — tranquility will come. // Dhs_31.16 //

body.translated_text: One who benefits others goes to the city of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>:

children.text: yo hi deśayate dharma pareṣāṃ hitakāṅkṣayā /
children.translated_text: One who teaches dharma to others out of desire for their welfare —

children.text: sa mātā sa pitā caiva nirvāṇapuradeśakaḥ // Dhs_31.17 //
children.translated_text: he is a mother, he is a father, a guide to the city of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_31.17 //

body.translated_text: The Teacher's well-spoken word is priceless:

children.translated_text: The one teacher who is supremely devoted to the good and who teaches —
he, knowing the path to the other destination, becomes a protector of embodied beings.

children.text: na mūlyaṃ vidyate śāstuḥ subhāṣitapadasya vai // Dhs_31.18 //
children.translated_text: There is no price for the Teacher's well-spoken word indeed. // Dhs_31.18 //

body.translated_text: The difference between ordinary wealth and dharma-wealth:

children.text: na padaṃ labhate śāntaṃ yad dhanairupalabhyate /
children.translated_text: The peaceful state is not obtained by wealth that can be acquired.

children.text: dravyaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ na dharmo buddhibandhanam // Dhs_31.19 //
children.translated_text: Ordinary wealth is seen — but dharma is not a bondage of intellect. // Dhs_31.19 //

body.translated_text: Dharma-wealth is indestructible:

children.text: dravyaṃ vinaśyati nṛṇāṃ dharmadravyaṃ na jātu vai /
children.translated_text: The wealth of men perishes, but dharma-wealth never.
Through thousands of lives, dharma alone follows. // Dhs_31.20 //

body.translated_text: Not even one step of wealth follows one who is going.

children.translated_text: Their possessions are lost to kings, thieves, and fire.
But dharma-wealth cannot in any way be taken. // Dhs_31.21 //

body.translated_text: Therefore one should be devoted to dharma:

children.translated_text: After enjoying happiness in many ways for a short time,

children.text: bhavatyavaśyaṃ patanaṃ tasmād dharmaparo bhavet // Dhs_31.22 //
children.translated_text: the fall is inevitable — therefore one should be devoted to dharma. // Dhs_31.22 //

children.text: dharma ekaḥ paraṃ trāṇaṃ dharma ekaḥ parā gatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Dharma alone is the supreme protection; dharma alone is the supreme destination.
By dharma one advances; and death comes from adharma. // Dhs_31.23 //

body.translated_text: Praise of the dharma-practitioner:

children.translated_text: Dharma is excellent — a dharma-practitioner devotes himself to dharma alone.

children.text: sa sukhāt sukhamāpnoti na duḥkhamanupaśyati // Dhs_31.24 //
children.translated_text: He attains happiness upon happiness and does not see suffering. // Dhs_31.24 //

body.translated_text: Condemnation of the adharma-practitioner:

children.translated_text: When a person who practices adharma devotes himself to adharma,

children.text: sa tadā duḥkhamāpnoti narakeṣu punaḥ punaḥ // Dhs_31.25 //
children.translated_text: then he attains suffering — in hells, again and again. // Dhs_31.25 //

body.translated_text: The greatness of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>:

children.translated_text: The fruit of faith in the Three Jewels, cultivated in many ways,
is <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, preceded by heaven in former lives. // Dhs_31.26 //

body.translated_text: Merit should be practiced by oneself:

children.translated_text: Merit is done by oneself, attained by oneself.

children.text: sukhaṃ vā yadi vā duḥkhamātmanaivopabhujyate // Dhs_31.27 //
children.translated_text: Whether happiness or suffering — it is experienced by oneself alone. // Dhs_31.27 //

body.translated_text: The power of merit for one who is moral is vast:

children.translated_text: Like the current of a river, it flows unceasingly for a person —

children.text: puṇyaprabhāvo vipulo yasya śīle rataṃ manaḥ // Dhs_31.28 //
children.translated_text: vast is the power of merit for one whose mind delights in morality. // Dhs_31.28 //

children.text: bhavajanyaṃ phalaṃ yasya (yasmai) dharmo na rocate /
children.translated_text: The fruit born of existence — for one in whom dharma does not please,

children.text: dharmo hi nayati svarga dharmacārī sukhānvitaḥ // Dhs_31.29 //
children.translated_text: dharma leads to heaven; the dharma-practitioner is endowed with happiness. // Dhs_31.29 //

body.translated_text: Without dharma, a person goes to hell:

children.translated_text: This alone is sufficient — the protection of dharma.
Without dharma, a person runs after hells. // Dhs_31.30 //

body.translated_text: Death is better than condemning dharma:

children.text: śreyo bhaveddhi maraṇaṃ na tu dharmavigarhaṇam /
children.translated_text: Death would be better than the condemnation of dharma.

children.text: dharmeṇa varjito lokaḥ saṃsāre sarvadā bhramet // Dhs_31.31 //
children.translated_text: A world devoid of dharma would always wander in <s>saṃsāra</s>. // Dhs_31.31 //

body.translated_text: The life of one devoid of dharma is full of suffering:

children.translated_text: For one devoid of the eye of dharma, whose mind is overcome by delusion,

children.text: vṛthā saukhyamidaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭvā yāto yathāparaḥ // Dhs_31.32 //
children.translated_text: this happiness is seen as vain — having seen it, one goes as if to another. // Dhs_31.32 //
The sprout of dharma does not grow in the field of the mind of one without consciousness.
One whose intellect bestows morality, devoted to the practice of dharma, // Dhs_31.33 //
through goodness, thoroughly pure, cultivated with effort —

children.text: prayānti tat padaṃ śāntaṃ yatra duḥkhaṃ na vidyate // Dhs_31.34 //
children.translated_text: they go to that peaceful state where suffering does not exist. // Dhs_31.34 //

body.translated_text: One subject to the senses does not overcome <s>Māra</s>:

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ vaśe yastu viṣayeṣu tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: One who is subject to the senses and likewise to sense-objects —

children.text: sa sarvabandhanairbaddhaḥ sa māraṃ nātivartate // Dhs_31.35 //
children.translated_text: bound by all bonds, he does not overcome <s>Māra</s>. // Dhs_31.35 //

body.translated_text: One unstained by evil dharmas is truly well:

children.translated_text: Unstained by evil dharmas, shining like gold beyond poverty —

children.text: sa muktabhavakāntāraḥ svastho bhavati sarvataḥ // Dhs_31.36 //
children.translated_text: freed from the wilderness of existence, he is well on all sides. // Dhs_31.36 //

body.translated_text: Through worship of the <s>Buddha</s> and others, one gains <s>nirvāṇa</s>

children.text: buddho yeṣāṃ bahumato nityaṃ dharmaśca gocaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Those for whom the <s>Buddha</s> is always held in high esteem and the Dharma is their domain,
who serve the feet of their teacher and have faith in actions — // Dhs_31.37 //
through worship of the Three Jewels always, with good and pure understanding,
through worship of mother and father, they go toward the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_31.38 //
The dharmas of renunciation and the nature of existence are proclaimed for all alike;
from the celibate life and such practices, all supreme happiness is produced. // Dhs_31.39 //

body.translated_text: The gift of the Dharma is the most supreme

children.translated_text: Among gifts, the supreme gift is said to be the gift of the Dharma;

children.text: udyogānāṃ sadā dhyānaṃ yena gacchati nirvṛtim // Dhs_31.40 //
children.translated_text: among exertions, meditation always, by which one attains peace. // Dhs_31.40 //

body.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s> is declared the foremost

children.translated_text: Of the world above, below, and across, with its manifold actions,
the <s>Tathāgata</s> is declared the foremost, the seer of the truth of dharmas. // Dhs_31.41 //
Among groups, the noble one is said to be the best in the terrible [quest for] meaning;

children.text: kṣetrāṇāṃ trividhaṃ puṇyaṃ guṇaduḥkhobhayaṃ tataḥ // Dhs_31.42 //
children.translated_text: the threefold merit of fields — both virtue and suffering — [arises] from that. // Dhs_31.42 //

children.text: mātā pitṛsamaḥ pūjya upādhyāyaḥ sadā bhavet /
children.translated_text: The preceptor, equal to mother and father, should always be revered;
he opens the eye toward the domain of mastery. // Dhs_31.43 //

body.translated_text: Sense objects are considered to be without happiness

children.text: agrāhyā vā sadā dṛṣṭā muninā tattvadarśinā /
children.translated_text: Always seen as ungraspable by the sage who sees truth,

children.text: sukhasya bhūmayo hyetā niḥsukhā viṣayā matāḥ // Dhs_31.44 //
children.translated_text: these grounds of happiness — sense objects are considered to be without happiness. // Dhs_31.44 //
If one thus practices the Dharma, stainless and path-revealing,

children.text: saukhyaṃ tasya bhavennityaṃ na saukhyaṃ devabhūmiṣu // Dhs_31.45 //
children.translated_text: his happiness will be eternal — not the happiness in the realms of the gods. // Dhs_31.45 //
Merit done in other existences stands behind embodied beings;

children.text: sa āhūya prayatnena sevitavyaḥ sadā naraiḥ // Dhs_31.46 //
children.translated_text: having invited it with effort, it should always be served by people. // Dhs_31.46 //

children.text: anāgate bhayaṃ yo hi paśyati buddhacakṣuṣā /
children.translated_text: He who sees danger in the future with the eye of the <s>Buddha</s> —

children.text: sa paṇḍitaḥ sadā dhīro mūrkhatvādatibhīrukaḥ // Dhs_31.47 //
children.translated_text: that wise one is always courageous, apprehensive of foolishness. // Dhs_31.47 //
Having seen the fear born of misfortune, the wise one sees the path;

children.text: sa hi vighne tu samprāpte na viṣādena bādhyate // Dhs_31.48 //
children.translated_text: he, when an obstacle has arrived, is not afflicted by dejection. // Dhs_31.48 //
But the one of deluded mind always serves sense objects;

children.text: vimohitaḥ sa viṣayaiḥ paścāttāpena dahyate // Dhs_31.49 //
children.translated_text: deluded by sense objects, he is later burned with remorse. // Dhs_31.49 //

body.translated_text: Throughout one's entire life, merit should be performed

children.text: yāvat samagraṃ janmedaṃ jñānaṃ yāti vināvilam /
children.translated_text: As long as this entire life goes toward knowledge without turbidity,

children.text: tāvat kuruta puṇyāni duḥkhaṃ hayakṛtapuṇyatā // Dhs_31.50 //
children.translated_text: so long perform meritorious deeds — for the state of having done no merit is suffering. // Dhs_31.50 //

children.text: kṣayaṃ prayānti puṇyāni tvaritaṃ yāti jīvitam /
children.translated_text: Merits proceed to exhaustion; life passes swiftly;
effort should be made in the accumulation of Dharma, to the satisfaction of the gods. // Dhs_31.51 //

children.text: yo hi dharma parityajya pramādopahato naraḥ /
children.translated_text: He who, having abandoned the Dharma, is a person struck by heedlessness,

children.text: na sañcinoti puṇyāni sa paścādapi tapyate // Dhs_31.52 //
children.translated_text: who does not accumulate merits — he is later scorched. // Dhs_31.52 //

children.text: na yāvadāyāti jarā na vyādhiḥ saha mṛtyunā /
children.translated_text: Before old age comes, before disease comes with death,

children.text: tāvat kāryāṇi puṇyāni mā paścāt paritapyatha // Dhs_31.53 //
children.translated_text: so long perform meritorious deeds — lest you later grieve. // Dhs_31.53 //
For one who has not accumulated merit, who is struck by heedlessness,

children.text: narake kāraṇaṃ duḥkhaṃ pramādastvāṃ haniṣyati // Dhs_31.54 //
children.translated_text: suffering is the cause of hell — heedlessness will destroy you. // Dhs_31.54 //

children.text: kiṃ tasya jīvitenārthaḥ kiṃ bhāgyaiḥ kiṃ ca bāndhavaiḥ /
children.translated_text: What use is his life? What use his fortune? What use his kinsmen?

children.text: sabalendriyatāṃ prāpya yo na dharmarataḥ sadā // Dhs_31.55 //
children.translated_text: One who, having attained the fullness of faculties, does not always delight in the Dharma. // Dhs_31.55 //
Day by day, the mind should be set on the accumulation of Dharma,

children.text: viratiścāpi pāpebhyaḥ sādhūnāṃ darśane na ca // Dhs_31.56 //
children.translated_text: and on abstention from sins — and not on the sight of the good [alone]. // Dhs_31.56 //

children.text: śīlena yaḥ suro janma labdhvedaṃ kāmamohitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The god who by moral conduct has obtained this birth, yet is deluded by desire,

children.text: na sañcinoti puṇyāni sa bhavaṃ nātivartate // Dhs_31.57 //
children.translated_text: and does not accumulate merits — he does not go beyond existence. // Dhs_31.57 //

body.translated_text: Those who delight in the Dharma should always be honored

children.translated_text: Those who delight in the undertaking of knowledge, adorned with the jewel of moral conduct,

children.text: kāmarāgāddhi ye bhītā devānāṃ devasammatāḥ // Dhs_31.58 //
children.translated_text: who are fearful of desire and passion — they are esteemed as gods among gods. // Dhs_31.58 //

children.text: devāste hi sadā vandyā ye dharme niratāḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: Those gods should always be honored who are always devoted to the Dharma;

children.text: ye tu nityaṃ bhavāsaktāste sarve nidhanaṃ gatāḥ // Dhs_31.59 //
children.translated_text: but those who are always attached to existence — they have all gone to destruction. // Dhs_31.59 //
Having obtained this bridge of Dharma, great, leading to the other shore,

children.text: na sañcarati yastūrṇa bhavānnaiva pramucyate // Dhs_31.60 //
children.translated_text: one who does not traverse it quickly is never freed from existence. // Dhs_31.60 //

body.translated_text: Merit never perishes

children.translated_text: Through the dharmas that follow after merit, there is always merit;
in thousands of billions of <s>kalpas</s>, merit never perishes. // Dhs_31.61 //

body.translated_text: For the sake of obtaining merit, duties should be performed

children.text: saṅgṛhītaṃ sadā śīlaṃ jñānaṃ ca parivartitam /
children.translated_text: Moral conduct always guarded, knowledge always turned over,

children.text: dānaṃ cābhikṣayā dattaṃ bhavati svarasātmakam // Dhs_31.62 //
children.translated_text: generosity given without stinginess — becomes one's own nature. // Dhs_31.62 //

body.translated_text: Virtues should always be cultivated

children.translated_text: The three faults are destroyed by the three [virtues] — generosity and the rest — for humans;

children.text: tasmād doṣān parityajya guṇāḥ sevyāḥ prayatnataḥ // Dhs_31.63 //
children.translated_text: therefore, having abandoned faults, virtues should be diligently cultivated. // Dhs_31.63 //

body.translated_text: Through knowledge, worldly suffering is destroyed

children.translated_text: Association with the Dharma-minded, and the undertaking of knowledge with effort —
suffering born of existence is destroyed, as darkness by the rays of the sun. // Dhs_31.64 //
One who is to be approached, who delights the gods, is worshiped by the deities;

children.text: prāpya janmāntara cāpi nirvṛtiṃ cāśu gacchati // Dhs_31.65 //
children.translated_text: having obtained another birth, he also quickly attains peace. // Dhs_31.65 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the thirty-first chapter, on Merit. //
(32) Chapter on the Gods (<s>Deva</s>)
Persons who walk the path of the <s>Sugata</s> are equal to gods

children.text: panthāno muninā śāstre uktā ye tattvadarśinā /
children.translated_text: The paths declared by the sage, the teacher, the seer of truth —
those who have set forth on those are indeed persons esteemed as gods. // Dhs_32.1 //

body.translated_text: The path declared by the <s>Sugata</s>

children.text: satyaṃ hi dānaṃ ca tathaiva maitrī sattveṣu rakṣā priyavāditā ca /
children.translated_text: Truth and generosity and likewise loving-kindness, protection of beings and pleasant speech,
right view and a pure mind — the Buddhas call this the path to heaven. // Dhs_32.2 //
One endowed with bright dharmas, possessed of a bright mind,
goes from happiness to greater happiness, seeking light upon light. // Dhs_32.3 //
Full of light upon light, like a lamp from another lamp,
from that one proceeds and attains the supreme worlds. // Dhs_32.4 //

body.translated_text: One of good conduct goes to the proximity of the gods

children.text: yasya śuddhaṃ sadā cittaṃ nirmalaṃ maṇivat sadā /
children.translated_text: One whose mind is always pure, always stainless like a jewel —

children.text: sa śānto nirmamo dhīmān devānāmantikaṃ vrajet // Dhs_32.5 //
children.translated_text: that peaceful, selfless, wise one goes to the proximity of the gods. // Dhs_32.5 //
One whose mind is endowed with merit through meditation, moral conduct, and <s>samādhi</s> —

children.text: sa dhīmān kāñcanaprakhyo devānāmantikaṃ vrajet // Dhs_32.6 //
children.translated_text: that wise one, radiant as gold, goes to the proximity of the gods. // Dhs_32.6 //
One who abstains from taking life, devoted to compassion for all beings,
who follows the stream of seasons and compassion — goes to the proximity of the gods. // Dhs_32.7 //
One who is learned, who has avoided cruel actions toward all the world,
untouched by sinful dharmas — goes to the proximity of the gods. // Dhs_32.8 //

children.text: tṛṇavat kāñcanaṃ yasya kāmā yasya viṣopamāḥ /
children.translated_text: One for whom gold is like grass, for whom desires are like poison —

children.text: sa kāmavarjako dhīmān devānāmantikaṃ vrajet // Dhs_32.9 //
children.translated_text: that wise one who avoids desires goes to the proximity of the gods. // Dhs_32.9 //
One whose mind is not dragged by desires and sense objects that cause passion,
nor by the wilderness of existence on all sides — goes to the proximity of the gods. // Dhs_32.10 //
One who, when lineages were broken at first, was a friend with wealth and kinsmen,

children.text: yaḥ karoti susaṃśliṣṭā devānāmantikaṃ vrajet // Dhs_32.11 //
children.translated_text: who makes them well-united — goes to the proximity of the gods. // Dhs_32.11 //

children.text: yasya buddhisthitaṃ veśma na buddhiḥ kvāpi rāgiṇī /
children.translated_text: One whose abode is established in wisdom, whose wisdom is never passionate —
that one who has conquered enemies, of purified self — goes to the proximity of the gods. // Dhs_32.12 //
