One whose bodily action is praiseworthy, who has ceased from sin and is happy,

children.text: sa kāmavirato dhyāyī devānāmantikaṃ vrajet // Dhs_32.13 //
children.translated_text: that meditator who is free from desires — goes to the proximity of the gods. // Dhs_32.13 //
Freed from evil friends, free from the poison of craving,

children.text: na baddhaḥ strībhayaiḥ pāśairdevānāmantikaṃ vrajet // Dhs_32.14 //
children.translated_text: not bound by the fetters of the fear of women — goes to the proximity of the gods. // Dhs_32.14 //
One who speaks with effort regarding the Dharma, possessed of generosity, morality, and <s>samādhi</s>,
always diligent, of firm resolve — goes to the proximity of the gods. // Dhs_32.15 //
One by whom the fetter of right bondage has been cut as if by a sword,
whose fetters are truly cut, who is self-mastered — goes to the proximity of the gods. // Dhs_32.16 //

body.translated_text: Through the ripening of meritorious karma, one is born in the heavenly realm

children.translated_text: Those beings who, while human, practice what brings merit —
through that ripening of karma, they are born in the heavenly realm. // Dhs_32.17 //

body.translated_text: Only those who resort to the path of Dharma are strong

children.text: manuṣyāṇāṃ balād devā devānāṃ balino narāḥ /
children.translated_text: Gods are stronger than humans; among gods, those persons are stronger
who are mutually strong — those who are established on the path of the true Dharma. // Dhs_32.18 //

body.translated_text: The three grounds of lower rebirth

children.translated_text: For the gods, the good destiny is the mortal realm; for mortals, the good destiny is the gods;
there are three grounds of lower rebirth — for those devoid of meritorious karma. // Dhs_32.19 //

body.translated_text: All happiness depends on the Dharma

children.text: dharmādhīnaṃ sukhaṃ sarva dharmādhīnā hi nirvṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: All happiness depends on the Dharma; peace too depends on the Dharma;

children.text: dharmaḥ supteṣu jāgarti dharmo hi paramā gatiḥ // Dhs_32.20 //
children.translated_text: the Dharma is awake among the sleeping; the Dharma indeed is the supreme destination. // Dhs_32.20 //

body.translated_text: The <s>asuras</s> are defeated by the gods

children.translated_text: Through dharma, non-dharma is defeated; through truth, the liar is defeated;

children.text: jñānena varjito moho devaistu hyasurā jitāḥ // Dhs_32.21 //
children.translated_text: through knowledge, delusion is eliminated; the <s>asuras</s> are defeated by the gods. // Dhs_32.21 //

body.translated_text: The heavenly realm is the arising of happiness

children.text: sopānabhūtā ye tāni karmāṇi tridivasya hi /
children.translated_text: Those actions which are the stairway to heaven —

children.text: yoniṃ tyaktvā narā yānti devalokaṃ sukhodayam // Dhs_32.22 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned [lower] birth, people go to the heavenly realm, the arising of happiness. // Dhs_32.22 //

body.translated_text: Through restraint of speech, the wise enjoy happiness in heaven

children.translated_text: The fourfold discipline of speech — some say threefold, some fivefold —
ascending the sevenfold stairway, the wise go to heaven. // Dhs_32.23 //

children.text: prabhayā te ca divyantaḥ svaśarīreṇa jātayā /
children.translated_text: Shining with their divine radiance, born from their own bodies,

children.text: ramante svargabhuvane rañjitāḥ svena karmaṇā // Dhs_32.24 //
children.translated_text: they delight in the heavenly realm, delighted by their own karma. // Dhs_32.24 //

body.translated_text: Moral conduct alone is the cause of merit

children.translated_text: Those who always dwell in fragrance, who always dwell in happiness —

children.text: yad devā devabhavane śīlaṃ tatra hi kāraṇam // Dhs_32.25 //
children.translated_text: the reason that the gods [live] in the heavenly realm is indeed moral conduct. // Dhs_32.25 //
That they are surrounded by <s>apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs), that they are resplendent like the sun and moon —
all that, for the gods among gods, has merit as its cause. // Dhs_32.26 //

children.text: yadīpsitaṃ sambhavati sambhūtaṃ ca na hīyate /
children.translated_text: That what is desired comes into being, and having come into being does not diminish,

children.text: vartate ca śubhaṃ nityaṃ tat sarva śubhahetukam // Dhs_32.27 //
children.translated_text: and merit always continues — all that has merit as its cause. // Dhs_32.27 //

body.translated_text: One who practices merit goes to the equality of the gods

children.translated_text: One who always practices merit, generous, devoted to compassion for all beings,

children.text: dānamaitryā sadā yukto devānāṃ samatāṃ vrajet // Dhs_32.28 //
children.translated_text: always endowed with generosity and loving-kindness — goes to the equality of the gods. // Dhs_32.28 //
One who abstains from taking life, devoted to compassion for all beings,
of right livelihood and conduct — goes to the company of the gods. // Dhs_32.29 //

children.text: adatte na ratiḥ kiñcid dāne cāsya sadāmatiḥ /
children.translated_text: One who takes no delight in what is not given, whose mind is always set on giving,
with peaceful senses, the wise one — attains the company of the gods. // Dhs_32.30 //
One who is freed from false desires, who always delights in the true path,
who desires <s>nirvāṇa</s>, who is pure — goes to the proximity of the gods. // Dhs_32.31 //

children.text: vimanaskaṃ hi yat prīte puruṣe kurute laghu /
children.translated_text: One who, when another person is pleased, does not make light of [it],

children.text: madyavarjī paraṃ dhīro devānāmantikaṃ vrajet // Dhs_32.32 //
children.translated_text: the wise one who avoids liquor — goes to the proximity of the gods. // Dhs_32.32 //

body.translated_text: One free from heedlessness attains happiness

children.text: sukha (prāṇo) hi yo devaḥ pramādaṃ nānusevate /
children.translated_text: That god who, possessed of the breath of happiness, does not serve heedlessness —
he obtains happiness after happiness and attains peace. // Dhs_32.33 //
That happiness whose end is exhaustion — <s>nirvāṇa</s> is eternal;
having attained that, the best among persons shine in celestial palaces. // Dhs_32.34 //
Higher and higher is <s>Meru</s>; from that, happiness is always higher;
the being bound by merit would conquer the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> (highest) gods. // Dhs_32.35 //
In what is blameless, how can there be satiation, especially in the heavenly realm?

children.text: atīva saukhyaṃ labhate kasmād deveṣu sarvadā // Dhs_32.36 //
children.translated_text: Exceedingly great happiness is obtained — why [not] always among the gods? // Dhs_32.36 //

body.translated_text: Who obtains happiness?

children.translated_text: One who is burned by the fire of craving does not obtain happiness;
likewise, one who is burned of his own merit does not obtain happiness. // Dhs_32.37 //
Having performed the threefold meritorious deed, of three kinds and three causes,

children.text: etadagryaṃ tribhūmiṣṭhaṃ (triguṇaṃ ca) phalaṃ mahat // Dhs_32.38 //
children.translated_text: this is the foremost — situated in the three grounds, with three qualities, and great fruit. // Dhs_32.38 //
Those devoted to non-violence and generosity, who are intent on the true Dharma,
endowed with truth, patience, and self-control — they have reached heaven. // Dhs_32.39 //
Endowed with divine ornaments, adorned with divine garlands —

children.text: yad devā divyamatayaḥ (kurvanti) śubhameva tat // Dhs_32.40 //
children.translated_text: whatever the gods of divine intellect do — that is auspicious alone. // Dhs_32.40 //
The great happiness of the gods, established as neither deficient nor excessive —

children.text: nyūnamadhyaṃ tu yasyaitat phalaṃ puṇyasya dṛśyate // Dhs_32.41 //
children.translated_text: whether inferior or middling, this fruit of merit is seen. // Dhs_32.41 //

body.translated_text: The maker of merit goes to the realm of the gods

children.text: yena yāvaddhi yat puṇyaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavati dehinā /
children.translated_text: Whatever merit has been performed by an embodied being, to whatever extent —

children.text: tasya tāvaddhi tat saukhyaṃ devalokeṣu pacyate // Dhs_32.42 //
children.translated_text: to that same extent, that happiness ripens for him in the realms of the gods. // Dhs_32.42 //

body.translated_text: The guarding of morality is essential

children.text: svāgataṃ tava bho bhadra! sukṛtaṃ kṛtavānasi /
children.translated_text: Welcome to you, O good one! You have performed good deeds;

children.text: saptadhā rakṣitaṃ śīlaṃ tasyaitat phalamāgatam // Dhs_32.43 //
children.translated_text: morality guarded in seven ways — this fruit thereof has come. // Dhs_32.43 //

body.translated_text: Delight with the divinities!

children.translated_text: In forests, parks, and mountains, in lotus-filled groves,
on the tops of golden palaces — delight always with the divinities! // Dhs_32.44 //
In forests, parks, and mountains, on peaks of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli),

children.text: vanādriṣu ca naikeṣu ramasva saha daivataiḥ // Dhs_32.45 //
children.translated_text: in many forest-mountains — delight with the divinities! // Dhs_32.45 //
Among lovely wish-fulfilling trees, at river springs,

children.text: saritsu ca viśālāsu (ramasva) saha daivataiḥ // Dhs_32.46 //
children.translated_text: and on broad rivers — delight with the divinities! // Dhs_32.46 //
On mountains endowed with flowing streams and rivers,

children.text: nagareṣu mahārtheṣu ramasva saha daivataiḥ // Dhs_32.47 //
children.translated_text: in great and prosperous cities — delight with the divinities! // Dhs_32.47 //
Among fragrant blossoming trees, in blue lotus groves,

children.text: yakṣasadmasu ramyeṣu ramasva saha daivataiḥ // Dhs_32.48 //
children.translated_text: in lovely abodes of <s>Yakṣas</s> — delight with the divinities! // Dhs_32.48 //
In remote regions of the earth, in jewel-mine forests,

children.text: vimāneṣu ca ramyeṣu ramasva saha daivataiḥ // Dhs_32.49 //
children.translated_text: in lovely celestial chariots — delight with the divinities! // Dhs_32.49 //
With fivefold musical instruments that gladden the mind,

children.text: nṛtyamānaḥ sukhī nityaṃ ramasva saha daivataiḥ // Dhs_32.50 //
children.translated_text: dancing and always happy — delight with the divinities! // Dhs_32.50 //
Having purified the seed of morality, through various moralities,
play with various divine pleasures, as you enjoy what is fitting. // Dhs_32.51 //
That the gods, garlanded with radiance, delight in various pleasures —

children.text: tacchubhasya phalaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ nirmalasya viśeṣataḥ // Dhs_32.52 //
children.translated_text: that is seen as the fruit of the auspicious, especially of the spotless. // Dhs_32.52 //
That these gods play with various pleasures in many ways —

children.text: na vayaṃ hetavastatra (tatra hetuḥ) purākṛtam // Dhs_32.53 //
children.translated_text: we are not the causes therein; the cause is what was done before. // Dhs_32.53 //
All the mansions, always variegated by <s>karma</s> —
the god enjoys among the gods, nourished by good deeds. // Dhs_32.54 //
For one freed from the threefold noose, guarded by the five,
having transcended a single dharma — the realm of the gods is exalted. // Dhs_32.55 //
Of people with joyful minds, their clear conduct is well-composed —
they have arrived at the abode of the gods, witnesses of the fruit of their own <s>karma</s>. // Dhs_32.56 //

body.translated_text: The fruit of good deeds

children.translated_text: Happiness upon happiness, and also of good deeds —

children.text: bhuñjanti vibudhāḥ svarga yaddhi pūrvakṛtānugam // Dhs_32.57 //
children.translated_text: the wise enjoy heaven, for it follows what was formerly done. // Dhs_32.57 //
These various trees are witnesses of all <s>karmas</s>;
the wise speak ceaselessly and fittingly. // Dhs_32.58 //

body.translated_text: Fortune bears fruit everywhere

children.translated_text: By whatever ripening, wherever one is reborn —

children.text: puruṣo labhate svasya prārabdhasya śubhāśubham // Dhs_32.59 //
children.translated_text: a person obtains the auspicious and inauspicious of what was undertaken. // Dhs_32.59 //

body.translated_text: By good <s>karma</s>, a being is always born among the gods

children.translated_text: By good <s>karma</s>, a being is always born among the gods;
and by evil <s>karma</s>, the lowest of men fall into hell. // Dhs_32.60 //

body.translated_text: Those attached to desires do not perceive death

children.translated_text: Attached to the auspicious and inauspicious, those desirous ones deluded by desire —
they do not perceive the death that will inevitably come. // Dhs_32.61 //
This ripening of good and evil that is observed in trees —

children.text: na saukhyād viramantyete manaḥ saukhyena mohitāḥ // Dhs_32.62 //
children.translated_text: they do not cease from pleasure, their minds deluded by happiness. // Dhs_32.62 //

body.translated_text: Having performed good deeds, people go to the gods

children.text: trividhaṃ sukṛtaṃ kṛtvā bhāvayitvā ca saptadhā /
children.translated_text: Having performed the threefold good deed and cultivated it in seven ways,

children.text: trisaṃkhyākān ripūn hatvā yānti deveṣu mānavāḥ // Dhs_32.63 //
children.translated_text: having slain the threefold enemies — people go to the gods. // Dhs_32.63 //

body.translated_text: Who goes to the presence of the gods?

children.translated_text: One who does not envy the hardships of action and does not envy joy —

children.text: sa nandyasūyakaḥ śuddho devānāmantikaṃ gataḥ // Dhs_32.64 //
children.translated_text: that one, free from envy, purified, has gone to the presence of the gods. // Dhs_32.64 //
Having censured this envy, the great abode of suffering,

children.text: samaṃ ca trividhaṃ dattvā devānāmantikaṃ gataḥ // Dhs_32.65 //
children.translated_text: and having given equally in threefold manner — one has gone to the presence of the gods. // Dhs_32.65 //
Having always protected the lives of beings with compassion,

children.text: maitracittaḥ sadā dānto devānāmantikaṃ gataḥ // Dhs_32.66 //
children.translated_text: with a mind of loving-kindness, always restrained — one has gone to the presence of the gods. // Dhs_32.66 //

children.text: adattaṃ ca dhanaṃ dattvā dattvānandaṃ ca sarvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having given wealth that was not given, and having given joy everywhere,
with a mind cultivated by intention — one should go to the presence of the gods. // Dhs_32.67 //
Having regarded the wives of others as mothers, a contemplator of true meaning,
unstained by evil dharmas — one should go to the presence of the gods. // Dhs_32.68 //
That which arises from the fire-stick of the tongue, done for the pleasure of one's own mind —

children.text: kathyate sa mṛṣāvādastaṃ hitvā sugatiṃ vrajet // Dhs_32.69 //
children.translated_text: that is called false speech; having abandoned it, one should go to a good destination. // Dhs_32.69 //

children.text: paiśūnyaṃ ca sadā hitvā maitryanarthakaraṃ padam /
children.translated_text: Having always abandoned slander, the basis of harm to friendship,
one of gentle radiance and gentle mind should go to the presence of the gods. // Dhs_32.70 //
The hero always avoids harsh speech as if it were an enemy;
one of gentle radiance and mind always goes to all destinations. // Dhs_32.71 //

children.text: adharmo yasya jihvāgre na bhūto na bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: One on whose tongue-tip <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) has never been and will never be,
always knowing the truth of adversity — one should go to the presence of the gods. // Dhs_32.72 //
By whom this morality has been guarded in the sevenfold way taught by the <s>Buddha</s> —

children.text: sa dhīraḥ śīlatattvajño devānāmantikaṃ vrajet // Dhs_32.73 //
children.translated_text: that steadfast one, knowing the truth of morality, should go to the presence of the gods. // Dhs_32.73 //

body.translated_text: Who is a fruitful knower of Dharma?

children.translated_text: This birth, subject to the power of various <s>karmas</s>, is obtained among the gods;

children.text: tatprāpya yo na dharmajñaḥ sa paścāt paritapyate // Dhs_32.74 //
children.translated_text: having obtained it, one who does not know the Dharma repents afterward. // Dhs_32.74 //

body.translated_text: From good deeds, auspicious fruit

children.translated_text: This world, lovely with forests, parks, and creeper-pavilions —

children.text: yadvicitramayo lokastat sarva śubhajaṃ phalam // Dhs_32.75 //
children.translated_text: whatever is wondrous in the world, all that is the fruit born of the auspicious. // Dhs_32.75 //

children.text: yena yena yathā karma kṛtaṃ bhavati śobhanam /
children.translated_text: By whomever, in whatever way, beautiful <s>karma</s> has been performed —

children.text: tasya tasya tathā dṛṣṭaṃ phalaṃ tadanugāmikam // Dhs_32.76 //
children.translated_text: for that person, accordingly, the fruit that follows is seen. // Dhs_32.76 //
Happiness — inferior, middling, and supreme — is seen directly by the gods;

children.text: yena yena yathā cīrṇaṃ tasya tasya tathā phalam // Dhs_32.77 //
children.translated_text: by whomever, in whatever way it was practiced — for that person, accordingly, is the fruit. // Dhs_32.77 //

body.translated_text: From evil deeds, suffering-born fruit

children.translated_text: The gods of variegated appearance, deluded, following the power of delusion —

children.text: tannāśānmanasā mūḍhā na paśyanti mahadbhayam // Dhs_32.78 //
children.translated_text: their minds bewildered by its destruction, they do not see the great danger. // Dhs_32.78 //
Those of variegated sensual delights, desiring variegated fruits —

children.text: na vā kurvanti karmāṇi te 'surā mūḍhacetasaḥ // Dhs_32.79 //
children.translated_text: they do not perform good <s>karmas</s>, those <s>asuras</s> of deluded minds. // Dhs_32.79 //

body.translated_text: Who are devoted to affection?

children.text: phalaṃ yeṣāṃ priyaṃ cittaṃ na ca śīle ratā matiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those whose minds are dear to fruit but whose understanding does not delight in morality —
they, having abandoned the lamp, are devoted to the light of affection. // Dhs_32.80 //

body.translated_text: Those who know the truth of cause and fruit are happy

children.translated_text: Those who desire the best among the gods through the resemblance of cause and fruit —
those knowers of the truth of cause and fruit become partakers of happiness. // Dhs_32.81 //

body.translated_text: Liberation is through knowledge alone

children.text: vinābījaṃ phalaṃ nāsti vinā dīpaṃ kutaḥ prabhā? /
children.translated_text: Without a seed there is no fruit; without a lamp, whence is light?

children.text: vinā śīlaiḥ kutaḥ svargo muktirjñānaṃ vinā kutaḥ? // Dhs_32.82 //
children.translated_text: Without morality, whence is heaven? Without knowledge, whence is liberation? // Dhs_32.82 //

body.translated_text: Who is the wise one?

children.translated_text: That happiness belongs to the liberated one, whose longing has departed, the protector,
who is freed from the thirst for desire, free from possessiveness — the wise one. // Dhs_32.83 //

body.translated_text: Through good deeds, happiness indeed comes

children.translated_text: Whatever happiness is born of <s>karma</s> — all that should be known as tainted;

children.text: yaṃ neṣṭakaṃ bhavatyeva tat sarvamamalaṃ smṛtam // Dhs_32.84 //
children.translated_text: that which is undesired indeed comes to be — all that is remembered as spotless. // Dhs_32.84 //

body.translated_text: Description of the realm of the gods

children.translated_text: That which fulfills all desires, within and without, everywhere —
always luminous in all radiance, attended by hosts of divinities. // Dhs_32.85 //
The excellent mountain shines, resembling jewels and precious gems,
abundant with water and surrounded by lotus ponds. // Dhs_32.86 //
This world is lovely with forests and parks, frequented by deer and birds,
resounding with the roar of mountain caves, rising to pierce the sky. // Dhs_32.87 //

body.translated_text: Where is it attended by the divinities?

children.translated_text: It is always attended by divinities adorned with divine garlands,
and by divinities eminent in dance and song from all sides. // Dhs_32.88 //
As if propelled by fivefold musical instruments, it is perceived —
the supreme and greatly lovely one, garlanded with radiance on all sides. // Dhs_32.89 //
By auspicious and good <s>karma</s>, of surpassing quality —

children.text: yaṃ samāśritya krīḍanti devavṛndāni sarvataḥ // Dhs_32.90 //
children.translated_text: having resorted to which, hosts of gods play everywhere. // Dhs_32.90 //

body.translated_text: Who goes to heaven?

children.translated_text: Those endowed with generosity and morality, the elders, whose minds are always directed thereto,

children.text: ye bhavanti sadā dāntāste janāḥsvargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.91 //
children.translated_text: who are always restrained — those people are heaven-goers. // Dhs_32.91 //
Those of collected minds, peaceful — those people are heaven-goers;

children.text: vairiṇāṃ viṣayo nityaṃ praśāntamanasastu ye // Dhs_32.92 //
children.translated_text: always the domain of enemies indeed are those whose minds are not at peace. // Dhs_32.92 //
Those free from passion, free from delusion — those people are heaven-goers;
where the means is obstructed by intense existence and non-existence,
those of well-tamed minds, the steadfast — those people are heaven-goers. // Dhs_32.93 //
Those who linger on the path of truth enjoy happiness as partakers;
those who know the method of essence and non-essence — those people are heaven-goers. // Dhs_32.94 //

children.text: saṃsāre ye na rakṣanti svamano (nanu) dehinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those embodied ones in <s>saṃsāra</s> who do not guard their own minds —

children.text: nirvāṇābhiratā nityaṃ te janāḥ svargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.95 //
children.translated_text: those always delighting in <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — those people are heaven-goers. // Dhs_32.95 //

children.text: vṛkṣamūle śmaśāne vā tathā ca girikandare /
children.translated_text: At the root of trees, in cremation grounds, and likewise in mountain caves —
those meditators with minds set on beings — those people are heaven-goers. // Dhs_32.96 //
Those who know proper measure, who know place and time, who have avoided evil friends,

children.text: maitreṇa cetasā ye tu te janāḥ svargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.97 //
children.translated_text: those with minds of loving-kindness — those people are heaven-goers. // Dhs_32.97 //
People not delighting in the spectacle of bathing with the water of passion,
those going to solitude, peaceful — those people are heaven-goers. // Dhs_32.98 //
Moment by moment they always see the body as born of impurity;

children.text: kāryākāryavidhijñā ye te janāḥ svargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.99 //
children.translated_text: those who know the method of what should and should not be done — those people are heaven-goers. // Dhs_32.99 //

children.text: dharmāṇāṃ dharmatāṃ ye ca paśyanti vividhā samāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who see the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of dharmas in various and equal ways,

children.text: na ca rakṣanti saṃsāre te janāḥ svargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.100 //
children.translated_text: and who do not cling to <s>saṃsāra</s> — those people are heaven-goers. // Dhs_32.100 //
Feeling, the truth of the middle, arising in manifold ways —

children.text: paśyanti ca na rakṣanti te janāḥ svargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.101 //
children.translated_text: those who see it and do not cling — those people are heaven-goers. // Dhs_32.101 //
Illusion-like, momentary, resembling a <s>Gandharva</s> city —

children.text: ye jānanti (sadā) cittāḥ te janāḥ svargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.102 //
children.translated_text: those who always know the mind to be thus — those people are heaven-goers. // Dhs_32.102 //
Those who know the truth of the single characteristic, themselves knowers of distinction,
with minds passionate for <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — those people are heaven-goers. // Dhs_32.103 //
Those who regard the wives of others as mothers and all embodied beings as fathers,

children.text: paśyanti ye bhayaṃ loke te janāḥ svargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.104 //
children.translated_text: those who see danger in the world — those people are heaven-goers. // Dhs_32.104 //
Always dwelling in the class of emptiness, speaking pleasantly to beings,
not cruel, with minds of prosperity — those people are heaven-goers. // Dhs_32.105 //
Those who regard all others' wealth as sticks and clods,

children.text: saṃtuṣṭāḥ svena cittena te janāḥ svargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.106 //
children.translated_text: content with their own minds — those people are heaven-goers. // Dhs_32.106 //

children.text: na rātrau na divā yeṣāṃ kausīdyadyutiriṣyate /
children.translated_text: Those for whom the light of laziness does not shine, neither by night nor by day,

children.text: nityodyuktavihārā ye te janāḥ svargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.107 //
children.translated_text: those always dwelling in energetic effort — those people are heaven-goers. // Dhs_32.107 //

children.text: kaukṛtyaṃ styānamiddhaṃ ca kausīdyaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: Remorse, sloth-and-torpor, and especially laziness —

children.text: varjayanti sadā dhanyāste janāḥ svargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.108 //
children.translated_text: the blessed ones who always avoid these — those people are heaven-goers. // Dhs_32.108 //
Immorality through the five openings, purified in many ways —

children.text: saṃkṣipanti sadā duḥkhaṃ te janāḥ svargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.109 //
children.translated_text: those who always compress suffering — those people are heaven-goers. // Dhs_32.109 //
Those who know the fourfold <s>upādāna</s> (clinging) and likewise the truths,

children.text: ye paśyanti budhāḥ prajñāṃ te janāḥ svargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.110 //
children.translated_text: the wise who see with <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) — those people are heaven-goers. // Dhs_32.110 //

children.text: duḥkhaṃ duḥkhavipākaśca duḥkheṣu ca manaśca yat /
children.translated_text: Suffering, the ripening of suffering, and the mind set on suffering —

children.text: paśyanti ye sadā tattvaṃ te janāḥ svargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.111 //
children.translated_text: Those who always see the truth of these — those people go to heaven. // Dhs_32.111 //
Those who have undergone severe calamity yet do not abandon the Dharma,
Peaceful and of Dharma-understanding minds — those people go to heaven. // Dhs_32.112 //

children.text: śuklāvadātaṃ ye vastraṃ pāṃsukūlaṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Those who wear bright, white clothing or likewise rag-robes,

children.text: piṇḍapātaratā nityaṃ te janāḥ svargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.113 //
children.translated_text: Who always delight in alms-food — those people go to heaven. // Dhs_32.113 //
Without sticks, of peaceful minds, always dwelling in meditation,

children.text: naiṣkarmyaniratāḥ sarve te janāḥ svargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.114 //
children.translated_text: All devoted to non-action — those people go to heaven. // Dhs_32.114 //
Whether food is refined or unrefined, received according to their wish,

children.text: santuṣyanti na kupyanti te janāḥ svargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.115 //
children.translated_text: They are content and do not become angry — those people go to heaven. // Dhs_32.115 //

children.text: śuklāvadātaṃ ye vastraṃ pāṃsukūlaṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Those who wear bright, white clothing or likewise rag-robes,

children.text: saṃvṛtau caiva saṃtuṣṭāste janāḥ svargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.116 //
children.translated_text: Who are content in restraint — those people go to heaven. // Dhs_32.116 //

children.text: śayyātale yathā bhūmau harmyāgre vā tathāpare /
children.translated_text: Whether on a bed on the ground or atop a palace,

children.text: na duṣyanti (na hṛṣyanti) te janāḥ svargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.117 //
children.translated_text: They are neither displeased nor elated — those people go to heaven. // Dhs_32.117 //
Whatever <s>karma</s> has come within the range of the eye, pertaining to the next life,

children.text: tattvato ye prapaśyanti te janāḥ svargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.118 //
children.translated_text: Those who see it as it truly is — those people go to heaven. // Dhs_32.118 //

children.text: apriyaṃ vā priyaṃ vāpi ye śrutvā tīvrasambhramāt /
children.translated_text: Whether hearing the unpleasant or the pleasant, through intense agitation,
Those whose minds are undisturbed and liberated — those people go to heaven. // Dhs_32.119 //
All six sense faculties and likewise the sense objects —

children.text: saṃkṣipanti na rakṣanti te janāḥ svargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.120 //
children.translated_text: Those who withdraw and guard them — those people go to heaven. // Dhs_32.120 //
All <s>karma</s> that has been done, without distinction, as it truly is —
The blessed ones of stainless minds who see thus — those people go to heaven. // Dhs_32.121 //

children.text: karmaṇāṃ ca vipākaṃ ca kṛtaṃ (ye dhīracetasā) /
children.translated_text: Both <s>karma</s> and its ripening — those who, with steadfast minds, have done them,

children.text: bibhyatīha sadā duḥkhete janāḥ svargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.122 //
children.translated_text: Who always fear suffering here — those people go to heaven. // Dhs_32.122 //
These things of great meaning, and also those that always cause suffering —

children.text: kurvanti vidhivat sarva te janāḥ svargagāminaḥ // Dhs_32.123 //
children.translated_text: Those who do everything according to proper method — those people go to heaven. // Dhs_32.123 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the thirty-second chapter on the Gods (<s>Devavarga</s>). //
(33) Chapter on Happiness (<s>Sukhavarga</s>)
Examination of the nature of happiness

children.translated_text: Those who delight in unsurpassed happiness attained through meditation —

children.text: teṣāṃ sukhaṃ yathāvat syāt nirvāṇapuradarśakam // Dhs_33.1 //
children.translated_text: Their happiness would be as it should, showing the way to the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_33.1 //
By new happiness and suffering, the old is struck down;
For a god, this old is struck down by the new. // Dhs_33.2 //

children.text: dhū(ma) miśraṃ yathā kāṣṭhaṃ vi(ṣṭhā) miśraṃ yathodanam /
children.translated_text: Just as firewood is mixed with smoke, and rice is mixed with filth,
So is all this happiness — its non-ownership is not understood. // Dhs_33.3 //

body.translated_text: The happiness of those bound for the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>

children.translated_text: That is happiness which belongs to the desireless, who walk in solitary bliss,
Free from delusion, free from passion, bound for the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_33.4 //
For them, that happiness among happinesses is pure from beginning to end —

children.text: yeṣāṃ tṛṣṇānugā cāśā sarvathā naiva cetasi // Dhs_33.5 //
children.translated_text: For those in whose minds there is no expectation following after craving. // Dhs_33.5 //
For one whose mind is restrained, who is selfless in every way,
Who is bewildered regarding what should and should not be done — happiness is always present. // Dhs_33.6 //

body.translated_text: Who is the supreme happy one?

children.translated_text: One by whom that delight which is the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> has been externally destroyed —

children.text: sa dhīraḥ pāragaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ sukhī nirvāṇamāśritaḥ // Dhs_33.7 //
children.translated_text: That steadfast one, gone beyond, supreme, happy, taking refuge in <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_33.7 //
That which is conjoined with passion and hatred — that is not the happiness of cravings;

children.text: yatra rāgādinirmuktaṃ tat sukhaṃ nirmalaṃ matam // Dhs_33.8 //
children.translated_text: Wherever one is freed from passion and the rest — that is considered pure happiness. // Dhs_33.8 //

body.translated_text: Where does craving not afflict?

children.translated_text: A god who, having attained the heavenly realm, does not look down with contempt —

children.text: sa sukhāt sukhatāṃ yāti yatra tṛṣṇā na bādhate // Dhs_33.9 //
children.translated_text: He goes from happiness to greater happiness, where craving does not afflict. // Dhs_33.9 //

body.translated_text: That ultimate happiness is better, where death is not found;

children.text: mṛtyupāśairna baddhasya na sukhaṃ vidyate kvacit /
children.translated_text: For one not bound by the nooses of death, no happiness is found anywhere.

children.text: yat sukhaṃ kāmajanakaṃ na tat saukhyaṃ satāṃ matam // Dhs_33.10 //
children.translated_text: That happiness which gives rise to desire — that is not considered happiness by the good. // Dhs_33.10 //
Where one is freed from desire — that happiness is the supreme among happinesses.

children.text: yat sukhaṃ janayet śreyaḥ (payomiśraṃ) yathodanam // Dhs_33.11 //
children.translated_text: That happiness which would produce welfare — like rice mixed with milk; // Dhs_33.11 //
Where there is liberation from craving — like rice mixed with milk.

children.text: yathā padmavane gṛddhā yānti(te) kravyabhakṣiṇaḥ // Dhs_33.12 //
children.translated_text: Just as carrion-eaters go, greedy, into a lotus forest, // Dhs_33.12 //
So too those who practice the impure do not shine in peaceful forests.

children.text: kvacicchāntaṃ vanaṃ ramyaṃ kvacid devāḥ pramādinaḥ // Dhs_33.13 //
children.translated_text: Somewhere the forest is peaceful and delightful; somewhere the gods are heedless. // Dhs_33.13 //

body.translated_text: Who attains supreme happiness?

children.text: viparītaṃ na sadṛśaṃ bhānoḥ śītā yathā prabhā /
children.translated_text: The opposite is not similar — as the cool radiance of the sun.

children.text: gatatṛṣṇasya yat saukhyaṃ muktaduḥkhasya tāyinaḥ // Dhs_33.14 //
children.translated_text: The happiness of one who has gone beyond craving, of the protector freed from suffering — // Dhs_33.14 //
Apart from that happiness, this happiness is not counted;
Of the meditator, the non-heedless, the one freed from sin always — // Dhs_33.15 //

children.text: tat sukhaṃ tat paraṃ saukhyaṃ nedaṃ tṛṣṇāvidāṃ matam /
children.translated_text: That is happiness, that is supreme bliss — not the view of those afflicted by craving.

children.text: munisevyaṃ vanamidaṃ sevitaṃ ca subhāṣitaiḥ // Dhs_33.16 //
children.translated_text: This forest, frequented by sages, and cultivated by well-spoken words — // Dhs_33.16 //
You are not fit to pursue the group of passions, O best of gods;

children.text: yadetad bhavatāṃ saukhyametanna khalu śāśvatam // Dhs_33.17 //
children.translated_text: This happiness of yours is surely not eternal. // Dhs_33.17 //

children.text: tat sukhaṃ paramaṃ śāntaṃ vītatṛṣṇai niṣevyate /
children.translated_text: That supreme, peaceful happiness is cultivated by those free from craving;

children.text: niḥsevitaṃ vanamidaṃ ye gatāḥ paramaṃ padam // Dhs_33.18 //
children.translated_text: This forest is well-cultivated — those who have gone to the supreme state. // Dhs_33.18 //
Upon attaining which, there is the complete cessation of all suffering.
Those not released from the holy life, deceived by the talk of morality — // Dhs_33.19 //

body.translated_text: For monks, dwelling in the forest alone brings happiness

children.text: nārhanti sevituṃ ramyaṃ vanaṃ śāntaṃ subhāṣitam /
children.translated_text: Are not fit to frequent the delightful, peaceful forest, praised by well-spoken words;

children.text: śāntaṃ ca bhāvitaṃ (caiva) ramate śubhagocare // Dhs_33.20 //
children.translated_text: The peaceful and cultivated mind delights in an auspicious domain. // Dhs_33.20 //
The mind of those who pursue passion does not delight in the forest domain;

children.text: na rāgavyākulaṃ cittaṃ vaneṣu labhate dhṛtim // Dhs_33.21 //
children.translated_text: A mind disturbed by passion does not find steadiness in forests. // Dhs_33.21 //

body.translated_text: Who is the best of men?

children.translated_text: One whose understanding, hearing what is worthy, always holds the three worlds in hand —

children.text: sa ratiṃ labhate śāntiṃ vane puruṣasattamaḥ // Dhs_33.22 //
children.translated_text: He finds delight and peace in the forest — the best of men. // Dhs_33.22 //

body.translated_text: The forest should be frequented for happiness

children.translated_text: One who is crooked with the passion of mental fabrication, always surrounded by passion and the rest,

children.text: sa śāntiṃ naiva labhate vane śānte sukhāvahe // Dhs_33.23 //
children.translated_text: Does not find peace in the peaceful forest that brings happiness. // Dhs_33.23 //

children.text: yeṣāṃ tu manasā nityaṃ vane dhyānaniyoginām /
children.translated_text: But those whose minds are always yoked to meditation in the forest —

children.text: vanaṃ teṣāṃ sadāramyaṃ na tu rāgagaveṣiṇām // Dhs_33.24 //
children.translated_text: For them the forest is always delightful, not for those who seek passion. // Dhs_33.24 //

children.text: vaneṣu bhāvitaṃ cittaṃ nagareṣu na kupyate /
children.translated_text: A mind cultivated in forests is not disturbed in cities;

children.text: tasmād vanaṃ sadā sevyaṃ nagaraṃ naiva śasyate // Dhs_33.25 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the forest should always be frequented — the city is never praised. // Dhs_33.25 //
In the city, a person is distracted, surrounded by passion and the rest;

children.text: vikṣipta mohakuṭilaṃ vanaṃ bhūyaḥ prasīdati // Dhs_33.26 //
children.translated_text: But when distracted and crooked with delusion, the forest again brings peace. // Dhs_33.26 //

children.text: tasmād vanaṃ paraṃ śāntaṃ yogināmālayaṃ mahat /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the forest is supremely peaceful, the great abode of <s>yogins</s>;

children.text: saṃsevyaṃ vītamanasā yasya tad vītakalmaṣam // Dhs_33.27 //
children.translated_text: It should be frequented by one of calm mind — that which is free from defilement. // Dhs_33.27 //

body.translated_text: Do not make delight in passions

children.translated_text: The delight that dwells in the heart of the <s>yogin</s> whose senses and mind are calmed —
That power will not belong to a thousand human beings. // Dhs_33.28 //
The delight seen in the meditator, always for purification —

children.text: na yāmeṣvapi sā dṛṣṭā nityaṃ rāgānurāgiṇī // Dhs_33.29 //
children.translated_text: That is not seen even in the night-watches, which are always colored by passion. // Dhs_33.29 //
Delight that is subject to desire always gives rise to suffering;

children.text: yā tu kleśavaśāt prītiḥ (sā prītiḥ) śāśvatā nahi // Dhs_33.30 //
children.translated_text: The joy that arises from the power of defilements — that joy is not eternal. // Dhs_33.30 //

body.translated_text: Who attains the state of welfare?

children.translated_text: Welfare is the practice in forests — that is the good conduct of men;

children.text: yasmāt tat pratibaddhaṃ hi śreyasāṃ padamucyate // Dhs_33.31 //
children.translated_text: Since that is connected with it, it is called the state of welfare. // Dhs_33.31 //
By Dharma well-accumulated, by a mind well-guarded,

children.text: sudṛṣṭaṃ labhate sthānaṃ yatra doṣo na vidyate // Dhs_33.32 //
children.translated_text: One attains a well-seen state where no fault is found. // Dhs_33.32 //

children.text: yaḥ kṣiptamanasā nityaṃ na ca dharmaparāyaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: One whose mind is always distracted, who is not devoted to the Dharma —

children.text: teṣāṃ vṛthā sukhamidaṃ gacchati na nivartate // Dhs_33.33 //
children.translated_text: For them, this happiness departs in vain and does not return. // Dhs_33.33 //

body.translated_text: Knowers of truth do not see suffering

children.text: ye tu tattvavido dhīrāḥ paśyanti jagataḥ sthitim /
children.translated_text: Those who are knowers of truth, the steadfast, who see the condition of the world —

children.text: anityaduḥkhaśūnyānāṃ teṣāṃ duḥkhaṃ na vidyate // Dhs_33.34 //
children.translated_text: Impermanent, suffering, and empty — for them there is no suffering. // Dhs_33.34 //
The practice of the dharma of happiness and the cultivation of knowledge,
Non-violence and truthful speech — that too is established absolutely. // Dhs_33.35 //

body.translated_text: Who goes to heaven?

children.translated_text: Those who have transcended the one dharma, who are deceivers of non-dharma,
Who are possessed of the marks of the three stations — those people go to heaven. // Dhs_33.36 //

body.translated_text: The nature of happiness

children.translated_text: For things whose nature is arising and passing away, that is impermanent and born of <s>karma</s>;

children.text: tat sukhaṃ sāstravaṃ nityaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati // Dhs_33.37 //
children.translated_text: That happiness which is always with defilements has never been and will never be. // Dhs_33.37 //

children.text: tat sukhaṃ tadvitṛṣṇasya nīrāgasya hi dehinaḥ /
children.translated_text: That happiness belongs to the desireless, to the passionless embodied being;

children.text: muktirbhavati doṣasya pārasthasya hi tāpinaḥ // Dhs_33.38 //
children.translated_text: Liberation comes from faults for the tormented one who has reached the far shore. // Dhs_33.38 //

children.text: tat kiñcit sāsravaṃ saukhyaṃ tat sarva kṣaṇikaṃ matam /
children.translated_text: That which is happiness with defilements — all that is considered momentary;

children.text: rāgabandhād vinirmuktaṃ tat sarva niścalaṃ sukham // Dhs_33.39 //
children.translated_text: That which is freed from the bondage of passion — all that is unshakeable happiness. // Dhs_33.39 //

children.text: ye na kṣipanti duḥkhena sukhe yeṣāṃ na saṅgatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who are not cast down by suffering, who have no association with happiness —
They, freed from both suffering and happiness, go toward the happiness of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // Dhs_33.40 //

children.text: anupāyena ye mūḍhāḥ prārthayanti sukhaṃ sadā /
children.translated_text: Those fools who always seek happiness by wrong means —

children.text: bālukābhiryathā tailaṃ yallabhyaṃ nityameva tat // Dhs_33.41 //
children.translated_text: Like seeking oil from sand — that which is to be obtained is always just that. // Dhs_33.41 //
Not even by mind, not even a wise person, not even by a hundred mental wishes,

children.text: śakro 'pi tat sukhaṃ kartu yathā karma kṛtaṃ mahat // Dhs_33.42 //
children.translated_text: Not even <s>Śakra</s> can produce that happiness — only great <s>karma</s> done produces it. // Dhs_33.42 //

body.translated_text: One should practice Dharma for the sake of happiness

children.text: sasukhaṃ yasya tu manaḥ saddharmānucaro bhavet /
children.translated_text: One whose mind is happy, who becomes a follower of the true Dharma —

children.text: duḥkhairmuktyabhilāṣo 'yaṃ sa dharme kurute matim // Dhs_33.43 //
children.translated_text: This is the desire for liberation from suffering — he sets his mind on the Dharma. // Dhs_33.43 //

children.text: nāhetukaṃ sukhaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ duḥkhaṃ vā trividhātmakam /
children.translated_text: No causeless happiness is seen, nor suffering which is of threefold nature;

children.text: sukhe duḥkhe pṛthagbhāve tasmānnu sukṛta caret // Dhs_33.44 //
children.translated_text: Since happiness and suffering have separate existences, therefore one should practice good deeds. // Dhs_33.44 //

children.text: nedaṃ saukhyaṃ sadā śastamadhruvaṃ vipralopi ca /
children.translated_text: This happiness is not always praised — it is unstable and deceptive,
Mixed with the poison of craving — like rice mixed with poison. // Dhs_33.45 //

children.text: tat saukhyaṃ (hi)satāṃ śastaṃ yatra mṛtyurna vidyate /
children.translated_text: That happiness is praised by the good where death is not found,

children.text: na ca priyeṇa viśleṣo nāpriyeṇa samāgamaḥ // Dhs_33.46 //
children.translated_text: Where there is no separation from the beloved, nor encounter with the unloved. // Dhs_33.46 //

body.translated_text: What kind of happiness produces suffering?

children.translated_text: That happiness which consists of women — that is reckoned to produce suffering;
That is seen as the seed-turning toward rebirth in hells. // Dhs_33.47 //

body.text: yat sukhaṃ duḥkhajanakaṃ kathaṃ tat sukhamiṣyate?

children.text: duḥkhād duḥkhataraṃ jñeyaṃ pariṇāmavaśena tat // Dhs_33.48 //
children.translated_text: It should be known as worse than suffering, through the power of its ripening. // Dhs_33.48 //

body.translated_text: That happiness which generates suffering — how can that be desired as happiness?

children.translated_text: This happiness that is experienced — it perishes with time;
Just as the rays of the setting sun are companions in departure. // Dhs_33.49 //
One whose mind does not undergo alteration through happiness and suffering —

children.text: sa dhīmān suraloke ca gatvānyallabhate sukham // Dhs_33.50 //
children.translated_text: That wise one, having gone to the heavenly realm, obtains another happiness. // Dhs_33.50 //

children.text: bhuktaṃ sukhaṃ purāṇaṃ tu hīnakarma karoti ca /
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed old happiness, one commits inferior deeds;

children.text: purāṇaṃ sukṛtaṃ śīrṇa mṛtyukāle na budhyate // Dhs_33.51 //
children.translated_text: Old merit has decayed — at the time of death one does not understand. // Dhs_33.51 //

body.translated_text: All happiness is impermanent

children.translated_text: This happiness that is seen, greatly born of the mind, speech, and desire —
That is impermanent, of perishable nature — it will not last long. // Dhs_33.52 //
Resembling foam and bubbles, like water in a mirage,

children.text: cañcalormi sukhaṃ sarva vinipāto bhavārṇave // Dhs_33.53 //
children.translated_text: All happiness is an unsteady wave — a fall in the ocean of existence. // Dhs_33.53 //
Without remedy, uneven, frightening to all beings —
This king of death rushes with the force of a whirlwind. // Dhs_33.54 //

children.text: nāśayitvā sukhaṃ sarva nāśayitvā ca jīvitam /
children.translated_text: Having destroyed all happiness, having destroyed life,
He will lead the world elsewhere, upon those borne by the intention of <s>karma</s>. // Dhs_33.55 //

children.text: yadatīva sukhaṃ nṛṇāṃ taddhi saukhyāya kalpyate /
children.translated_text: That which is supremely pleasant to people — that indeed is reckoned for happiness;

children.text: yannaiṣyati sukhaṃ kiñcit taddhi naiva vigaṇyate // Dhs_33.56 //
children.translated_text: That which brings no happiness whatsoever — that indeed is not counted. // Dhs_33.56 //
But that present happiness which is free from the poison of craving —

children.text: sarva hyanātmajaṃ duḥkhamanityaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ balam // Dhs_33.57 //
children.translated_text: All suffering born of non-self is impermanent, conditioned, and powerful. // Dhs_33.57 //

body.translated_text: Worldly happiness is not true happiness:

children.text: yad sukhaṃ triṣu lokeṣu na śastaṃ tattvadarśibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: That happiness which in the three worlds is not praised by seers of truth —

children.text: tena matvā kathaṃ devā bhavanti vigatajvarāḥ? // Dhs_33.58 //
children.translated_text: knowing this, how do the gods become free from fever? // Dhs_33.58 //
This terrible time of non-cessation passes swiftly,

children.text: yo bhokṣyate surān sarvān śuṣkendhanamivānalaḥ // Dhs_33.59 //
children.translated_text: which will consume all the gods like fire consumes dry fuel. // Dhs_33.59 //

children.text: atiyāti sukhaṃ sarva kriyatāṃ śraiyasaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: All happiness passes away — let the mind be set upon what is beneficial;

children.text: mā paścāt saṃbhavo yoge mṛtyukālo bhaviṣyati // Dhs_33.60 //
children.translated_text: lest afterward, at the time of death, there be no opportunity for practice. // Dhs_33.60 //

body.translated_text: Happiness is unstable:

children.translated_text: Whatever happiness born of <s>karma</s> is released over thousands of births —
like a wave, this fool should know it to be unstable. // Dhs_33.61 //

body.translated_text: Who is satisfied by happiness?

children.translated_text: A fool is not sated by pleasures, just as fire is not sated by wood;

children.text: tasmānna (sukha) saktasya sukhaṃ bhavati naiṣṭhikam // Dhs_33.62 //
children.translated_text: therefore, for one attached to pleasure, ultimate happiness does not exist. // Dhs_33.62 //
For one free from the fault of poison, who sees the faults of desires,
who meditates and is heedful — that happiness which is untroubled belongs to such a one. // Dhs_33.63 //

children.text: sukhī bhavati tat prāpya na sukhaṃ bhavajanmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: One becomes happy having attained that; the happiness of worldly birth is not such —
like poison mixed with bondage, so is the arising of the happiness of Dharma. // Dhs_33.64 //

body.translated_text: One free from desires enjoys happiness:

children.translated_text: Therefore, for those attached to that pleasure, always seeking desires —
there are manifold pleasures, yet desire is not thereby born to cease. // Dhs_33.65 //

body.translated_text: Through knowledge alone do the senses turn back in their own domain:

children.translated_text: It is not possible to conquer the senses in the domain of sense objects;

children.text: jñānena hi nivartante indriyāṇi svagocare // Dhs_33.66 //
children.translated_text: through knowledge indeed do the senses turn back in their own domain. // Dhs_33.66 //

body.translated_text: Only fools wander in the five destinies:

children.translated_text: Attached to happiness in suffering, fools always of confused understanding,
perverted and bewildered, wander in the five destinies. // Dhs_33.67 //

body.translated_text: Where does happiness become like suffering?

children.translated_text: That which is seen as ultimate happiness — that is called true happiness;

children.text: yatra duḥkhaṃ vipākaṃ syāt tat sukhaṃ duḥkhameva tat // Dhs_33.68 //
children.translated_text: where the ripening is suffering — that happiness is indeed suffering. // Dhs_33.68 //

body.translated_text: The non-commission of evil is itself happiness:

children.translated_text: The wise one wards off suffering that has not yet come;

children.text: pāpasya hetujaṃ duḥkhaṃ pāpasyākaraṇaṃ sukham // Dhs_33.69 //
children.translated_text: suffering born from the cause of evil — the non-commission of evil is happiness. // Dhs_33.69 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the thirty-third chapter, the chapter on happiness. //
(34) The Chapter on Friends.
Who turns one away from evil?

children.translated_text: That friend is called a true friend who is a friend for the next world,

children.text: nivartayati yaḥ pāpād vyasanāccāpi rakṣati // Dhs_34.1 //
children.translated_text: who turns one away from evil and also protects from misfortune. // Dhs_34.1 //
One who always leads toward what is beneficial for the next world —

children.text: mitraṃ bhavati tannṛṇāṃ na mitraṃ pāpakārakam // Dhs_34.2 //
children.translated_text: that one becomes a friend of people; one who does evil is not a friend. // Dhs_34.2 //

body.translated_text: Faults and virtues arise from association:

children.translated_text: What is not putrid, through contact with the putrid, becomes putrid itself;
the putrid is not able to make what is not putrid into something pure through contact with purity. // Dhs_34.3 //
Whatever kind of association a person always makes —

children.text: taddoṣāt sadṛśo dṛṣṭaḥ śubho vā yadi vāśubhaḥ // Dhs_34.4 //
children.translated_text: one is seen as similar to its faults, whether auspicious or inauspicious. // Dhs_34.4 //

body.translated_text: The auspicious does not cause suffering:

children.translated_text: A person desiring the auspicious does not resort to any inauspicious things;

children.text: tenāsau duḥkhamāpnoti na śubhaṃ duḥkhakāraṇam // Dhs_34.5 //
children.translated_text: by that one obtains suffering — the auspicious is not the cause of suffering. // Dhs_34.5 //

body.translated_text: The characteristic of virtues and faults:

children.translated_text: Virtues are seen to arise from association, and faults are born of association;
this characteristic of virtues and faults is declared to be inherent in nature. // Dhs_34.6 //

children.text: yaśasā yujyate yo hi nityaṃ sādhusamāgamāt /
children.translated_text: One who is always united with fame through the company of the good —
through the company of the wicked, the lowest of persons quickly falls. // Dhs_34.7 //

body.translated_text: The fruit of the company of the good:

children.translated_text: This should always be the essence of practice: the avoidance of the wicked,

children.text: sādhubhiśca sadā vāso duṣṭāṇāṃ ca vivarjanam // Dhs_34.8 //
children.translated_text: constant dwelling with the good, and the avoidance of the corrupt. // Dhs_34.8 //
The wise one should remove faults, cultivate the growth of virtues,
make good friends, and be free from laziness. // Dhs_34.9 //

children.text: na māninaṃ kusīdaṃ vā nityaṃ sarvānuśaṅkinam /
children.translated_text: One should not make a friend of one who is proud, or lazy, or always suspicious of everything,
or one smeared with evil and exceedingly cruel — the wise one should not. // Dhs_34.10 //
One should resort to a friend who is diligent, of gentle nature, righteous, free from faults,
of right views, and steady — the wise one should resort to such a friend. // Dhs_34.11 //
An evil one should not be a friend; one should be of the highest manliness;

children.text: uttamaṃ bhajamānasya na doṣebhyo bhayaṃ bhavet // Dhs_34.12 //
children.translated_text: for one who resorts to the best, there is no fear from faults. // Dhs_34.12 //

body.translated_text: Who becomes contemptible?

children.translated_text: An embodied being whose beauty, wealth, family, and the like are fractured —

children.text: bhayapradaṃ taṃ mātaṅgaḥ prayāntaṃ naiva paśyati // Dhs_34.13 //
children.translated_text: the outcast does not even see that one, who inspires fear, as departing. // Dhs_34.13 //
A person who is always arrogant, with senses agitated by heedlessness,

children.text: laghutāṃ yāti loke 'smin pretyapāpeṣu pacyate // Dhs_34.14 //
children.translated_text: becomes contemptible in this world; after death, one is cooked in evil destinies. // Dhs_34.14 //
Those people who commit evil for the sake of beauty, wealth, and pride —

children.text: teṣāṃ na suśamaṃ (karma) pretyapāpeṣu pacyate // Dhs_34.15 //
children.translated_text: for them there is no peaceful <s>karma</s>; after death they are cooked in evil destinies. // Dhs_34.15 //

children.text: rūpaiśvaryakulārthā ye na te tattvasya bhāginaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who seek beauty, wealth, and family — they are not sharers of truth;

children.text: atattvabuddhayo bālā na taranti bhavārṇavam // Dhs_34.16 //
children.translated_text: fools of untrue understanding do not cross the ocean of existence. // Dhs_34.16 //

body.translated_text: A family endowed with knowledge and morality is the best:

children.translated_text: This family, those riches, and whatever other happiness is desired —
all these are impermanent; therefore one should not find rest in them. // Dhs_34.17 //
The wise do not go to that which is devoid of knowledge and morality;

children.text: yeṣāṃ jñānaṃ ca śīlaṃ ca te kule mahati sthitāḥ // Dhs_34.18 //
children.translated_text: those who possess knowledge and morality — they are established in a great family. // Dhs_34.18 //
To practice stainless morality — morality itself is most wondrous;
those born of great families are wise and self-controlled. // Dhs_34.19 //
Those who are united with giving, morality, austerity, meditation, truth, sovereignty, and valor —

children.text: saṃyuktā ye kulīnāste ye na dharmavivarjitāḥ // Dhs_34.20 //
children.translated_text: they are of noble family, they who are not devoid of Dharma. // Dhs_34.20 //
For one devoid of sovereignty and knowledge, there is neither family nor companionship;

children.text: tasmātkulaṃ jñānamayaṃ jñānahīnaṃ na tat kulam // Dhs_34.21 //
children.translated_text: therefore, family consists of knowledge — devoid of knowledge, that is not family. // Dhs_34.21 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter, the chapter on friends. //
(35) The Chapter on Admonition to Kings.
A righteous king goes to heaven:

children.translated_text: One who watches over the earth and its people, practicing Dharma, with conquered senses —

children.text: sa rājā dhārmiko dhīmān svargalokopapattaye // Dhs_35.1 //
children.translated_text: that righteous, wise king is destined for the world of heaven. // Dhs_35.1 //

body.translated_text: What kind of king is free from greed?

children.text: niyataṃ yaḥ karaṃ kāle dharmeṇa paribhujyate /
children.translated_text: One who, at the appointed time, collects taxes and enjoys them righteously —

children.text: sa rājā lobhanirmukto yāmānāmadhipo bhavet // Dhs_35.2 //
children.translated_text: that king, free from greed, becomes the lord of the <s>Yāmas</s> (celestial beings). // Dhs_35.2 //

body.translated_text: The true nature of a king:

children.translated_text: One who is patient, of pleasant speech, who controls anger and joy —

children.text: sa mahīṃ pālayettvenāṃ loke hi śreṣṭhatāṃ gataḥ // Dhs_35.3 //
children.translated_text: such one should protect this earth, having attained supreme distinction in the world. // Dhs_35.3 //
The faith of the impartial one is not destroyed by a friend;
that leader of the assembly of nobles is destined for the world of the gods. // Dhs_35.4 //

children.text: baddhadarśī mahātmā yo gurupūjaka eva ca /
children.translated_text: A great soul who sees the bound, who honors teachers,
who is not fickle, of firm understanding — such one goes to the presence of the gods. // Dhs_35.5 //
One who follows what was given by ancestors in former times and what the gods teach,

children.text: na ca hiṃsati bhūtāni sa deveṣūpapadyate // Dhs_35.6 //
children.translated_text: and who does not harm beings — such one is reborn among the gods. // Dhs_35.6 //
Always skilled in giving and morality, speaking of Dharma, with conquered senses —

children.text: sa matvāryāṃ mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ devalokaṃ mahīyate // Dhs_35.7 //
children.translated_text: such one, having considered the whole noble earth, is honored in the world of the gods. // Dhs_35.7 //
One who does not uphold the unrighteous but protects the righteous —
that one, purified by righteous conduct, goes to the presence of the gods. // Dhs_35.8 //

children.text: na strīṇāṃ vaśago rājā sādhūnāṃ ca vaset sadā /
children.translated_text: A king should not be under the power of women and should always dwell with the good;
that wise one of stainless understanding is destined for the world of the gods. // Dhs_35.9 //

children.text: na sarvasya vacogrāhī priyaḥ sādhujanasya tu /
children.translated_text: Not accepting everyone's words but being dear to good people —
such one, immortal and seeing truth, grows like an unsown plant. // Dhs_35.10 //

body.translated_text: Who becomes the lord of the <s>Yāmas</s>?

children.translated_text: One who comes to covet Dharma and will not obtain wealth —
that one, freed from the stain of greed, becomes the lord of the <s>Yāmas</s>. // Dhs_35.11 //
Not through wrong seeing, nor through devotion to the sight of women —

children.text: sa śuddha eva vimalo yāmānāmadhipo bhavet // Dhs_35.12 //
children.translated_text: that one is indeed pure and stainless, and becomes the lord of the <s>Yāmas</s>. // Dhs_35.12 //

body.translated_text: What kind of king becomes beloved of the gods?

children.translated_text: A wise one always devoted to morality, who has attained constant generosity,

children.text: pravijitya mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ pretya devapriyo bhavet // Dhs_35.13 //
children.translated_text: having conquered the whole earth — after death becomes beloved of the gods. // Dhs_35.13 //

children.text: priyasya tu bhaved vākyaṃ stotrotsavakaraṃ param /
children.translated_text: The speech of the beloved would be supremely delightful, producing joy like a hymn of praise;
having gladdened the earth, one is destined for the world of the gods. // Dhs_35.14 //
One whose speech is truthful, unshakable like <s>Meru</s> —
ascending the stairway of truth, such one goes to the presence of the gods. // Dhs_35.15 //

children.text: hrāsavṛddhī ca bhūtānāmakasmāt kurute hi yaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who does not cause the diminution or increase of beings without reason —

children.text: sa rājā vai paro devairdevaloke ca tiṣṭhati // Dhs_35.16 //
children.translated_text: that king is indeed supreme among the gods and dwells in the world of the gods. // Dhs_35.16 //
One who knows the inner truth of people, who knows strength and weakness —

children.text: sa dhībalābhyāṃ saṃyukto yāmānāmadhipo bhavet // Dhs_35.17 //
children.translated_text: that one, endowed with wisdom and strength, becomes the lord of the <s>Yāmas</s>. // Dhs_35.17 //
The station of the triple realm, and what is called the Three Jewels here —

children.text: yastat pūjayate rājā sa deveṣūpajāyate // Dhs_35.18 //
children.translated_text: the king who worships that is reborn among the gods. // Dhs_35.18 //

children.text: kālaṃ niyatadarśī yaḥ prajānāṃ ca hite rataḥ /
children.translated_text: One who always sees the proper time and delights in the welfare of the people,
who is auspicious in every direction — is remembered as the lord of the gods. // Dhs_35.19 //
Freed from the stain of blame, free from the fault of attachment,

children.text: jñānagocarasampūjyo niyataṃ deva eva saḥ // Dhs_35.20 //
children.translated_text: honored in the domain of knowledge — that one is indeed certainly a god. // Dhs_35.20 //

body.translated_text: Who goes to heaven?

children.translated_text: One free from the fault of laziness, always of firm valor,

children.text: nāśayitvā sa doṣaughān pretya svargeṣu jāyate // Dhs_35.21 //
children.translated_text: having destroyed the flood of faults — after death is born in the heavens. // Dhs_35.21 //

body.translated_text: A king surrounded by good friends becomes lord of the gods:

children.translated_text: One whose friends are always doers of beneficial deeds —

children.text: sa mitraiḥ samparivṛto nṛpo devādhipo bhavet // Dhs_35.22 //
children.translated_text: that king, surrounded by friends, becomes lord of the gods. // Dhs_35.22 //
One should not resort to the ill-behaved and should avoid verbal abuse;

children.text: sa sadyo viṣanirmuktaḥ surāṇāmadhipo bhavet // Dhs_35.23 //
children.translated_text: that one, instantly freed from poison, becomes lord of the gods. // Dhs_35.23 //
For the destruction of anger and elation, one is not protected in evil deeds;
that one, cleansed of the mire of evil, is always lord of the world of the gods. // Dhs_35.24 //

children.text: na śaktaḥ pānabhojyeṣu saṃsaktastu śubhe sadā /
children.translated_text: Not attached to drink and food, but always devoted to the auspicious —
that one, seeing the pure Dharma, a wise one, goes to the highest state. // Dhs_35.25 //

body.translated_text: Who attains the supreme station?

children.translated_text: One who thinks well-considered thoughts and abides in Dharma —

children.text: dharmodayena dṛṣṭena yathā yāti triviṣṭapam // Dhs_35.26 //
children.translated_text: through the visible arising of Dharma, thus goes to heaven. // Dhs_35.26 //
One who, from the long thread of <s>saṃsāra</s>, swiftly practices Dharma —
that one, freed from the long thread, goes to the supreme station. // Dhs_35.27 //

body.translated_text: One who protects the people through Dharma goes to the happiness of heaven:

children.translated_text: The king who always protects the people through Dharma alone —

children.text: sa dhārmikaḥ praśastātmā suraloke mahīyate // Dhs_35.28 //
children.translated_text: that righteous one of praiseworthy soul is honored in the world of the gods. // Dhs_35.28 //
These ten wholesome dharmas have been declared here by the seer of truth;

children.text: yaste prakurute dharmān sa surādhipatāṃ vrajet // Dhs_35.29 //
children.translated_text: one who practices those dharmas goes to the lordship of the gods. // Dhs_35.29 //
One who sees causes and conditions, and likewise the path and the non-path —
that one, freed from the stain of wrong views, a wise one, has gone to the highest state. // Dhs_35.30 //

body.translated_text: With what qualities does a king become lord of the gods?

children.text: yo devatāṃ pūjayati yathā cāhni mahīpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: The king who worships the deities daily, as is proper —

children.text: sa devapūjito bhūyo devānāmadhipo bhavet // Dhs_35.31 //
children.translated_text: that one, honored by the gods in return, becomes lord of the gods. // Dhs_35.31 //
With an untroubled mind, serene, a protector of dependents,
content with one's own wives — such one becomes lord of the gods. // Dhs_35.32 //

body.translated_text: Who is virtuous?

children.translated_text: One who is not diminished by sense objects that carry away all fools —

children.text: sa śīlavān divaṃ yāti nityaṃ śīlena rakṣitaḥ // Dhs_35.33 //
children.translated_text: that virtuous one goes to heaven, always protected by morality. // Dhs_35.33 //
One who always resorts to the righteous who ward off ignorance,
a contemplator of the true Dharma — is fit for happiness in the assembly of the gods. // Dhs_35.34 //
One whose mind is at ease with duties, free from those who carry away assemblies —

children.text: sa śīlavān divaṃ yāti nityaṃ śīlena rakṣitaḥ // Dhs_35.35 //
children.translated_text: that virtuous one goes to heaven, always protected by morality. // Dhs_35.35 //

body.translated_text: A king who upholds the true Dharma is indeed lord of the earth:

children.translated_text: A king who protects this dharma through righteous activity,

children.text: praśāsti ca mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ yāmānāmadhipo bhavet // Dhs_35.36 //
children.translated_text: rules the entire earth and becomes lord of the watches. // Dhs_35.36 //

body.translated_text: Even the servant of a king devoted to righteous action shines.

children.translated_text: A servant devoted to righteous action, when the king possesses good qualities,

children.text: jano nirmalatāṃ yāti śaraccandra ivāmbare // Dhs_35.37 //
children.translated_text: the people attain purity, like the autumn moon in the sky. // Dhs_35.37 //

body.translated_text: Which king becomes equal to the gods?

children.translated_text: Those who know the method of cause, aim, and procedure, who are not opposed to one another,
who rightly accomplish the purposes of their lord — they have come under the power of the gods. // Dhs_35.38 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the thirty-fifth chapter on advice to kings. //
(36) Chapter on Praise:
Praise of the <s>Buddha</s>:

children.translated_text: To the foremost knower of equal beings, the kinsman of all beings,
the caravan-leader of the true path, the breaker of the bonds of existence — // Dhs_36.1 //
to the destroyer of various wrong views, the liberator from all doubts,
to the establisher of right view — homage to the one whose eye is awakened knowledge! // Dhs_36.2 //
To the breaker of all distress, the purifier of the stain of the three faults,
homage to the one who is like a star, from whom all seeds bear fruit! // Dhs_36.3 //
To the foremost of all sources of wisdom, the foremost knower of all meditations,
to the noblest of all supreme jewels — homage to the foremost seer of the tethering-post! // Dhs_36.4 //
This image of him who is separated from the destruction of the world, the tormentor,
is seen as peaceful — the opener of the door to liberation. // Dhs_36.5 //
The person who always worships this image with a peaceful mind
is freed from the fear of existence and attains cessation. // Dhs_36.6 //
This is the peaceful, delightful state; this is declared to be the ultimate —
that which this guide to the city of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> teaches as dharma. // Dhs_36.7 //
Relying on his word, persons of self-dependent valor
always draw near that state which brings infinite happiness. // Dhs_36.8 //
Having mounted this beforehand, persons who contemplate reality
cross the terrible ocean-flood of the three worlds, the sea of existence. // Dhs_36.9 //
He is the eye of the world, which is entirely without eyes;
he is the supreme light, the light born from the ultimate source of light. // Dhs_36.10 //
The stains of passion and the rest in the minds of beings at the end of an age —
the King of Speech purifies them with the great water of knowledge. // Dhs_36.11 //
That state which was not seen by all the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers) with their hands of knowledge —
that state was shown by you to men through stainless words. // Dhs_36.12 //
This heedless, protectorless people was carried across by you;
the protector who has crossed and reached the other shore carries others across, through the destruction of evil. // Dhs_36.13 //
For the benefit of all the world, you alone stand established;
for the welfare of the unwelfare — you alone are the Supreme Person. // Dhs_36.14 //
In this beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>, by words that remove the afflictions of men,

children.text: tvayā viśodhito vākyaistamaḥ sūryodaye yathā // Dhs_36.15 //
children.translated_text: the darkness was purified by you — as at sunrise. // Dhs_36.15 //
Inexhaustible, the great illuminator of the realm of all dharmas,
you alone are the Lord of the World, an ocean of supramundane qualities. // Dhs_36.16 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter on praise. //

children.translated_text: Endowed with merit, divine happiness, friendship, praise of kings,
true dharma, mindfulness, and extensiveness — this collection is compiled. //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the fourth declaration. //

children.text: ye ca dharmā hetubhavā teṣāṃ tathāgato 'vadat /
children.translated_text: Whatever dharmas arise from causes, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared their cause;
and that which is their cessation — thus speaks the Great Ascetic. //
Having obtained merit, having split the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), of beauty like <s>Vālā</s> to the unborn —
as long as the world is disturbed, he knows it as agitated by those who rest in reasoning, through truthful words. //

body.translated_text: Drawn forth by the monk <s>Avalokitasiṃha</s> from the excellent <s>sūtra</s> that is a vast and profound ocean of extensiveness —

body.text: mohāśivādirahitasya vākyavidyasya vipulārjanasya 'dharmasamuccayo' nāma dharmaparyāyaḥ samāptaḥ /
body.translated_text: the dharma-discourse named '<s>Dharmasamuccaya</s>' (Collection of Dharmas), belonging to one free from delusion and <s>Śiva</s>-doctrine, a knower of words, of vast acquisition, is completed. /
// Thus, may there be auspiciousness. //
